became.t: v. become 的过去式；成为、变成

e.en: She {became} a software engineer after years of study.
e.zh: 经过多年学习,她成为了一名软件工程师。

e.en: The startup {became} profitable within its first year.
e.zh: 这家初创公司在第一年就实现了盈利。

because.t:
conj. 因为
prep. 因为（because of）

e.en: I stayed home {because} the weather was awful.
e.zh: 我待在家里,因为天气太糟糕了。

e.en: She got the job {because} of her strong portfolio.
e.zh: 她得到这份工作是因为作品集很出色。

e.en: The lasagna is layered with cheese and rich {bechamel}.
e.zh: 这道千层面层层叠着奶酪和浓郁的白汁。

e.en: Whisk the {bechamel} sauce until it thickens evenly.
e.zh: 搅打白酱,直到它均匀变稠。

e.en: The musician {Beck} released a new album last month.
e.zh: 音乐人贝克上个月发行了一张新专辑。

e.en: His assistant is always at his {beck} and call.
e.zh: 他的助理总是随叫随到。

beckenham.t: n. 贝肯汉姆（英国地名）

e.en: David Bowie spent his early career in {Beckenham}.
e.zh: 大卫·鲍伊早年的职业生涯在贝肯汉姆度过。

e.en: {Beckenham} has good train links into central London.
e.zh: 贝肯汉姆有便利的火车线路通往伦敦市中心。

e.en: Thomas {Becket} was murdered in Canterbury Cathedral.
e.zh: 托马斯·贝克特在坎特伯雷大教堂被刺杀。

e.en: Pilgrims still visit the shrine of Saint {Becket}.
e.zh: 朝圣者至今仍前往拜访圣贝克特的圣殿。

beckett.t: n. 贝克特（姓氏，如塞缪尔·贝克特）

e.en: Samuel {Beckett} won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
e.zh: 塞缪尔·贝克特获得了诺贝尔文学奖。

e.en: We watched a {Beckett} play at the small theater downtown.
e.zh: 我们在市中心的小剧院看了一场贝克特的戏剧。

e.en: {Beckley} is a small city in southern West Virginia.
e.zh: 贝克利是西弗吉尼亚州南部的一座小城。

e.en: She drove through {Beckley} on her road trip east.
e.zh: 她在东行的公路旅行中经过了贝克利。

e.en: The waiter saw me {beckon} and came right over.
e.zh: 服务员看到我招手就立刻过来了。

e.en: Tropical beaches {beckon} travelers escaping winter.
e.zh: 热带海滩吸引着逃避冬天的旅行者。

beckoning.t:
adj. 诱人的
v. 招手（beckon 的现在分词）

e.en: She gave a {beckoning} wave from across the street.
e.zh: 她从街对面挥手示意我过去。

e.en: The warm fireplace was {beckoning} after the cold walk.
e.zh: 在寒冷的散步之后,温暖的壁炉显得格外诱人。

e.en: He wants to {become} a doctor after graduation.
e.zh: 他想在毕业后成为一名医生。

e.en: Remote work has {become} the norm at many companies.
e.zh: 远程办公已经成为许多公司的常态。

becomes.t: v. become 的第三人称单数形式

e.en: Water {becomes} ice when the temperature drops below zero.
e.zh: 当温度降至零度以下时,水会变成冰。

e.en: She {becomes} more confident with every presentation.
e.zh: 她每做一次演讲都变得更自信。

becoming.t:
adj. 得体的、合适的
v. 正在成为

e.en: That dress is very {becoming} on you.
e.zh: 那条裙子非常衬你。

e.en: AI is rapidly {becoming} part of everyday work.
e.zh: 人工智能正迅速成为日常工作的一部分。

bed.t:
n. 床；河床、花坛
v. 铺设

e.en: I usually go to {bed} around eleven o'clock.
e.zh: 我通常在十一点左右上床睡觉。

e.en: She planted tulips in the flower {bed} by the porch.
e.zh: 她在门廊旁的花坛里种了郁金香。

e.en: {Bedale} is a charming market town in North Yorkshire.
e.zh: 贝代尔是北约克郡一座迷人的集市小镇。

e.en: We stopped in {Bedale} for tea on the way north.
e.zh: 我们北上途中在贝代尔停下来喝茶。

e.en: The magician's tricks always {bedazzle} young audiences.
e.zh: 魔术师的把戏总能让年轻观众目眩神迷。

e.en: She likes to {bedazzle} her phone case with rhinestones.
e.zh: 她喜欢用水钻装饰她的手机壳。

bedazzled.t: adj. 被迷住的、眼花缭乱的

e.en: The audience was {bedazzled} by the dazzling fireworks display.
e.zh: 观众被绚丽的烟花表演迷住了。

e.en: She wore a {bedazzled} jacket covered in tiny crystals.
e.zh: 她穿着一件镶满小水晶的闪亮夹克。

e.en: The hotel had to fumigate after a {bedbug} outbreak.
e.zh: 那家酒店在臭虫爆发后不得不进行熏蒸消毒。

e.en: Check the mattress seams for any sign of {bedbug} eggs.
e.zh: 检查床垫缝隙,看看是否有臭虫卵的痕迹。

bedchamber.t: n. 寝室、卧房（古雅用法）

e.en: The queen's {bedchamber} was decorated with silk tapestries.
e.zh: 女王的寝宫装饰着丝绸挂毯。

e.en: Servants were forbidden from entering the royal {bedchamber}.
e.zh: 仆人被禁止进入王室寝宫。

e.en: She stripped the {bedclothes} and tossed them in the wash.
e.zh: 她把床上用品扯下来扔进了洗衣机。

e.en: The child kicked off all the {bedclothes} during the night.
e.zh: 那孩子夜里把被褥全踢开了。

e.en: Grandma stitched a beautiful patchwork {bedcover} by hand.
e.zh: 奶奶手工缝制了一条漂亮的拼布床罩。

e.en: The hotel uses a crisp white {bedcover} on every bed.
e.zh: 那家酒店每张床上都铺着一块洁白的床罩。

bedded.t: v. bed 的过去式；安置入睡、种入

e.en: The hens have already {bedded} down for the night.
e.zh: 母鸡已经安顿下来过夜了。

e.en: Rough stones were {bedded} in fresh concrete along the path.
e.zh: 粗糙的石头被嵌入小路旁新浇的混凝土中。

bedding.t: n. 床上用品；(动物的) 垫草

e.en: I bought new cotton {bedding} during the holiday sale.
e.zh: 我在假日促销时买了一套新的棉质床品。

e.en: Change the rabbit's {bedding} at least twice a week.
e.zh: 每周至少给兔子换两次窝里的垫料。

beddings.t: n. bedding 的复数；床上用品

e.en: The hotel orders fresh {beddings} from a local supplier.
e.zh: 酒店从当地供应商订购新的床上用品。

e.en: She compared {beddings} of different thread counts online.
e.zh: 她在网上比较了不同支数的床品。

e.en: Locals {bedeck} the streets with lanterns for the festival.
e.zh: 当地人在节日期间用灯笼装饰街道。

e.en: They {bedeck} the church with white lilies for the wedding.
e.zh: 他们用白百合装饰教堂以迎接婚礼。

e.en: Software bugs continue to {bedevil} the development team.
e.zh: 软件漏洞不断困扰着开发团队。

e.en: Supply chain issues {bedevil} small electronics makers.
e.zh: 供应链问题困扰着小型电子产品制造商。

e.en: Politics often makes for a strange {bedfellow}.
e.zh: 政治常常会造就奇怪的同盟者。

e.en: Innovation and tradition can be an unlikely {bedfellow}.
e.zh: 创新与传统可能成为意想不到的伙伴。

bedford.t: n. 贝德福德（英国城市）

e.en: {Bedford} sits on the River Great Ouse in England.
e.zh: 贝德福德坐落在英格兰大乌斯河畔。

e.en: She caught the train from {Bedford} into London.
e.zh: 她从贝德福德搭火车进伦敦。

bedfordshire.t: n. 贝德福德郡（英格兰郡名）

e.en: {Bedfordshire} is known for its rolling countryside and villages.
e.zh: 贝德福德郡以连绵的乡村和村庄闻名。

e.en: He moved to {Bedfordshire} for a quieter way of life.
e.zh: 他搬到贝德福德郡寻求更安静的生活方式。

e.en: The wooden {bedframe} creaked every time she rolled over.
e.zh: 她每翻一次身,木床架就吱呀作响。

e.en: We assembled the new metal {bedframe} in under an hour.
e.zh: 我们在不到一小时内组装好了新的金属床架。

bedhead.t: n. 床头板；睡乱的头发

e.en: He showed up to the meeting with serious {bedhead}.
e.zh: 他顶着一头乱糟糟的睡发出现在会议上。

e.en: A quick shower usually fixes my morning {bedhead}.
e.zh: 快速冲个澡通常就能搞定我早上的乱发。

e.en: The performers {bedizen} themselves in feathers and sequins.
e.zh: 表演者们用羽毛和亮片把自己打扮得花枝招展。

e.en: Critics said the film tries to {bedizen} a thin plot.
e.zh: 评论家说这部电影试图用花哨手法掩盖单薄的剧情。

e.en: The classroom turned into total {bedlam} when the bell broke.
e.zh: 铃声坏了之后,教室里乱成了一锅粥。

e.en: It was {bedlam} at the airport during the holiday rush.
e.zh: 假期高峰期的机场一片混乱。

bedlinen.t: n. 床上亚麻制品（床单、枕套等）

e.en: Fresh {bedlinen} makes the guest room feel inviting.
e.zh: 换上干净的床单被罩，客房显得格外舒适。

e.en: The hotel changes the {bedlinen} every single day.
e.zh: 酒店每天都会更换床上用品。

bedlington.t: n. 贝德灵顿（地名/梗犬品种）

e.en: Her {bedlington} terrier looks just like a small lamb.
e.zh: 她的贝灵顿梗看起来就像一只小羊羔。

e.en: The {bedlington} won first prize at the dog show.
e.zh: 那只贝灵顿梗在犬展上获得了一等奖。

bedouin.t: n. 贝都因人（阿拉伯游牧民族）

e.en: A {bedouin} guide led the tourists across the desert.
e.zh: 一位贝都因向导带领游客穿越沙漠。

e.en: The {bedouin} tribes have lived nomadically for centuries.
e.zh: 贝都因部落几个世纪以来一直过着游牧生活。

e.en: The nurse gently brought a {bedpan} to the patient.
e.zh: 护士轻轻地给病人拿来一个便盆。

e.en: Hospital staff sterilize every {bedpan} after use.
e.zh: 医院员工每次使用后都会对便盆消毒。

e.en: She hung her bag on the {bedpost} before sleeping.
e.zh: 睡觉前她把包挂在了床柱上。

e.en: The carved {bedpost} was a family heirloom.
e.zh: 那根雕花床柱是家族的传家宝。

bedraggled.t: adj. 湿透的；狼狈不堪的

e.en: The {bedraggled} cat came home soaked from the rain.
e.zh: 那只浑身湿透的猫从雨中回到了家。

e.en: Hikers arrived {bedraggled} but cheerful after the storm.
e.zh: 徒步者在暴风雨后到达，虽然狼狈但很开心。

e.en: They installed a {bedrail} to keep the toddler safe.
e.zh: 他们装了一根床栏，以保障幼儿安全。

e.en: The hospital {bedrail} folds down for easy access.
e.zh: 医院的床栏可以放下，方便操作。

e.en: Grandma has been {bedridden} since her hip surgery.
e.zh: 自从髋部手术后，奶奶就一直卧床不起。

e.en: Volunteers visit {bedridden} patients to keep them company.
e.zh: 志愿者会去探望卧床的病人，陪他们聊天。

e.en: Trust is the {bedrock} of any healthy relationship.
e.zh: 信任是任何健康关系的基石。

e.en: Engineers drilled down to the {bedrock} before building.
e.zh: 工程师在动工前钻探到了岩床。

e.en: The hiker tied his {bedroll} to the backpack.
e.zh: 徒步者把睡袋卷好绑在背包上。

e.en: Cowboys slept under the stars in their {bedroll}.
e.zh: 牛仔们裹着行军被卷睡在星空下。

e.en: Her {bedroom} is painted a calming shade of blue.
e.zh: 她的卧室刷成了让人放松的蓝色。

e.en: The apartment has two {bedroom} suites and a balcony.
e.zh: 这套公寓有两间套房卧室和一个阳台。

bedroomed.t: adj. 有…间卧室的（如 two-bedroomed）

e.en: They bought a three-{bedroomed} house in the suburbs.
e.zh: 他们在郊区买了一套三居室的房子。

e.en: The two-{bedroomed} flat suits a small family well.
e.zh: 这套两居室公寓很适合小家庭居住。

e.en: The villa has five {bedrooms} and three bathrooms.
e.zh: 这栋别墅有五间卧室和三间浴室。

e.en: All the upstairs {bedrooms} face the morning sun.
e.zh: 楼上所有的卧室都朝向晨阳。

e.en: The hostel offers bunk {beds} at a low price.
e.zh: 这家青旅提供低价的双层床位。

e.en: She planted tulips in the flower {beds} out front.
e.zh: 她在前院的花圃里种了郁金香。

e.en: He wrapped himself in a {bedsheet} for the costume.
e.zh: 他用一张床单裹住自己作为服装。

e.en: The cotton {bedsheet} feels cool on summer nights.
e.zh: 这张棉床单在夏夜摸起来很凉爽。

e.en: She left a glass of water on the {bedside} table.
e.zh: 她在床头柜上留了一杯水。

e.en: The doctor sat at his {bedside} all night.
e.zh: 医生整夜守在他的床边。

e.en: Nurses moved quietly between the patients' {bedsides}.
e.zh: 护士们在病人床边之间安静地走动。

e.en: Family photos sat on both {bedsides} of the room.
e.zh: 房间两侧的床头都摆着家人的照片。

bedsit.t: n. 带床的单间出租房（英式）

e.en: As a student, she rented a tiny {bedsit} in London.
e.zh: 学生时代，她在伦敦租了一间小小的单间公寓。

e.en: The {bedsit} had a kitchenette tucked behind a curtain.
e.zh: 那间单间公寓有个藏在帘子后的小厨房。

bedsitter.t: n. 带床的单间出租房（英式）

e.en: He shared a cramped {bedsitter} with his cousin.
e.zh: 他和表弟合租了一间狭小的单间公寓。

e.en: The {bedsitter} above the shop rents out cheaply.
e.zh: 店铺楼上的单间公寓租金便宜。

e.en: Nurses turn patients regularly to prevent every {bedsore}.
e.zh: 护士会定时给病人翻身，以预防褥疮。

e.en: He developed a painful {bedsore} after weeks in bed.
e.zh: 卧床数周后，他长出了一个疼痛的褥疮。

e.en: A floral {bedspread} brightened up the dull room.
e.zh: 一条花卉床罩让沉闷的房间亮了起来。

e.en: She folded the {bedspread} neatly at the foot.
e.zh: 她把床罩整齐地叠在床尾。

e.en: A broken {bedspring} kept poking him all night.
e.zh: 一根坏掉的床垫弹簧整夜都在戳他。

e.en: The old mattress sagged where the {bedspring} gave out.
e.zh: 旧床垫在弹簧塌陷的地方凹了下去。

e.en: My phone charges on the {bedstand} every night.
e.zh: 我每晚都把手机放在床头柜上充电。

e.en: She set her glasses on the {bedstand} and yawned.
e.zh: 她把眼镜放到床头柜上，打了个哈欠。

e.en: The antique iron {bedstead} creaked under his weight.
e.zh: 那张古董铁床架在他身下吱呀作响。

e.en: They restored a wooden {bedstead} from the attic.
e.zh: 他们把阁楼里的一张木床架修复了。

e.en: Reading a story before {bedtime} helps kids relax.
e.zh: 睡前读个故事能帮孩子放松下来。

e.en: My {bedtime} routine includes a cup of warm tea.
e.zh: 我的睡前习惯包括喝一杯热茶。

e.en: A {bee} buzzed lazily around the lavender bush.
e.zh: 一只蜜蜂懒洋洋地在薰衣草丛旁嗡嗡飞舞。

e.en: She won the school spelling {bee} last year.
e.zh: 她去年赢得了学校的拼字比赛。

beeb.t: n. BBC 的俗称（英国广播公司）

e.en: My grandparents only watch the {beeb} for the news.
e.zh: 我祖父母只看BBC的新闻节目。

e.en: That comedy first aired on the {beeb} in 1995.
e.zh: 那部喜剧最早于1995年在BBC播出。

e.en: A massive {beech} tree shaded the entire backyard.
e.zh: 一棵巨大的山毛榉树荫蔽了整个后院。

e.en: The furniture is crafted from solid {beech} wood.
e.zh: 这些家具是用实心山毛榉木打造的。

e.en: Squirrels gathered every {beechnut} from the forest floor.
e.zh: 松鼠们把林地上的每一颗山毛榉果都收集起来。

e.en: She roasted a handful of {beechnut} kernels for snacks.
e.zh: 她烤了一把山毛榉果仁当零食吃。

e.en: The chef prefers a {beechwood} cutting board for vegetables.
e.zh: 这位厨师切菜偏爱用山毛榉木砧板。

e.en: Smoking the ham over {beechwood} adds a sweet flavor.
e.zh: 用山毛榉木熏火腿能增添一种甜香味。

beef.t:
n. 牛肉
v. 抱怨（俚语）

e.en: He grilled some {beef} burgers for the barbecue.
e.zh: 他在烧烤会上烤了几个牛肉汉堡。

e.en: The two rappers had a long-running {beef} online.
e.zh: 那两位说唱歌手在网上长期不和。

e.en: I ordered a double {beefburger} with extra cheese.
e.zh: 我点了一个加了双份芝士的牛肉汉堡。

e.en: The cafe serves the juiciest {beefburger} in town.
e.zh: 这家咖啡馆做的牛肉汉堡是全城最多汁的。

e.en: The magazine cover featured a tanned {beefcake} model.
e.zh: 杂志封面登着一位古铜肤色的肌肉男模。

e.en: That action film is full of {beefcake} stunts.
e.zh: 那部动作片里满是肌肉男的特技场面。

e.en: A {beefeater} guards the entrance to the Tower of London.
e.zh: 一名皇家卫士守卫着伦敦塔的入口。

e.en: Tourists love photographing every {beefeater} in red uniform.
e.zh: 游客们爱给每一位红制服的皇家卫士拍照。

e.en: He ordered a thick {beefsteak} cooked medium rare.
e.zh: 他点了一份三分熟的厚切牛排。

e.en: The {beefsteak} tomatoes are perfect for sandwiches.
e.zh: 这些大番茄做三明治再合适不过了。

beefy.t: adj. 强壮结实的；牛肉味浓的

e.en: The bouncer was a {beefy} guy with tattoos.
e.zh: 那个保安是个浑身肌肉的纹身男。

e.en: This laptop has a {beefy} processor for video editing.
e.zh: 这台笔记本配有强劲的处理器，适合剪视频。

e.en: A wild {beehive} hung from the old oak branch.
e.zh: 一个野蜂巢挂在那棵老橡树的枝头。

e.en: The office buzzed like a {beehive} before the deadline.
e.zh: 截止日前，办公室像蜂窝一样忙得嗡嗡作响。

e.en: The {beekeeper} carefully harvested honey from the hive.
e.zh: 养蜂人小心地从蜂巢里取出蜂蜜。

e.en: My uncle became a {beekeeper} after he retired.
e.zh: 我叔叔退休后做起了养蜂人。

e.en: She took a weekend class on urban {beekeeping}.
e.zh: 她参加了一个周末的城市养蜂课程。

e.en: {Beekeeping} requires patience and protective gear.
e.zh: 养蜂需要耐心和防护装备。

beeline.t: n. 直奔的路线（make a beeline for）

e.en: The kids made a {beeline} for the dessert table.
e.zh: 孩子们径直冲向了甜点桌。

e.en: He made a {beeline} to his favorite coffee shop.
e.zh: 他直奔他最喜欢的那家咖啡店。

e.en: The novel portrays {beelzebub} as a cunning trickster.
e.zh: 这部小说把别西卜描绘成一个狡猾的骗子。

e.en: Medieval art often depicted {beelzebub} as a giant fly.
e.zh: 中世纪艺术常把别西卜画成一只巨大的苍蝇。

e.en: I have {been} to Tokyo three times this year.
e.zh: 我今年已经去过东京三次了。

e.en: She has {been} working from home since March.
e.zh: 自三月以来她一直在家办公。

beep.t:
n. 嘟嘟声
v. 发出嘟声

e.en: The microwave gave a loud {beep} when the timer ended.
e.zh: 计时结束时，微波炉发出了响亮的哔声。

e.en: Drivers {beep} their horns during rush hour traffic.
e.zh: 高峰时段司机们会按喇叭发出嘟嘟声。

e.en: Doctors used to carry a {beeper} before smartphones existed.
e.zh: 在智能手机出现之前，医生们都随身带着传呼机。

e.en: Her {beeper} went off in the middle of dinner.
e.zh: 晚餐进行到一半，她的呼机响了。

beeping.t: v. 发出嘟嘟声（beep 现在分词）

e.en: The smoke alarm kept {beeping} until I changed batteries.
e.zh: 烟雾报警器一直在响，直到我换了电池。

e.en: I can't sleep with that fridge {beeping} all night.
e.zh: 冰箱整夜哔哔响，我根本睡不着。

e.en: They shared a cold {beer} on the rooftop terrace.
e.zh: 他们在屋顶露台上共享了一瓶冰啤酒。

e.en: This brewery makes the best craft {beer} in town.
e.zh: 这家啤酒厂酿造的精酿啤酒是全城最棒的。

beery.t: adj. 带啤酒味的；醉醺醺的

e.en: The pub had a warm, {beery} smell on Friday nights.
e.zh: 周五晚上，酒吧里飘着一股暖暖的啤酒味。

e.en: He greeted me with a loud, {beery} laugh.
e.zh: 他用一阵醉醺醺的大笑迎接了我。

e.en: The {bees} pollinate the apple trees every spring.
e.zh: 每年春天，蜜蜂都会为苹果树授粉。

e.en: Wild {bees} are vanishing because of pesticide use.
e.zh: 由于农药的使用，野生蜜蜂正在消失。

beeston.t: n. 地名 比斯顿（英国）

e.en: She grew up in {beeston}, just outside Nottingham.
e.zh: 她在诺丁汉郊外的比斯顿长大。

e.en: The train to {beeston} leaves every twenty minutes.
e.zh: 开往比斯顿的列车每二十分钟一班。

e.en: She makes candles from pure {beeswax} and essential oils.
e.zh: 她用纯蜂蜡和精油制作蜡烛。

e.en: My finances are none of your {beeswax}.
e.zh: 我的财务状况不关你的事。

e.en: She roasted a {beet} for the salad.
e.zh: 她烤了一个甜菜放进沙拉里。

e.en: Fresh {beet} juice is popular at health cafes.
e.zh: 鲜榨甜菜汁在健康餐厅很受欢迎。

e.en: The orchestra performed {Beethoven} last night.
e.zh: 乐团昨晚演奏了贝多芬的作品。

e.en: She studies {Beethoven} sonatas every weekend.
e.zh: 她每个周末都钻研贝多芬奏鸣曲。

e.en: A small {beetle} crawled across the leaf.
e.zh: 一只小甲虫爬过叶子。

e.en: He restored a vintage Volkswagen {Beetle} last summer.
e.zh: 他去年夏天修复了一辆老款大众甲壳虫。

e.en: Roasted {beetroot} adds color to the salad.
e.zh: 烤甜菜根给沙拉增添了色彩。

e.en: Her cheeks turned {beetroot} red from embarrassment.
e.zh: 她羞得脸红得像甜菜根。

beeves.t: n. 肉牛（beef 的古旧复数）

e.en: The rancher counted his {beeves} before sundown.
e.zh: 农场主在日落前清点了他的肉牛。

e.en: Old farm records list dozens of {beeves} sold.
e.zh: 老农场记录里列出卖出的几十头肉牛。

e.en: The abbreviation {bef} sometimes appears in old notes for 'before.'
e.zh: 缩写 bef 有时出现在旧笔记中表示"之前"。

e.en: She wrote {bef} lunch in her quick shorthand.
e.zh: 她在速记里写下 bef lunch 表示"午饭前"。

befall.t: v. (灾祸等) 降临、发生于

e.en: No harm shall {befall} the children on this trip.
e.zh: 这次旅行中不会有任何伤害降临到孩子们身上。

e.en: Strange things often {befall} travelers in remote villages.
e.zh: 在偏远村庄,旅人常会遇到怪事。

e.en: Her speech did not {befit} the solemn occasion.
e.zh: 她的发言与这庄严的场合不相称。

e.en: Wear something that will {befit} a formal dinner.
e.zh: 穿一件适合正式晚宴的衣服。

before.t:
prep. 在…之前
adv. 以前

e.en: Please wash your hands {before} dinner.
e.zh: 请在吃晚饭前洗手。

e.en: I had never seen the ocean {before} that trip.
e.zh: 在那次旅行之前我从没见过大海。

e.en: Book your tickets {beforehand} to avoid the queue.
e.zh: 提前订票可以避免排队。

e.en: She prepared the slides {beforehand} so the meeting ran smoothly.
e.zh: 她事先准备好幻灯片,会议进行得很顺利。

e.en: Factories continue to {befoul} the river with waste.
e.zh: 工厂仍在用废料污染这条河。

e.en: Don't let rumors {befoul} her good reputation.
e.zh: 别让谣言玷污了她的好名声。

e.en: She tried to {befriend} the new student in class.
e.zh: 她试着和班上的新同学交朋友。

e.en: Stray cats are easier to {befriend} with patience.
e.zh: 耐心一点,流浪猫更容易亲近。

e.en: Tax forms always {befuddle} me in April.
e.zh: 每年四月,报税表总是让我一头雾水。

e.en: The magician's tricks {befuddle} even adults.
e.zh: 魔术师的把戏连大人也搞糊涂。

befuddled.t: adj. 迷糊的、晕头转向的

e.en: He looked {befuddled} after the long flight.
e.zh: 长途飞行后他看上去晕头转向。

e.en: The professor seemed {befuddled} by the new software.
e.zh: 教授似乎被新软件搞糊涂了。

e.en: Her question caused visible {befuddlement} on his face.
e.zh: 她的问题让他脸上明显露出困惑。

e.en: Tourists' {befuddlement} at the subway map is common.
e.zh: 游客对地铁线路图感到困惑很常见。

beg.t:
v. 乞求、恳求
v. 乞讨

e.en: I {beg} you not to share that photo.
e.zh: 我求你别把那张照片传出去。

e.en: Hungry dogs may {beg} for scraps at dinner.
e.zh: 饿狗在饭桌边可能会讨要剩菜。

began.t: v. 开始（begin 的过去式）

e.en: The concert {began} just after eight.
e.zh: 演唱会八点刚过就开始了。

e.en: She {began} learning Chinese in college.
e.zh: 她大学时开始学中文。

begat.t: v. 生育（beget 的古旧过去式）

e.en: In the old text, Abraham {begat} Isaac.
e.zh: 在那古老的文本中,亚伯拉罕生了以撒。

e.en: That early invention {begat} an entire industry.
e.zh: 那项早期发明催生了一整个行业。

e.en: Violence tends to {beget} more violence.
e.zh: 暴力往往会引发更多的暴力。

e.en: Good ideas often {beget} even better ones.
e.zh: 好点子往往会激发出更好的点子。

e.en: He is regarded as the {begetter} of modern jazz.
e.zh: 他被视为现代爵士乐的开创者。

e.en: Curiosity is the true {begetter} of science.
e.zh: 好奇心才是科学真正的源头。

e.en: A {beggar} sat quietly outside the station.
e.zh: 一名乞丐安静地坐在车站外。

e.en: The view from the cliff would {beggar} description.
e.zh: 悬崖上的景色简直无法用语言形容。

beggarly.t: adj. 贫困的、少得可怜的

e.en: They offered him a {beggarly} salary for the work.
e.zh: 他们给他这份工作的薪水少得可怜。

e.en: The room had only {beggarly} furnishings.
e.zh: 房间里只有寒酸的几件家具。

begged.t: v. 乞求（beg 的过去式）

e.en: She {begged} her parents for a puppy.
e.zh: 她苦苦央求父母给她买只小狗。

e.en: The fans {begged} the band for an encore.
e.zh: 歌迷恳求乐队再来一首。

begging.t: v. 乞讨、恳求（beg 的现在分词）

e.en: The kids kept {begging} for ice cream all afternoon.
e.zh: 孩子们整个下午都在闹着要冰淇淋。

e.en: That last cookie is just {begging} to be eaten.
e.zh: 最后那块饼干简直在等人来吃掉。

e.en: Let's {begin} the meeting at nine sharp.
e.zh: 我们九点准时开始会议吧。

e.en: I don't even know where to {begin}.
e.zh: 我都不知道该从哪里开始。

e.en: This yoga class is perfect for a {beginner}.
e.zh: 这节瑜伽课非常适合初学者。

e.en: Even as a {beginner}, she picked up coding fast.
e.zh: 虽然是新手,她学编程上手很快。

e.en: The app has a free tutorial for {beginners}.
e.zh: 这款应用为初学者提供了免费教程。

e.en: Most {beginners} struggle with pronunciation at first.
e.zh: 大多数初学者一开始都被发音困住。

e.en: At the {beginning} of the film, she lives in Paris.
e.zh: 电影开头,她住在巴黎。

e.en: It's a great {beginning} to a long career.
e.zh: 这是漫长职业生涯的一个好开端。

e.en: The company had humble {beginnings} in a garage.
e.zh: 这家公司起步于一个简陋的车库。

e.en: Cracks in the wall hint at the {beginnings} of damage.
e.zh: 墙上的裂缝预示着损坏正在开始。

e.en: School {begins} again next Monday morning.
e.zh: 下周一早上学校又开学了。

e.en: Every great novel {begins} with a strong sentence.
e.zh: 每一部伟大小说都从一句有力的话开始。

e.en: A pink {begonia} bloomed on the balcony.
e.zh: 阳台上开了一朵粉色的秋海棠。

e.en: She watered the {begonia} every other morning.
e.zh: 她每隔一天早上给秋海棠浇水。

begotten.t:
v. beget 的过去分词
adj. 亲生的

e.en: This success was hard-{begotten} after many failures.
e.zh: 这次成功是经历多次失败后好不容易得来的。

e.en: Their fortune was {begotten} through years of careful work.
e.zh: 他们的财富是多年精心经营换来的。

e.en: I don't {begrudge} her the promotion at all.
e.zh: 我一点也不嫉妒她升职。

e.en: He seemed to {begrudge} every dollar he spent.
e.zh: 他似乎舍不得花掉每一块钱。

e.en: He {begrudgingly} admitted that she was right.
e.zh: 他不情愿地承认她是对的。

e.en: She {begrudgingly} agreed to share her dessert.
e.zh: 她极不情愿地同意分享她的甜点。

e.en: That answer {begs} another important question.
e.zh: 那个答案引出了另一个重要的问题。

e.en: He {begs} for a second chance every time.
e.zh: 他每次都恳求再给一次机会。

e.en: The salesman tried to {beguile} her with promises.
e.zh: 销售员试图用各种承诺哄骗她。

e.en: Soft music can {beguile} a long evening at home.
e.zh: 轻柔的音乐能让漫长的夜晚不那么无聊。

e.en: She has a {beguiling} smile that disarms strangers.
e.zh: 她有一种迷人的微笑,让陌生人放下戒备。

e.en: The offer sounded {beguiling} but turned out fake.
e.zh: 那提议听着很诱人,结果却是假的。

e.en: She spoke {beguilingly} about her travels abroad.
e.zh: 她娓娓动听地讲述自己在国外的旅行。

e.en: The package was {beguilingly} simple on the outside.
e.zh: 包装从外面看简单得让人着迷。

e.en: The {begum} hosted a charity dinner at the palace.
e.zh: 那位贵妇人在宫殿里举办了一场慈善晚宴。

e.en: Locals still call her the {begum} of the estate.
e.zh: 当地人仍称她为这座庄园的女主人。

begun.t: v. 开始（begin 的过去分词）

e.en: The renovations have already {begun} on the kitchen.
e.zh: 厨房的翻新工程已经开始了。

e.en: She has {begun} writing her second novel.
e.zh: 她已经开始写第二部小说了。

behalf.t: n. 代表、利益（on behalf of）

e.en: I'm calling on {behalf} of my grandmother.
e.zh: 我是代表我奶奶打这通电话的。

e.en: She accepted the award on {behalf} of the team.
e.zh: 她代表团队领了奖。

e.en: The lawyer spoke on the {behalves} of all plaintiffs.
e.zh: 律师代表所有原告发言。

e.en: Petitions were filed on the {behalves} of several families.
e.zh: 请愿书是代表好几个家庭提交的。

behave.t:
v. 表现、举止
v. 守规矩

e.en: Please {behave} yourself at grandma's house.
e.zh: 在奶奶家请规矩点。

e.en: Different metals {behave} differently under heat.
e.zh: 不同金属在高温下表现各不相同。

behaved.t: v. 表现；举止（behave 的过去式）

e.en: The puppy {behaved} perfectly during the vet visit.
e.zh: 小狗在看兽医时表现得非常乖。

e.en: He {behaved} as if nothing had happened.
e.zh: 他表现得好像什么都没发生过。

behaves.t: v. 表现；举止（behave 第三人称单数）

e.en: She {behaves} differently when her boss is around.
e.zh: 老板在场时她的表现就会不一样。

e.en: Water {behaves} strangely near the freezing point.
e.zh: 水在接近冰点时表现得很奇怪。

behaving.t: v. 表现；举止（behave 的现在分词）

e.en: The kids are finally {behaving} during dinner.
e.zh: 孩子们晚餐时终于乖了。

e.en: My laptop has been {behaving} oddly since the update.
e.zh: 自从更新后我的笔记本就一直怪怪的。

e.en: His {behavior} at the party surprised everyone.
e.zh: 他在派对上的举止让所有人都吃惊。

e.en: The app tracks user {behavior} to improve the design.
e.zh: 这款应用通过追踪用户行为来优化设计。

behavioral.t: adj. 行为的；与行为有关的

e.en: The clinic specializes in {behavioral} therapy for kids.
e.zh: 这家诊所专门为儿童提供行为疗法。

e.en: We noticed clear {behavioral} changes after the new policy.
e.zh: 新政策实施后我们看到了明显的行为变化。

e.en: The two species are {behaviorally} very similar.
e.zh: 这两个物种在行为上非常相似。

e.en: The program is {behaviorally} focused rather than medical.
e.zh: 该项目侧重于行为干预而非药物治疗。

behaviorism.t: n. 行为主义（心理学流派）

e.en: Skinner is a leading figure in {behaviorism}.
e.zh: 斯金纳是行为主义的代表人物。

e.en: Modern psychology has moved beyond strict {behaviorism}.
e.zh: 现代心理学已不再局限于严格的行为主义。

behaviorist.t:
n. 行为主义者
adj. 行为主义的

e.en: The {behaviorist} explained how rewards shape long-term habits.
e.zh: 那位行为主义者解释了奖励如何塑造长期习惯。

e.en: A strict {behaviorist} approach ignores internal mental states.
e.zh: 严格的行为主义方法忽略了内在的心理状态。

e.en: His teaching style is heavily {behavioristic}, focused on observable outcomes.
e.zh: 他的教学风格非常行为主义,注重可观察的结果。

e.en: The therapy uses {behavioristic} techniques like positive reinforcement.
e.zh: 该疗法采用正向强化等行为主义技术。

behaviors.t: n. 行为；举止（behavior 的复数）

e.en: The app tracks user {behaviors} to improve recommendations.
e.zh: 这款应用会追踪用户行为以优化推荐。

e.en: Some {behaviors} in puppies fade as they grow older.
e.zh: 小狗的一些行为会随着长大而消失。

behaviour.t: n. 行为；举止（英式拼写）

e.en: The teacher praised the children's {behaviour} during the trip.
e.zh: 老师表扬了孩子们旅途中的表现。

e.en: Strange {behaviour} from the server suggests a memory leak.
e.zh: 服务器的异常行为暗示存在内存泄漏。

e.en: She studies {behavioural} economics at a London university.
e.zh: 她在伦敦的一所大学研究行为经济学。

e.en: The clinic offers {behavioural} therapy for anxiety.
e.zh: 该诊所提供针对焦虑的行为疗法。

behaviourally.t: adv. 行为上地（英式拼写）

e.en: The two breeds differ {behaviourally} more than physically.
e.zh: 这两个品种在行为上的差异比外形更明显。

e.en: Children {behaviourally} mimic the adults around them.
e.zh: 孩子们在行为上会模仿身边的大人。

behaviourism.t: n. 行为主义（英式拼写）

e.en: {Behaviourism} dominated psychology in the early twentieth century.
e.zh: 行为主义在二十世纪初主导了心理学界。

e.en: Critics argue {behaviourism} oversimplifies how humans learn.
e.zh: 批评者认为行为主义过度简化了人类的学习方式。

behaviourist.t: n. 行为主义者（英式拼写）

e.en: The {behaviourist} designed an experiment using rats and levers.
e.zh: 那位行为主义学家设计了一项用老鼠和拉杆的实验。

e.en: As a {behaviourist}, she focuses only on what can be measured.
e.zh: 作为行为主义者,她只关注可测量的事物。

e.en: Parents try to model healthy {behaviours} for their kids.
e.zh: 父母会努力为孩子树立健康行为的榜样。

e.en: The study identified risky online {behaviours} among teens.
e.zh: 该研究发现了青少年中存在的高风险网络行为。

e.en: The king ordered his guards to {behead} the traitor.
e.zh: 国王下令侍卫处决那名叛徒。

e.en: Cooks often {behead} the fish before grilling it.
e.zh: 厨师通常会先去掉鱼头再烤。

beheaded.t: v. 斩首（过去式/过去分词）

e.en: Anne Boleyn was famously {beheaded} at the Tower of London.
e.zh: 安妮·博林在伦敦塔被处以斩首,这一事件广为人知。

e.en: The storm {beheaded} several tulips in the front garden.
e.zh: 暴风雨把前花园里的几株郁金香吹断了头。

beheading.t:
n. 斩首
v. 正在斩首

e.en: The novel describes a public {beheading} in vivid detail.
e.zh: 小说生动地描写了一场公开斩首。

e.en: He shuddered at the thought of {beheading} a chicken himself.
e.zh: 想到要亲手宰杀一只鸡,他打了个寒战。

beheld.t: v. 看见；注视（behold 的过去式）

e.en: Travelers {beheld} the snowy peaks for the first time.
e.zh: 旅人们第一次目睹了那些雪山。

e.en: She {beheld} her newborn daughter with quiet joy.
e.zh: 她静静欣喜地凝视着刚出生的女儿。

e.en: Amazon has grown into a retail {behemoth}.
e.zh: 亚马逊已成长为零售业的庞然大物。

e.en: The {behemoth} truck barely fit through the tunnel.
e.zh: 那辆巨无霸卡车勉强穿过隧道。

e.en: The investigation began at the {behest} of Congress.
e.zh: 调查是应国会的要求展开的。

e.en: At her mother's {behest}, he wrote a formal apology.
e.zh: 在她母亲的要求下,他写了一封正式道歉信。

e.en: The minister obeyed the prime minister's {behests} without question.
e.zh: 那位部长毫无异议地服从首相的指示。

e.en: Ancient kings issued {behests} that no one dared ignore.
e.zh: 古代国王下达的命令无人敢忽视。

behind.t:
prep. 在…后面
adv. 落后地

e.en: Please leave your shoes {behind} the front door.
e.zh: 请把鞋子放在前门后面。

e.en: Our team is two points {behind} with five minutes left.
e.zh: 我们队还落后两分,只剩五分钟。

behold.t: v. 看见；注视（文学用语）

e.en: Tap the link and {behold} the redesigned dashboard.
e.zh: 点击链接,一睹全新设计的仪表盘。

e.en: Tourists gathered at dawn to {behold} the eclipse.
e.zh: 游客们黎明时分聚集观看日食。

e.en: Independent journalists are {beholden} to no political party.
e.zh: 独立记者不受任何政党的束缚。

e.en: I feel {beholden} to the friend who lent me money.
e.zh: 我对那位借钱给我的朋友心怀感激。

e.en: Beauty, as they say, is in the eye of the {beholder}.
e.zh: 俗话说,美在观者眼中。

e.en: Each {beholder} interpreted the abstract painting differently.
e.zh: 每位观者对那幅抽象画都有不同的理解。

e.en: It would {behoove} startups to listen to early customers.
e.zh: 创业公司理应认真倾听早期客户的声音。

e.en: It {behooves} every driver to check the brakes regularly.
e.zh: 每位司机都应定期检查刹车。

e.en: It would {behove} the minister to apologise publicly.
e.zh: 那位部长理应公开道歉。

e.en: It {behoves} students to back up their work daily.
e.zh: 学生们应当每天备份自己的作业。

beige.t:
n. 米色；米黄色
adj. 米色的

e.en: She painted the living room a soft {beige}.
e.zh: 她把客厅刷成了柔和的米色。

e.en: His {beige} trench coat looked great with jeans.
e.zh: 他那件米色风衣搭配牛仔裤很好看。

beignet.t: n. 法式炸面团；贝奈特饼

e.en: We ordered a fresh {beignet} dusted with powdered sugar.
e.zh: 我们点了一个撒满糖粉的新鲜法式甜甜圈。

e.en: No trip to New Orleans is complete without a {beignet}.
e.zh: 去新奥尔良不吃法式甜甜圈就不算完整。

e.en: My flight to {Beijing} departs early Saturday morning.
e.zh: 我飞往北京的航班周六一早起飞。

e.en: {Beijing} hosted both the Summer and Winter Olympics.
e.zh: 北京举办过夏季和冬季奥运会。

being.t:
n. 存在；生物
v. be 的现在分词

e.en: Every human {being} deserves access to clean water.
e.zh: 每个人都应享有获得清洁饮用水的权利。

e.en: The app is {being} updated, so login is temporarily disabled.
e.zh: 应用正在更新,登录功能暂时关闭。

beings.t: n. 生物；存在（being 的复数）

e.en: Many cultures believe in unseen spiritual {beings}.
e.zh: 许多文化都相信存在看不见的灵性存在。

e.en: Humans are social {beings} who thrive on connection.
e.zh: 人类是社交的生物,依靠人际联系而茁壮成长。

beirut.t: n. 贝鲁特（黎巴嫩首都）

e.en: The conference will be held in downtown {Beirut} next March.
e.zh: 会议将于明年三月在贝鲁特市中心举行。

e.en: {Beirut} is famous for its vibrant nightlife and seaside cafés.
e.zh: 贝鲁特以热闹的夜生活和海边咖啡馆闻名。

bejesus.t: n. 表强烈惊恐的俚语感叹

e.en: That horror film scared the {bejesus} out of me.
e.zh: 那部恐怖片把我吓得魂飞魄散。

e.en: The sudden thunder scared the {bejesus} out of the dog.
e.zh: 突如其来的雷声把狗吓得魂不附体。

e.en: She wore a {bejeweled} crown to the costume party.
e.zh: 她戴着一顶镶满珠宝的王冠去化装舞会。

e.en: The actress arrived in a {bejeweled} silver gown.
e.zh: 那位女演员身穿镶满宝石的银色礼服到场。

e.en: The queen's {bejewelled} fingers sparkled under the chandeliers.
e.zh: 女王戴满珠宝的手指在吊灯下闪闪发光。

e.en: He gifted her a {bejewelled} brooch shaped like a peacock.
e.zh: 他送给她一枚孔雀造型的镶宝石胸针。

bekaa.t: n. 贝卡（黎巴嫩贝卡谷地）

e.en: The {Bekaa} Valley produces some of Lebanon's finest wines.
e.zh: 贝卡谷地出产黎巴嫩一些最优质的葡萄酒。

e.en: Farmers in the {Bekaa} grow grapes, potatoes and wheat.
e.zh: 贝卡谷地的农民种植葡萄、土豆和小麦。

e.en: Sound intensity is measured in {bel} or decibel units.
e.zh: 声音强度以贝尔或分贝为单位测量。

e.en: One {bel} equals ten decibels in acoustic measurement.
e.zh: 在声学测量中,一贝尔等于十分贝。

belabor.t: v. 过分强调；喋喋不休（美式）

e.en: I won't {belabor} the point any further—let's move on.
e.zh: 我就不再赘述了,我们继续下一项。

e.en: Critics tend to {belabor} small flaws in popular movies.
e.zh: 评论家往往会对热门电影的小缺点反复挑剔。

e.en: There's no need to {belabour} the obvious in your essay.
e.zh: 论文里没必要对显而易见的内容反复啰嗦。

e.en: The speaker began to {belabour} every minor statistic.
e.zh: 演讲者开始对每个小统计数据反复纠缠。

belarusian.t:
adj. 白俄罗斯的
n. 白俄罗斯人/语

e.en: My new colleague speaks fluent {Belarusian} and Russian.
e.zh: 我的新同事能说流利的白俄罗斯语和俄语。

e.en: The restaurant serves traditional {Belarusian} potato pancakes.
e.zh: 这家餐厅供应传统的白俄罗斯土豆煎饼。

belarussian.t: adj. 白俄罗斯的（异体拼写）

e.en: Some textbooks still use the older spelling {Belarussian}.
e.zh: 有些教科书仍使用较旧的拼写 Belarussian。

e.en: He identified himself as {Belarussian} on the immigration form.
e.zh: 他在入境表上把自己填为白俄罗斯人。

e.en: Please accept my {belated} birthday wishes—I totally forgot.
e.zh: 请接受我迟来的生日祝福,我完全忘了。

e.en: The company issued a {belated} apology to affected users.
e.zh: 公司向受影响的用户发出了迟来的道歉。

e.en: The airline {belatedly} admitted the flight had been overbooked.
e.zh: 航空公司事后才承认那班航班超售了。

e.en: He {belatedly} realized he had left his passport at home.
e.zh: 他后知后觉地意识到护照落在家里了。

e.en: The {belatedness} of the response frustrated many customers.
e.zh: 回应的迟缓让许多客户感到失望。

e.en: She apologized for the {belatedness} of her thank-you note.
e.zh: 她为感谢信寄得太晚而道歉。

belay.t:
v. （登山）系绳保护
v. 停止

e.en: Always have a partner {belay} you while climbing.
e.zh: 攀岩时一定要让搭档为你做保护。

e.en: The captain shouted, "{Belay} that order!" from the bridge.
e.zh: 船长在舰桥上喊道:“取消那道命令!”

belch.t:
v. 打嗝；喷出
n. 嗝

e.en: It's rude to {belch} loudly at the dinner table.
e.zh: 在餐桌上大声打嗝是很不礼貌的。

e.en: Old factories still {belch} thick smoke into the sky.
e.zh: 老旧的工厂仍在向天空喷出浓烟。

belcher.t: n. 打嗝的人；姓氏 贝尔彻

e.en: My uncle is a notorious {belcher} after every meal.
e.zh: 我叔叔是出了名的饭后爱打嗝的人。

e.en: That dragon in the cartoon is quite the fire {belcher}.
e.zh: 动画片里那条龙真是个喷火高手。

e.en: Supply shortages continue to {beleaguer} small businesses.
e.zh: 供应短缺持续困扰着小企业。

e.en: Reporters {beleaguer} the senator with questions after the vote.
e.zh: 投票结束后记者们围着参议员追问个不停。

beleaguered.t: adj. 受困扰的；被围困的

e.en: The {beleaguered} CEO finally resigned after months of scandal.
e.zh: 那位陷入困境的首席执行官在数月丑闻后终于辞职。

e.en: Aid finally reached the {beleaguered} city after weeks.
e.zh: 援助物资在数周后终于送达了那座被围困的城市。

e.en: The museum displays a fossil {belemnite} from the Jurassic period.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一块侏罗纪时期的箭石化石。

e.en: She found a {belemnite} while hunting fossils on the beach.
e.zh: 她在海滩上找化石时发现了一块箭石。

belfast.t: n. 贝尔法斯特（北爱尔兰首府）

e.en: We took an early train from Dublin to {Belfast}.
e.zh: 我们搭乘清晨的火车从都柏林前往贝尔法斯特。

e.en: The Titanic was built in the shipyards of {Belfast}.
e.zh: 泰坦尼克号是在贝尔法斯特的造船厂建造的。

e.en: Bats roosted quietly in the church {belfry} all summer.
e.zh: 整个夏天蝙蝠都在教堂的钟楼里安静栖息。

e.en: The old {belfry} still rings every Sunday morning.
e.zh: 那座古老的钟楼每周日早晨仍会鸣响。

belgian.t:
adj. 比利时的
n. 比利时人

e.en: I love a hot {Belgian} waffle topped with strawberries.
e.zh: 我喜欢吃配草莓的热腾腾比利时华夫饼。

e.en: The {Belgian} team won bronze at the world championships.
e.zh: 比利时队在世锦赛上获得了铜牌。

e.en: {Belgium} is famous for its chocolate, beer and waffles.
e.zh: 比利时以巧克力、啤酒和华夫饼闻名。

e.en: She studied French and Dutch while living in {Belgium}.
e.zh: 她在比利时生活时学习了法语和荷兰语。

belgrade.t: n. 贝尔格莱德（塞尔维亚首都）

e.en: We spent a long weekend exploring the cafes of {Belgrade}.
e.zh: 我们用一个长周末逛遍了贝尔格莱德的咖啡馆。

e.en: The flight from London to {Belgrade} takes about three hours.
e.zh: 从伦敦飞往贝尔格莱德大约需要三个小时。

belgrano.t: n. 贝尔格拉诺（人名/地名）

e.en: My cousin lives in the {Belgrano} neighborhood of Buenos Aires.
e.zh: 我表哥住在布宜诺斯艾利斯的贝尔格拉诺街区。

e.en: The sinking of the {Belgrano} remains a controversial wartime event.
e.zh: 贝尔格拉诺号被击沉至今仍是颇具争议的战时事件。

belgrave.t: n. 贝尔格雷夫（伦敦地名）

e.en: The embassy sits on a quiet corner of {Belgrave} Square.
e.zh: 大使馆坐落在贝尔格雷夫广场一个安静的角落。

e.en: She booked a small hotel just off {Belgrave} Road.
e.zh: 她在贝尔格雷夫路附近订了一家小酒店。

belgravia.t: n. 贝尔格莱维亚（伦敦高档住宅区）

e.en: Property prices in {Belgravia} have always been astronomical.
e.zh: 贝尔格雷维亚区的房价一直高得离谱。

e.en: They strolled through {Belgravia}, admiring the white stucco mansions.
e.zh: 他们漫步在贝尔格雷维亚区,欣赏着白色灰泥豪宅。

e.en: Her calm voice {belied} the panic she actually felt.
e.zh: 她平静的声音掩饰了内心真实的恐慌。

e.en: The tidy office {belies} how chaotic the team really is.
e.zh: 整洁的办公室掩盖了团队实际上的混乱。

e.en: His {belief} in the project kept the team motivated.
e.zh: 他对项目的信念让团队始终充满干劲。

e.en: It is a common {belief} that breakfast is the most important meal.
e.zh: 人们普遍认为早餐是一天中最重要的一餐。

e.en: Travel often challenges the {beliefs} we grew up with.
e.zh: 旅行常常会挑战我们从小养成的观念。

e.en: Their religious {beliefs} shape almost every daily decision.
e.zh: 他们的宗教信仰几乎影响着每一个日常决定。

e.en: The actor's accent really hurt the {believability} of the film.
e.zh: 那位演员的口音严重影响了影片的可信度。

e.en: Adding small flaws actually boosts a character's {believability}.
e.zh: 加入一些小缺点反而能让角色更可信。

e.en: The plot twist was clever but barely {believable}.
e.zh: 那个剧情反转很巧妙,但几乎让人难以信服。

e.en: She gave a {believable} performance as a tired single mother.
e.zh: 她把一位疲惫的单亲妈妈演得十分逼真。

e.en: He {believably} portrayed a man slowly losing his memory.
e.zh: 他逼真地诠释了一个记忆逐渐衰退的男人。

e.en: The dialogue flows {believably} from start to finish.
e.zh: 整段对白从头到尾都自然可信。

e.en: I {believe} we can finish the report before Friday.
e.zh: 我相信我们能在周五前完成这份报告。

e.en: Many kids still {believe} in Santa Claus at age six.
e.zh: 许多孩子到六岁时仍然相信圣诞老人。

believed.t: v. 相信（believe 的过去式）

e.en: For years she {believed} the rumor was completely true.
e.zh: 多年来她一直以为那个传言完全属实。

e.en: The painting is {believed} to be over 400 years old.
e.zh: 这幅画据信已有四百多年的历史。

e.en: I'm a firm {believer} in taking short breaks while coding.
e.zh: 我坚信编程时应该多休息一会儿。

e.en: After using the app for a week, she became a {believer}.
e.zh: 用了一周这个应用后,她彻底被圈粉了。

believes.t: v. 相信（believe 的第三人称单数）

e.en: He {believes} that honesty matters more than being clever.
e.zh: 他认为诚实比聪明更重要。

e.en: Nobody really {believes} the weather forecast around here.
e.zh: 这一带没人真把天气预报当回事。

believing.t: v. 相信（believe 的现在分词）

e.en: I kept {believing} the bug was in my code, not the library.
e.zh: 我一直认定问题出在我的代码上,而不是库里。

e.en: Seeing is {believing}, so let me show you the demo.
e.zh: 眼见为实,我直接给你演示一遍。

e.en: Good managers never {belittle} their team in public.
e.zh: 优秀的管理者绝不会当众贬低自己的团队。

e.en: Don't {belittle} small wins—they add up over time.
e.zh: 别小看每一次小小的胜利,它们会日积月累。

belittling.t:
adj. 贬低的
v. 贬低（belittle 的现在分词）

e.en: His {belittling} comments made the new intern want to quit.
e.zh: 他那些贬低人的话让新来的实习生都想辞职了。

e.en: Stop {belittling} yourself—your work is genuinely impressive.
e.zh: 别再贬低自己了,你的作品其实非常出色。

belize.t: n. 伯利兹（中美洲国家）

e.en: We went snorkeling at the barrier reef off {Belize}.
e.zh: 我们去伯利兹外的堡礁浮潜了一番。

e.en: {Belize} is the only Central American country where English is official.
e.zh: 伯利兹是中美洲唯一以英语为官方语言的国家。

belizean.t:
adj. 伯利兹的
n. 伯利兹人

e.en: The chef shared his grandmother's classic {Belizean} stew recipe.
e.zh: 那位厨师分享了他祖母经典的伯利兹炖菜配方。

e.en: She married a {Belizean} musician she met in Mexico.
e.zh: 她嫁给了在墨西哥认识的一位伯利兹音乐家。

bell.t:
n. 铃；钟
v. 鸣钟

e.en: The {bell} above the shop door jingled as I walked in.
e.zh: 我推门进店时,门上的铃铛叮当作响。

e.en: Please ring the {bell} at reception if no one is there.
e.zh: 如果前台没人,请按铃叫人。

e.en: In small doses, {belladonna} was once used as a medicine.
e.zh: 小剂量的颠茄过去曾被用作药物。

e.en: The garden book warned that {belladonna} berries are highly toxic.
e.zh: 那本园艺书警告说颠茄的浆果毒性极强。

e.en: The {bellboy} carried our heavy suitcases up to the room.
e.zh: 行李员把我们沉重的行李箱送到了房间。

e.en: He worked as a hotel {bellboy} during his college summers.
e.zh: 大学暑假他在酒店当过行李员。

belle.t: n. 美女；最受瞩目的女子

e.en: At eighteen, her grandmother had been the {belle} of the town.
e.zh: 她奶奶十八岁时是镇上的头号美女。

e.en: My niece insists on dressing up as {Belle} every Halloween.
e.zh: 我侄女每年万圣节都坚持要扮成贝儿公主。

belled.t: v. 系上铃铛（bell 的过去式）

e.en: The cat wore a {belled} collar so birds could hear it coming.
e.zh: 那只猫戴着带铃铛的项圈,鸟儿一听就知道它来了。

e.en: She wore {belled} sleeves that flared dramatically at the wrist.
e.zh: 她穿着喇叭袖,袖口在手腕处夸张地张开。

bellevue.t: n. 贝尔维尤（美国地名）

e.en: Many tech workers commute from Seattle to {Bellevue} every morning.
e.zh: 许多科技从业者每天早上从西雅图通勤到贝尔维尤。

e.en: The conference is being held at a hotel in downtown {Bellevue}.
e.zh: 会议将在贝尔维尤市中心的一家酒店举行。

e.en: A patch of purple {bellflower} bloomed beside the garden path.
e.zh: 花园小径旁开了一丛紫色的风铃草。

e.en: She painted a delicate watercolor of a single {bellflower}.
e.zh: 她用水彩细腻地画了一朵风铃草。

e.en: The {bellhop} smiled politely and pointed us toward the elevator.
e.zh: 行李员礼貌地微笑,并指引我们去电梯方向。

e.en: Tip the {bellhop} a couple of dollars per bag.
e.zh: 给行李员每件行李两美元左右的小费。

e.en: His {bellicose} tweets only escalated tensions between the two nations.
e.zh: 他那些好战的推文只让两国关系更加紧张。

e.en: She avoided her uncle's {bellicose} rants at family dinners.
e.zh: 家庭聚餐时她总避开舅舅那些好斗的长篇大论。

e.en: The senator's growing {bellicosity} worried his moderate colleagues.
e.zh: 那位参议员日益强硬的好战姿态让温和派同僚十分担忧。

e.en: Markets dropped sharply after the leader's surprising {bellicosity}.
e.zh: 该领导人突如其来的好战言论使股市大幅下挫。

e.en: After the buffet, everyone leaned back rubbing their full {bellies}.
e.zh: 自助餐过后,大家都靠在椅背上揉着撑得圆鼓鼓的肚子。

e.en: The puppies rolled over to have their {bellies} scratched.
e.zh: 小狗们翻过身让人挠它们的肚皮。

e.en: His sudden {belligerence} at the meeting shocked everyone.
e.zh: 他在会上突然变得咄咄逼人,把所有人都惊到了。

e.en: The dog's {belligerence} faded once it realized I had treats.
e.zh: 那只狗一发现我有零食,凶狠劲儿立刻消失了。

e.en: Historians documented the various {belligerences} that defined the century.
e.zh: 史学家记录下了定义那个世纪的种种交战行为。

e.en: Repeated {belligerences} along the border eventually led to a treaty.
e.zh: 边境上一次次的敌对冲突最终促成了一项条约。

e.en: The state of {belligerency} between the two nations lasted a decade.
e.zh: 两国之间的交战状态持续了整整十年。

e.en: International law clearly defines what counts as {belligerency}.
e.zh: 国际法明确规定了何种行为构成交战状态。

e.en: A {belligerent} customer was demanding a refund at the counter.
e.zh: 一位气势汹汹的顾客在柜台要求退款。

e.en: He gets {belligerent} after a couple of drinks, so we left early.
e.zh: 他喝两杯就开始挑衅,所以我们提早离开了。

e.en: The driver honked {belligerently} at every cyclist on the road.
e.zh: 那位司机对路上每个骑行者都气势汹汹地按喇叭。

e.en: He stared {belligerently} across the table without saying a word.
e.zh: 他隔着桌子怒目而视,一言不发。

e.en: We drove up to {Bellingham} for the weekend farmers market.
e.zh: 我们开车去贝灵汉赶周末的农夫市集。

e.en: {Bellingham} sits about thirty minutes south of the Canadian border.
e.zh: 贝灵汉位于加拿大边境以南大约三十分钟车程的地方。

bellini.t: n. 贝里尼（人名/鸡尾酒名）

e.en: She ordered a peach {Bellini} to start the brunch.
e.zh: 她点了一杯桃子贝里尼鸡尾酒来开启早午餐。

e.en: The museum's {Bellini} portrait draws crowds every weekend.
e.zh: 博物馆里那幅贝利尼的肖像每个周末都吸引大批观众。

e.en: The lawn was dotted with tiny white {Bellis} daisies.
e.zh: 草坪上点缀着一朵朵白色的小雏菊。

e.en: Gardeners often plant {Bellis} for early spring color.
e.zh: 园丁们常种雏菊,为早春增添色彩。

bellman.t: n. 打铃人；酒店行李员

e.en: The {bellman} loaded our luggage onto a polished brass cart.
e.zh: 行李员把我们的行李装上了一辆擦得锃亮的黄铜推车。

e.en: A friendly {bellman} held the door as we entered the lobby.
e.zh: 一位和善的门童在我们进入大堂时为我们扶着门。

e.en: The Italian waiter greeted everyone with a cheerful "{bello}!"
e.zh: 那位意大利侍者愉快地用一声“bello”问候每位客人。

e.en: Andrés {Bello} is celebrated across Latin America as a great scholar.
e.zh: 安德烈斯·贝洛在整个拉丁美洲被尊为伟大的学者。

bellow.t:
v. 怒吼；大声喊叫
n. 吼声

e.en: I heard the coach {bellow} instructions from across the field.
e.zh: 我听见教练隔着球场大声吼出指令。

e.en: His angry {bellow} echoed through the empty warehouse.
e.zh: 他愤怒的吼声在空荡的仓库里回响。

bellowed.t: v. 怒吼（bellow 的过去式）

e.en: The drill sergeant {bellowed} orders that no one dared ignore.
e.zh: 教官大声咆哮着发号施令,没人敢不当回事。

e.en: "Get out of my kitchen!" the chef {bellowed} at the intern.
e.zh: “滚出我的厨房!”主厨冲实习生大吼道。

bellowing.t: v. 怒吼（bellow 的现在分词）

e.en: A man was {bellowing} into his phone on the crowded train.
e.zh: 拥挤的火车上,一个男人正对着电话大吼大叫。

e.en: You could hear the cattle {bellowing} from miles away.
e.zh: 几英里外都能听到牛群哞哞的吼叫声。

e.en: He pumped the {bellows} until the fire roared back to life.
e.zh: 他拉动风箱,直到火苗重新熊熊燃起。

e.en: The blacksmith's old leather {bellows} still worked perfectly.
e.zh: 铁匠那只古老的皮制风箱依然好用。

e.en: Church {bells} rang across the valley on Sunday morning.
e.zh: 周日清晨,教堂的钟声响彻整个山谷。

e.en: The new phone has all the latest {bells} and whistles.
e.zh: 这款新手机配齐了所有最新的花哨功能。

e.en: Tech stocks are often a {bellwether} for the broader market.
e.zh: 科技股往往是整个大盘的风向标。

e.en: This small town has long been a political {bellwether}.
e.zh: 这个小镇长期以来都是政治风向标。

e.en: After lunch, the dog flopped over for a {belly} rub.
e.zh: 午饭后,那只狗翻过身求人挠肚皮。

e.en: He laughed so hard his {belly} actually started to ache.
e.zh: 他笑得肚子都开始发疼了。

bellyache.t:
n. 肚子痛
v. 抱怨

e.en: Stop {bellyache} about the weather and grab an umbrella.
e.zh: 别再抱怨天气了,拿把伞就行。

e.en: Too much candy gave the kids a serious {bellyache}.
e.zh: 糖吃多了,孩子们闹起了严重的肚子疼。

e.en: The toddler kept poking her own {bellybutton} and giggling.
e.zh: 那个小女孩不停戳自己的肚脐,笑个不停。

e.en: He got a tiny tattoo just above his {bellybutton}.
e.zh: 他在肚脐上方纹了一个小小的纹身。

bellyful.t: n. 满腹；过量（令人厌烦）

e.en: I've had a {bellyful} of his excuses this week.
e.zh: 这周我已经受够了他那一堆借口。

e.en: After a {bellyful} of dumplings, nobody had room for dessert.
e.zh: 吃了满满一肚子饺子,谁也没胃口再吃甜点了。

e.en: We took the train out to {Belmont} for the weekend.
e.zh: 我们周末坐火车去了贝尔蒙特。

e.en: The horse won the {Belmont} Stakes by two lengths.
e.zh: 那匹马以两个身位赢得了贝尔蒙特锦标赛。

e.en: These books {belong} on the top shelf.
e.zh: 这些书应该放在最上层书架上。

e.en: I finally feel like I {belong} in this team.
e.zh: 我终于觉得自己属于这个团队了。

belonged.t: v. 属于（belong 的过去式）

e.en: This watch {belonged} to my grandfather.
e.zh: 这块手表是我祖父的。

e.en: She {belonged} to a small book club downtown.
e.zh: 她加入了市中心的一个小读书俱乐部。

belonging.t:
n. 归属感
v. 属于（现在分词）

e.en: A sense of {belonging} matters more than salary.
e.zh: 归属感比薪水更重要。

e.en: He left without {belonging} to any group.
e.zh: 他没加入任何团体就离开了。

belongings.t: n. 个人财物；随身物品

e.en: Please collect your {belongings} before leaving the train.
e.zh: 下车前请带好您的随身物品。

e.en: All her {belongings} fit into two suitcases.
e.zh: 她所有的家当都装进了两个行李箱。

e.en: This jacket {belongs} to someone in the office.
e.zh: 这件外套是办公室某个人的。

e.en: He {belongs} to the new generation of designers.
e.zh: 他属于新一代的设计师。

e.en: My grandparents emigrated from {Belorussia} after the war.
e.zh: 我祖父母在战后从白俄罗斯移民而来。

e.en: The map still labeled the region as {Belorussia}.
e.zh: 那张地图仍把该地区标为白俄罗斯。

beloved.t:
adj. 深爱的；心爱的
n. 爱人

e.en: The cafe is {beloved} by students and tourists alike.
e.zh: 这家咖啡馆深受学生和游客的喜爱。

e.en: She lost her {beloved} dog last winter.
e.zh: 她去年冬天失去了心爱的狗狗。

below.t:
prep. 在…下面
adv. 在下方

e.en: Please leave a comment {below} the video.
e.zh: 请在视频下方留言。

e.en: Temperatures dropped {below} freezing overnight.
e.zh: 夜间气温降到了零度以下。

belowground.t:
adj. 地下的
adv. 在地下

e.en: The parking garage extends three floors {belowground}.
e.zh: 停车场向地下延伸了三层。

e.en: Most of the cable infrastructure runs {belowground}.
e.zh: 大部分电缆设施都铺设在地下。

belsen.t: n. 贝尔森（集中营地名）

e.en: The documentary covered the liberation of {Belsen} in 1945.
e.zh: 这部纪录片讲述了1945年贝尔森集中营的解放。

e.en: Survivors of {Belsen} shared their stories at the memorial.
e.zh: 贝尔森集中营的幸存者在纪念活动上分享了他们的经历。

belt.t:
n. 腰带；地带
v. 用带系住

e.en: He tightened his {belt} after losing some weight.
e.zh: 瘦了一些之后他把腰带勒紧了。

e.en: The conveyor {belt} moves packages to the trucks.
e.zh: 传送带把包裹送到卡车上。

belted.t:
adj. 系腰带的
v. 系带（过去式）

e.en: She {belted} her coat against the cold wind.
e.zh: 她把大衣束紧抵御寒风。

e.en: The singer {belted} out the chorus with full power.
e.zh: 那位歌手放声唱出副歌部分。

belter.t: n. 高声歌者；极出色之物

e.en: That last song was a real {belter} at the concert.
e.zh: 演唱会上最后那首歌真是首劲爆金曲。

e.en: She's a powerful {belter} with an incredible vocal range.
e.zh: 她是个嗓音强劲、音域惊人的高音歌手。

e.en: He wore loose, {beltless} trousers around the house.
e.zh: 他在家穿着宽松无腰带的裤子。

e.en: The new dress design is intentionally {beltless} and flowing.
e.zh: 这款新连衣裙设计上特意不带腰带,飘逸自然。

e.en: The store sells leather {belts} in many colors.
e.zh: 这家店出售各种颜色的真皮腰带。

e.en: Always fasten your seat {belts} before takeoff.
e.zh: 起飞前请务必系好安全带。

beltway.t: n. 环城公路；政界圈子

e.en: Traffic on the {beltway} was terrible this morning.
e.zh: 今早环城高速上的交通糟透了。

e.en: Inside the {beltway}, politics is a daily obsession.
e.zh: 在华盛顿政治圈内,政治是每日热议的话题。

e.en: We watched a {beluga} whale swim past the glass.
e.zh: 我们看着一头白鲸从玻璃前游过。

e.en: Real {beluga} caviar is incredibly expensive these days.
e.zh: 如今真正的白鲸鱼子酱贵得离谱。

e.en: The hotel's {belvedere} offers stunning views of the lake.
e.zh: 酒店的观景台可俯瞰壮丽的湖景。

e.en: We sipped wine on the {belvedere} at sunset.
e.zh: 夕阳西下时,我们在观景台上品酒。

bely.t: v. 掩饰；与…不符（belie 的变体）

e.en: Her calm voice {bely} the panic she was feeling.
e.zh: 她平静的嗓音掩饰了内心的恐慌。

e.en: His youthful looks {bely} his sixty years.
e.zh: 他年轻的外表掩盖了他六十岁的年纪。

e.en: The sci-fi novel was full of strange {BEM} villains.
e.zh: 这本科幻小说里满是怪异的虫眼怪物反派。

e.en: Old pulp covers often featured a green-skinned {BEM}.
e.zh: 老式通俗小说封面上常出现绿皮外星怪物。

e.en: Critics {bemoan} the rise of clickbait headlines online.
e.zh: 评论家们哀叹网上标题党的盛行。

e.en: Don't just {bemoan} the situation — try to fix it.
e.zh: 别光顾着抱怨现状,试着去改变它。

e.en: The strange ending of the film tends to {bemuse} viewers.
e.zh: 这部电影怪异的结局常让观众感到困惑。

e.en: His odd questions {bemuse} the new interns daily.
e.zh: 他古怪的问题每天都让新实习生一头雾水。

e.en: She wore a {bemused} expression throughout the meeting.
e.zh: 整个会议期间她都带着一副困惑的表情。

e.en: The toddler stared, {bemused}, at the magic trick.
e.zh: 小孩一脸茫然地盯着那个魔术。

e.en: He smiled {bemusedly} as the kids explained their game.
e.zh: 孩子们解释他们的游戏时,他茫然地笑了笑。

e.en: She watched {bemusedly} as the puppy chased its tail.
e.zh: 她饶有兴味又困惑地看着小狗追自己的尾巴。

e.en: The audience watched the performance with quiet {bemusement}.
e.zh: 观众们带着默默的困惑观看了表演。

e.en: To my {bemusement}, the cat opened the door itself.
e.zh: 令我惊奇的是,那只猫自己把门打开了。

ben.t: n. 本（人名）；山峰（苏格兰语）

e.en: My friend {Ben} is moving to Berlin next month.
e.zh: 我朋友本下个月要搬去柏林。

e.en: They climbed {Ben} Nevis in just under six hours.
e.zh: 他们在不到六小时内登上了本尼维斯山。

benares.t: n. 贝拿勒斯（印度城市，今瓦拉纳西）

e.en: We took an early boat ride along the ghats of {Benares}.
e.zh: 我们清晨在贝拿勒斯的河坛边乘船游览。

e.en: Pilgrims travel to {Benares} to bathe in the Ganges.
e.zh: 朝圣者们前往贝拿勒斯在恒河中沐浴。

benbecula.t: n. 本贝丘拉（苏格兰岛屿）

e.en: We caught the ferry to {Benbecula} early in the morning.
e.zh: 我们一大早搭上了去本贝丘拉岛的渡轮。

e.en: {Benbecula} sits between North and South Uist.
e.zh: 本贝丘拉岛位于北尤伊斯特岛和南尤伊斯特岛之间。

bench.t: n. 长凳；工作台；法官席

e.en: We sat on a park {bench} watching the ducks.
e.zh: 我们坐在公园长椅上看鸭子。

e.en: The coach decided to {bench} the star player.
e.zh: 教练决定把那位明星球员换下场。

benched.t: v. 让…坐冷板凳；使退场

e.en: The striker was {benched} after missing two open goals.
e.zh: 那位前锋错失两次空门后被换下了场。

e.en: He {benched} 120 kilos at the gym today.
e.zh: 他今天在健身房卧推了120公斤。

bencher.t: n. 律师公会资深成员

e.en: He's been a back-{bencher} in parliament for years.
e.zh: 他在议会当后排议员已经好几年了。

e.en: She was elected as a {bencher} of the Inn.
e.zh: 她当选为律师学院的资深委员。

e.en: New wooden {benches} were installed along the riverside path.
e.zh: 河边小路上新装了几张木长椅。

e.en: All the {benches} in the courtroom were full.
e.zh: 法庭里所有的长椅都坐满了。

benching.t: v. 让…坐冷板凳；举重中做卧推

e.en: The coach is {benching} the goalkeeper for the next match.
e.zh: 教练下一场比赛会把守门员替换下来。

e.en: He's {benching} more weight than ever this month.
e.zh: 这个月他卧推的重量比以往都多。

benchmark.t:
n. 基准；性能测试
v. 对标、跑分

e.en: This phone sets a new {benchmark} for camera quality.
e.zh: 这款手机为相机画质树立了新标杆。

e.en: We use last year's sales as a {benchmark}.
e.zh: 我们以去年的销售额作为基准。

e.en: The new chip beat all previous {benchmarks} by a wide margin.
e.zh: 这款新芯片大幅超越了之前所有的跑分成绩。

e.en: Industry {benchmarks} help startups measure their progress.
e.zh: 行业基准帮助初创公司衡量自身的进步。

bend.t:
v. 弯曲；使屈服
n. 弯道

e.en: {Bend} your knees slightly when lifting the box.
e.zh: 搬箱子时膝盖稍微弯曲一些。

e.en: The river takes a sharp {bend} near the bridge.
e.zh: 河流在桥附近有个急转弯。

e.en: This phone has a {bendable} screen that folds in half.
e.zh: 这款手机有可弯曲的屏幕,能对折起来。

e.en: The toy comes with {bendable} arms and legs.
e.zh: 这款玩具的胳膊和腿都可以弯折。

bended.t: adj. 弯曲的（多用于 on bended knee）

e.en: He proposed to her on {bended} knee.
e.zh: 他单膝跪地向她求婚。

e.en: The knight prayed on {bended} knee before the king.
e.zh: 那位骑士单膝跪在国王面前祷告。

bender.t: n. 狂饮作乐；弯管工具

e.en: He went on a weekend {bender} after the breakup.
e.zh: 分手后他周末狂饮了一场。

e.en: That fall was a real fender-{bender}, not a major crash.
e.zh: 那次撞车只是小擦碰,不算严重事故。

bending.t:
v. 弯曲（bend 的现在分词）
n. 弯折

e.en: She was {bending} down to tie her shoelace.
e.zh: 她正弯腰系鞋带。

e.en: The willow branches were {bending} in the strong wind.
e.zh: 柳枝在大风中弯了下来。

bends.t:
v. 弯曲（第三人称单数）
n. 潜水减压病

e.en: The road {bends} sharply just past the old church.
e.zh: 过了那座老教堂,路就急转弯了。

e.en: Divers can get the {bends} if they ascend too fast.
e.zh: 潜水员上升过快会得减压病。

e.en: The kids love these {bendy} colorful drinking straws.
e.zh: 孩子们喜欢这些可弯曲的彩色吸管。

e.en: She's incredibly {bendy} from years of yoga practice.
e.zh: 多年练瑜伽让她身体格外柔软。

beneath.t:
prep. 在…下方
adv. 在下面

e.en: A small note was hidden {beneath} the keyboard.
e.zh: 键盘下面藏着一张小纸条。

e.en: He felt the work was {beneath} his skill level.
e.zh: 他觉得这份工作配不上他的水平。

e.en: I always order eggs {Benedict} for brunch.
e.zh: 早午餐我总是点班尼迪克蛋。

e.en: He was branded a {Benedict} Arnold by his former teammates.
e.zh: 他被前队友们斥为叛徒。

benedictine.t:
adj. 本笃会的
n. 本笃会修士；本尼迪克汀甜酒

e.en: The {Benedictine} monks brewed beer in this abbey for centuries.
e.zh: 本笃会修士在这座修道院里酿酒已有几百年。

e.en: She poured a small glass of {Benedictine} after dinner.
e.zh: 晚餐后她倒了一小杯本笃甜酒。

e.en: The priest gave a final {benediction} before the wedding ended.
e.zh: 婚礼结束前神父做了最后的祝祷。

e.en: Soft sunlight felt like a {benediction} after the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨过后,柔和的阳光宛如一种祝福。

e.en: The library was built through the {benefaction} of a local family.
e.zh: 这座图书馆是靠当地一家人的捐赠建成的。

e.en: His generous {benefaction} funded scholarships for decades.
e.zh: 他慷慨的捐助为奖学金提供了数十年的资金。

e.en: An anonymous {benefactor} paid off the school's debts.
e.zh: 一位匿名捐助者偿清了学校的债务。

e.en: She thanked her {benefactor} in her acceptance speech.
e.zh: 她在获奖致辞中感谢了她的资助人。

e.en: The orphanage was funded by a wealthy {benefactress}.
e.zh: 这家孤儿院由一位富有的女资助人出资兴办。

e.en: She became the museum's most generous {benefactress}.
e.zh: 她成了博物馆最慷慨的女赞助人。

e.en: The young priest received a {benefice} in the rural parish.
e.zh: 那位年轻牧师在乡村教区获得了一份圣俸。

e.en: Medieval lords often granted a {benefice} to loyal clergymen.
e.zh: 中世纪领主常将圣俸授予忠诚的神职人员。

e.en: The foundation is famous for its {beneficence} toward students.
e.zh: 该基金会以对学生的慈善之举而闻名。

e.en: Her quiet {beneficence} touched everyone in the village.
e.zh: 她默默的善行打动了村里的每个人。

e.en: The {beneficent} donor funded a new children's hospital.
e.zh: 那位仁慈的捐助者资助建造了一座新儿童医院。

e.en: Sunshine has a {beneficent} effect on people's mood.
e.zh: 阳光对人的心情有积极有益的作用。

e.en: Regular exercise is {beneficial} to your mental health.
e.zh: 经常锻炼对心理健康有好处。

e.en: The new policy proved {beneficial} for small businesses.
e.zh: 新政策被证明对小企业有利。

e.en: The trust fund is {beneficially} owned by his children.
e.zh: 该信托基金的实益所有人是他的孩子们。

e.en: The merger {beneficially} affected both companies' stock prices.
e.zh: 此次合并对两家公司的股价都产生了有利影响。

e.en: The main {beneficiaries} of the policy are low-income families.
e.zh: 该政策的主要受益者是低收入家庭。

e.en: He named his three children as {beneficiaries} on the policy.
e.zh: 他在保单上指定三个孩子为受益人。

e.en: She is the sole {beneficiary} of her uncle's will.
e.zh: 她是她叔叔遗嘱的唯一受益人。

e.en: Update the {beneficiary} on your life insurance after marriage.
e.zh: 婚后记得更新人寿保险的受益人。

benefit.t:
n. 好处；福利
v. 受益

e.en: What's the main {benefit} of upgrading to the premium plan?
e.zh: 升级到高级套餐的主要好处是什么?

e.en: The concert was held to {benefit} earthquake victims.
e.zh: 那场音乐会是为地震灾民举办的义演。

e.en: Thousands of students {benefited} from the scholarship program.
e.zh: 成千上万的学生从这项奖学金计划中受益。

e.en: The company {benefited} greatly from the new tax law.
e.zh: 公司从新税法中获益匪浅。

e.en: The charity is {benefiting} families across the entire region.
e.zh: 这个慈善机构正在惠及整个地区的家庭。

e.en: Remote work is {benefiting} parents with young children.
e.zh: 远程办公正在让有小孩的父母受益。

benefits.t:
n. 好处；福利（复数）
v. 受益

e.en: This job offers great health {benefits} and paid leave.
e.zh: 这份工作提供丰厚的医疗福利和带薪假期。

e.en: Meditation {benefits} both your mind and body.
e.zh: 冥想对身心都有好处。

benelux.t: n. 比荷卢（比利时、荷兰、卢森堡三国）

e.en: The {Benelux} countries cooperate closely on trade and policy.
e.zh: 比荷卢三国在贸易和政策上密切合作。

e.en: Our company has offices throughout the {Benelux} region.
e.zh: 我们公司在比荷卢地区各处设有办事处。

benetton.t: n. 贝纳通（意大利服饰品牌）

e.en: She bought a colorful sweater at the {Benetton} store.
e.zh: 她在贝纳通店里买了一件彩色毛衣。

e.en: {Benetton} ads in the nineties sparked huge controversy.
e.zh: 九十年代贝纳通的广告引发了巨大争议。

e.en: The community thanked her for years of quiet {benevolence}.
e.zh: 社区感谢她多年来默默的善行。

e.en: His {benevolence} toward strangers earned him many friends.
e.zh: 他对陌生人的善心为他赢得了许多朋友。

e.en: The king extracted forced {benevolences} from wealthy merchants.
e.zh: 国王向富商强征所谓的乐捐税。

e.en: Her small daily {benevolences} brightened the nursing home.
e.zh: 她每天的小善举让养老院充满温暖。

e.en: He gave the children a {benevolent} smile.
e.zh: 他向孩子们露出慈祥的微笑。

e.en: The {benevolent} foundation supports schools in poor areas.
e.zh: 这家慈善基金会资助贫困地区的学校。

e.en: The grandfather smiled {benevolently} at his grandchildren.
e.zh: 祖父慈爱地对孙子孙女们微笑。

e.en: She {benevolently} agreed to mentor the new intern.
e.zh: 她善意地同意指导那位新实习生。

benfica.t: n. 本菲卡（葡萄牙足球俱乐部）

e.en: {Benfica} won the Portuguese league title again this year.
e.zh: 本菲卡今年再次夺得葡萄牙联赛冠军。

e.en: He has supported {Benfica} since he was a child.
e.zh: 他从小就是本菲卡的球迷。

e.en: The {Bengal} tiger is the national animal of India.
e.zh: 孟加拉虎是印度的国家动物。

e.en: Cuisine from {Bengal} is famous for its fish dishes.
e.zh: 孟加拉地区的菜肴以鱼类料理而闻名。

bengali.t:
n. 孟加拉人；孟加拉语
adj. 孟加拉的

e.en: She speaks fluent {Bengali} with her grandparents at home.
e.zh: 她在家和祖父母用流利的孟加拉语交谈。

e.en: {Bengali} literature has produced several Nobel laureates.
e.zh: 孟加拉语文学曾产生过多位诺贝尔奖得主。

benghazi.t: n. 班加西（利比亚城市）

e.en: {Benghazi} is the second largest city in Libya.
e.zh: 班加西是利比亚的第二大城市。

e.en: The journalist reported live from {Benghazi} during the conflict.
e.zh: 那名记者在冲突期间从班加西现场报道。

e.en: The {Beni} River flows through northern Bolivia.
e.zh: 贝尼河流经玻利维亚北部。

e.en: Sushi chefs sometimes garnish dishes with {beni} ginger.
e.zh: 寿司师傅有时会用红姜来装饰菜肴。

benighted.t: adj. 蒙昧的；愚昧无知的

e.en: He dismissed the village as a {benighted} backwater.
e.zh: 他贬低那个村子是愚昧落后的地方。

e.en: The hikers became {benighted} on the mountain trail.
e.zh: 登山者在山道上被夜色困住了。

benign.t: adj. 良性的（肿瘤）；和善的

e.en: The doctor confirmed that the tumor was {benign}.
e.zh: 医生确认那个肿瘤是良性的。

e.en: She gave him a {benign} smile from across the room.
e.zh: 她从房间另一头向他露出温和的微笑。

e.en: The teacher looked {benignly} upon the noisy children.
e.zh: 老师慈祥地看着吵闹的孩子们。

e.en: He nodded {benignly} as the speaker continued his story.
e.zh: 演讲者继续讲述时,他温和地点了点头。

e.en: {Benin} is a small country in West Africa.
e.zh: 贝宁是西非的一个小国。

e.en: The ancient bronzes of {Benin} are world famous.
e.zh: 贝宁的古代青铜器闻名于世。

e.en: The priest offered a {benison} on the new couple.
e.zh: 牧师为这对新人献上祝福。

e.en: Cool rain was a {benison} after weeks of drought.
e.zh: 在数周干旱之后,凉爽的雨水真是上天的恩赐。

e.en: Charleston is famous for its crispy {benne} wafers.
e.zh: 查尔斯顿以其酥脆的芝麻薄饼而闻名。

e.en: She sprinkled {benne} seeds over the salad.
e.zh: 她在沙拉上撒了些芝麻籽。

bent.t:
adj. 弯曲的；执意的
n. 爱好；倾向

e.en: She {bent} down to tie her shoelaces.
e.zh: 她弯下腰系鞋带。

e.en: He has a natural {bent} for solving puzzles.
e.zh: 他天生擅长解谜。

bentgrass.t: n. 翦股颖（一种草坪草）

e.en: Most golf course greens are planted with {bentgrass}.
e.zh: 大多数高尔夫球场的果岭都种植翦股颖。

e.en: {Bentgrass} requires careful mowing and frequent watering.
e.zh: 翦股颖需要精心修剪和频繁浇水。

benthamite.t:
n. 边沁学派信徒
adj. 边沁主义的

e.en: His {Benthamite} approach prioritized the greatest good for everyone.
e.zh: 他持边沁主义观点,优先考虑大多数人的最大利益。

e.en: Critics call the policy a cold {Benthamite} calculation.
e.zh: 批评者称该政策是冷冰冰的边沁式功利计算。

benthic.t: adj. 海底的；水底生物的

e.en: Crabs and starfish are typical {benthic} creatures.
e.zh: 螃蟹和海星是典型的海底生物。

e.en: Scientists studied the {benthic} community on the ocean floor.
e.zh: 科学家研究了海底的底栖生物群落。

benthos.t: n. 底栖生物（水域底部生物群）

e.en: The {benthos} includes all organisms living on the seabed.
e.zh: 底栖生物指所有生活在海床上的生物。

e.en: Pollution has dramatically reduced the local {benthos}.
e.zh: 污染已使当地底栖生物群落大幅减少。

bentley.t: n. 宾利（汽车品牌）；姓氏

e.en: He pulled up to the hotel in a black {Bentley}.
e.zh: 他开着一辆黑色宾利停在酒店门口。

e.en: A new {Bentley} can cost over three hundred thousand dollars.
e.zh: 一辆新宾利可能要价超过三十万美元。

e.en: She packs a homemade {bento} for lunch every day.
e.zh: 她每天都会带自制的便当作午餐。

e.en: The shop sells colorful {bento} boxes for kids.
e.zh: 那家店出售色彩缤纷的儿童便当盒。

bentwood.t: n. 弯曲木（制家具用的蒸弯木材）

e.en: The cafe was furnished with classic {bentwood} chairs.
e.zh: 咖啡馆里摆放着经典的曲木椅。

e.en: She inherited a beautiful {bentwood} rocking chair from her grandmother.
e.zh: 她从祖母那里继承了一把漂亮的曲木摇椅。

e.en: The freezing wind began to {benumb} her fingers.
e.zh: 刺骨的寒风开始让她的手指麻木。

e.en: Constant bad news can {benumb} our sense of empathy.
e.zh: 持续的坏消息会让我们的同理心变得麻木。

benz.t: n. 奔驰（汽车，Mercedes-Benz 简称）

e.en: He drives a vintage {Benz} to car shows on weekends.
e.zh: 他周末开着一辆老款奔驰去参加车展。

e.en: Karl {Benz} invented the first practical automobile.
e.zh: 卡尔·本茨发明了第一辆实用汽车。

e.en: Long-term exposure to {benzene} can cause serious health problems.
e.zh: 长期接触苯会引起严重的健康问题。

e.en: {Benzene} is a key ingredient in many industrial chemicals.
e.zh: 苯是许多工业化学品的关键原料。

e.en: She used {benzine} to remove the grease stain from her coat.
e.zh: 她用石油醚去除大衣上的油污。

e.en: Old dry cleaners often relied on {benzine} as a solvent.
e.zh: 以前的干洗店常用石油醚作溶剂。

benzodiazepine.t: n. 苯二氮䓬类（镇静安眠药）

e.en: Her doctor prescribed a {benzodiazepine} for severe anxiety.
e.zh: 医生开了苯二氮䓬类药物治疗她的严重焦虑。

e.en: Long-term {benzodiazepine} use can lead to dependence.
e.zh: 长期使用苯二氮䓬类药物可能导致依赖。

beowulf.t: n. 贝奥武夫（古英语史诗）

e.en: We read {Beowulf} in our medieval literature class.
e.zh: 我们在中世纪文学课上读了《贝奥武夫》。

e.en: {Beowulf} battles a fearsome monster named Grendel.
e.zh: 贝奥武夫与一个名叫格伦德尔的可怕怪兽战斗。

e.en: She plans to {bequeath} her art collection to the museum.
e.zh: 她打算将她的艺术收藏遗赠给博物馆。

e.en: Parents often {bequeath} family traditions along with property.
e.zh: 父母往往把家族传统连同财产一起留给后代。

bequeathed.t: v. bequeath 的过去式/过去分词；遗赠

e.en: His grandfather {bequeathed} him a vintage pocket watch.
e.zh: 他祖父把一块古董怀表遗赠给了他。

e.en: The professor {bequeathed} her library to the university.
e.zh: 那位教授把她的藏书遗赠给了大学。

bequeathing.t: v. bequeath 的现在分词；遗赠中

e.en: He is {bequeathing} most of his fortune to charity.
e.zh: 他正把大部分财产遗赠给慈善机构。

e.en: She thought carefully about {bequeathing} the house to her niece.
e.zh: 她仔细考虑过把房子留给侄女的事。

bequeaths.t: v. bequeath 的第三人称单数；遗赠

e.en: The will {bequeaths} the family farm to the eldest son.
e.zh: 遗嘱将家庭农场遗赠给长子。

e.en: Each generation {bequeaths} its language to the next.
e.zh: 每一代人都把自己的语言传给下一代。

e.en: The library received a generous {bequest} from a former patron.
e.zh: 图书馆收到了一位老赞助人的慷慨遗赠。

e.en: Her {bequest} funded scholarships for music students.
e.zh: 她的遗赠资助了音乐专业学生的奖学金。

e.en: The coach began to {berate} the team for their lazy performance.
e.zh: 教练开始痛斥球队表现散漫。

e.en: Don't {berate} yourself for one small mistake.
e.zh: 别为一个小错误而苛责自己。

berber.t:
n. 柏柏尔人（北非民族）
adj. 柏柏尔的

e.en: The {Berber} people have lived in North Africa for millennia.
e.zh: 柏柏尔人在北非生活了数千年。

e.en: She bought a beautiful handwoven {Berber} rug in Morocco.
e.zh: 她在摩洛哥买了一块漂亮的手工编织柏柏尔地毯。

berchtesgaden.t: n. 贝希特斯加登（德国城镇）

e.en: {Berchtesgaden} is a picturesque town in the Bavarian Alps.
e.zh: 贝希特斯加登是巴伐利亚阿尔卑斯山中一座风景如画的小镇。

e.en: Tourists visit {Berchtesgaden} for its stunning mountain views.
e.zh: 游客们因壮丽的山景而前往贝希特斯加登。

berdichev.t: n. 别尔季切夫（乌克兰城市）

e.en: My grandmother was born in {Berdichev}, a small Ukrainian town.
e.zh: 我的祖母出生在乌克兰的小城别尔基切夫。

e.en: The history of {Berdichev} reflects centuries of Jewish culture.
e.zh: 别尔基切夫的历史承载着几个世纪的犹太文化。

bereave.t: v. 使丧失（亲人）；使痛失

e.en: War can {bereave} families of their loved ones overnight.
e.zh: 战争可能一夜之间夺走家庭中至亲的生命。

e.en: The accident would {bereave} the small village of its mayor.
e.zh: 那场事故将使小村庄痛失他们的镇长。

bereaved.t:
adj. 丧亲的
n. 丧亲者

e.en: The {bereaved} family received messages of support from neighbors.
e.zh: 失去亲人的家庭收到了邻居们的慰问。

e.en: Counselors offer free sessions to the {bereaved} after the tragedy.
e.zh: 悲剧发生后,辅导员为遗属提供免费咨询。

bereavement.t: n. 丧亲之痛；亲人去世

e.en: She took {bereavement} leave after her father passed away.
e.zh: 父亲去世后她请了丧假。

e.en: The charity helps children cope with {bereavement} and loss.
e.zh: 该慈善机构帮助儿童应对丧亲之痛。

e.en: After the breakup, he felt utterly {bereft} and alone.
e.zh: 分手后他感到彻底失落和孤独。

e.en: The town was {bereft} of jobs after the factory closed.
e.zh: 工厂关闭后,小镇就业机会几乎全无。

e.en: She stared {bereftly} at the empty chair across the table.
e.zh: 她茫然失落地望着对面那张空椅子。

e.en: The dog whined {bereftly} when its owner left for work.
e.zh: 主人去上班后,狗狗失落地呜咽着。

e.en: He wore a black {beret} tilted to one side.
e.zh: 他歪戴着一顶黑色贝雷帽。

e.en: The art student bought a wool {beret} in Paris.
e.zh: 那位艺术系学生在巴黎买了一顶羊毛贝雷帽。

berg.t: n. 冰山（iceberg 简称）；姓氏

e.en: A massive {berg} drifted slowly past the research ship.
e.zh: 一座巨大的冰山缓缓从科考船旁漂过。

e.en: Climate change is causing more {berg} calving in the Arctic.
e.zh: 气候变化正导致北极更多冰山崩裂。

bergamo.t: n. 贝加莫（意大利城市）

e.en: We spent a weekend exploring the old town of {Bergamo}.
e.zh: 我们花了一个周末游览贝加莫老城。

e.en: {Bergamo} is famous for its medieval walls and hilltop views.
e.zh: 贝加莫以中世纪城墙和山顶美景闻名。

e.en: Earl Grey tea gets its distinctive flavor from {bergamot} oil.
e.zh: 伯爵茶独特的香味来自佛手柑油。

e.en: She added a few drops of {bergamot} to her perfume blend.
e.zh: 她在调香中加了几滴佛手柑精油。

e.en: It rains almost every day in {Bergen}, Norway's coastal city.
e.zh: 挪威沿海城市卑尔根几乎天天下雨。

e.en: We took the scenic train from Oslo to {Bergen}.
e.zh: 我们坐风景列车从奥斯陆前往卑尔根。

e.en: Professor {Berger} published a new book on social theory.
e.zh: 伯格教授出版了一本社会理论新书。

e.en: My neighbor Mr. {Berger} runs the bakery on Main Street.
e.zh: 我的邻居伯格先生在主街经营那家面包店。

bergerac.t: n. 贝热拉克（法国地名/人名）

e.en: The wines of {Bergerac} are often compared to Bordeaux.
e.zh: 贝热拉克的葡萄酒常被拿来与波尔多对比。

e.en: Cyrano de {Bergerac} remains one of the most beloved plays.
e.zh: 《大鼻子情圣》至今仍是最受喜爱的剧作之一。

berghaus.t: n. 贝豪斯（户外品牌）；姓氏

e.en: She bought a {Berghaus} jacket for her hiking trip.
e.zh: 她为徒步旅行买了一件Berghaus夹克。

e.en: My old {Berghaus} backpack has lasted nearly twenty years.
e.zh: 我那只旧Berghaus背包已经用了近二十年。

e.en: The little girl's {beribboned} hair bounced as she ran.
e.zh: 小女孩扎着丝带的头发随着奔跑一上一下。

e.en: She handed me a {beribboned} gift box for my birthday.
e.zh: 她递给我一个系着丝带的生日礼盒。

beriberi.t: n. 脚气病（维生素B1缺乏症）

e.en: {Beriberi} results from a serious deficiency of vitamin B1.
e.zh: 脚气病是由严重缺乏维生素B1引起的。

e.en: Sailors once suffered from {beriberi} on long ocean voyages.
e.zh: 水手们曾在远洋航行中患上脚气病。

bering.t: n. 白令（白令海、白令海峡）

e.en: Whales migrate through the {Bering} Sea every summer.
e.zh: 鲸鱼每年夏天迁徙穿越白令海。

e.en: Ancient peoples crossed the {Bering} land bridge into America.
e.zh: 古代人类经白令陆桥迁入美洲。

berk.t: n. 蠢人，傻瓜（英式俚语）

e.en: Don't be such a {berk} — apologize to your sister.
e.zh: 别这么蠢,快向你妹妹道歉。

e.en: I felt like a complete {berk} after locking myself out.
e.zh: 把自己锁在门外后我觉得自己像个十足的傻瓜。

berkeley.t: n. 伯克利（美国加州城市）

e.en: She studies computer science at {Berkeley} this fall.
e.zh: 今年秋天她在伯克利攻读计算机科学。

e.en: {Berkeley} is known for its progressive politics and cafes.
e.zh: 伯克利以进步政治和咖啡馆文化闻名。

berkhamsted.t: n. 伯克姆斯特德（英国城镇）

e.en: We caught the train from London out to {Berkhamsted}.
e.zh: 我们从伦敦坐火车到伯克姆斯特德。

e.en: {Berkhamsted} has a ruined castle worth visiting on weekends.
e.zh: 伯克姆斯特德有座值得周末一游的古堡遗迹。

e.en: My cousin lives in {Berkley}, a quiet Detroit suburb.
e.zh: 我表哥住在伯克利,底特律一个安静的郊区。

e.en: {Berkley} Books published the paperback edition last year.
e.zh: 伯克利出版社去年出版了这本书的平装本。

e.en: A few {berks} at the back kept shouting through the lecture.
e.zh: 后排几个蠢货在讲座中一直大声嚷嚷。

e.en: Honestly, only complete {berks} would believe that scam email.
e.zh: 说实话,只有彻底的蠢蛋才会相信那封诈骗邮件。

berkshire.t: n. 伯克郡（英格兰郡名）

e.en: We hiked through the rolling hills of {Berkshire} last weekend.
e.zh: 上周末我们徒步穿越了伯克郡起伏的丘陵。

e.en: Warren Buffett runs {Berkshire} Hathaway from Omaha, Nebraska.
e.zh: 沃伦·巴菲特在内布拉斯加州奥马哈执掌伯克希尔·哈撒韦。

e.en: I'm flying to {Berlin} next week for a conference.
e.zh: 我下周飞柏林参加一个会议。

e.en: {Berlin} has an amazing nightlife and a rich art scene.
e.zh: 柏林夜生活精彩,艺术氛围浓厚。

berliner.t: n. 柏林人；果酱甜甜圈

e.en: As a true {Berliner}, she knows every quiet corner of the city.
e.zh: 作为地道的柏林人,她熟悉这座城市的每个角落。

e.en: He bought a jam-filled {Berliner} from the corner bakery.
e.zh: 他在街角面包店买了一个夹果酱的柏林甜甜圈。

berlitz.t: n. 贝立兹（语言培训品牌）

e.en: She's taking Spanish lessons at the local {Berlitz} school.
e.zh: 她在当地的贝立兹学校上西班牙语课。

e.en: My old {Berlitz} phrasebook has been everywhere with me.
e.zh: 我那本旧的贝立兹会话手册陪我走遍各地。

e.en: Cyclists raced along the dirt {berm} at high speed.
e.zh: 自行车手沿着土制弯道高速飞驰。

e.en: They built a grass {berm} to block traffic noise.
e.zh: 他们筑起一道草丘以阻挡交通噪音。

e.en: We spent our honeymoon in {Bermuda} last summer.
e.zh: 去年夏天我们在百慕大度蜜月。

e.en: He showed up to the meeting in {Bermuda} shorts.
e.zh: 他穿着百慕大短裤来开会。

bermudian.t:
adj. 百慕大的
n. 百慕大人

e.en: The chef is {Bermudian} and uses local fish in every dish.
e.zh: 那位厨师是百慕大人,每道菜都用当地的鱼。

e.en: A {Bermudian} accent has hints of both British and Caribbean.
e.zh: 百慕大口音兼有英式与加勒比的影子。

e.en: {Bern} is the capital of Switzerland, not Zurich.
e.zh: 瑞士的首都是伯尔尼,不是苏黎世。

e.en: We visited Einstein's old apartment in {Bern}.
e.zh: 我们参观了爱因斯坦在伯尔尼的故居。

berne.t: n. 伯尔尼（Bern 的异拼）

e.en: The {Berne} Convention protects authors' copyrights internationally.
e.zh: 《伯尔尼公约》在国际范围内保护作者的版权。

e.en: She moved to {Berne} for a diplomatic posting.
e.zh: 她调任至伯尔尼担任外交职务。

bernini.t: n. 贝尔尼尼（意大利雕塑家）

e.en: {Bernini} sculpted the famous fountain in Piazza Navona.
e.zh: 贝尼尼雕刻了纳沃纳广场上著名的喷泉。

e.en: Tourists marveled at {Bernini}'s dramatic baroque sculptures.
e.zh: 游客们惊叹于贝尼尼极富戏剧张力的巴洛克雕塑。

e.en: Leonard {Bernstein} composed the music for West Side Story.
e.zh: 伦纳德·伯恩斯坦为《西区故事》谱写了音乐。

e.en: The orchestra performed a tribute to {Bernstein} last night.
e.zh: 乐团昨晚演出了一场致敬伯恩斯坦的音乐会。

e.en: The {berried} branches of the holly looked festive in December.
e.zh: 挂满浆果的冬青枝条在十二月显得喜气洋洋。

e.en: Birds flocked to the {berried} bushes near our window.
e.zh: 鸟儿成群飞到我们窗边那些结满浆果的灌木上。

e.en: I picked fresh {berries} for the breakfast pancakes.
e.zh: 我摘了新鲜浆果来做早餐松饼。

e.en: Wild {berries} grow along the trail in late summer.
e.zh: 夏末时山间小径上长满了野生浆果。

e.en: She topped her yogurt with a single ripe {berry}.
e.zh: 她在酸奶上放了一颗熟透的浆果。

e.en: Each {berry} on this bush is safe to eat raw.
e.zh: 这丛灌木上的每颗浆果都可以生吃。

berserk.t:
adj. 狂暴的，失控的
adv. 发狂地

e.en: The fans went {berserk} when the team scored in overtime.
e.zh: 球队加时赛进球时,球迷们都疯狂了。

e.en: My printer suddenly went {berserk} and spat out blank pages.
e.zh: 我的打印机突然抽风,不停吐出空白纸。

berserker.t: n. 狂战士（北欧神话/游戏职业）

e.en: In Norse legend, a {berserker} fought with terrifying fury.
e.zh: 在北欧传说中,狂战士以骇人的狂怒投入战斗。

e.en: The video game's {berserker} class deals massive melee damage.
e.zh: 这款游戏中的狂战士职业能造成巨大的近战伤害。

berth.t:
n. 卧铺；泊位
v. 停泊

e.en: The cruise ship eased into its {berth} at dawn.
e.zh: 邮轮在黎明时分缓缓驶入泊位。

e.en: I booked a lower {berth} on the overnight train.
e.zh: 我在夜行列车上订了一个下铺。

e.en: {Berwick} sits right on the border between England and Scotland.
e.zh: 贝里克正好坐落在英格兰与苏格兰的边界上。

e.en: We watched salmon swimming up the river at {Berwick}.
e.zh: 我们在贝里克看到鲑鱼逆流而上。

berwyn.t: n. 贝尔温（威尔士山脉/地名）

e.en: The {Berwyn} mountains offer some of the best hiking in Wales.
e.zh: 贝温山脉拥有威尔士最棒的徒步线路之一。

e.en: My uncle lives in {Berwyn}, a leafy suburb of Chicago.
e.zh: 我叔叔住在贝温,芝加哥一个绿树成荫的郊区。

e.en: The ring featured a stunning green {beryl} stone.
e.zh: 那枚戒指镶嵌着一颗惊艳的绿色绿柱石。

e.en: Miners discovered a vein of {beryl} deep underground.
e.zh: 矿工们在地下深处发现了一条绿柱石矿脉。

e.en: {Beryllium} is used in aerospace because it's incredibly light.
e.zh: 铍因极轻,被广泛用于航空航天领域。

e.en: Workers must wear masks when handling {beryllium} dust.
e.zh: 工人在处理铍粉尘时必须佩戴口罩。

e.en: Ancient Egyptians worshipped {Bes} as a protector of households.
e.zh: 古埃及人崇拜贝斯神,视其为家庭的守护者。

e.en: A small statue of {Bes} guarded the doorway of the tomb.
e.zh: 一尊小小的贝斯神像守护着墓室入口。

e.en: I {beseech} you to reconsider before signing the contract.
e.zh: 我恳求你在签合同前再考虑一下。

e.en: She wrote to {beseech} the governor for her brother's pardon.
e.zh: 她写信恳求州长赦免她的弟弟。

beseeching.t:
adj. 恳求的
v. 恳求（现在分词）

e.en: The puppy gave him a {beseeching} look at dinnertime.
e.zh: 晚饭时小狗用乞求的眼神望着他。

e.en: She sent a {beseeching} email begging for an extension.
e.zh: 她发了一封苦苦哀求延期的邮件。

e.en: He looked at his mother {beseechingly} for one more cookie.
e.zh: 他乞求般地望着妈妈,想再要一块饼干。

e.en: The defendant gazed {beseechingly} at the jury during the verdict.
e.zh: 宣判时被告以恳求的目光望向陪审团。

e.en: The startup was {beset} by funding problems from day one.
e.zh: 这家初创公司从第一天起就被资金问题困扰。

e.en: Doubts {beset} her as she walked toward the stage.
e.zh: 走向舞台时,种种疑虑涌上她的心头。

besetting.t:
adj. 纠缠不休的
v. 困扰（现在分词）

e.en: Procrastination is his {besetting} sin at work.
e.zh: 拖延是他工作中根深蒂固的毛病。

e.en: Self-doubt remains the {besetting} weakness of many writers.
e.zh: 自我怀疑仍是许多作家挥之不去的弱点。

e.en: She sat down {beside} me on the park bench.
e.zh: 她在公园长椅上坐到了我旁边。

e.en: He was {beside} himself with joy after the proposal.
e.zh: 求婚成功后他高兴得忘乎所以。

besides.t:
adv. 此外、而且
prep. 除……之外

e.en: {Besides} coffee, she ordered a chocolate croissant.
e.zh: 除了咖啡,她还点了一个巧克力可颂。

e.en: I'm too tired to go out, and {besides}, it's raining.
e.zh: 我太累了不想出门,再说外面还在下雨。

e.en: Reporters {besiege} the actor whenever he leaves the hotel.
e.zh: 每次那位演员离开酒店,记者都会蜂拥围住他。

e.en: Enemy troops planned to {besiege} the walled city.
e.zh: 敌军计划围攻这座有城墙的城市。

besieged.t:
adj. 被围困的
v. 围攻（过去式）

e.en: The customer service team was {besieged} with complaints after the outage.
e.zh: 故障发生后,客服团队被投诉淹没了。

e.en: Roman legions {besieged} the fortress for three months.
e.zh: 罗马军团围困了那座要塞整整三个月。

e.en: The {besieger} cut off the city's water supply.
e.zh: 围攻者切断了城里的供水。

e.en: Each {besieger} built a wooden tower to scale the walls.
e.zh: 每个围攻者都搭起木塔以攀越城墙。

besieges.t: v. 围攻（第三人称单数）

e.en: The army {besieges} the capital from every direction.
e.zh: 军队从四面八方围攻首都。

e.en: Fan mail {besieges} the singer after every new release.
e.zh: 每次新歌发行后,粉丝来信都把这位歌手淹没。

e.en: Photographers were {besieging} the courthouse all morning.
e.zh: 摄影师整个上午都把法院团团围住。

e.en: The general spent two years {besieging} the coastal city.
e.zh: 将军花了两年时间围攻这座沿海城市。

e.en: He sued the tabloid for trying to {besmirch} his reputation.
e.zh: 他起诉那家小报试图玷污他的名誉。

e.en: Don't let one mistake {besmirch} your entire career.
e.zh: 不要让一次失误毁掉你的整个职业生涯。

e.en: Fame can {besot} even the most level-headed performer.
e.zh: 名气会让最冷静的艺人都神魂颠倒。

e.en: Cheap wine seemed to {besot} him within minutes.
e.zh: 廉价葡萄酒似乎几分钟就让他醉得糊涂。

e.en: He's completely {besotted} with his new girlfriend.
e.zh: 他对新女友完全神魂颠倒。

e.en: The {besotted} fan waited six hours for an autograph.
e.zh: 那个痴迷的粉丝等了六个小时只为一个签名。

bespeak.t:
v. 表明、预示
v. 预订

e.en: Her steady hands {bespeak} years of surgical training.
e.zh: 她稳健的双手显示出多年外科训练的功底。

e.en: The empty shelves {bespeak} a serious supply problem.
e.zh: 空荡的货架表明供应出现了严重问题。

e.en: A {bespectacled} librarian quietly stamped each book.
e.zh: 一位戴眼镜的图书管理员安静地给每本书盖章。

e.en: The {bespectacled} professor peered over his notes.
e.zh: 那位戴眼镜的教授越过讲稿看了看。

bespoke.t: adj. 定制的、量身定做的

e.en: He ordered a {bespoke} suit for the wedding.
e.zh: 他为婚礼定制了一套西装。

e.en: Our agency builds {bespoke} software for small businesses.
e.zh: 我们公司为小企业定制软件。

bessarabia.t: n. 比萨拉比亚（地区名）

e.en: My grandmother emigrated from {Bessarabia} before the war.
e.zh: 我祖母在战前从比萨拉比亚移民出来。

e.en: {Bessarabia} once lay between the Dniester and Prut rivers.
e.zh: 比萨拉比亚曾位于德涅斯特河与普鲁特河之间。

bessemer.t: n. 贝塞麦（炼钢法发明人）

e.en: The {Bessemer} process revolutionized steel production in the 1800s.
e.zh: 贝塞麦炼钢法在19世纪彻底改变了钢铁生产。

e.en: Old mills in Pittsburgh once relied on {Bessemer} converters.
e.zh: 匹兹堡的老钢厂曾依赖贝塞麦转炉。

best.t:
adj. 最好的
adv. 最佳地

e.en: This is the {best} pizza I've ever eaten.
e.zh: 这是我吃过最好吃的披萨。

e.en: Try your {best} on the exam tomorrow.
e.zh: 明天考试尽你最大努力就好。

e.en: The novel describes the {bestial} cruelty of the regime.
e.zh: 小说描写了那个政权野兽般的残忍。

e.en: His {bestial} table manners shocked the other guests.
e.zh: 他粗野的餐桌礼仪让其他客人震惊。

e.en: The report condemned the {bestiality} of wartime atrocities.
e.zh: 报告谴责了战时暴行的兽性。

e.en: Witnesses described scenes of unimaginable {bestiality}.
e.zh: 目击者描述了难以想象的兽性场面。

e.en: The medieval {bestiary} described unicorns alongside real animals.
e.zh: 那本中世纪动物寓言集把独角兽和真实动物一起描述。

e.en: This game features a {bestiary} of over a hundred monsters.
e.zh: 这款游戏收录了上百种怪物图鉴。

e.en: It's noon — time to {bestir} yourself and get to work.
e.zh: 已经中午了,该打起精神去干活了。

e.en: Nothing could {bestir} him from the couch on Sundays.
e.zh: 周日没有什么能让他从沙发上动起来。

e.en: The university will {bestow} an honorary degree on her tomorrow.
e.zh: 大学明天将授予她荣誉学位。

e.en: Parents often {bestow} their values on their children.
e.zh: 父母常常把自己的价值观传给子女。

e.en: The {bestowal} of the medal moved everyone to tears.
e.zh: 颁授勋章的那一刻让所有人感动落泪。

e.en: His {bestowal} of so much trust surprised the new hire.
e.zh: 他给予如此多的信任让新员工感到意外。

e.en: The queen {bestowed} a knighthood on the scientist.
e.zh: 女王授予那位科学家骑士爵位。

e.en: Nature has {bestowed} this island with rare wildlife.
e.zh: 大自然赐予这座岛屿罕见的野生动物。

e.en: The committee is {bestowing} this year's prize on a young poet.
e.zh: 评委会正把今年的奖项授予一位年轻诗人。

e.en: She thanked her mentor for {bestowing} so much wisdom on her.
e.zh: 她感谢导师赐予她如此多的智慧。

bestows.t: v. 授予（第三人称单数）

e.en: The app {bestows} badges on users who finish daily challenges.
e.zh: 这款应用会给完成每日挑战的用户颁发徽章。

e.en: Citizenship {bestows} both rights and responsibilities.
e.zh: 公民身份既赋予权利也带来责任。

e.en: Few companies {bestride} the tech industry like this one.
e.zh: 很少有公司能像这家一样雄踞科技行业。

e.en: The statue shows the hero about to {bestride} his horse.
e.zh: 雕像描绘了英雄即将跨上战马的瞬间。

e.en: She {bestrode} the motorcycle and roared off into the night.
e.zh: 她跨上摩托车,轰鸣着冲入夜色。

e.en: For decades that author {bestrode} the literary world.
e.zh: 几十年来那位作家在文坛叱咤风云。

e.en: Her latest novel easily {bests} everything she's written before.
e.zh: 她最新的小说轻松超越了之前所有作品。

e.en: No one {bests} him at chess in this club.
e.zh: 在这个俱乐部没人能在国际象棋上赢过他。

e.en: Her debut novel became a surprise {bestseller}.
e.zh: 她的处女作意外成为畅销书。

e.en: The cookbook has been a {bestseller} for three years running.
e.zh: 这本食谱连续三年都是畅销书。

bestsellers.t: n. 畅销书、畅销商品（复数）

e.en: The shop displays new {bestsellers} right by the entrance.
e.zh: 书店把新晋畅销书摆在入口处。

e.en: Two of his books made the year's top ten {bestsellers}.
e.zh: 他有两本书进入了年度十大畅销书榜。

e.en: She's the {bestselling} author of three thriller series.
e.zh: 她是三部惊悚系列小说的畅销作家。

e.en: That phone became the year's {bestselling} model worldwide.
e.zh: 那款手机成为全球年度最畅销机型。

bet.t:
v. 打赌、下注
n. 赌注

e.en: I'd {bet} twenty dollars that it rains tomorrow.
e.zh: 我敢赌二十块钱明天会下雨。

e.en: Taking the train is your safest {bet} during rush hour.
e.zh: 高峰期坐火车是最稳妥的选择。

beta.t:
n. 测试版（软件）
n. 希腊字母β

e.en: The new feature is still in {beta} testing.
e.zh: 这个新功能还在测试版阶段。

e.en: Sign up to try the {beta} version of our app.
e.zh: 注册即可试用我们应用的测试版。

e.en: Many older villagers still chew {betel} nuts after meals.
e.zh: 许多年长的村民饭后仍会嚼槟榔。

e.en: The market sold fresh {betel} leaves wrapped in bundles.
e.zh: 市场上卖的新鲜槟榔叶都是成捆包好的。

e.en: The small {bethel} on the hill has stood for two centuries.
e.zh: 山上那座小礼拜堂已经矗立了两个世纪。

e.en: Sailors used to worship at the harbor {bethel}.
e.zh: 水手们过去常在港口的小教堂做礼拜。

e.en: She works at a research lab in {Bethesda}, Maryland.
e.zh: 她在马里兰州贝塞斯达的一家研究实验室工作。

e.en: The new game studio is based outside {Bethesda}.
e.zh: 这家新游戏工作室位于贝塞斯达郊外。

bethlehem.t: n. 伯利恒（耶稣出生地）

e.en: Tourists flock to {Bethlehem} every Christmas season.
e.zh: 每年圣诞季游客都涌向伯利恒。

e.en: The carol describes a quiet night in {Bethlehem}.
e.zh: 那首颂歌描绘了伯利恒一个宁静的夜晚。

e.en: Woe {betide} anyone who interrupts the boss during a call.
e.zh: 老板通话时谁敢打断,谁就要倒霉。

e.en: Whatever may {betide}, we'll face it together.
e.zh: 无论发生什么,我们都会一起面对。

e.en: Dark clouds usually {betoken} a coming storm.
e.zh: 乌云通常预示着暴风雨即将来临。

e.en: His silence seemed to {betoken} disappointment.
e.zh: 他的沉默似乎透露出失望。

betray.t:
v. 背叛；出卖
v. 泄露（秘密）

e.en: A true friend would never {betray} your trust.
e.zh: 真正的朋友永远不会辜负你的信任。

e.en: Try not to {betray} how nervous you are during the interview.
e.zh: 面试时尽量别流露出你有多紧张。

e.en: Leaking the document felt like a personal {betrayal}.
e.zh: 泄露那份文件让人觉得像是一次私人的背叛。

e.en: The novel's central theme is love and {betrayal}.
e.zh: 这部小说的核心主题是爱与背叛。

betrayed.t: v. 背叛（过去式/过去分词）

e.en: She felt {betrayed} when her partner shared the secret.
e.zh: 伴侣把秘密说出去时,她感到被背叛了。

e.en: His trembling voice {betrayed} how scared he really was.
e.zh: 他颤抖的声音暴露了他其实有多害怕。

e.en: History remembers him as the {betrayer} of the rebellion.
e.zh: 历史把他记作那场起义的背叛者。

e.en: No one wants to be branded a {betrayer} by their own team.
e.zh: 谁也不想被自己的团队贴上叛徒的标签。

e.en: She kept smiling without {betraying} her disappointment.
e.zh: 她一直微笑着,没有流露出半点失望。

e.en: He was accused of {betraying} confidential client data.
e.zh: 他被指控泄露客户的机密数据。

betrays.t: v. 背叛（第三人称单数）

e.en: His accent slightly {betrays} where he grew up.
e.zh: 他的口音略微透露了他在哪里长大。

e.en: The novel {betrays} the author's love of old films.
e.zh: 这部小说流露出作者对老电影的喜爱。

e.en: In the play, the king plans to {betroth} his daughter to a duke.
e.zh: 剧中国王打算把女儿许配给一位公爵。

e.en: It was once common to {betroth} children at a young age.
e.zh: 过去把孩子在年幼时订婚是常见的事。

e.en: Their {betrothal} was announced at a family dinner.
e.zh: 他们的订婚是在一次家庭聚餐上宣布的。

e.en: The {betrothal} ring belonged to her great-grandmother.
e.zh: 那枚订婚戒指原本属于她的曾祖母。

betrothed.t:
adj. 已订婚的
n. 未婚夫/妻

e.en: She introduced her {betrothed} to her colleagues at the party.
e.zh: 她在派对上把未婚夫介绍给同事们。

e.en: The couple were {betrothed} for two years before the wedding.
e.zh: 这对夫妇在结婚前订婚了两年。

bets.t:
n. 赌注（复数）
v. 打赌（第三人称单数）

e.en: He places small {bets} on football matches every weekend.
e.zh: 他每个周末都在足球比赛上下点小注。

e.en: All {bets} are off if the lead actor drops out.
e.zh: 如果主演退出,一切就说不准了。

better.t:
adj. 更好的
adv. 更好地

e.en: This translation is {better} than the previous draft.
e.zh: 这版译文比之前的草稿要好。

e.en: You'd {better} bring an umbrella — it's pouring outside.
e.zh: 你最好带把伞,外面正下大雨。

e.en: The foundation funds programs for the {betterment} of rural schools.
e.zh: 基金会资助旨在改善乡村学校的项目。

e.en: He devoted his life to the {betterment} of public health.
e.zh: 他毕生致力于改善公共卫生。

betters.t:
v. 改善（第三人称单数）
n. 上级；前辈

e.en: Practice {betters} your chances of passing the exam.
e.zh: 练习能提高你通过考试的机会。

e.en: The new model {betters} the old one in every way.
e.zh: 新款在各方面都优于旧款。

betting.t:
n. 打赌；下注
v. 打赌（进行时）

e.en: Online {betting} apps are now banned in several states.
e.zh: 网上博彩应用在好几个州已被禁止。
