e.zh: 我对昨晚的记忆有一大堆空白。

blare.t:
v. 发出刺耳声
n. 刺耳声响

e.en: The car alarms {blare} every night on this street.
e.zh: 这条街上每晚都有汽车警报器在狂响。

e.en: I heard the {blare} of trumpets from the parade.
e.zh: 我听到游行队伍传来响亮的喇叭声。

e.en: The neighbor's TV was {blaring} again at midnight.
e.zh: 邻居家的电视半夜又开得震天响。

e.en: She woke up to sirens {blaring} outside her window.
e.zh: 她被窗外刺耳的警笛声吵醒了。

e.en: Don't believe his {blarney} about working all weekend.
e.zh: 别信他说整个周末都在加班的鬼话。

e.en: The salesman's charm was pure {blarney}.
e.zh: 那个推销员的魅力完全是花言巧语。

e.en: Tourists looked amazed, but the locals seemed {blase}.
e.zh: 游客们一脸惊叹，本地人却显得满不在乎。

e.en: After ten launches, the team had grown {blase} about deadlines.
e.zh: 经历十次发版后，团队对截止日期已经麻木了。

e.en: In some countries it's still illegal to {blaspheme} in public.
e.zh: 在一些国家，公开亵渎神明仍然是违法的。

e.en: Fans would say it's wrong to {blaspheme} the original recipe.
e.zh: 粉丝们会说，亵渎原版配方是不对的。

e.en: The crowd branded the writer a {blasphemer} after the speech.
e.zh: 演讲过后，人群把这位作家斥为亵渎者。

e.en: Suggesting pineapple on pizza makes him a {blasphemer} here.
e.zh: 在这里提议菠萝披萨，会让他被当成大逆不道的人。

e.en: The film was banned for being {blasphemous}.
e.zh: 这部电影因被认为亵渎神明而遭到禁映。

e.en: To true fans, remixing the song felt {blasphemous}.
e.zh: 对真正的粉丝来说，给这首歌混音简直是大不敬。

e.en: In ancient times, {blasphemy} could carry the death penalty.
e.zh: 在古代，亵渎神明可能会被判处死刑。

e.en: Calling that pasta authentic is culinary {blasphemy}.
e.zh: 把那个意面说成正宗，简直是对烹饪的亵渎。

blast.t:
n. 爆炸；一阵
v. 炸开

e.en: The {blast} shattered windows two blocks away.
e.zh: 那次爆炸震碎了两个街区外的窗户。

e.en: We had a {blast} at the rooftop party last night.
e.zh: 我们昨晚在天台派对上玩得超级开心。

blasted.t:
v. 炸毁（blast 过去式）
adj. 该死的

e.en: Workers {blasted} a tunnel through the mountain.
e.zh: 工人们在山中炸开了一条隧道。

e.en: My phone {blasted} alerts all morning during the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨期间，我的手机一整个上午都在狂响警报。

e.en: The kids fought over the new water {blaster}.
e.zh: 孩子们抢着玩那把新的水枪。

e.en: He carried a portable {blaster} on his shoulder back in the 80s.
e.zh: 上世纪八十年代，他常把便携式音响扛在肩上。

blackball.t:
v. 投反对票排斥
n. 反对票

e.en: The club voted to {blackball} the new applicant.
e.zh: 俱乐部投票否决了那位新申请人。

e.en: She felt the industry had {blackballed} her unfairly.
e.zh: 她觉得这个行业不公平地把她排挤出去了。

blackbeard.t: n. 黑胡子（著名海盗名）

e.en: {Blackbeard} terrorized ships across the Caribbean Sea.
e.zh: 黑胡子在加勒比海上让船只闻风丧胆。

e.en: Legend says {Blackbeard} buried treasure along the coast.
e.zh: 传说黑胡子把宝藏埋在了沿海一带。

e.en: We picked a basket of {blackberry} fruit by the trail.
e.zh: 我们在小路边摘了一篮黑莓。

e.en: She baked a warm {blackberry} pie for dessert.
e.zh: 她烤了一个热乎乎的黑莓派当甜点。

e.en: A {blackbird} sang outside the kitchen window at dawn.
e.zh: 一只黑鸟在黎明时分在厨房窗外歌唱。

e.en: The {blackbird} built its nest in the hawthorn bush.
e.zh: 那只乌鸫在山楂树丛里筑了巢。

e.en: The teacher wrote the formula on the {blackboard}.
e.zh: 老师把公式写在了黑板上。

e.en: Chalk dust covered the old wooden {blackboard}.
e.zh: 粉笔灰覆盖着那块旧木黑板。

e.en: Most classrooms replaced {blackboards} with whiteboards years ago.
e.zh: 大多数教室多年前就把黑板换成白板了。

e.en: The old school still uses {blackboards} in every room.
e.zh: 那所老学校每间教室仍在使用黑板。

e.en: A perfect {blackbody} absorbs all incoming radiation.
e.zh: 理想黑体会吸收所有入射的辐射。

e.en: Stars are often modeled as {blackbody} radiators in physics.
e.zh: 在物理学中恒星常被建模为黑体辐射源。

blackburn.t: n. 布莱克本（英国地名/姓氏）

e.en: {Blackburn} Rovers play their home matches at Ewood Park.
e.zh: 布莱克本流浪者队在尤伍德公园进行主场比赛。

e.en: She grew up in {Blackburn}, a town in Lancashire.
e.zh: 她在兰开夏郡的布莱克本镇长大。

e.en: She spread {blackcurrant} jam on her toast this morning.
e.zh: 她今早在吐司上抹了黑加仑果酱。

e.en: This juice has a tart {blackcurrant} flavor that I love.
e.zh: 这款果汁有我喜欢的酸甜黑加仑味。

e.en: Smoke from the fire began to {blacken} the ceiling.
e.zh: 火灾的烟开始把天花板熏黑。

e.en: Critics tried to {blacken} the senator's reputation online.
e.zh: 批评者试图在网上抹黑这位参议员的名声。

blackened.t:
adj. 变黑的；被抹黑的
v. blacken 的过去式

e.en: He ordered {blackened} catfish with rice and beans.
e.zh: 他点了一份焦香鲶鱼配米饭和豆子。

e.en: The walls were {blackened} by years of candle smoke.
e.zh: 墙壁因多年的蜡烛烟熏而变黑。

blackening.t:
v. 使变黑（现在分词）
n. 发黑

e.en: The {blackening} sky warned of an approaching storm.
e.zh: 渐渐变黑的天空预示着暴风雨即将来临。

e.en: Tabloids kept {blackening} the actor's name without evidence.
e.zh: 小报不断毫无证据地抹黑这位演员的名声。

blacker.t: adj. 更黑的（black 比较级）

e.en: The night grew {blacker} as the clouds covered the moon.
e.zh: 乌云遮住月亮,夜色变得更加漆黑。

e.en: Her mood seemed {blacker} after reading the bad news.
e.zh: 看到坏消息后,她的心情显得更加阴沉。

blackface.t: n. 黑脸扮装（带种族含义的化妆）

e.en: The old film featured actors in {blackface}, which is now condemned.
e.zh: 那部老电影里有演员涂黑脸出演,如今受到谴责。

e.en: Wearing {blackface} for a costume sparked widespread outrage.
e.zh: 用涂黑脸装扮成戏服引发了广泛的愤怒。

blackfish.t: n. 黑鱼（多种深色鱼的统称）

e.en: Local fishermen caught a large {blackfish} off the rocky coast.
e.zh: 当地渔民在礁石海岸捕到了一条大黑鱼。

e.en: The documentary {Blackfish} changed views on captive orcas.
e.zh: 这部名为《黑鱼》的纪录片改变了人们对圈养虎鲸的看法。

e.en: A swarm of {blackfly} ruined our hike near the river.
e.zh: 一群黑蝇毁了我们在河边的徒步行程。

e.en: Gardeners hate {blackfly} because they damage bean plants.
e.zh: 园丁讨厌黑蝇,因为它们会损害豆类植物。

blackford.t: n. 布莱克福德（地名/姓氏）

e.en: They drove past {Blackford} on their way to Edinburgh.
e.zh: 他们在前往爱丁堡的路上经过了布莱克福德。

e.en: Dr. {Blackford} published a new paper on philosophy of mind.
e.zh: 布莱克福德博士发表了一篇关于心灵哲学的新论文。

e.en: The novel's villain is a charming but ruthless {blackguard}.
e.zh: 小说中的反派是个迷人却冷酷的恶棍。

e.en: She called the swindler a complete {blackguard} to his face.
e.zh: 她当着骗子的面骂他是个十足的无赖。

e.en: She uses a clay mask to remove every stubborn {blackhead}.
e.zh: 她用泥膜去除每一个顽固的黑头。

e.en: Squeezing a {blackhead} can leave scars on your skin.
e.zh: 挤黑头可能会在皮肤上留下疤痕。

blackheath.t: n. 布莱克希思（伦敦地名）

e.en: They picnicked on {Blackheath} during the warm spring weekend.
e.zh: 温暖的春日周末,他们在布莱克希思野餐。

e.en: The marathon route passes through {Blackheath} early on.
e.zh: 马拉松路线在前段会经过布莱克希思。

blackie.t: n. 小黑（宠物昵称）；姓氏

e.en: Their old cat {Blackie} loves to nap on the windowsill.
e.zh: 他们的老猫小黑喜欢在窗台上打盹。

e.en: Grandpa always called the family dog {Blackie} for short.
e.zh: 爷爷总是把家里的狗简称叫小黑。

e.en: The sauce had a {blackish} color from the soy and vinegar.
e.zh: 酱汁因加了酱油和醋而呈现微黑色。

e.en: He wore a {blackish} blue suit to the evening event.
e.zh: 他穿着一身近乎黑的蓝色西装出席晚宴。

blackjack.t:
n. 21点（纸牌游戏）
n. 短棍

e.en: He won three hundred dollars playing {blackjack} last night.
e.zh: 他昨晚玩二十一点赢了三百美元。

e.en: The casino offers {blackjack} tables with low minimum bets.
e.zh: 这家赌场提供低底注的二十一点牌桌。

blackleg.t: n. 工贼（罢工期间照常上工者）

e.en: Striking miners shouted insults at every {blackleg} crossing the line.
e.zh: 罢工的矿工对每一个越线的工贼大声辱骂。

e.en: The union refused to forgive any {blackleg} who broke the strike.
e.zh: 工会拒绝原谅任何破坏罢工的工贼。

blacklist.t:
n. 黑名单
v. 列入黑名单

e.en: The company added that supplier to its internal {blacklist}.
e.zh: 公司把那家供应商加进了内部黑名单。

e.en: Spam filters {blacklist} domains that send junk mail.
e.zh: 垃圾邮件过滤器会把发送垃圾邮件的域名列入黑名单。

blacklisted.t: v. 被列入黑名单（过去式/过去分词）

e.en: Several writers were {blacklisted} during the McCarthy era.
e.zh: 在麦卡锡时代,有几位作家被列入了黑名单。

e.en: His IP got {blacklisted} after too many failed login attempts.
e.zh: 他的 IP 因为多次登录失败被加入了黑名单。

e.en: He stared {blackly} at the referee after the bad call.
e.zh: 在裁判误判后,他阴沉地瞪着对方。

e.en: She joked {blackly} about her rough week at work.
e.zh: 她用黑色幽默调侃自己这一周糟糕的工作。

blackmail.t:
v. 敲诈；勒索
n. 敲诈

e.en: The hackers tried to {blackmail} the company with leaked emails.
e.zh: 黑客试图用泄露的邮件勒索这家公司。

e.en: Threatening to expose private photos is a form of {blackmail}.
e.zh: 威胁公开私人照片是一种敲诈行为。

e.en: The {blackmailer} demanded ten thousand dollars in cryptocurrency.
e.zh: 那名敲诈者要求支付一万美元的加密货币。

e.en: Police finally arrested the {blackmailer} after a long investigation.
e.zh: 经过长期调查,警方终于逮捕了那个敲诈者。

e.en: Professor {Blackman} taught economics at the university for decades.
e.zh: 布莱克曼教授在这所大学教经济学几十年了。

e.en: Detective {Blackman} solved the case within a single week.
e.zh: 布莱克曼警探在一周之内就破了案。

e.en: The {blackness} of the cave swallowed the beam of his flashlight.
e.zh: 洞穴的漆黑吞没了他手电筒的光束。

e.en: She stared into the {blackness} outside the train window.
e.zh: 她凝视着火车窗外的一片漆黑。

blackout.t:
n. 停电；断电
n. 昏厥；封锁消息

e.en: A massive storm caused a citywide {blackout} last night.
e.zh: 一场大风暴导致昨晚全市停电。

e.en: He suffered a brief {blackout} after standing up too quickly.
e.zh: 他起身太快,短暂晕厥了一下。

blackpool.t: n. 布莱克浦（英国海滨城市）

e.en: Families flock to {Blackpool} for the seaside amusement park.
e.zh: 许多家庭涌向布莱克浦的海滨游乐园。

e.en: The {Blackpool} Tower offers stunning views of the coast.
e.zh: 布莱克浦塔可以俯瞰壮丽的海岸景色。

blacks.t: n. 黑色系（复数）；黑人（复数）

e.en: She mostly wears {blacks} and grays to the office.
e.zh: 她去办公室时大多穿黑色和灰色的衣服。

e.en: The contrast between the deep {blacks} and bright whites looks stunning.
e.zh: 深黑与亮白之间的对比看起来非常惊艳。

blackshirt.t: n. 黑衫党（意大利法西斯党徒）

e.en: Old footage shows a {blackshirt} marching through the Italian streets.
e.zh: 旧影像显示一名黑衫党人在意大利街道上行进。

e.en: Mussolini's {blackshirt} militia terrorized political opponents.
e.zh: 墨索里尼的黑衫党民兵恐吓政治对手。

e.en: The village {blacksmith} hammered horseshoes by the glowing forge.
e.zh: 村里的铁匠在炽热的炉火旁锤打马蹄铁。

e.en: He trained as a {blacksmith} and now makes custom knives.
e.zh: 他做过铁匠学徒,现在制作定制刀具。

blackspot.t: n. 事故多发地；问题地段

e.en: That junction is a notorious accident {blackspot} in the city.
e.zh: 那个路口是市内臭名昭著的事故黑点。

e.en: Roses in the garden suffered from {blackspot} this rainy summer.
e.zh: 花园里的玫瑰在这个多雨的夏天得了黑斑病。

e.en: {Blackstone} acquired another tech company for two billion dollars.
e.zh: 黑石以二十亿美元收购了另一家科技公司。

e.en: Sir William {Blackstone} wrote influential commentaries on English law.
e.zh: 威廉·布莱克斯通爵士撰写了具有重大影响的英国法律评注。

e.en: A {blacktail} deer wandered into the campsite at dawn.
e.zh: 一头黑尾鹿在黎明时分溜进了营地。

e.en: Hunters spotted a young {blacktail} grazing near the ridge.
e.zh: 猎人在山脊附近看到一只小黑尾鹿在吃草。

e.en: The hedge of {blackthorn} bloomed white in early April.
e.zh: 四月初,黑刺李树篱开满了白花。

e.en: She picked sloes from a wild {blackthorn} for homemade gin.
e.zh: 她从一棵野生黑刺李上摘了些果子,准备自酿杜松子酒。

blacktop.t:
n. 沥青路面
v. 铺沥青

e.en: Kids played basketball on the steaming summer {blacktop}.
e.zh: 孩子们在炎热的夏日柏油球场上打篮球。

e.en: Workers laid fresh {blacktop} along the highway last week.
e.zh: 工人们上周沿着高速公路铺设了新的沥青路面。

blackwall.t: n. 布莱克沃尔（伦敦地名）

e.en: Drivers use the {Blackwall} Tunnel to cross under the Thames.
e.zh: 司机们通过布莱克沃尔隧道穿越泰晤士河底。

e.en: Traffic at the {Blackwall} approach was heavy this morning.
e.zh: 今早通往布莱克沃尔的路口交通非常拥堵。

e.en: The plant treats {blackwater} from toilets before releasing it.
e.zh: 这家工厂会先处理来自厕所的污水再排放。

e.en: The {Blackwater} River runs slowly through the cypress swamp.
e.zh: 布莱克沃特河缓缓流经柏树沼泽。

blackwell.t: n. 布莱克韦尔（姓氏/地名）

e.en: Elizabeth {Blackwell} was the first woman to earn a medical degree.
e.zh: 伊丽莎白·布莱克威尔是首位获得医学学位的女性。

e.en: {Blackwell}'s bookshop in Oxford has served students for centuries.
e.zh: 牛津的布莱克威尔书店已经为学生服务了几百年。

e.en: The cabinet was crafted from beautifully grained Australian {blackwood}.
e.zh: 这个柜子是用纹理精美的澳洲黑木做成的。

e.en: Ms. {Blackwood} hosted a reading at the local library.
e.zh: 布莱克伍德女士在当地图书馆主持了一场朗读会。

bladder.t:
n. 膀胱
n. 气囊；内胆

e.en: Drinking too much water made my {bladder} feel uncomfortably full.
e.zh: 喝太多水让我膀胱涨得很难受。

e.en: The doctor scheduled tests after he reported {bladder} pain.
e.zh: 在他报告膀胱疼痛后,医生安排了检查。

blade.t:
n. 刀刃；刀片
n. 叶片；桨叶

e.en: Be careful — the {blade} of this knife is extremely sharp.
e.zh: 小心——这把刀的刀刃非常锋利。

e.en: A single {blade} of grass poked through the cracked sidewalk.
e.zh: 一根草叶从裂开的人行道里钻了出来。

e.en: Security confiscated any {bladed} item before the concert started.
e.zh: 演唱会开始前,保安没收了任何带刀刃的物品。

e.en: The chef prefers a single-{bladed} cleaver for chopping vegetables.
e.zh: 厨师切菜时偏爱一把单刃菜刀。

blasting.t:
n. 爆破
adj. 强劲的（风、声）

e.en: They were {blasting} hip-hop from the open car window.
e.zh: 他们摇下车窗，把嘻哈音乐放得震天响。

e.en: Crews are {blasting} rock to widen the highway.
e.zh: 施工队正在爆破岩石以拓宽高速公路。

e.en: The embryo reaches the {blastocyst} stage about five days after fertilization.
e.zh: 受精后大约第五天，胚胎进入囊胚阶段。

e.en: Doctors transferred a single {blastocyst} during the IVF cycle.
e.zh: 医生在这次试管婴儿周期中只移植了一个囊胚。

e.en: The crowd cheered at the moment of {blastoff}.
e.zh: 火箭升空的那一刻，人群欢呼起来。

e.en: Mission control announced {blastoff} right on schedule.
e.zh: 任务控制中心准时宣布发射升空。

e.en: Each {blastomere} is created by early divisions of the embryo.
e.zh: 每个卵裂球都是胚胎早期分裂形成的。

e.en: The lab biopsied a single {blastomere} for genetic testing.
e.zh: 实验室取出单个卵裂球进行基因检测。

blasts.t:
n. 爆炸；冲击波
v. 爆破

e.en: Two loud {blasts} echoed across the harbor.
e.zh: 两声巨响在港口上空回荡。

e.en: The fan {blasts} cold air directly at my desk.
e.zh: 风扇正对着我的办公桌猛吹冷风。

blat.t: v. 发出刺耳声；咩咩叫

e.en: The old trumpet could only {blat} a few sour notes.
e.zh: 那把旧小号只能吹出几个走音的刺耳声。

e.en: His motorcycle gave a loud {blat} before it died.
e.zh: 他的摩托车响亮地噗了一声就熄火了。

e.en: That was a {blatant} foul, even the fans saw it.
e.zh: 那明显是犯规，连球迷都看出来了。

e.en: The ad contained a {blatant} lie about the product.
e.zh: 那则广告对产品做了赤裸裸的虚假宣传。

blatantly.t: adv. 公然地；明目张胆地

e.en: He {blatantly} copied her slides for his own pitch.
e.zh: 他明目张胆地把她的幻灯片抄去做自己的提案。

e.en: The driver {blatantly} ran the red light in front of police.
e.zh: 那个司机当着警察的面公然闯了红灯。

e.en: Mrs. {Blatch} taught third grade for forty years.
e.zh: 布拉奇老师教了四十年三年级。

e.en: The book is dedicated to a friend named {Blatch}.
e.zh: 这本书是献给一位名叫布拉奇的朋友。

blather.t:
v. 喋喋不休
n. 废话

e.en: Stop the {blather} and tell me what actually happened.
e.zh: 别废话连篇了，告诉我到底发生了什么。

e.en: He tends to {blather} on whenever he's nervous.
e.zh: 他一紧张就会喋喋不休。

blaxploitation.t: n. 黑人剥削电影类型

e.en: The 70s {blaxploitation} films inspired a whole generation of directors.
e.zh: 七十年代的黑人剥削电影启发了整整一代导演。

e.en: Tarantino's movie pays homage to classic {blaxploitation} style.
e.zh: 塔伦蒂诺的电影致敬了经典的黑人剥削片风格。

blaze.t:
n. 烈火
v. 燃烧；闪耀

e.en: Firefighters battled the {blaze} for over six hours.
e.zh: 消防员奋战了六个多小时扑灭这场大火。

e.en: Maple leaves {blaze} red and gold every October.
e.zh: 每年十月，枫叶都会燃成一片红黄。

e.en: A bonfire {blazed} on the beach long after midnight.
e.zh: 沙滩上的篝火一直烧到午夜以后。

e.en: She {blazed} a trail for women in tech leadership.
e.zh: 她为科技领域的女性领导者开辟了道路。

blazer.t: n. 西装外套；运动上衣

e.en: He wore a navy {blazer} over a plain white tee.
e.zh: 他在素白T恤外搭了一件海军蓝西装外套。

e.en: Every student needs the school {blazer} for assembly.
e.zh: 每个学生集会时都得穿校服西装外套。

e.en: What in {blazes} are you doing on the roof?
e.zh: 你到底在屋顶上搞什么鬼？

e.en: Wildfire {blazes} have burned thousands of acres this summer.
e.zh: 今年夏天，野火烧毁了数千英亩土地。

e.en: We hiked under a {blazing} afternoon sun.
e.zh: 我们顶着烈日的下午徒步前行。

e.en: The new SSD delivers {blazing} read speeds.
e.zh: 这款新固态硬盘的读取速度快得惊人。

e.en: Rust compiles slowly but runs {blazingly} fast.
e.zh: Rust 编译很慢，但运行起来快得惊人。

e.en: The new search feature is {blazingly} quick on mobile.
e.zh: 新的搜索功能在手机上快得飞起。

blazon.t:
n. 纹章
v. 公开宣扬

e.en: The knight's shield was {blazon}ed with a golden lion.
e.zh: 骑士的盾牌上绘有一只金狮纹章。

e.en: The newspaper {blazon}ed the scandal across its front page.
e.zh: 报纸把这桩丑闻醒目地刊登在头版。

bleach.t:
v. 漂白
n. 漂白剂

e.en: Add a cup of {bleach} to whiten the towels.
e.zh: 加一杯漂白剂可以让毛巾变白。

e.en: The summer sun will {bleach} your hair noticeably.
e.zh: 夏日的阳光会明显地让你的头发褪色。

e.en: She wore a {bleached} denim jacket to the concert.
e.zh: 她穿着一件漂白牛仔外套去看演唱会。

e.en: Climate change has {bleached} large sections of the reef.
e.zh: 气候变化让大片珊瑚礁发生了白化。

e.en: He found an empty {bleacher} seat near the dugout.
e.zh: 他在球员席附近找到一个空的看台座位。

e.en: The factory {bleacher} processes thousands of shirts each day.
e.zh: 工厂的漂白工每天处理成千上万件衬衫。

e.en: Fans packed the {bleachers} for the championship game.
e.zh: 球迷们把看台挤得水泄不通来看冠军赛。

e.en: We sat on wooden {bleachers} watching the high school match.
e.zh: 我们坐在木制看台上观看高中比赛。

bleaching.t:
n. 漂白
adj. 漂白用的

e.en: Coral {bleaching} is devastating ecosystems across the Pacific.
e.zh: 珊瑚白化正在摧毁整个太平洋的生态系统。

e.en: She is {bleaching} the bathroom tiles this morning.
e.zh: 她今早正在用漂白剂清洗浴室瓷砖。

e.en: The job market looks {bleak} for new graduates.
e.zh: 对应届毕业生来说,就业市场前景黯淡。

e.en: We hiked across the {bleak} winter moorland for hours.
e.zh: 我们在荒凉的冬日荒原上徒步走了好几个小时。

e.en: He stared {bleakly} out the window at the rain.
e.zh: 他神情黯然地望着窗外的雨。

e.en: The economist spoke {bleakly} about next year's outlook.
e.zh: 经济学家对明年的前景发表了悲观的看法。

e.en: The film captures the {bleakness} of post-war Berlin.
e.zh: 这部电影捕捉到了战后柏林的萧瑟。

e.en: A sudden warmth broke the {bleakness} of the morning.
e.zh: 一阵突来的暖意打破了清晨的阴沉。

e.en: He blinked {blearily} at the alarm clock at six.
e.zh: 六点钟他睡眼惺忪地望着闹钟。

e.en: She stared {blearily} at her laptop after pulling an all-nighter.
e.zh: 熬了一整夜后,她迷迷糊糊地盯着笔记本电脑。

bleary.t: adj. (眼睛) 模糊的；朦胧的

e.en: His {bleary} eyes told me he hadn't slept.
e.zh: 他朦胧的双眼告诉我他没睡。

e.en: I drove home {bleary} after the long flight.
e.zh: 长途飞行后,我睡眼惺忪地开车回家。

e.en: The lambs {bleat} loudly whenever the gate opens.
e.zh: 每当大门打开,羊羔就会大声咩叫。

e.en: Stop {bleat}ing about the rules and just play.
e.zh: 别再抱怨规则了,好好打就是了。

bleating.t:
n. 咩咩声
v. 咩叫

e.en: The {bleating} of sheep echoed across the valley.
e.zh: 羊的咩咩叫声在山谷中回荡。

e.en: He kept {bleating} about how unfair the test was.
e.zh: 他一直在抱怨这次考试有多不公平。

e.en: The cut on my finger {bled} for ten minutes.
e.zh: 我手指上的伤口流了十分钟血。

e.en: Red dye {bled} into the white shirts in the wash.
e.zh: 洗衣时红色染料渗到了白衬衫上。

e.en: Press the wound firmly so it stops {bleed}ing.
e.zh: 用力按住伤口,让它止血。

e.en: Streaming services slowly {bleed} cash from cable subscriptions.
e.zh: 流媒体服务正慢慢蚕食有线电视的订阅收入。

e.en: That last play was a real {bleeder} for the team.
e.zh: 上一次进攻对球队来说真是惨痛的一击。

e.en: The mechanic loosened the brake {bleeder} valve to release air.
e.zh: 修理工拧松刹车放气阀以排出空气。

bleeding.t:
n. 出血
adj. 流血的

e.en: Apply pressure to stop the {bleeding} immediately.
e.zh: 立刻按压伤口以止血。

e.en: My startup is {bleeding} money on cloud costs.
e.zh: 我的创业公司在云服务上烧钱烧得厉害。

bleeds.t: v. 流血（第三人称单数）

e.en: The designer always {bleeds} images to the page edge.
e.zh: 设计师总是把图片做出血到页面边缘。

e.en: His nose {bleeds} whenever the air gets too dry.
e.zh: 空气一干燥他就会流鼻血。

bleep.t:
n. 哔的一声
v. 用哔声消音

e.en: The microwave gave a sharp {bleep} when finished.
e.zh: 微波炉完成时发出一声尖锐的哔声。

e.en: Editors {bleep} swear words out of live broadcasts.
e.zh: 编辑会把直播中的脏话用哔声盖掉。

e.en: The doctor's {bleeper} went off during dinner again.
e.zh: 医生的传呼机晚饭时又响了。

e.en: Hospitals still rely on the humble {bleeper} for urgent calls.
e.zh: 医院在紧急呼叫时仍依赖那种朴素的传呼机。

e.en: The {bleeping} smoke alarm woke the whole house.
e.zh: 那哔哔作响的烟雾报警器吵醒了全家人。

e.en: Turn off that {bleeping} oven timer, please.
e.zh: 请把那个一直哔哔响的烤箱定时器关掉。

blemish.t:
n. 瑕疵；污点
v. 玷污

e.en: This concealer hides any {blemish} on your skin.
e.zh: 这款遮瑕膏可以遮盖皮肤上的任何瑕疵。

e.en: The scandal was a serious {blemish} on his record.
e.zh: 这桩丑闻是他履历上的一大污点。

e.en: The grocer sold {blemished} apples at half price.
e.zh: 杂货商以半价出售有瑕疵的苹果。

e.en: His resignation {blemished} an otherwise distinguished career.
e.zh: 他的辞职给原本辉煌的职业生涯抹上了污点。

e.en: She didn't {blench} when she heard the diagnosis.
e.zh: 听到诊断结果时她没有退缩。

e.en: Even veteran soldiers {blench}ed at the gruesome scene.
e.zh: 就连老兵看到这血腥场面也不寒而栗。

blend.t:
v. 混合
n. 混合物

e.en: {Blend} the spinach and banana for thirty seconds.
e.zh: 把菠菜和香蕉搅打三十秒。

e.en: This coffee is a {blend} of Brazilian and Ethiopian beans.
e.zh: 这款咖啡是巴西豆和埃塞俄比亚豆的混合。

e.en: She works at a {blended} family counseling center.
e.zh: 她在一家重组家庭咨询中心工作。

e.en: I {blended} the strawberries into the yogurt this morning.
e.zh: 我今早把草莓搅进了酸奶里。

e.en: My new {blender} crushes ice in seconds.
e.zh: 我的新搅拌机几秒钟就能粉碎冰块。

e.en: Pour the soup into the {blender} carefully while it's hot.
e.zh: 汤还热时小心地倒入搅拌机里。

e.en: She is {blending} smoothies for the whole team.
e.zh: 她正在给整个团队打果昔。

e.en: His clothes are perfect for {blending} into the crowd.
e.zh: 他的衣着非常适合融入人群。

blends.t: v. 混合（第三人称单数）

e.en: This app {blends} fitness tracking with social media.
e.zh: 这款应用把健身追踪和社交媒体融合在一起。

e.en: The store sells various tea {blends} from around the world.
e.zh: 这家店出售来自世界各地的各种调配茶。

blenheim.t: n. 布莱尼姆（地名/犬种）

e.en: We toured {Blenheim} Palace on a sunny afternoon.
e.zh: 我们在一个阳光明媚的下午参观了布伦海姆宫。

e.en: The {Blenheim} spaniel curled up beside the fireplace.
e.zh: 那只布伦海姆猎犬蜷缩在壁炉旁。

e.en: Doctors prescribed {bleomycin} as part of her chemotherapy.
e.zh: 医生在她的化疗中开了博来霉素。

e.en: {Bleomycin} can cause lung side effects in some patients.
e.zh: 博来霉素在某些患者身上可能引起肺部副作用。

e.en: My optometrist diagnosed me with chronic {blepharitis}.
e.zh: 我的验光师诊断我患有慢性睑缘炎。

e.en: Warm compresses help relieve the symptoms of {blepharitis}.
e.zh: 热敷有助于缓解睑缘炎的症状。

e.en: May the new year {bless} you with good health.
e.zh: 愿新年带给你健康。

e.en: The priest will {bless} the couple at the ceremony.
e.zh: 神父将在仪式上为这对新人祝福。

blithe.t: adj. 无忧无虑的；漫不经心的

e.en: She gave a {blithe} wave and walked off into the crowd.
e.zh: 她随意挥了挥手,便走入了人群中。

e.en: His {blithe} disregard for the rules annoyed his colleagues.
e.zh: 他对规则毫不在意的态度让同事们很恼火。

blithely.t: adv. 轻率地；无忧无虑地

e.en: He {blithely} ignored the deadline and went on vacation.
e.zh: 他满不在乎地无视截止日期,跑去度假了。

e.en: She {blithely} agreed without reading the contract.
e.zh: 她没看合同就轻率地同意了。

blithering.t: adj. 胡言乱语的；十足的（蠢）

e.en: Stop being a {blithering} idiot and read the instructions.
e.zh: 别再像个糊涂蛋一样,认真读读说明书吧。

e.en: He stood there {blithering} nonsense at the camera.
e.zh: 他站在那里对着镜头胡言乱语。

blitz.t:
n. 闪电战；密集攻势
v. 猛烈袭击

e.en: The startup launched a marketing {blitz} before the product release.
e.zh: 这家初创公司在产品发布前发起了一波营销闪电战。

e.en: The defense sent a {blitz} on third down to pressure the quarterback.
e.zh: 防守方在第三档发起突袭以向四分卫施压。

e.en: Fans use {blitze} loosely to mean any quick attack play.
e.zh: 球迷常常宽泛地用这个词来指任何快攻战术。

e.en: The coach diagrammed several {blitze} variations on the whiteboard.
e.zh: 教练在白板上画出了几种突袭战术的变化。

blitzed.t: adj. 被闪电式袭击的；（俚）烂醉的

e.en: They {blitzed} social media with ads during the Super Bowl.
e.zh: 他们在超级碗期间用广告轰炸了社交媒体。

e.en: The defense {blitzed} the quarterback on nearly every play.
e.zh: 防守方几乎每一次进攻都对四分卫发起突袭。

e.en: The team is {blitzing} through their playoff opponents this year.
e.zh: 今年这支球队在季后赛中势如破竹地击败对手。

e.en: She's {blitzing} through her inbox before the meeting.
e.zh: 她正在开会前飞快地处理收件箱里的邮件。

e.en: The film depicts the German {blitzkrieg} across Europe in 1940.
e.zh: 这部电影描绘了1940年德军横扫欧洲的闪电战。

e.en: Their advertising {blitzkrieg} dominated headlines for weeks.
e.zh: 他们的广告闪电战连续几周占据了各大头条。

e.en: The defense ran several {blitzs} to confuse the offense.
e.zh: 防守方使用了多次突袭以迷惑进攻方。

e.en: Modern playbooks include dozens of pre-designed {blitzs}.
e.zh: 现代战术手册中包含数十种预设的突袭战术。

e.en: A massive {blizzard} shut down airports across the Northeast.
e.zh: 一场大暴风雪让东北部各机场全面关闭。

e.en: We were snowed in for three days during the {blizzard}.
e.zh: 暴风雪期间,我们被困在家里整整三天。

bloat.t:
v. 使膨胀；臃肿
n. 臃肿；软件冗余

e.en: Software {bloat} is making the app slow and unresponsive.
e.zh: 软件臃肿让这款应用又慢又卡。

e.en: Eating too much salt can cause uncomfortable {bloat}.
e.zh: 摄入过多盐分会引起难受的腹胀。

e.en: The company's {bloated} bureaucracy slows every decision.
e.zh: 公司臃肿的官僚机构让每个决定都拖沓不前。

e.en: I felt {bloated} after eating that huge buffet lunch.
e.zh: 吃完那顿丰盛的自助午餐后,我感到肚子胀胀的。

e.en: Drinking peppermint tea can help reduce {bloating}.
e.zh: 喝薄荷茶有助于缓解腹胀。

e.en: The framework keeps adding features, {bloating} the install size.
e.zh: 这个框架不断添加功能,让安装包越来越臃肿。

blob.t: n. 一团；斑点；二进制大对象 (BLOB)

e.en: A small {blob} of ketchup landed on his white shirt.
e.zh: 一小坨番茄酱落在了他的白衬衫上。

e.en: The image looked like a fuzzy gray {blob} on the screen.
e.zh: 那张图片在屏幕上看起来像一团模糊的灰色斑块。

blobby.t: adj. 一团团的；圆滚滚的

e.en: The 3D model came out {blobby} instead of sharp and angular.
e.zh: 3D模型做出来软塌塌的,而不是棱角分明。

e.en: She prefers clean shapes over {blobby} cartoon designs.
e.zh: 她喜欢简洁的造型,不喜欢圆滚滚的卡通设计。

bloc.t: n. 集团（政治、经济联盟）

e.en: The European trading {bloc} agreed to new climate rules.
e.zh: 欧洲贸易集团就新的气候规则达成了一致。

e.en: A {bloc} of senators blocked the proposed legislation.
e.zh: 一批参议员联合阻止了拟议的立法。

block.t:
v. 阻止；屏蔽
n. 街区；块

e.en: Please don't {block} the driveway with your car.
e.zh: 请不要把车停在车道上挡住出入口。

e.en: The coffee shop is just two streets down the {block}.
e.zh: 那家咖啡店就在前面两个路口的街区。

e.en: Naval ships set up a {blockade} around the disputed island.
e.zh: 海军舰艇在争议岛屿周围设置了封锁。

e.en: Protesters formed a {blockade} at the factory's main gate.
e.zh: 抗议者在工厂大门口组成了一道封锁线。

e.en: A {blockage} in the pipe caused water to back up.
e.zh: 管道里的堵塞导致水倒流。

e.en: Doctors found a serious {blockage} in his artery.
e.zh: 医生在他的动脉里发现了严重的堵塞。

blockbuster.t: n. 轰动之作；卖座大片

e.en: The studio released its latest summer {blockbuster} last weekend.
e.zh: 这家电影公司上周末发布了最新的暑期大片。

e.en: Her debut novel became an unexpected {blockbuster}.
e.zh: 她的处女作小说意外成了畅销书。

e.en: Marvel has produced several {blockbusters} in the last decade.
e.zh: 漫威在过去十年里推出了好几部大片。

e.en: Streaming platforms now compete for global {blockbusters}.
e.zh: 流媒体平台如今争抢着全球大片。

e.en: The website is {blocked} in several countries.
e.zh: 该网站在好几个国家被屏蔽了。

e.en: A fallen tree {blocked} the road for hours.
e.zh: 一棵倒下的树堵住了道路好几个小时。

blocker.t: n. 阻止者；拦截程序（如广告拦截）

e.en: I installed an ad {blocker} to clean up my browser.
e.zh: 我装了一个广告拦截器来清理浏览器。

e.en: Lack of funding is the main {blocker} for this project.
e.zh: 资金不足是这个项目的主要阻碍。

e.en: Don't be such a {blockhead} and read the instructions.
e.zh: 别这么笨,看一下说明书。

e.en: He called himself a {blockhead} for forgetting the password.
e.zh: 他骂自己是个笨蛋,竟然忘了密码。

e.en: The old {blockhouse} once guarded the harbor entrance.
e.zh: 那座老碉堡曾经守卫着港口入口。

e.en: Soldiers retreated to the wooden {blockhouse} for safety.
e.zh: 士兵们退到木制碉堡里寻求掩护。

e.en: Stop {blocking} the doorway, people need to pass.
e.zh: 别挡着门口,大家要过。

e.en: The firewall is {blocking} our access to the server.
e.zh: 防火墙正在阻止我们访问服务器。

blocks.t:
n. 块；街区（复数）
v. 阻止

e.en: The cafe is just two {blocks} from my apartment.
e.zh: 那家咖啡馆离我公寓只有两个街区。

e.en: Children love stacking colorful {blocks} into towers.
e.zh: 孩子们喜欢把彩色积木堆成塔。

blockwork.t: n. 砌块建筑；分区作业

e.en: The exterior {blockwork} needs repointing before winter.
e.zh: 外墙的砌块结构入冬前需要重新勾缝。

e.en: Solid {blockwork} gives the building excellent sound insulation.
e.zh: 坚实的砌块墙体让这栋楼隔音效果很好。

blocky.t: adj. 方块状的；粗糙像素感的

e.en: The game has a charming {blocky} pixel art style.
e.zh: 这款游戏有着迷人的方块像素风格。

e.en: She prefers {blocky} sneakers over sleek running shoes.
e.zh: 她更喜欢方头运动鞋而不是流线型跑鞋。

bloemfontein.t: n. 布隆方丹（南非城市）

e.en: {Bloemfontein} is the judicial capital of South Africa.
e.zh: 布隆方丹是南非的司法首都。

e.en: We flew to {Bloemfontein} for a rugby tournament.
e.zh: 我们飞去布隆方丹参加一场橄榄球比赛。

blog.t:
n. 博客
v. 写博客

e.en: She updates her travel {blog} every Sunday night.
e.zh: 她每个周日晚上都更新她的旅行博客。

e.en: I'll {blog} about my new recipe later this week.
e.zh: 我这周晚些时候会写博客介绍我的新食谱。

e.en: The food {blogger} has over a million followers online.
e.zh: 这位美食博主在网上有超过一百万粉丝。

e.en: She quit her job to become a full-time {blogger}.
e.zh: 她辞了工作,成了一名全职博主。

e.en: Fashion {bloggers} were invited to the runway show.
e.zh: 时尚博主们都被邀请去看时装秀。

e.en: Tech {bloggers} quickly reviewed the new phone.
e.zh: 科技博主们很快就评测了这款新手机。

e.en: She started {blogging} about her recovery journey.
e.zh: 她开始写博客记录自己的康复历程。

e.en: {Blogging} consistently helped him build a loyal audience.
e.zh: 持续写博客帮他积累了一批忠实读者。

e.en: News of the merger spread fast across the {blogosphere}.
e.zh: 合并的消息在博客圈里迅速传开了。

e.en: The {blogosphere} reacted strongly to the controversial speech.
e.zh: 博客圈对这场有争议的演讲反应强烈。

e.en: Many product reviews now come from independent {blogs}.
e.zh: 如今许多产品测评都来自独立博客。

e.en: He {blogs} about minimalist living every weekend.
e.zh: 他每个周末都写博客分享极简生活。

e.en: The chateau at {Blois} attracts thousands of tourists yearly.
e.zh: 布卢瓦的城堡每年吸引成千上万的游客。

e.en: We took a train from Paris to {Blois}.
e.zh: 我们从巴黎坐火车去布卢瓦。

bloke.t: n. 家伙；男子（英式口语）

e.en: He's a friendly {bloke} who works at the pub.
e.zh: 他是个在酒吧工作的友善家伙。

e.en: Some {bloke} on the train helped me with my luggage.
e.zh: 火车上有个家伙帮我拿行李。

blond.t:
adj. 金发的
n. 金发男子

e.en: Her son has curly {blond} hair just like hers.
e.zh: 她儿子和她一样有一头卷曲的金发。

e.en: The actor dyed his hair {blond} for the role.
e.zh: 那位演员为这个角色把头发染成了金色。

blonde.t:
n. 金发女郎
adj. 金发的

e.en: The {blonde} woman in the photo is my sister.
e.zh: 照片里那个金发女子是我姐姐。

e.en: She went {blonde} for the summer and loved the change.
e.zh: 她夏天染了金发,很喜欢这个改变。

blondish.t: adj. 偏金色的；浅金发的

e.en: His hair is more {blondish} brown than truly fair.
e.zh: 他的头发偏金棕色,不算真正的金色。

e.en: She has {blondish} highlights woven through her hair.
e.zh: 她的头发里挑染了一些浅金色。

blondness.t: n. 金发特质；浅色发质

e.en: Her natural {blondness} faded slightly as she aged.
e.zh: 随着年龄增长,她天生的金发颜色稍微变淡了。

e.en: The shampoo is designed to preserve {blondness} and shine.
e.zh: 这款洗发水专门用来保持金发的色泽和光亮。

e.en: The nurse drew {blood} for the routine test.
e.zh: 护士抽血做常规检查。

e.en: Donating {blood} can save several lives at once.
e.zh: 捐血能一次性挽救好几条生命。

bloodbath.t: n. 大屠杀；惨烈损失（如股市暴跌）

e.en: The stock market suffered a {bloodbath} on Monday morning.
e.zh: 周一上午股市遭遇了一场惨烈的暴跌。

e.en: The final battle scene was an absolute {bloodbath}.
e.zh: 最后的战斗场面简直是一场大屠杀。

e.en: A {bloodcurdling} scream came from the haunted house.
e.zh: 鬼屋里传出一声令人毛骨悚然的尖叫。

e.en: She told us a {bloodcurdling} ghost story by the fire.
e.zh: 她在炉火旁给我们讲了一个吓死人的鬼故事。

e.en: He owns several pure-{blooded} Arabian horses.
e.zh: 他养了好几匹纯种阿拉伯马。

e.en: Snakes and lizards are cold-{blooded} animals.
e.zh: 蛇和蜥蜴是冷血动物。

e.en: The police {bloodhound} tracked the missing child for miles.
e.zh: 警方的寻血猎犬循着气味追踪失踪儿童好几英里。

e.en: That reporter is a real {bloodhound} for political scandals.
e.zh: 那个记者追政治丑闻像猎犬一样执着。

e.en: The boxer's nose was {bloodied} after the third round.
e.zh: 第三回合后,拳击手的鼻子被打得流血了。

e.en: She found a {bloodied} bandage on the bathroom floor.
e.zh: 她在浴室地上发现了一条沾血的绷带。

e.en: The rebellion was {bloodily} suppressed within a week.
e.zh: 那场叛乱在一周内被血腥镇压。

e.en: The two armies clashed {bloodily} along the border.
e.zh: 两支军队在边境血腥交火。

e.en: The coup was surprisingly {bloodless} and quick.
e.zh: 那场政变出人意料地不流血,而且迅速结束。

e.en: His pale, {bloodless} face frightened everyone in the room.
e.zh: 他苍白无血色的脸吓坏了房间里的每个人。

bloodletting.t: n. 放血（疗法）；流血冲突

e.en: Medieval doctors believed {bloodletting} could cure many diseases.
e.zh: 中世纪的医生相信放血能治许多疾病。

e.en: The corporate restructuring led to massive {bloodletting} in management.
e.zh: 公司重组导致管理层遭到大规模裁员。

e.en: This horse comes from a champion racing {bloodline}.
e.zh: 这匹马出自冠军赛马的血统。

e.en: The royal {bloodline} has been traced back centuries.
e.zh: 这条皇室血脉可以追溯到数百年前。

e.en: The crowd's {bloodlust} grew louder during the cage fight.
e.zh: 笼斗赛中观众的嗜血狂热越来越高涨。

e.en: His {bloodlust} for revenge clouded all rational thought.
e.zh: 他对复仇的渴望蒙蔽了所有理智的思考。

e.en: {Bloodroot} blooms briefly in early spring forests.
e.zh: 血根草在早春的森林里短暂开花。

e.en: Native Americans used {bloodroot} for natural red dye.
e.zh: 美洲原住民用血根草制作天然红色染料。

e.en: Diplomats worked tirelessly to prevent further {bloodshed}.
e.zh: 外交官们不懈努力,以防止更多流血事件发生。

e.en: The peaceful protest ended without any {bloodshed}.
e.zh: 这场和平抗议没有发生任何流血事件。

bloodshot.t: adj. (眼睛) 充血的、布满血丝的

e.en: His {bloodshot} eyes betrayed how little he had slept.
e.zh: 他布满血丝的眼睛暴露了他几乎没怎么睡。

e.en: After hours of staring at screens, my eyes turned {bloodshot}.
e.zh: 盯了几个小时屏幕后,我的眼睛布满了血丝。

e.en: Investigators found a {bloodstain} near the kitchen window.
e.zh: 调查人员在厨房窗户附近发现了一处血迹。

e.en: The old carpet still had a faint {bloodstain}.
e.zh: 那块旧地毯上还有一处淡淡的血迹。

e.en: Police recovered a {bloodstained} shirt from the suspect's car.
e.zh: 警方从嫌疑人车里找到一件沾血的衬衫。

e.en: The novel describes a {bloodstained} chapter of colonial history.
e.zh: 这部小说描写了殖民史上沾满鲜血的一段。

e.en: The farm sells racing {bloodstock} to international buyers.
e.zh: 这家农场向国际买家出售赛马良种。

e.en: Investing in {bloodstock} requires deep knowledge of pedigrees.
e.zh: 投资良种马需要对血统有深入了解。

e.en: The drug enters the {bloodstream} within minutes.
e.zh: 药物在几分钟内就进入血液循环。

e.en: Caffeine reaches the {bloodstream} faster on an empty stomach.
e.zh: 空腹时咖啡因更快进入血液循环。

e.en: Vaccines train antibodies in our {bloodstreams} to fight viruses.
e.zh: 疫苗训练我们血液中的抗体去对抗病毒。

e.en: Microplastics have been detected in human {bloodstreams}.
e.zh: 人类的血液中已经检测到微塑料。

e.en: The mosquito is the most annoying {bloodsucker} of summer.
e.zh: 蚊子是夏天最让人讨厌的吸血鬼。

e.en: He called the loan shark a heartless {bloodsucker}.
e.zh: 他骂那个放高利贷的是个冷血吸血鬼。

e.en: The villain in the movie was utterly {bloodthirsty}.
e.zh: 电影里的反派极其嗜血残暴。

e.en: A {bloodthirsty} crowd cheered every brutal hit.
e.zh: 嗜血的人群为每一记残忍的重击欢呼。

e.en: Anglers often use {bloodworm} as bait for trout.
e.zh: 钓鱼人经常用血虫作鱼饵钓鳟鱼。

e.en: My pet fish goes crazy for frozen {bloodworm}.
e.zh: 我的宠物鱼对冷冻血虫疯狂着迷。

bloody.t: adj. 血腥的；该死的（英式口语）

e.en: He came home with a {bloody} nose after the fight.
e.zh: 他打完架回家时鼻子还在流血。

e.en: That was a {bloody} brilliant performance tonight.
e.zh: 今晚的演出真是太他妈精彩了。

bloom.t:
v. 开花；绽放
n. 花朵；青春焕发

e.en: The cherry trees {bloom} for only two weeks each spring.
e.zh: 樱花每年春天只盛开两周左右。

e.en: A toxic algae {bloom} has closed several beaches.
e.zh: 一场有毒藻华导致好几个海滩关闭。

bloomed.t: v. 开花了（bloom 的过去式）

e.en: The roses {bloomed} beautifully after the warm rain.
e.zh: 暖雨过后,玫瑰开得非常美。

e.en: Her confidence {bloomed} once she joined the new team.
e.zh: 加入新团队后,她的自信心绽放了。

e.en: He was a late {bloomer} who became a successful chef.
e.zh: 他是大器晚成的人,后来成了一位成功的厨师。

e.en: This rose variety is a reliable summer {bloomer}.
e.zh: 这个玫瑰品种是夏季可靠的开花植物。

bloomers.t: n. 女式灯笼裤；宽松内裤

e.en: Grandma still calls her old underwear {bloomers}.
e.zh: 奶奶还把她那条旧内裤叫做灯笼裤。

e.en: The vintage shop sold lace {bloomers} from the 1920s.
e.zh: 那家复古店在卖1920年代的蕾丝灯笼裤。

bloomfield.t: n. 布卢姆菲尔德（地名/姓氏）

e.en: She grew up in {Bloomfield}, a quiet New Jersey town.
e.zh: 她在新泽西安静的布卢姆菲尔德镇长大。

e.en: The {Bloomfield} library hosts free coding classes weekly.
e.zh: 布卢姆菲尔德图书馆每周举办免费编程课。

e.en: The cherry trees are {blooming} all over campus.
e.zh: 校园里的樱花树正在盛开。

e.en: Her career is finally {blooming} after years of effort.
e.zh: 经过多年努力,她的事业终于蒸蒸日上。

blooms.t:
n. 花朵（复数）
v. 开花（第三人称单数）

e.en: The garden {blooms} brightly every spring morning.
e.zh: 花园每个春天的清晨都绽放得绚丽多彩。

e.en: She arranged white {blooms} in a crystal vase.
e.zh: 她把白色花朵插进水晶花瓶里。

bloomsbury.t: n. 布卢姆斯伯里（伦敦地区）

e.en: Virginia Woolf lived in London's {Bloomsbury} district.
e.zh: 弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫住在伦敦的布鲁姆斯伯里区。

e.en: {Bloomsbury} Publishing released the new fantasy novel today.
e.zh: 布鲁姆斯伯里出版社今天发布了那本新奇幻小说。

bloop.t:
n. 噗一声
v. (视频) 出糗

e.en: The chat app made a soft {bloop} when messages arrived.
e.zh: 聊天软件收到消息时发出轻柔的提示音。

e.en: He hit a lucky {bloop} single over the shortstop.
e.zh: 他幸运地把球轻巧地打过游击手头顶上垒。

blooper.t: n. 搞笑失误；NG 花絮

e.en: The film's {blooper} reel had everyone laughing for hours.
e.zh: 那部电影的花絮集让大家笑了好几个小时。

e.en: His on-air {blooper} went viral on social media overnight.
e.zh: 他直播中的口误一夜之间在社交媒体上爆红。

bloor.t: n. Bloor（多伦多街道名/姓氏）

e.en: We took the subway down {Bloor} Street to Yorkville.
e.zh: 我们沿着布卢尔街坐地铁去约克维尔。

e.en: The bookstore on {Bloor} stays open until midnight.
e.zh: 布卢尔街那家书店营业到午夜。

blossom.t:
n. (果树) 花
v. 开花；蓬勃发展

e.en: Cherry {blossom} season draws huge crowds to the park.
e.zh: 樱花季吸引了大批游客来到公园。

e.en: Their friendship began to {blossom} during college.
e.zh: 他们的友谊在大学时期开始蓬勃发展。

blossoming.t: adj. 盛开的；蓬勃发展的

e.en: The plum trees are {blossoming} earlier than usual this year.
e.zh: 今年的李树比往常开得更早。

e.en: She has a {blossoming} career as a UX designer.
e.zh: 她作为用户体验设计师的事业正蒸蒸日上。

blossoms.t:
n. 花朵（复数）
v. 开花（第三人称单数）

e.en: Pink {blossoms} covered the path near the old temple.
e.zh: 粉色花朵铺满了古寺旁的小路。

e.en: Their startup {blossoms} into a major tech company.
e.zh: 他们的初创公司发展成了一家大型科技公司。

blot.t:
n. 污渍；污点
v. 吸干；弄脏

e.en: A coffee {blot} ruined the front of her notebook.
e.zh: 一滴咖啡渍弄脏了她笔记本的封面。

e.en: Use a tissue to {blot} the spilled ink quickly.
e.zh: 用纸巾快速吸掉洒出来的墨水。

blotch.t: n. (皮肤或表面) 斑块、污斑

e.en: A red {blotch} appeared on his arm after the bee sting.
e.zh: 被蜜蜂蜇后,他的手臂上出现了一块红斑。

e.en: There's a strange ink {blotch} on the printed page.
e.zh: 打印的那页纸上有一块奇怪的墨迹。

e.en: His face was {blotched} red from running in the heat.
e.zh: 他在酷热中跑步,脸涨得红一块红一块的。

e.en: The old wallpaper looked {blotched} with damp stains.
e.zh: 旧墙纸被潮湿的污渍弄得斑斑点点。

e.en: Her skin gets {blotchy} whenever she drinks red wine.
e.zh: 她一喝红酒皮肤就会起红斑。

e.en: The printer left the photo looking {blotchy} and faded.
e.zh: 打印机把照片印得斑驳褪色。

e.en: The detective checked the police {blotter} for last night's incidents.
e.zh: 侦探查看了警局值班记录里昨晚的案件。

e.en: An old leather {blotter} sat on the antique desk.
e.zh: 古董桌上摆着一块旧皮革吸墨垫。

e.en: She was {blotting} her tears with a paper napkin.
e.zh: 她正用纸巾轻轻擦拭眼泪。

e.en: Try {blotting} the stain instead of rubbing it.
e.zh: 试着轻按吸干污渍,而不是用力擦。

e.en: She wore a silk {blouse} to the job interview.
e.zh: 她穿着一件丝绸衬衫去面试。

e.en: This linen {blouse} is perfect for hot summer days.
e.zh: 这件亚麻女衬衫非常适合炎热的夏天。

e.en: He zipped up his leather {blouson} before riding off.
e.zh: 他拉上皮质短夹克的拉链,骑车离开了。

e.en: The model wore a satin {blouson} on the runway.
e.zh: 模特在T台上穿着一件缎面短款夹克。

blow.t:
v. 吹；刮风；搞砸
n. 一击；打击

e.en: Don't forget to {blow} out the candles on your cake.
e.zh: 别忘了吹灭蛋糕上的蜡烛。

e.en: Losing the championship was a huge {blow} to the team.
e.zh: 输掉冠军赛对球队是一次沉重打击。

e.en: The new policy received serious {blowback} from local residents.
e.zh: 新政策遭到了当地居民的强烈反弹。

e.en: Expect some {blowback} when you raise subscription prices.
e.zh: 提高订阅价格时,要做好遭受抵制的准备。

blowdown.t: n. (树木) 被风吹倒；排污吹除

e.en: The storm caused massive {blowdown} across the forest trail.
e.zh: 风暴在林间小道上吹倒了大量树木。

e.en: Engineers scheduled a boiler {blowdown} for Tuesday morning.
e.zh: 工程师把锅炉排污安排在周二上午。

e.en: Use the leaf {blower} to clear the driveway quickly.
e.zh: 用吹叶机快速把车道清理干净。

e.en: The hair {blower} in this hotel barely works.
e.zh: 这家酒店的吹风机几乎没法用。

e.en: The chef carefully prepared {blowfish} for the brave diners.
e.zh: 厨师小心地为勇敢的食客烹制河豚。

e.en: A spotted {blowfish} puffed up when divers approached.
e.zh: 潜水员靠近时,一条带斑点的河豚鼓了起来。

e.en: The hunter aimed his {blowgun} at the small bird.
e.zh: 猎人用吹箭瞄准了那只小鸟。

e.en: Indigenous tribes still craft the traditional {blowgun} by hand.
e.zh: 原住民部落仍然手工制作传统的吹箭筒。

e.en: Everyone avoided the {blowhard} bragging at the office party.
e.zh: 大家都避开了那个在公司聚会上吹牛的家伙。

e.en: He's a total {blowhard} who never delivers on promises.
e.zh: 他完全是个只会吹牛、从不兑现承诺的人。

blowhole.t: n. 鲸的喷水孔；通气孔

e.en: The whale's {blowhole} sprayed mist high into the air.
e.zh: 鲸鱼的喷气孔向空中喷出高高的水雾。

e.en: Tourists watched waves crash through the coastal {blowhole}.
e.zh: 游客们看着海浪从海岸喷潮孔涌出。

blowing.t: v. 吹；刮（blow 的现在分词）

e.en: The wind was {blowing} hard along the coast last night.
e.zh: 昨晚海岸边风刮得很猛。

e.en: She kept {blowing} bubbles to entertain the toddler.
e.zh: 她不停地吹泡泡逗那个小孩开心。

e.en: The film's {blowjob} scene was edited out for television.
e.zh: 电影中的口交镜头在电视播出时被剪掉了。

e.en: Sex educators discussed safer {blowjob} practices in the workshop.
e.zh: 性教育者在工作坊讨论了更安全的口交方式。

blessed.t:
adj. 幸福的；神圣的
v. 保佑（bless 过去式）

e.en: I feel {blessed} to have such supportive friends.
e.zh: 有这样支持我的朋友,我觉得很幸运。

e.en: The grandmother {blessed} the children before bed.
e.zh: 奶奶在孩子们睡前为他们祈福。

blessedly.t: adv. 幸运地；令人欣慰地

e.en: The meeting was {blessedly} short this Monday morning.
e.zh: 这周一早上的会议幸运地很短。

e.en: Traffic was {blessedly} light on the way to the airport.
e.zh: 去机场的路上车流幸运地很稀疏。

e.en: She spoke of the quiet {blessedness} of motherhood.
e.zh: 她谈到了为人母那份静谧的幸福。

e.en: There's a real {blessedness} in unhurried mornings at home.
e.zh: 在家中悠闲的清晨有一种真切的幸福感。

blesses.t: v. 祝福；保佑（bless 第三人称单数）

e.en: Grandma always {blesses} the food before we eat.
e.zh: 奶奶总是在我们吃饭前为食物祈福。

e.en: Life {blesses} us in ways we don't always notice.
e.zh: 生活以我们未必察觉的方式恩待我们。

blessing.t:
n. 祝福；幸事
v. 祝福（进行时）

e.en: Having a flexible job is a real {blessing}.
e.zh: 有一份弹性的工作真是一种福气。

e.en: The startup launched with the {blessing} of its investors.
e.zh: 这家初创公司在投资人的支持下启动。

e.en: Count your {blessings} before complaining about minor things.
e.zh: 在为琐事抱怨之前,先想想自己的福气。

e.en: She listed her daily {blessings} in a small journal.
e.zh: 她在一本小日记本里记下每天值得感恩的事。

blest.t: adj. 蒙福的（blessed 旧式写法）

e.en: He felt truly {blest} after the surgery succeeded.
e.zh: 手术成功后他感到自己真是有福气。

e.en: The poet wrote of a land forever {blest} by peace.
e.zh: 诗人写下了一片永远蒙受和平眷顾的土地。

bletchley.t: n. 布莱切利（英国地名，二战密码破译地）

e.en: Codebreakers at {Bletchley} Park helped shorten World War Two.
e.zh: 布莱切利园的密码破译者帮助缩短了第二次世界大战。

e.en: We caught the train from London to {Bletchley} this morning.
e.zh: 今天早上我们从伦敦坐火车去了布莱切利。

bleu.t: adj. 蓝纹的（法语 blue，多用于奶酪）

e.en: I ordered chicken cordon {bleu} for dinner.
e.zh: 我点了蓝带鸡作为晚餐。

e.en: The salad came with crumbled {bleu} cheese on top.
e.zh: 沙拉上面撒着碎蓝纹奶酪。

blew.t: v. 吹；刮（blow 的过去式）

e.en: The wind {blew} my umbrella inside out yesterday.
e.zh: 昨天大风把我的伞吹翻了。

e.en: He {blew} his entire bonus on a new gaming PC.
e.zh: 他把整笔奖金都花在了一台新游戏电脑上。

blight.t:
n. 枯萎病；祸根
v. 使凋零；毁坏

e.en: Potato {blight} destroyed half the harvest this year.
e.zh: 马铃薯枯萎病毁了今年一半的收成。

e.en: Empty storefronts are a {blight} on the neighborhood.
e.zh: 空置的店面是这个社区的一处景观毒瘤。

blighted.t:
adj. 凋敝的；受损的
v. 毁坏（过去式）

e.en: The pandemic {blighted} small businesses across the city.
e.zh: 疫情重创了全市的小企业。

e.en: Farmers ploughed under the {blighted} tomato plants.
e.zh: 农民们把染病的番茄植株犁进了土里。

blighter.t: n. 讨厌鬼；家伙（英式俚语）

e.en: That little {blighter} ate my entire sandwich.
e.zh: 那个小坏蛋把我的三明治全吃光了。

e.en: The lucky {blighter} won the lottery twice.
e.zh: 那个走运的家伙居然中了两次彩票。

blighting.t: v. 使枯萎；毁坏（进行时）

e.en: Pollution is {blighting} the city's once-beautiful river.
e.zh: 污染正在毁掉这座城市曾经美丽的河流。

e.en: Constant interruptions were {blighting} her writing progress.
e.zh: 不断的打扰正在严重影响她的写作进度。

blights.t:
v. 毁坏（第三人称单数）
n. 枯萎病（复数）

e.en: Corruption {blights} the lives of ordinary citizens.
e.zh: 腐败毁掉了普通百姓的生活。

e.en: Several fungal {blights} threaten coffee farms in Colombia.
e.zh: 几种真菌枯萎病威胁着哥伦比亚的咖啡农场。

blighty.t: n. 英国；故乡（英军俚语）

e.en: The soldier dreamed of returning home to {Blighty}.
e.zh: 那位士兵梦想着回到老家英国。

e.en: After ten years abroad, he was finally back in {Blighty}.
e.zh: 在国外待了十年后,他终于回到了英国老家。

blimey.t: int. 我的天！（英式惊叹语）

e.en: {Blimey}, that pizza was bigger than my head!
e.zh: 我的天,这披萨比我的头还大!

e.en: {Blimey}, the rent in London has gotten ridiculous.
e.zh: 老天啊,伦敦的房租已经贵得离谱了。

e.en: A {blimp} hovered above the stadium during the championship game.
e.zh: 一艘飞艇在锦标赛期间盘旋在体育场上空。

e.en: The Goodyear {blimp} is a famous sight at sporting events.
e.zh: 固特异飞艇是体育赛事上的标志性景观。

blind.t:
adj. 失明的；盲目的
n. 百叶窗

e.en: He was born {blind} but became a celebrated pianist.
e.zh: 他生来失明,却成为了著名的钢琴家。

e.en: Please pull down the {blind} to block the afternoon sun.
e.zh: 请把百叶窗拉下来挡住下午的阳光。

blinded.t:
v. 使失明（过去式）
adj. 被蒙蔽的

e.en: The driver was momentarily {blinded} by oncoming headlights.
e.zh: 司机被对面来车的车灯瞬间晃花了眼。

e.en: She was {blinded} by love and ignored the warning signs.
e.zh: 她被爱情冲昏了头,无视了那些警示信号。

e.en: The horse wore {blinders} to keep it focused on the track.
e.zh: 那匹马戴着眼罩以便专注于跑道。

e.en: Stop wearing {blinders} and look at the bigger picture.
e.zh: 别再目光狭隘了,要看看大局。

blindfold.t:
n. 蒙眼布
v. 蒙住眼睛

e.en: They tied a {blindfold} over her eyes for the surprise.
e.zh: 他们为了制造惊喜,蒙上了她的眼睛。

e.en: He could solve the puzzle {blindfold}, that's how easy it was.
e.zh: 他闭着眼睛都能解出这道题,就是这么简单。

blindfolded.t:
adj. 被蒙住眼的
v. 蒙眼（过去式）

e.en: The hostages were {blindfolded} and led into a van.
e.zh: 人质被蒙上眼睛后被押进了一辆面包车。

e.en: She walked {blindfolded} across the stage as part of the trust exercise.
e.zh: 作为信任练习,她蒙着眼睛走过舞台。

blinding.t:
adj. 刺眼的；极强烈的
v. 使失明（进行时）

e.en: The snow reflected a {blinding} white light across the field.
e.zh: 雪地反射出刺眼的白光,照亮了整片田野。

e.en: She had a {blinding} headache after staring at the screen.
e.zh: 盯着屏幕看了一会儿后,她头疼得厉害。

e.en: The answer was {blindingly} obvious once he explained it.
e.zh: 他一解释,答案就显得再明显不过了。

e.en: The desert sun shone {blindingly} bright at noon.
e.zh: 正午时分,沙漠的太阳刺眼得令人睁不开眼。

e.en: Don't {blindly} follow trends without thinking for yourself.
e.zh: 不要不加思考地盲目跟风。

e.en: She reached {blindly} into the bag for her keys.
e.zh: 她伸手在包里摸索着找钥匙。

e.en: Early treatment can prevent permanent {blindness} in many cases.
e.zh: 在许多情况下,及早治疗可以预防永久性失明。

e.en: His political {blindness} caused him to overlook clear warnings.
e.zh: 他在政治上的盲目让他忽视了明显的警告。

e.en: Researchers categorize different {blindnesses} based on their causes.
e.zh: 研究人员根据成因对不同类型的失明进行了分类。

e.en: Various color {blindnesses} affect about eight percent of men.
e.zh: 各种色盲症影响着约百分之八的男性。

blinds.t:
n. 百叶窗（复数）
v. 使失明

e.en: She closed the {blinds} to keep the room cool.
e.zh: 她拉上百叶窗,让房间保持凉爽。

e.en: Greed often {blinds} people to obvious risks.
e.zh: 贪婪常常使人对明显的风险视而不见。

blindside.t:
v. 冷不防袭击
n. 视野盲区

e.en: The new tariffs will {blindside} small importers next month.
e.zh: 新关税下个月会让小进口商措手不及。

e.en: Don't let market shifts {blindside} your business strategy.
e.zh: 别让市场变化打乱你的商业策略。

e.en: The rapper showed off his diamond {bling} on stage.
e.zh: 这位说唱歌手在舞台上炫耀他闪闪发光的钻石首饰。

e.en: Her phone case is covered in pink {bling}.
e.zh: 她的手机壳上贴满了粉色的闪亮饰品。

e.en: They served caviar on tiny buckwheat {blini} at the party.
e.zh: 派对上他们用小小的荞麦薄饼配鱼子酱。

e.en: Russian {blini} are traditionally eaten with sour cream.
e.zh: 俄式薄饼传统上要配酸奶油一起吃。

blink.t:
v. 眨眼；闪烁
n. 眨眼

e.en: Don't {blink} or you'll miss the magic trick.
e.zh: 千万别眨眼,不然你就错过这个魔术了。

e.en: The router's light started to {blink} red after the outage.
e.zh: 停电之后,路由器的指示灯开始闪红光。

e.en: She {blinked} back tears as she read the letter.
e.zh: 她读信时眨了眨眼,强忍住了泪水。

e.en: Neither side {blinked} during the tense negotiation.
e.zh: 在紧张的谈判中,双方都没有退让。

e.en: He forgot to turn off his {blinker} after changing lanes.
e.zh: 换道之后他忘了关转向灯。

e.en: The driver's left {blinker} flashed for half a mile.
e.zh: 那辆车的左转向灯闪了大半英里。

e.en: His {blinkered} view ignored the team's actual concerns.
e.zh: 他目光狭隘的看法忽视了团队真正的顾虑。

e.en: The company took a {blinkered} approach to innovation.
e.zh: 这家公司在创新上采取了狭隘的思路。

blinkers.t: n. 转向灯；马眼罩（复数）

e.en: Take off your {blinkers} and consider other perspectives.
e.zh: 摘掉你的有色眼镜,考虑一下其他视角吧。

e.en: Always use your {blinkers} when merging onto the highway.
e.zh: 汇入高速公路时一定要打转向灯。

blinking.t:
adj. 闪烁的
v. 眨眼（进行时）

e.en: The cursor kept {blinking} as she stared at the empty page.
e.zh: 她盯着空白页面,光标一直在闪烁。

e.en: A {blinking} red light warned drivers of construction ahead.
e.zh: 闪烁的红灯提醒司机前方有施工。

blinks.t:
v. 眨眼（第三人称单数）
n. 眨眼（复数）

e.en: The smoke alarm {blinks} every few seconds when the battery is low.
e.zh: 电池电量低时,烟雾报警器会每隔几秒闪一下。

e.en: She {blinks} rapidly when she's nervous in interviews.
e.zh: 面试紧张时她会快速地眨眼。

e.en: The sales drop was just a {blip}, not a real trend.
e.zh: 销售下滑只是一个小波动,并非真正的趋势。

e.en: A small {blip} appeared on the radar screen.
e.zh: 雷达屏幕上出现了一个小光点。

e.en: That first sip of coffee in the morning is pure {bliss}.
e.zh: 早晨喝下第一口咖啡简直是一种幸福。

e.en: They spent their honeymoon in absolute {bliss}.
e.zh: 他们的蜜月过得无比幸福。

e.en: She wrote about the small daily {blisses} of country life.
e.zh: 她描写了乡村生活中那些日常的小小幸福。

e.en: The book lists simple {blisses} like fresh bread and warm tea.
e.zh: 这本书列举了一些简单的快乐,比如新鲜面包和热茶。

blissful.t: adj. 极幸福的；无忧无虑的

e.en: They shared a {blissful} weekend at the beach house.
e.zh: 他们在海滨别墅度过了一个无比幸福的周末。

e.en: She wore a {blissful} smile after the massage.
e.zh: 按摩之后,她脸上挂着幸福的笑容。

e.en: The baby slept {blissfully} through the noisy party.
e.zh: 在嘈杂的聚会中,宝宝依然睡得香甜安详。

e.en: He was {blissfully} unaware that his team had been promoted.
e.zh: 他根本不知道自己的团队已经升职了。

blister.t:
n. 水泡
v. 起泡

e.en: New shoes always give me a {blister} on my heel.
e.zh: 新鞋总会把我的脚后跟磨出水泡。

e.en: Don't pop the {blister} or it might get infected.
e.zh: 别把水泡弄破,否则可能会感染。

blistered.t:
adj. 起泡的
v. 起泡（过去式）

e.en: His hands were {blistered} from chopping wood all day.
e.zh: 他的双手因为整天劈柴而起了水泡。

e.en: The paint had {blistered} under the harsh summer sun.
e.zh: 在炎炎夏日的烈日下,油漆已经起泡了。

e.en: The runner set a {blistering} pace from the start.
e.zh: 那名跑步者从一开始就保持着飞快的速度。

e.en: We hiked through the {blistering} desert heat.
e.zh: 我们在酷热难当的沙漠中徒步穿行。

e.en: The new chip is {blisteringly} fast at running AI models.
e.zh: 这款新芯片运行人工智能模型的速度快得惊人。

e.en: Critics gave the film a {blisteringly} negative review.
e.zh: 影评人对这部电影给出了极其严厉的负面评价。

blisters.t:
n. 水泡（复数）
v. 起泡

e.en: Long hikes often cause painful {blisters} on the toes.
e.zh: 长时间徒步常常会让脚趾起痛苦的水泡。

e.en: The old wallpaper {blisters} in humid weather.
e.zh: 潮湿天气里,旧墙纸会起泡。

blown.t:
v. blow 的过去分词
adj. 被吹动的；气喘吁吁的

e.en: The fuse has {blown} again because of the heater.
e.zh: 保险丝因为暖气又烧断了。

e.en: Her mind was {blown} by the movie's twist ending.
e.zh: 电影的反转结局让她大开眼界。

blowout.t:
n. 爆胎；（电路）烧断
n. 盛大聚会

e.en: We had a tire {blowout} on the highway last weekend.
e.zh: 我们上周末在高速公路上爆胎了。

e.en: The team won by a {blowout} score of forty points.
e.zh: 那支球队以四十分的悬殊比分大胜对手。

e.en: The glass artist shaped the vase using a long {blowpipe}.
e.zh: 玻璃艺人用长长的吹管塑造出花瓶的形状。

e.en: Amazonian hunters use a {blowpipe} with poisoned darts.
e.zh: 亚马逊的猎人使用带毒飞镖的吹管打猎。

blows.t:
v. blow 的第三人称单数
n. 打击（复数）

e.en: The wind {blows} fiercely off the lake every winter.
e.zh: 每到冬天,湖面上的风都刮得很猛。

e.en: The boxer landed several heavy {blows} in the third round.
e.zh: 那位拳击手在第三回合打出了几记重拳。

blowsy.t: adj. 邋遢的；（女子）粗俗的

e.en: She arrived looking {blowsy} after running through the rain.
e.zh: 她冒雨跑过来后,看上去蓬头垢面。

e.en: His hair was {blowsy} and unkempt that windy morning.
e.zh: 那个刮风的早晨,他的头发凌乱不堪。

e.en: The chef used a {blowtorch} to caramelize the crème brûlée.
e.zh: 厨师用喷枪给焦糖布丁烤出脆糖面。

e.en: Plumbers use a {blowtorch} to solder copper pipes together.
e.zh: 水管工用喷灯把铜管焊接在一起。

e.en: He bought the movie on {Blu}-ray for better quality.
e.zh: 为了更好的画质,他买了那部电影的蓝光碟。

e.en: The streaming service still beats {Blu}-ray in convenience.
e.zh: 流媒体服务在便利性上仍然胜过蓝光。

e.en: The toddler started to {blub} when his ice cream fell.
e.zh: 小朋友的冰淇淋掉了,就开始抽噎着哭起来。

e.en: Don't {blub} about it; just try again tomorrow.
e.zh: 别哭哭啼啼了,明天再试一次就好。

blubber.t:
n. 鲸脂；肥肉
v. 抽泣

e.en: Whales rely on thick {blubber} to survive freezing waters.
e.zh: 鲸鱼靠厚厚的鲸脂在冰冷的海水中生存。

e.en: Try not to {blubber} during the sad ending.
e.zh: 看到悲伤的结局时尽量别嚎啕大哭。

blubbers.t:
v. blubber 的第三人称单数
n. 鲸脂（复数）

e.en: He always {blubbers} whenever they watch romantic movies.
e.zh: 每次看爱情片他都会哭得稀里哗啦。

e.en: The seal carries {blubbers} of fat to stay warm.
e.zh: 海豹身上覆盖着层层脂肪来保暖。

e.en: The walrus has a {blubbery} layer protecting it from cold.
e.zh: 海象身上厚厚的脂肪层能抵御寒冷。

e.en: His voice turned {blubbery} as he recalled his late dog.
e.zh: 想起去世的爱犬,他的声音哽咽起来。

bludgeon.t:
n. 大头棒
v. 用棒打；胁迫

e.en: Critics accused him of trying to {bludgeon} opponents into agreement.
e.zh: 批评者指责他试图强迫对手就范。

e.en: The robber used a heavy {bludgeon} during the attack.
e.zh: 劫匪在袭击时使用了一根沉重的棍棒。

blue.t:
adj. 蓝色的；忧郁的
n. 蓝色

e.en: She painted her bedroom walls a soft {blue}.
e.zh: 她把卧室的墙壁刷成了柔和的蓝色。

e.en: He's been feeling {blue} since the breakup last month.
e.zh: 上个月分手后,他一直心情低落。

e.en: The opera retells the dark tale of {Bluebeard}'s castle.
e.zh: 这部歌剧重述了蓝胡子城堡的黑暗故事。

e.en: He earned a creepy {Bluebeard} reputation among his ex-wives.
e.zh: 他在前妻们中落下了蓝胡子般可怕的名声。

e.en: The forest floor was carpeted with {bluebell} flowers in May.
e.zh: 五月里,林间地面铺满了蓝铃花。

e.en: She picked a single {bluebell} for her grandmother.
e.zh: 她为奶奶摘了一朵蓝铃花。

e.en: I ordered a {blueberry} muffin with my morning coffee.
e.zh: 我点了一个蓝莓松饼配早晨的咖啡。

e.en: Fresh {blueberry} pancakes are her favorite weekend breakfast.
e.zh: 新鲜蓝莓松饼是她最爱的周末早餐。

e.en: A {bluebird} landed on the fence outside our window.
e.zh: 一只蓝鸲落在我们窗外的栅栏上。

e.en: Spotting a {bluebird} is considered good luck in some cultures.
e.zh: 在一些文化里,看到蓝鸲被视为好兆头。

bluebonnet.t: n. 矢车菊；德州羽扇豆

e.en: Texas highways are lined with {bluebonnet} flowers each spring.
e.zh: 每到春天,德州的公路两旁都开满矢车菊。

e.en: Families take photos in the {bluebonnet} fields every April.
e.zh: 每年四月,家庭都会去蓝帽花田里拍照。

e.en: A noisy {bluebottle} kept buzzing around the kitchen window.
e.zh: 一只吵闹的蓝头苍蝇一直在厨房窗边嗡嗡飞。

e.en: Swimmers were warned about {bluebottle} jellyfish along the beach.
e.zh: 游泳者被告知海滩上有蓝瓶水母出没。

bluecoat.t: n. 穿蓝制服者（警察或士兵）

e.en: A {bluecoat} officer directed traffic at the busy intersection.
e.zh: 一名身穿蓝制服的警员在繁忙的路口指挥交通。

e.en: The museum displays an original Revolutionary War {bluecoat} uniform.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一件独立战争时期的蓝制服原件。

blued.t: v. blue 的过去式；染蓝；（金属）发蓝处理

e.en: The gunsmith {blued} the steel barrel for rust protection.
e.zh: 枪匠把钢制枪管发蓝处理以防止生锈。

e.en: His old rifle had a beautifully {blued} finish.
e.zh: 他那把旧步枪有一层漂亮的发蓝镀层。

e.en: The chef sliced fresh {bluefin} for the sushi platter.
e.zh: 厨师为寿司拼盘切了新鲜的蓝鳍金枪鱼。

e.en: Overfishing has pushed {bluefin} tuna toward extinction.
e.zh: 过度捕捞已使蓝鳍金枪鱼濒临灭绝。

e.en: We caught a huge {bluefish} off the pier yesterday.
e.zh: 昨天我们在码头钓到了一条大蓝鱼。

e.en: Grilled {bluefish} tastes best with lemon and herbs.
e.zh: 烤蓝鱼配柠檬和香草最美味。

e.en: My son caught his first {bluegill} at the lake.
e.zh: 我儿子在湖边钓到了他的第一条蓝鳃太阳鱼。

e.en: The pond is full of {bluegill} and bass.
e.zh: 池塘里满是蓝鳃太阳鱼和鲈鱼。

e.en: He plays banjo in a {bluegrass} band on weekends.
e.zh: 他周末在一个蓝草音乐乐队里弹班卓琴。

e.en: Kentucky is famous for its rolling {bluegrass} hills.
e.zh: 肯塔基州以连绵起伏的蓝草丘陵而闻名。

e.en: The {blueness} of the ocean took my breath away.
e.zh: 大海的湛蓝令我屏住了呼吸。

e.en: Doctors noticed a slight {blueness} in the baby's lips.
e.zh: 医生注意到婴儿嘴唇有些发青。

blueprint.t:
n. 蓝图；方案
v. 制定蓝图

e.en: The CEO unveiled a {blueprint} for company growth.
e.zh: 首席执行官公布了公司发展的蓝图。

e.en: Architects revised the {blueprint} after the client meeting.
e.zh: 建筑师在客户会议后修改了设计图纸。

blues.t: n. 蓝调音乐；忧郁情绪

e.en: He played the {blues} on a battered old guitar.
e.zh: 他用一把破旧的吉他弹奏蓝调。

e.en: She had the post-holiday {blues} all week.
e.zh: 她整周都有节后忧郁情绪。

e.en: The aging {bluesman} sang about hard times in Mississippi.
e.zh: 那位年迈的蓝调歌手唱着密西西比州的艰苦岁月。

e.en: Every {bluesman} I met carried a worn harmonica.
e.zh: 我见过的每位蓝调歌手都带着一把磨损的口琴。

e.en: Native {bluestem} grass covers much of the prairie.
e.zh: 本土的蓝茎草覆盖了大部分草原。

e.en: Ranchers value {bluestem} for its drought resistance.
e.zh: 牧场主看重蓝茎草的抗旱能力。

bluestocking.t: n. 女才子；卖弄学问的女性

e.en: Critics dismissed her as a pretentious {bluestocking}.
e.zh: 评论家把她当作自命不凡的女学究而不屑一顾。

e.en: The salon welcomed every aspiring {bluestocking} in London.
e.zh: 那间沙龙欢迎伦敦每一位有抱负的女才子。

e.en: The patio was paved with thick {bluestone} slabs.
e.zh: 露台铺着厚厚的青石板。

e.en: Stonehenge's inner ring uses Welsh {bluestone}.
e.zh: 巨石阵的内圈使用了威尔士青石。

bluesy.t: adj. 蓝调风格的；忧郁的

e.en: Her voice has a smoky, {bluesy} quality.
e.zh: 她的嗓音带着烟熏般的蓝调韵味。

e.en: The film's soundtrack is slow and {bluesy}.
e.zh: 这部电影的配乐缓慢而充满蓝调风。

e.en: A tiny {bluetit} landed on the garden feeder.
e.zh: 一只小蓝山雀落在花园的喂鸟器上。

e.en: Children watched the {bluetit} build its nest.
e.zh: 孩子们看着那只蓝山雀筑巢。

e.en: My kids watch {Bluey} every morning before school.
e.zh: 我家孩子每天上学前都看《布鲁伊》。

e.en: The sky had a faint {bluey} tint at dusk.
e.zh: 黄昏时天空泛着淡淡的蓝色调。

bluff.t:
v. 虚张声势；唬人
n. 悬崖；诈唬

e.en: His confident smile was just a clever {bluff}.
e.zh: 他自信的微笑不过是巧妙的虚张声势。

e.en: The cabin sat on a {bluff} above the river.
e.zh: 小屋坐落在河面之上的悬崖上。

bluing.t: n. 上蓝剂（洗衣用增白剂）

e.en: Grandma added {bluing} to keep the white sheets bright.
e.zh: 奶奶加了上蓝剂让白床单更亮白。

e.en: The gunsmith finished the barrel with cold {bluing}.
e.zh: 枪匠用冷发蓝处理完成了枪管。

e.en: The mountains looked {bluish} in the morning haze.
e.zh: 清晨薄雾中,群山呈现出淡蓝色。

e.en: His fingers turned {bluish} from the cold.
e.zh: 他的手指冻得发青。

blunder.t:
n. 愚蠢的错误
v. 犯大错；跌跌撞撞

e.en: Forgetting the client's name was a major {blunder}.
e.zh: 忘记客户的名字是一个重大失误。

e.en: The chess champion made a rare {blunder} in round three.
e.zh: 那位国际象棋冠军在第三轮罕见地走出了一步臭棋。

e.en: The pirate brandished a rusty {blunderbuss} on deck.
e.zh: 海盗在甲板上挥舞着一把生锈的喇叭口火枪。

e.en: His policy was a political {blunderbuss}, hitting everyone.
e.zh: 他的政策像一把政治喇叭枪,谁都伤到了。

blundering.t: adj. 笨手笨脚的；犯蠢的

e.en: The {blundering} intern sent the email to the wrong list.
e.zh: 那位笨手笨脚的实习生把邮件发错了名单。

e.en: Critics mocked the agency's {blundering} response to the crisis.
e.zh: 评论家嘲笑该机构对危机的笨拙应对。

blunt.t:
adj. 钝的；直率的
v. 使变钝

e.en: She gave a {blunt} answer that surprised everyone.
e.zh: 她给出了一个直截了当的回答,让所有人都感到意外。

e.en: The knife is too {blunt} to slice tomatoes.
e.zh: 这把刀太钝,切不动番茄。

e.en: Years of criticism had {blunted} her enthusiasm.
e.zh: 多年的批评已经磨灭了她的热情。

e.en: The pencil tip was {blunted} after hours of writing.
e.zh: 经过几小时书写,铅笔尖已经变钝了。

e.en: He {bluntly} told her the project would fail.
e.zh: 他直言不讳地告诉她这个项目会失败。

e.en: She spoke {bluntly} about the company's finances.
e.zh: 她坦率地谈到了公司的财务状况。

e.en: Her {bluntness} sometimes offends new colleagues.
e.zh: 她的直率有时会冒犯新同事。

e.en: I appreciate the {bluntness} of his feedback.
e.zh: 我很欣赏他反馈的直接坦率。

blur.t:
v. 使模糊
n. 模糊一片

e.en: The whole weekend was a {blur} of meetings.
e.zh: 整个周末都是一连串模糊的会议。

e.en: Tears began to {blur} her vision.
e.zh: 泪水开始模糊了她的视线。

blurb.t: n. （书籍、产品的）简短推介语

e.en: The book's back-cover {blurb} convinced me to buy it.
e.zh: 这本书的封底简介让我决定买下它。

e.en: She wrote a short {blurb} for the company website.
e.zh: 她为公司网站写了一段简短的宣传文字。

blurbs.t: n. blurb 的复数；简短推介语

e.en: Famous authors wrote glowing {blurbs} for her novel.
e.zh: 知名作家为她的小说写了热情洋溢的推荐语。

e.en: The app store {blurbs} oversold the new feature.
e.zh: 应用商店的简介把新功能吹得过头了。

e.en: The photo was {blurred} because the subject moved.
e.zh: 由于被拍者动了,照片变得模糊。

e.en: Working from home {blurred} the line between work and life.
e.zh: 居家办公模糊了工作与生活的界限。

e.en: Adjust the focus to remove the {blurriness}.
e.zh: 调一下焦距以消除模糊感。

e.en: The {blurriness} of the screenshot made it unreadable.
e.zh: 截图的模糊使它无法辨认。

blurring.t:
n. 模糊化
v. 使变模糊

e.en: Remote work is {blurring} traditional office boundaries.
e.zh: 远程办公正在模糊传统的办公界限。

e.en: Heavy rain was {blurring} the windshield as we drove.
e.zh: 开车时大雨把挡风玻璃打得模糊一片。

e.en: My memory of that night is a bit {blurry}.
e.zh: 我对那晚的记忆有点模糊。

e.en: The webcam looked {blurry} during the entire call.
e.zh: 整个通话过程中摄像头画面都很模糊。

blurs.t:
v. 使模糊
n. 模糊的一片

e.en: The new policy {blurs} the line between employee and contractor.
e.zh: 新政策模糊了员工和合同工之间的界限。

e.en: Speeding cars passed as colorful {blurs} on the highway.
e.zh: 高速路上飞驰的汽车化作一片片彩色光影。

e.en: Try not to {blurt} out the surprise before the party.
e.zh: 在派对开始前别不假思索地把惊喜说出来。

e.en: Children often {blurt} whatever pops into their heads.
e.zh: 孩子们常常脱口说出脑子里冒出的任何想法。

e.en: He always {blurts} the answer before others can think.
e.zh: 他总是抢在别人思考前脱口说出答案。

e.en: She {blurts} secrets whenever she gets nervous.
e.zh: 她一紧张就会脱口说出秘密。

blush.t:
v. 脸红
n. 红晕

e.en: Compliments always make her cheeks {blush}.
e.zh: 夸奖总会让她脸红。

e.en: She added a touch of pink {blush} to her cheeks.
e.zh: 她在脸颊上扫了一抹粉色腮红。

e.en: He {blushed} when she remembered his birthday.
e.zh: 她记得他的生日时,他脸红了。

e.en: The teenager {blushed} at the unexpected praise.
e.zh: 那名青少年因意外的称赞而脸红。

e.en: She dabbed peach {blusher} along her cheekbones.
e.zh: 她在颧骨上轻拍上桃色腮红。

e.en: This {blusher} blends easily and lasts all day.
e.zh: 这款腮红很好上色,而且能持妆一整天。

blushes.t:
v. 脸红
n. 红晕

e.en: She {blushes} every time he calls her name.
e.zh: 每次他叫她名字,她都会脸红。

e.en: The sunset paints rosy {blushes} across the clouds.
e.zh: 日落给云朵抹上了一片片玫瑰色的红晕。

blushing.t:
adj. 脸红的
v. 正在脸红

e.en: The {blushing} bride waved at the cheering crowd.
e.zh: 羞红了脸的新娘向欢呼的人群挥手。

e.en: Stop {blushing} every time he mentions your project.
e.zh: 别每次他提到你的项目就脸红。

bluster.t:
v. 气势汹汹地说
n. 虚张声势

e.en: Behind all the {bluster}, he was actually nervous.
e.zh: 在那一通虚张声势之下,他其实很紧张。

e.en: Politicians often {bluster} when they lack real answers.
e.zh: 政客们在拿不出真正答案时常常虚张声势。

blustering.t: adj. 气势汹汹的，狂风大作的

e.en: His {blustering} threats fooled no one in the room.
e.zh: 他虚张声势的威胁骗不了在场任何人。

e.en: The {blustering} wind tore leaves from every tree.
e.zh: 狂风从每棵树上扯下了树叶。

e.en: It was a cold, {blustery} morning by the coast.
e.zh: 那是一个海边寒冷而狂风大作的早晨。

e.en: We canceled the picnic because of {blustery} weather.
e.zh: 我们因为大风天气取消了野餐。

e.en: The town of {Blyth} sits on England's northeast coast.
e.zh: 布莱斯镇坐落在英格兰东北海岸。

e.en: Ronnie {Blyth} scored the winning goal in extra time.
e.zh: 罗尼·布莱斯在加时赛中打入了制胜进球。

bma.t: abbr. British Medical Association 英国医学会

e.en: The {BMA} represents doctors across the United Kingdom.
e.zh: 英国医学会代表着全英国的医生。

e.en: Junior doctors voted to strike following {BMA} guidance.
e.zh: 在英国医学会的指导下,初级医生投票决定罢工。

bmc.t: abbr. 多指英国汽车公司等机构的缩写

e.en: Startups often sketch a {BMC} on a single page.
e.zh: 创业公司通常在一页纸上勾画商业模式画布。

e.en: Our team uses {BMC} software to manage IT incidents.
e.zh: 我们团队用 BMC 软件来管理 IT 事件。

e.en: Save this URL as a {bmk} for quick access later.
e.zh: 把这个网址存为书签以便日后快速访问。

e.en: The folder named {bmk} stores all my browser favorites.
e.zh: 那个名为 bmk 的文件夹保存着我所有的浏览器收藏。

e.en: He drove a sleek black {BMW} to the airport.
e.zh: 他开着一辆流畅的黑色宝马去了机场。

e.en: {BMW} unveiled its new electric sedan in Munich.
e.zh: 宝马在慕尼黑发布了新款电动轿车。

bmx.t: n. BMX 小轮越野自行车

e.en: Kids practiced jumps on their {BMX} bikes at the park.
e.zh: 孩子们在公园里用 BMX 小轮车练习跳跃。

e.en: She won her first {BMX} race at age twelve.
e.zh: 她十二岁时赢得了人生第一场 BMX 比赛。

bnf.t: abbr. British National Formulary 英国国家处方集

e.en: Doctors check the {BNF} before prescribing unfamiliar drugs.
e.zh: 医生在开不熟悉的药前会查阅《英国国家处方集》。

e.en: The parser is defined using a strict {BNF} grammar.
e.zh: 该解析器使用严格的 BNF 文法来定义。

bnp.t: abbr. 法国巴黎银行；英国国家党

e.en: {BNP} Paribas reported strong earnings this quarter.
e.zh: 法国巴黎银行公布了本季度强劲的业绩。

e.en: Elevated {BNP} levels can indicate heart failure.
e.zh: BNP 水平升高可能提示心力衰竭。

e.en: A green {boa} coiled around the branch in the rainforest.
e.zh: 一条绿色的蟒蛇盘绕在雨林的树枝上。

e.en: She wore a feather {boa} to the costume party.
e.zh: 她戴着一条羽毛围巾去参加化装舞会。

boadicea.t: n. 布狄卡（古不列颠女王）

e.en: Statues of {Boadicea} stand near the Thames in London.
e.zh: 布迪卡的雕像矗立在伦敦泰晤士河畔。

e.en: {Boadicea} led a famous revolt against Roman rule.
e.zh: 布迪卡领导了一场著名的反抗罗马统治的起义。

e.en: A wild {boar} crossed the path ahead of the hikers.
e.zh: 一头野猪从徒步者前方的小路穿过。

e.en: The chef roasted {boar} with herbs for the feast.
e.zh: 厨师用香草烤了野猪肉作为宴会主菜。

board.t:
n. 木板；董事会
v. 上（车、船、飞机）

e.en: Please {board} the train at platform three.
e.zh: 请在三号站台上车。

e.en: The {board} approved the new marketing budget yesterday.
e.zh: 董事会昨天批准了新的营销预算。

boarded.t: v. 登上（交通工具）；用板封住

e.en: Passengers {boarded} the plane just before takeoff.
e.zh: 乘客们在起飞前刚好登上了飞机。

e.en: They {boarded} up the windows before the storm hit.
e.zh: 他们在暴风雨来临前用木板封住了窗户。

e.en: The widow took in a {boarder} to help pay rent.
e.zh: 那位寡妇接收了一位寄宿者来帮忙交房租。

e.en: Every {boarder} at the school must follow strict rules.
e.zh: 学校里每个寄宿生都必须遵守严格的规定。

boarding.t:
n. 登机，登船
adj. 寄宿的

e.en: {Boarding} for flight 207 begins in ten minutes.
e.zh: 207航班将在十分钟后开始登机。

e.en: She sent her dog to a {boarding} kennel during vacation.
e.zh: 她度假期间把狗送去了寄养犬舍。

e.en: He rented a small room in a Victorian {boardinghouse}.
e.zh: 他在一栋维多利亚式寄宿公寓租了一个小房间。

e.en: The {boardinghouse} served breakfast at seven every morning.
e.zh: 那家寄宿公寓每天早上七点供应早餐。

e.en: The CEO walked into the {boardroom} for the meeting.
e.zh: 首席执行官走进会议室参加会议。

e.en: Major decisions are made behind closed {boardroom} doors.
e.zh: 重大决策都在紧闭的董事会会议室门后做出。

boards.t:
n. 木板；董事会
v. 登上

e.en: The carpenter cut the wooden {boards} to size.
e.zh: 木匠把木板切割成合适的尺寸。

e.en: She {boards} the bus every morning at eight.
e.zh: 她每天早上八点上公交车。

e.en: We strolled along the {boardwalk} eating ice cream.
e.zh: 我们沿着海滨木栈道散步,边吃冰淇淋。

e.en: The {boardwalk} stretches for miles along the Atlantic coast.
e.zh: 那条木板路沿着大西洋海岸绵延数英里。

boast.t:
v. 吹嘘，自夸
n. 自夸的话

e.en: Don't {boast} about your salary in front of others.
e.zh: 不要在别人面前炫耀你的薪水。

e.en: The hotel can {boast} the best view in the city.
e.zh: 那家酒店可以自夸拥有全城最好的景观。

e.en: He {boasted} that he could run a marathon easily.
e.zh: 他吹嘘说自己能轻松跑完马拉松。

e.en: The new phone {boasted} a battery lasting three days.
e.zh: 这款新手机号称电池续航长达三天。

e.en: Nobody likes a {boastful} colleague who exaggerates achievements.
e.zh: 没人喜欢爱吹嘘、夸大成就的同事。

e.en: His {boastful} tone annoyed everyone at the dinner table.
e.zh: 他自夸的语气惹恼了餐桌上的所有人。

e.en: He spoke {boastfully} about his expensive new car.
e.zh: 他得意洋洋地谈论他那辆昂贵的新车。

e.en: She {boastfully} mentioned her promotion at every family gathering.
e.zh: 她在每次家庭聚会上都炫耀地提起自己升职的事。

boasting.t:
n. 吹嘘
v. 正在自夸

e.en: Stop {boasting} and let your work speak for itself.
e.zh: 别再吹嘘了,让你的成果替自己说话。

e.en: The resort is {boasting} five new luxury swimming pools.
e.zh: 那家度假村正炫耀着五个全新的豪华泳池。

boasts.t: v. 吹嘘；拥有（值得自豪的东西）

e.en: This city {boasts} some of the finest museums in Europe.
e.zh: 这座城市拥有欧洲一些最顶级的博物馆。

e.en: He always {boasts} about his children's grades online.
e.zh: 他总是在网上炫耀孩子们的成绩。

e.en: We rented a small {boat} to explore the lake.
e.zh: 我们租了一艘小船去探索那片湖。

e.en: The fishing {boat} returned to harbor at sunset.
e.zh: 渔船在日落时分返回了港口。

e.en: Every {boater} must wear a life jacket on the river.
e.zh: 每位划船者在河上都必须穿救生衣。

e.en: He wore a straw {boater} hat in the summer photo.
e.zh: 在夏天的照片里他戴着一顶草编平顶帽。

e.en: The {boathouse} by the lake stores kayaks and oars.
e.zh: 湖边的船屋里存放着皮划艇和船桨。

e.en: They renovated the old {boathouse} into a cozy café.
e.zh: 他们把那座旧船屋改造成了一家温馨的咖啡馆。

e.en: We went {boating} on the lake last weekend.
e.zh: 上周末我们去湖上划船了。

e.en: {Boating} is a popular weekend activity in this region.
e.zh: 在这个地区,划船是很受欢迎的周末活动。

boatlift.t: n. 船运（大规模用船运送人员）

e.en: The Mariel {boatlift} brought thousands of Cubans to Florida.
e.zh: 马列尔船运把成千上万的古巴人带到了佛罗里达。

e.en: Volunteers organized a {boatlift} to evacuate stranded residents.
e.zh: 志愿者们组织了一次船运行动来撤离被困居民。

boatload.t: n. 一船（的人或货物）；大量

e.en: She earned a {boatload} of money from her startup.
e.zh: 她从她的创业公司里赚了一大笔钱。

e.en: A {boatload} of tourists arrived at the small island.
e.zh: 一船游客抵达了那座小岛。

e.en: The {boatman} rowed us across the misty river.
e.zh: 船夫划着船载我们渡过雾蒙蒙的河。

e.en: An old {boatman} told stories of past floods.
e.zh: 一位年长的船夫讲述着过去洪水的故事。

boatmen.t: n. boatman 的复数；船夫们

e.en: The {boatmen} sang traditional songs as they paddled.
e.zh: 船夫们一边划桨一边唱着传统歌曲。

e.en: Local {boatmen} know every hidden cove along the coast.
e.zh: 当地的船夫熟悉海岸沿线的每一处隐秘小湾。

boats.t:
n. 船（复数）
v. 乘船（第三人称单数）

e.en: Several fishing {boats} were anchored near the pier.
e.zh: 几艘渔船停泊在码头附近。

e.en: Sailing {boats} dotted the harbor on Sunday morning.
e.zh: 周日早晨,港口里点缀着许多帆船。

boatswain.t: n. 水手长；船上甲板事务主管

e.en: The {boatswain} blew his whistle to signal the crew.
e.zh: 水手长吹响哨子向船员发出信号。

e.en: As {boatswain}, he supervised all deck operations on board.
e.zh: 作为水手长,他监管船上所有甲板事务。

e.en: They repaired the yacht's hull at the local {boatyard}.
e.zh: 他们在当地的船坞修理了游艇的船体。

e.en: The {boatyard} smelled of fresh paint and varnish.
e.zh: 船坞里弥漫着新油漆和清漆的味道。

bob.t:
v. 上下晃动；轻点头
n. 短发；浮标

e.en: Watch the float {bob} up and down on the waves.
e.zh: 看那个浮标在浪上一上一下地浮动。

e.en: She got a short {bob} haircut last Friday.
e.zh: 她上周五剪了一个短波波头。

bobbed.t:
v. bob 的过去式；上下晃动过
adj. 剪短的（头发）

e.en: The buoy {bobbed} gently in the calm harbor.
e.zh: 浮标在平静的港湾里轻轻地起伏。

e.en: She {bobbed} her hair into a chic, modern style.
e.zh: 她把头发剪成了时髦的现代波波头。

e.en: The {bobber} dipped underwater when a fish bit the hook.
e.zh: 鱼咬钩时浮漂猛地沉入水下。

e.en: He customized his motorcycle into a classic {bobber}.
e.zh: 他把自己的摩托车改装成了经典的短尾改装车。

e.en: Replace the empty {bobbin} before continuing your sewing project.
e.zh: 在继续缝纫之前请更换空的线轴。

e.en: The {bobbin} on the sewing machine is tangled again.
e.zh: 缝纫机上的线轴又缠住了。

bobbing.t: v. bob 的现在分词；上下起伏

e.en: Apples were {bobbing} in the tub at the Halloween party.
e.zh: 万圣节派对上苹果在水盆里一上一下地漂着。

e.en: Ducks were {bobbing} on the pond after the rainstorm.
e.zh: 暴雨过后,鸭子们在池塘里浮浮沉沉。

bobble.t:
n. 小绒球
v. 失误；漏接

e.en: The fielder let the ball {bobble} out of his glove.
e.zh: 那位外野手让球从手套里滑了出去。

e.en: Her winter hat had a fluffy {bobble} on top.
e.zh: 她的冬帽顶上有一个毛茸茸的绒球。

e.en: He keeps a baseball {bobblehead} on his office desk.
e.zh: 他在办公桌上摆着一个棒球摇头公仔。

e.en: The team gave away a free {bobblehead} to every fan.
e.zh: 球队向每位球迷免费赠送了一个摇头公仔。

bobby.t: n. 英国警察（俚语）；人名 Bobby

e.en: A friendly {bobby} gave us directions near the station.
e.zh: 一位友善的英国警察在车站附近给我们指了路。

e.en: She held her hair in place with a {bobby} pin.
e.zh: 她用一个发夹把头发固定住。

e.en: A {bobcat} stalked silently through the snowy forest.
e.zh: 一只短尾猫在雪林中无声地潜行。

e.en: Hikers spotted a {bobcat} near the canyon trail yesterday.
e.zh: 徒步者昨天在峡谷小径附近看到了一只短尾猫。

bobo.t: n. 布尔乔亚波希米亚人；文艺中产

e.en: The neighborhood is full of trendy {bobo} cafés and boutiques.
e.zh: 这个街区到处都是时髦的布波族咖啡馆和精品店。

e.en: He jokingly called himself a {bobo} for buying organic everything.
e.zh: 他开玩笑说自己什么都买有机的,真是个布波族。

bobsled.t:
n. 有舵雪橇
v. 乘雪橇滑行

e.en: The Jamaican {bobsled} team became famous after the Olympics.
e.zh: 牙买加雪橇队在奥运会后声名大噪。

e.en: They built a backyard {bobsled} run from packed snow.
e.zh: 他们用压实的雪在后院修了一条雪橇滑道。

e.en: A {bobwhite} called from the hedgerow at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明时分,一只山齿鹑在树篱中鸣叫。

e.en: The farmer protects {bobwhite} habitat on his rural land.
e.zh: 那位农民在他的乡间土地上保护山齿鹑的栖息地。

e.en: The shipping label was marked with a clear {BOC} code.
e.zh: 运货标签上标着一个清晰的BOC代码。

e.en: She works at {BOC} headquarters in the finance division.
e.zh: 她在BOC总部的财务部门工作。

boca.t: n. 河口；入海口（西班牙语借词）

e.en: They retired to a quiet condo in {Boca} Raton.
e.zh: 他们退休后搬到了博卡拉顿一处安静的公寓。

e.en: The Spanish word {boca} simply means mouth.
e.zh: 西班牙语单词boca的意思就是嘴巴。

boccaccio.t: n. 薄伽丘（意大利作家）

e.en: {Boccaccio} wrote the famous medieval collection called the Decameron.
e.zh: 薄伽丘写了著名的中世纪故事集《十日谈》。

e.en: Students often compare Chaucer with {Boccaccio} in literature class.
e.zh: 文学课上学生们常常把乔叟和薄伽丘相比较。

bocce.t: n. 意大利地掷球运动

e.en: The old men play {bocce} in the park every afternoon.
e.zh: 老人们每天下午都在公园里玩地掷球。

e.en: We set up a {bocce} court in the backyard.
e.zh: 我们在后院搭了一个地掷球场。

e.en: He works out daily to maintain that beach {bod}.
e.zh: 他每天健身保持那身海滩好身材。

e.en: She joked that her summer {bod} needed more work.
e.zh: 她开玩笑说自己的夏日身材还得再练练。

bodacious.t: adj. 了不起的；极好的（美俚）

e.en: That surfer caught a truly {bodacious} wave this morning.
e.zh: 那位冲浪者今早抓到了一个真正了不起的浪。

e.en: She wore a {bodacious} red dress to the gala.
e.zh: 她穿着一件夺人眼球的红裙子参加晚会。

boddington.t: n. 博丁顿（英国啤酒品牌/姓氏）

e.en: He ordered a pint of {Boddington} at the English pub.
e.zh: 他在那家英式酒馆点了一品脱博丁顿啤酒。

e.en: {Boddington} is a classic Manchester ale with a creamy head.
e.zh: 博丁顿是一款经典的曼彻斯特艾尔啤酒,带有奶油般的泡沫。

e.en: These early sales numbers {bode} well for the launch.
e.zh: 这些早期的销售数据预示着发布会很成功。

e.en: Heavy clouds {bode} ill for our outdoor wedding plans.
e.zh: 厚厚的云层对我们户外婚礼的计划来说不是好兆头。

e.en: I grabbed a coffee at the {bodega} on the corner.
e.zh: 我在街角的小杂货店买了一杯咖啡。

e.en: Every New York neighborhood has its beloved local {bodega}.
e.zh: 纽约每个街区都有自己心爱的当地小杂货店。

boden.t: n. 博登（英国服装品牌/姓氏）

e.en: She ordered a striped dress from the {Boden} catalog.
e.zh: 她从博登的目录里订了一条条纹连衣裙。

e.en: {Boden} is known for colorful, classic British casual wear.
e.zh: 博登以色彩鲜艳的经典英式休闲服饰而闻名。

bodge.t: v. 拙劣地修补；糊弄（英式口语）

e.en: He tried to {bodge} the broken shelf with tape.
e.zh: 他试图用胶带草草修补那个坏掉的架子。

e.en: That repair is a complete {bodge} job.
e.zh: 那次修理完全是糊弄了事的活儿。

e.en: The temple houses a golden {bodhisattva} statue.
e.zh: 这座寺庙里供奉着一尊金色的菩萨像。

e.en: In Buddhism, a {bodhisattva} delays nirvana to help others.
e.zh: 在佛教中,菩萨为帮助众生而推迟入涅槃。

bodice.t: n. 紧身胸衣；连衣裙上身

e.en: The dress has an embroidered {bodice} and flowing skirt.
e.zh: 这件连衣裙有绣花上身和飘逸的裙摆。

e.en: She loosened the tight {bodice} to breathe more easily.
e.zh: 她松开紧绷的紧身上衣以便呼吸顺畅。

bodied.t: adj. 有身躯的（常用作复合词，如 full-bodied）

e.en: This wine is full-{bodied} with rich tannins.
e.zh: 这款葡萄酒酒体饱满,单宁浓郁。

e.en: She prefers full-{bodied} coffee in the morning.
e.zh: 她早上偏爱口感醇厚的咖啡。

bodies.t: n. body 的复数；身体；团体

e.en: Several governing {bodies} regulate the industry.
e.zh: 多个监管机构负责管理这一行业。

e.en: Athletes train hard to keep their {bodies} in shape.
e.zh: 运动员刻苦训练以保持身材。

e.en: A {bodiless} voice echoed through the empty hall.
e.zh: 一个无形的声音在空荡的大厅回响。

e.en: The ghost appeared as a {bodiless} shadow.
e.zh: 那鬼魂以一团无形的影子出现。

bodily.t:
adj. 身体的
adv. 整个地；亲自地

e.en: Regular exercise improves {bodily} health and mood.
e.zh: 规律锻炼能改善身体健康和情绪。

e.en: The bouncer threw him {bodily} out of the club.
e.zh: 保安一把把他整个人扔出了俱乐部。

e.en: Dark clouds were ill-{boding} for the picnic.
e.zh: 乌云密布,预示着野餐恐怕泡汤了。

e.en: His silence was {boding} trouble ahead.
e.zh: 他的沉默预示着麻烦即将到来。

bodleian.t: adj. 博德利（牛津大学图书馆）的

e.en: She researched at the {Bodleian} Library in Oxford.
e.zh: 她在牛津的博德利图书馆做研究。

e.en: The {Bodleian} holds millions of rare manuscripts.
e.zh: 博德利图书馆藏有数百万件珍稀手稿。

e.en: They drove across {Bodmin} Moor at sunset.
e.zh: 他们在日落时分驱车穿过博德明高沼。

e.en: Legends of a wild beast haunt {Bodmin}.
e.zh: 关于一头野兽的传说一直萦绕在博德明。

bodo.t: n. 博多（印度民族/语言）

e.en: The {Bodo} people live mainly in northeast India.
e.zh: 博多族主要居住在印度东北部。

e.en: She is learning to speak {Bodo} fluently.
e.zh: 她正在学习流利地说博多语。

body.t:
n. 身体；主体部分；团体
n. 正文（邮件、文章）

e.en: Drink water to keep your {body} hydrated.
e.zh: 多喝水让身体保持水分。

e.en: The email {body} contained the meeting details.
e.zh: 邮件正文里写着会议的详细信息。

e.en: The {bodybuilder} flexed his arms on stage.
e.zh: 那位健美运动员在台上展示手臂肌肉。

e.en: She trained for years to become a professional {bodybuilder}.
e.zh: 她苦练多年才成为职业健美运动员。

bodybuilding.t: n. 健美运动；健身塑形

e.en: He took up {bodybuilding} after recovering from surgery.
e.zh: 他手术康复后开始练健美。

e.en: {Bodybuilding} requires strict diet and consistent training.
e.zh: 健美需要严格的饮食和持续的训练。

e.en: The celebrity travels with a personal {bodyguard}.
e.zh: 那位明星出行总带着私人保镖。

e.en: Her {bodyguard} stood quietly by the door.
e.zh: 她的保镖静静地站在门边。

e.en: The car's {bodyshell} was repainted after the crash.
e.zh: 事故后这辆车的车身外壳被重新喷漆。

e.en: Engineers tested the {bodyshell} for structural rigidity.
e.zh: 工程师测试了车身外壳的结构强度。

e.en: Push-ups are a great {bodyweight} exercise.
e.zh: 俯卧撑是很棒的自重训练动作。

e.en: He lost ten percent of his {bodyweight} this year.
e.zh: 他今年减掉了百分之十的体重。

e.en: The mechanic repaired the dented {bodywork}.
e.zh: 修理工修复了凹陷的车身。

e.en: Rust had damaged the car's {bodywork} badly.
e.zh: 锈蚀已经严重损坏了汽车的车身。

boeing.t: n. 波音（美国飞机制造公司）

e.en: They flew to Tokyo on a {Boeing} 787.
e.zh: 他们乘坐一架波音787飞往东京。

e.en: {Boeing} announced a new aircraft model yesterday.
e.zh: 波音公司昨天发布了一款新机型。

boer.t: n. 布尔人（南非荷兰裔）

e.en: The {Boer} War shaped South African history.
e.zh: 布尔战争深刻影响了南非的历史。

e.en: His grandfather was a {Boer} farmer in Transvaal.
e.zh: 他祖父是德兰士瓦的一位布尔农场主。

e.en: She ordered {boeuf} bourguignon at the French bistro.
e.zh: 她在那家法国小馆点了红酒炖牛肉。

e.en: His signature dish is a slow-cooked {boeuf} stew.
e.zh: 他的招牌菜是慢炖的法式牛肉。

boffin.t: n. 科研专家（英式俚语）

e.en: The lab {boffin} explained the experiment patiently.
e.zh: 那位实验室专家耐心地讲解了实验。

e.en: Tech {boffin} types love debating new gadgets.
e.zh: 技术宅们最喜欢争论新出的小玩意。

boffo.t: adj. 非常成功的；大卖的

e.en: The new movie had a {boffo} opening weekend.
e.zh: 这部新电影首映周末票房大获成功。

e.en: Critics gave the show {boffo} reviews.
e.zh: 评论家对这档节目给出了极高的评价。

bofors.t: n. 博福斯（瑞典军火公司）

e.en: The ship was armed with twin {Bofors} guns.
e.zh: 那艘军舰装备了双联博福斯炮。

e.en: {Bofors} cannons were widely used in World War II.
e.zh: 博福斯火炮在二战中被广泛使用。

bog.t:
n. 沼泽
v. 陷入（bog down）

e.en: Don't get {bogged} down in tiny details.
e.zh: 别在琐碎的细节上陷入泥潭。

e.en: They hiked carefully across the peat {bog}.
e.zh: 他们小心翼翼地穿过泥炭沼泽。

bogart.t:
v. 独占；霸着不分享
n. 鲍嘉（姓氏）

e.en: Stop trying to {bogart} all the snacks.
e.zh: 别想把所有零食都霸占了。

e.en: He used to {bogart} the remote every evening.
e.zh: 他过去每晚都独占着遥控器。

bogey.t: n. 柏忌（高尔夫超一杆）；恶魔

e.en: He scored a {bogey} on the difficult sixth hole.
e.zh: 他在难打的第六洞打出了高于标准杆一杆。

e.en: Inflation remains the central bank's biggest {bogey}.
e.zh: 通胀仍是央行最头疼的难题。

bogeyman.t: n. 妖怪；吓唬小孩的怪物

e.en: Parents sometimes use the {bogeyman} to scare kids.
e.zh: 父母有时用妖怪来吓唬小孩。

e.en: Hackers are the new {bogeyman} of corporate security.
e.zh: 黑客成了企业安全新的头号大敌。

e.en: The sheer scale of the universe {boggles} the mind.
e.zh: 宇宙的浩瀚程度令人难以想象。

e.en: It {boggles} me how fast technology evolves.
e.zh: 科技发展的速度让我大开眼界。

e.en: After the rain, the field became {boggy} and slippery.
e.zh: 下雨后,田地变得泥泞湿滑。

e.en: Wear boots — the trail gets {boggy} ahead.
e.zh: 穿上靴子吧,前面那段路很泥泞。

e.en: The train's rear {bogie} needed urgent maintenance.
e.zh: 列车的后转向架急需维修。

e.en: Engineers inspected each {bogie} before departure.
e.zh: 工程师在发车前检查了每个转向架。

e.en: Scottish folklore is full of mischievous {bogle} spirits.
e.zh: 苏格兰民间传说里充满了顽皮的妖精。

e.en: Children feared the {bogle} said to live nearby.
e.zh: 孩子们害怕那个传说住在附近的小妖怪。

bogota.t: n. 波哥大（哥伦比亚首都）

e.en: {Bogotá} sits high in the Andes mountains.
e.zh: 波哥大坐落在安第斯山脉的高处。

e.en: She moved to {Bogotá} for a teaching job.
e.zh: 她为了一份教职搬到了波哥大。

e.en: The website was selling {bogus} concert tickets.
e.zh: 那个网站在卖假的演唱会门票。

e.en: His excuse sounded completely {bogus} to everyone.
e.zh: 他的借口在所有人听来都很假。

bogwood.t: n. 沼木（埋于沼泽的古木）

e.en: The artist carved a sculpture from ancient {bogwood}.
e.zh: 那位艺术家用古老的沼木雕刻了一件作品。

e.en: {Bogwood} is prized for its dark, weathered appearance.
e.zh: 沼木因其深色的风化外观而备受珍视。

e.en: Rising costs are the latest economic {bogy}.
e.zh: 成本上涨是最新的经济难题。

e.en: Childhood fears often invent some imaginary {bogy}.
e.zh: 童年的恐惧常常会臆造出某种妖怪。

bohemia.t: n. 波希米亚（地区）；放浪文艺圈

e.en: She traveled through {Bohemia} researching folk music.
e.zh: 她游历波希米亚地区研究民间音乐。

e.en: The novel romanticizes life in artistic {Bohemia}.
e.zh: 这部小说浪漫化了艺术放浪的波希米亚生活。

bohemian.t:
adj. 波希米亚风的；不羁的
n. 波希米亚人

e.en: She lives a {bohemian} lifestyle in Paris.
e.zh: 她在巴黎过着波希米亚式的生活。

e.en: His apartment had a casual {bohemian} vibe.
e.zh: 他的公寓有一种随性的波希米亚风格。

bohemianism.t: n. 波希米亚作风；放浪不羁的生活

e.en: The 1920s embraced literary {bohemianism} in many cities.
e.zh: 二十年代许多城市都崇尚文学上的波希米亚主义。

e.en: Her fashion reflects a deep love of {bohemianism}.
e.zh: 她的穿搭体现出对波希米亚风的深深热爱。

boil.t:
v. 煮沸；沸腾
n. 疖子

e.en: Please {boil} the water before adding the noodles.
e.zh: 请先把水烧开再下面条。

e.en: The argument made his blood {boil}.
e.zh: 那场争吵气得他怒火中烧。

e.en: She served {boiled} eggs with toast for breakfast.
e.zh: 她早餐做了水煮蛋配吐司。

e.en: The kettle has already {boiled} — make the tea.
e.zh: 水壶已经烧开了,可以泡茶了。

e.en: The old {boiler} stopped working in winter.
e.zh: 那台旧锅炉在冬天罢工了。

e.en: A plumber came to fix the apartment's {boiler}.
e.zh: 水管工来修公寓的锅炉。

boilermaker.t: n. 锅炉工人；啤酒兑烈酒

e.en: He ordered a {boilermaker} after a long workday.
e.zh: 忙了一天后他点了一杯威士忌配啤酒。

e.en: The skilled {boilermaker} repaired the industrial tank.
e.zh: 技术熟练的锅炉工修好了那个工业储罐。

boilerplate.t: n. 样板代码；固定模板文字

e.en: The contract was full of legal {boilerplate}.
e.zh: 这份合同满是套话式的法律条款。

e.en: Skip the {boilerplate} and get to the point.
e.zh: 省去那些套话,直接讲重点。

e.en: It's absolutely {boiling} outside today.
e.zh: 今天外面热得要命。

e.en: Add pasta to the {boiling} water carefully.
e.zh: 小心地把意面下进沸腾的水里。

boils.t:
v. 煮沸（boil 的三单）
n. 疖子（复数）

e.en: The whole issue {boils} down to trust.
e.zh: 整件事归根到底是信任问题。

e.en: She {boils} a fresh pot of tea each morning.
e.zh: 她每天早上都煮一壶新茶。

e.en: The {Bois} de Boulogne is a popular Parisian park.
e.zh: 布洛涅森林是巴黎人喜爱的一座公园。

e.en: Lovers strolled through the {Bois} at twilight.
e.zh: 情侣们在暮色中漫步于树林。

e.en: The kids were {boisterous} after eating too much sugar.
e.zh: 孩子们吃了太多糖,变得活蹦乱跳。

e.en: A {boisterous} crowd cheered loudly at the stadium.
e.zh: 喧闹的人群在体育场里大声欢呼。

e.en: The fans cheered {boisterously} when the goal scored.
e.zh: 球进的那一刻球迷们喧闹地欢呼起来。

e.en: They laughed {boisterously} at his silly joke.
e.zh: 他们对他那个傻笑话哄堂大笑。

e.en: The gaucho threw a {bola} to catch the cattle.
e.zh: 高乔人扔出投掷绳套住了牛。

e.en: A {bola} consists of weights tied to cords.
e.zh: 投掷绳由几个重物拴在绳索上构成。

bold.t:
adj. 粗体的；大胆的
n. 粗体字

e.en: She made a {bold} decision to quit her stable job.
e.zh: 她做了一个大胆的决定，辞掉了稳定的工作。

e.en: Please make the title {bold} so it stands out.
e.zh: 请把标题加粗，让它更醒目。

boldface.t:
n. 粗体字
adj. 粗体的

e.en: Important terms appear in {boldface} throughout the textbook.
e.zh: 教科书中重要术语都用粗体显示。

e.en: The editor told her to {boldface} every section heading.
e.zh: 编辑让她把每个章节标题都加粗。

e.en: He {boldly} challenged the manager during the meeting.
e.zh: 他在会议上大胆地质疑了经理。

e.en: The startup {boldly} entered a market dominated by giants.
e.zh: 这家初创公司大胆进入了巨头垄断的市场。

e.en: Her {boldness} in negotiations earned everyone's respect.
e.zh: 她在谈判中的果敢赢得了大家的尊重。

e.en: The painting's {boldness} of color caught my eye.
e.zh: 这幅画大胆的用色吸引了我的目光。

bolds.t:
n. 粗体（复数）
v. 加粗

e.en: This font family includes several {bolds} and italics.
e.zh: 这个字体家族包含多种粗体和斜体。

e.en: The designer compared different {bolds} for the headline.
e.zh: 设计师比较了不同的粗体用于标题。

e.en: Moss covered the thick {bole} of the old oak.
e.zh: 苔藓覆盖着那棵老橡树粗壮的树干。

e.en: Lightning had split the tree's {bole} right down the middle.
e.zh: 闪电把那棵树的树干从中间劈开了。

bolero.t: n. 波莱罗舞曲；短款小外套

e.en: She wore a short {bolero} over her evening dress.
e.zh: 她在晚礼服外面穿了一件短款波蕾若上衣。

e.en: The dancers moved gracefully to a slow {bolero}.
e.zh: 舞者们随着缓慢的波莱罗舞曲优雅地起舞。

e.en: A bright {bolide} streaked across the night sky.
e.zh: 一颗明亮的火流星划过夜空。
