e.en: Scientists studied fragments left behind by the {bolide}.
e.zh: 科学家们研究了那颗火流星留下的碎片。

bolingbroke.t: n. 博林布鲁克（英国人名）

e.en: Henry {Bolingbroke} eventually became King Henry IV of England.
e.zh: 亨利·博林布鲁克最终成为英格兰国王亨利四世。

e.en: Shakespeare's play depicts {Bolingbroke} returning from exile.
e.zh: 莎士比亚的戏剧描绘了博林布鲁克从流放归来的情景。

bolivarian.t: adj. 玻利瓦尔主义的；玻利瓦尔的

e.en: Venezuela is officially called the {Bolivarian} Republic.
e.zh: 委内瑞拉的正式名称是玻利瓦尔共和国。

e.en: The {Bolivarian} movement drew inspiration from Simón Bolívar.
e.zh: 玻利瓦尔运动的灵感来自西蒙·玻利瓦尔。

bolivia.t: n. 玻利维亚（南美国家）

e.en: We hiked across the salt flats of {Bolivia} last summer.
e.zh: 去年夏天我们徒步穿越了玻利维亚的盐沼。

e.en: {Bolivia} is one of the highest countries in South America.
e.zh: 玻利维亚是南美洲海拔最高的国家之一。

bolivian.t:
adj. 玻利维亚的
n. 玻利维亚人

e.en: She tried a traditional {Bolivian} stew at the market.
e.zh: 她在集市上尝了一道传统的玻利维亚炖菜。

e.en: The {Bolivian} highlands offer breathtaking mountain views.
e.zh: 玻利维亚高原拥有令人惊叹的山景。

e.en: Each cotton {boll} contains soft white fibers and seeds.
e.zh: 每个棉桃里都装着柔软的白色纤维和种子。

e.en: Farmers wait until every {boll} fully opens before harvesting.
e.zh: 农民们要等到每个棉铃完全开裂后才采收。

e.en: The car crashed into a metal {bollard} near the entrance.
e.zh: 那辆车撞上了入口附近的金属护柱。

e.en: Workers installed a new {bollard} to block traffic.
e.zh: 工人们安装了一根新的护柱来阻挡车辆。

bollinger.t: n. 布林格（人名/香槟品牌）

e.en: They opened a bottle of {Bollinger} to celebrate the deal.
e.zh: 他们开了一瓶堡林爵香槟庆祝这笔交易。

e.en: Traders watch the {Bollinger} bands for volatility signals.
e.zh: 交易员通过布林带观察波动信号。

e.en: The coach gave him a real {bollock} after the loss.
e.zh: 输球后教练把他狠狠训了一顿。

e.en: Stop talking {bollock} and focus on the actual problem.
e.zh: 别再胡扯了，专心解决真正的问题。

e.en: The {bollworm} destroyed nearly half of the cotton crop.
e.zh: 棉铃虫毁掉了将近一半的棉花作物。

e.en: Farmers spray pesticides to control the {bollworm} infestation.
e.zh: 农民们喷洒农药来控制棉铃虫的侵害。

e.en: He wore a leather {bolo} tie with his cowboy shirt.
e.zh: 他穿着牛仔衬衫，配了一条皮质波洛领带。

e.en: The farmer cleared brush with a sharp {bolo} knife.
e.zh: 农夫用一把锋利的波洛刀清理灌木丛。

bologna.t: n. 博洛尼亚（意大利城市）；大红肠

e.en: He packed a {bologna} sandwich for lunch every day.
e.zh: 他每天都带一个博洛尼亚香肠三明治当午餐。

e.en: We spent a weekend exploring the old streets of {Bologna}.
e.zh: 我们用一个周末游览了博洛尼亚的老街。

bolognese.t:
n. 博洛尼亚肉酱
adj. 博洛尼亚的

e.en: She makes the best spaghetti {bolognese} I've ever tasted.
e.zh: 她做的肉酱意面是我吃过最好吃的。

e.en: The chef simmered the {bolognese} sauce for three hours.
e.zh: 厨师把博洛尼亚肉酱炖了整整三个小时。

e.en: The {Bolshevik} revolution transformed Russia in 1917.
e.zh: 布尔什维克革命在1917年改变了俄罗斯。

e.en: Lenin led the {Bolshevik} faction during the early years.
e.zh: 列宁在早年间领导了布尔什维克派系。

e.en: The book traces the rise of {Bolshevism} after World War I.
e.zh: 这本书追溯了一战后布尔什维克主义的兴起。

e.en: Western governments feared the spread of {Bolshevism} in Europe.
e.zh: 西方政府担心布尔什维克主义在欧洲蔓延。

e.en: My teenage son has gotten quite {bolshie} lately.
e.zh: 我那十几岁的儿子最近变得相当叛逆。

e.en: The {bolshie} workers refused to accept the new contract.
e.zh: 那些倔强的工人拒绝接受新合同。

bolsover.t: n. 博尔索弗（英国地名）

e.en: {Bolsover} Castle sits on a hill overlooking the valley.
e.zh: 博尔索弗城堡坐落在俯瞰山谷的山丘上。

e.en: He grew up in a small village near {Bolsover}.
e.zh: 他在博尔索弗附近的一个小村庄里长大。

bolster.t:
v. 支撑；增强
n. 长枕

e.en: The new evidence helped {bolster} her legal case significantly.
e.zh: 新证据大大加强了她的诉讼主张。

e.en: She added a soft {bolster} pillow to the couch.
e.zh: 她在沙发上加了一个柔软的长枕。

bolt.t:
n. 螺栓；闪电
v. 飞奔；闩门

e.en: Don't forget to {bolt} the door before going to bed.
e.zh: 睡觉前别忘了把门闩上。

e.en: A loose {bolt} caused the chair to wobble dangerously.
e.zh: 一颗松动的螺栓让椅子晃得很危险。

bolted.t: v. 闩上；飞奔（bolt 过去式）

e.en: The horse {bolted} when it heard the loud thunder.
e.zh: 那匹马一听到雷声就受惊狂奔了。

e.en: The shelves are {bolted} firmly to the wall for safety.
e.zh: 为了安全，架子被牢牢地用螺栓固定在墙上。

bolting.t: v. 飞奔；闩门（bolt 现分）

e.en: He kept {bolting} his food despite his mother's warnings.
e.zh: 尽管妈妈警告，他还是狼吞虎咽地吃饭。

e.en: The lettuce is {bolting} early because of the heat.
e.zh: 由于天气炎热，生菜过早抽薹了。

e.en: {Bolton} is a former mill town in northwest England.
e.zh: 博尔顿是英格兰西北部一座昔日的纺织城镇。

e.en: She supports the {Bolton} Wanderers football club every weekend.
e.zh: 她每个周末都为博尔顿流浪者足球俱乐部加油。

bolts.t:
n. 螺栓（复数）
v. 飞奔

e.en: He tightened all the {bolts} on the bicycle frame.
e.zh: 他把自行车车架上所有的螺栓都拧紧了。

e.en: Lightning {bolts} lit up the entire midnight sky.
e.zh: 闪电照亮了整片午夜的天空。

e.en: The nurse administered a {bolus} of saline through the IV.
e.zh: 护士通过静脉注射了一剂生理盐水。

e.en: The cow chewed its {bolus} of grass slowly.
e.zh: 那头牛慢慢地嚼着一团草。

bom.t: n. 物料清单（bill of materials 缩写）

e.en: The factory updated the {BOM} to reflect new components.
e.zh: 工厂更新了物料清单以反映新组件。

e.en: Engineers reviewed the {BOM} before approving the prototype.
e.zh: 工程师们在批准原型前审查了物料清单。

bomb.t:
n. 炸弹
v. 轰炸；（口）惨败

e.en: Police safely defused the {bomb} found at the station.
e.zh: 警方安全地拆除了车站发现的炸弹。

e.en: His new movie was a complete box-office {bomb}.
e.zh: 他的新电影在票房上彻底失败了。

bombard.t: v. 轰炸；连珠炮般质问

e.en: Reporters {bombard} the senator with questions every morning.
e.zh: 记者们每天早上都用问题轰炸那位参议员。

e.en: Advertisers {bombard} viewers with messages on every platform.
e.zh: 广告商在每个平台上向观众狂轰滥炸地推送信息。

e.en: The {bombardier} aimed carefully before releasing the payload.
e.zh: 投弹手仔细瞄准后才投下了炸弹。

e.en: He served as a {bombardier} in the air force during the war.
e.zh: 战时他在空军担任投弹手。

e.en: The city endured weeks of constant aerial {bombardment}.
e.zh: 这座城市连续遭受了数周的空中轰炸。

e.en: Social media subjects users to a {bombardment} of opinions.
e.zh: 社交媒体让用户被各种观点狂轰滥炸。

bombards.t: v. 轰炸（bombard 第三人称单数）

e.en: The press {bombards} celebrities with intrusive questions daily.
e.zh: 媒体每天用各种侵扰性的问题轰炸名人。

e.en: His inbox {bombards} him with promotional emails every hour.
e.zh: 他的收件箱每小时都被推广邮件轰炸。

bombast.t: n. 夸夸其谈；浮夸之词

e.en: The politician's speech was full of empty {bombast}.
e.zh: 那位政客的演讲充斥着空洞的夸夸其谈。

e.en: Critics dismissed the novel as pretentious {bombast}.
e.zh: 评论家们将这部小说斥为做作的浮夸之作。

bombastic.t: adj. 夸夸其谈的；浮夸的

e.en: His {bombastic} writing style turned off many readers.
e.zh: 他浮夸的写作风格让许多读者反感。

e.en: The CEO gave a {bombastic} speech full of buzzwords.
e.zh: 那位首席执行官发表了一通充斥着流行词的浮夸演讲。

bombay.t: n. 孟买（印度城市，今 Mumbai）

e.en: The flight from London to {Bombay} takes about nine hours.
e.zh: 从伦敦到孟买的航班大约需要九小时。

e.en: {Bombay} is now officially known as Mumbai.
e.zh: 孟买现在的正式名称是Mumbai。

bombed.t:
v. 轰炸（bomb 过去式）
adj. 喝醉的（俚）

e.en: Allied forces {bombed} the bridge to halt enemy advances.
e.zh: 盟军轰炸了那座桥以阻止敌军推进。

e.en: His comedy routine completely {bombed} with the audience.
e.zh: 他的脱口秀表演在观众面前彻底失败了。

e.en: The stealth {bomber} flew silently through the night sky.
e.zh: 那架隐形轰炸机在夜空中悄无声息地飞行。

e.en: She wore a leather {bomber} jacket over her sweater.
e.zh: 她在毛衣外套了一件皮质飞行员夹克。

e.en: Heavy {bombers} took off from the airbase before dawn.
e.zh: 重型轰炸机在黎明前从空军基地起飞。

e.en: Vintage {bombers} jackets are popular with fashion influencers.
e.zh: 复古飞行员夹克在时尚博主中很受欢迎。

bombing.t:
n. 轰炸
v. 轰炸（bomb 现分）

e.en: The {bombing} campaign destroyed much of the city's infrastructure.
e.zh: 轰炸行动摧毁了城市的大部分基础设施。

e.en: His stand-up set was {bombing} badly that night.
e.zh: 那晚他的脱口秀演出表现得非常糟糕。

e.en: A series of {bombings} shocked the capital last week.
e.zh: 上周一连串的爆炸事件震惊了首都。

e.en: Investigators linked the {bombings} to the same extremist group.
e.zh: 调查人员将这些爆炸案与同一个极端组织联系起来。

e.en: Each cluster munition releases dozens of small {bomblet} units.
e.zh: 每枚集束弹药都会释放出数十个小型子炸弹。

e.en: Unexploded {bomblet} devices remain a serious civilian hazard.
e.zh: 未爆炸的子炸弹仍然是平民面临的严重危险。

e.en: The embassy was rebuilt with {bombproof} walls and windows.
e.zh: 大使馆用防爆墙和防爆窗重建了。

e.en: Engineers designed a {bombproof} shelter beneath the building.
e.zh: 工程师们在大楼下面设计了一个防爆掩体。

bombs.t:
n. 炸弹（复数）
v. 轰炸

e.en: Soldiers carefully defused two unexploded {bombs} from World War II.
e.zh: 士兵们小心地拆除了两枚二战遗留的未爆炸弹。

e.en: His latest album {bombs} on the streaming charts.
e.zh: 他最新的专辑在流媒体榜单上一败涂地。

bombshell.t: n. 爆炸性消息；惊人之事

e.en: The reporter dropped a {bombshell} during the live interview.
e.zh: 记者在直播采访中爆出了一个惊人消息。

e.en: Her resignation came as a complete {bombshell} to colleagues.
e.zh: 她的辞职对同事们来说完全是个晴天霹雳。

e.en: The {bombsight} helped pilots calculate the exact release point.
e.zh: 投弹瞄准器帮助飞行员计算出精确的投弹点。

e.en: Engineers redesigned the {bombsight} to improve targeting accuracy.
e.zh: 工程师们重新设计了投弹瞄准器以提高瞄准精度。

bon.t: adj. 好的（法语借词，如 bon voyage）

e.en: She wished her friend {bon} voyage at the airport gate.
e.zh: 她在登机口祝朋友一路顺风。

e.en: The chef shouted {bon} appétit before serving the dish.
e.zh: 主厨上菜前喊了一声祝您用餐愉快。

bonanza.t: n. 富矿；横财；意外好运

e.en: The new game became a {bonanza} for the studio.
e.zh: 这款新游戏为工作室带来了滚滚财源。

e.en: Black Friday is a shopping {bonanza} for online retailers.
e.zh: 黑色星期五对网店来说是一场购物盛宴。

e.en: Saint {Bonaventure} was a famous medieval theologian and philosopher.
e.zh: 圣文德是著名的中世纪神学家和哲学家。

e.en: We stayed at the {Bonaventure} hotel during the conference.
e.zh: 开会期间我们住在博纳旺蒂尔酒店。

e.en: She nibbled a chocolate {bonbon} while watching the movie.
e.zh: 她一边看电影一边咬着一颗巧克力夹心糖。

e.en: The shop sells handmade {bonbon} boxes for Valentine's Day.
e.zh: 这家店出售情人节手工夹心糖礼盒。

bond.t:
n. 债券；纽带
v. 粘合；建立关系

e.en: They share a strong {bond} after years of friendship.
e.zh: 多年的友谊让他们之间有着深厚的感情。

e.en: He invested his savings in government {bond} funds.
e.zh: 他把积蓄投资在政府债券基金里。

e.en: The novel describes peasants escaping centuries of {bondage}.
e.zh: 这本小说描写了农民摆脱数百年奴役的故事。

e.en: Many people remain in economic {bondage} due to debt.
e.zh: 许多人因债务而陷于经济束缚之中。

bonded.t:
adj. 粘合的；保税的
v. 粘合（bond 过去式）

e.en: The two sisters {bonded} over their love of K-pop.
e.zh: 两姐妹因为同样喜欢韩流而变得亲密。

e.en: All our movers are licensed and {bonded} for your safety.
e.zh: 我们所有搬运工都持证并有担保,确保您的安全。

e.en: Every {bondholder} received the scheduled interest payment on time.
e.zh: 每位债券持有人都按时收到了利息。

e.en: The company defaulted, leaving each {bondholder} unpaid for months.
e.zh: 公司违约,每位债券持有人数月未拿到钱。

book.t:
n. 书籍
v. 预订

e.en: I just finished a great {book} about ancient Rome.
e.zh: 我刚读完一本很棒的关于古罗马的书。

e.en: You should {book} your flight before prices go up.
e.zh: 你应该在涨价前订好机票。

e.en: All rooms are {bookable} online through our website.
e.zh: 所有房间都可以通过我们的网站在线预订。

e.en: The meeting space is {bookable} by the hour.
e.zh: 这个会议空间可以按小时预订。

e.en: A skilled {bookbinder} restored the damaged old novel.
e.zh: 一位熟练的装订师修复了那本破损的旧小说。

e.en: The {bookbinder} stitched the pages together by hand.
e.zh: 装订师傅手工把书页缝合在一起。

e.en: She took a class on traditional {bookbinding} last weekend.
e.zh: 她上周末上了一堂传统装帧课程。

e.en: The museum displays tools used in medieval {bookbinding}.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了中世纪装帧用的工具。

e.en: He built a tall {bookcase} for the living room.
e.zh: 他给客厅做了一个高高的书柜。

e.en: The wooden {bookcase} is overflowing with novels and magazines.
e.zh: 那个木书柜里塞满了小说和杂志。

e.en: Two matching {bookcases} flank the fireplace nicely.
e.zh: 两个对称的书柜整齐地立在壁炉两侧。

e.en: The library has rows of tall oak {bookcases}.
e.zh: 图书馆里排列着一排排高大的橡木书柜。

booked.t:
adj. 已预订的
v. 预订（过去式）

e.en: I already {booked} a table for two at seven.
e.zh: 我已经预订了七点的双人桌。

e.en: The hotel was completely {booked} during the holiday weekend.
e.zh: 那家酒店在假日周末已被订满。

e.en: A heavy brass {bookend} kept the dictionaries upright.
e.zh: 一个沉重的铜书挡稳稳地撑着那些词典。

e.en: Two concerts {bookend} the summer music festival nicely.
e.zh: 两场演唱会恰好为夏季音乐节画上完美首尾。

e.en: The talent {booker} signed three new comedians this month.
e.zh: 这位星探这个月签下了三位新喜剧演员。

e.en: Our travel {booker} found us cheap flights to Tokyo.
e.zh: 我们的预订员帮我们找到了便宜的东京机票。

e.en: The {bookie} took bets on every horse in the race.
e.zh: 那个赌注经纪人接受比赛中每匹马的下注。

e.en: He owed his {bookie} a lot of money.
e.zh: 他欠那个赌注经纪人一大笔钱。

e.en: I made a {booking} for Friday night at the restaurant.
e.zh: 我在那家餐厅订了周五晚上的位子。

e.en: Please confirm your {booking} by replying to this email.
e.zh: 请回复此邮件确认您的预订。

e.en: Hotel {bookings} have surged since travel restrictions ended.
e.zh: 自旅行限制解除以来,酒店预订量大幅上升。

e.en: We accept online {bookings} up to six months ahead.
e.zh: 我们接受最长提前六个月的在线预订。

bookish.t: adj. 书卷气的；爱读书的

e.en: She was a quiet, {bookish} child who loved libraries.
e.zh: 她是个文静爱书的孩子,特别喜欢图书馆。

e.en: His {bookish} demeanor made him perfect for the research role.
e.zh: 他书卷气的气质让他非常适合做研究工作。

e.en: The {bookkeeper} reconciled the company accounts every Friday.
e.zh: 那位记账员每周五都会核对公司账目。

e.en: Our small business hired a part-time {bookkeeper}.
e.zh: 我们的小公司雇了一位兼职记账员。

e.en: Good {bookkeeping} is essential for running a small business.
e.zh: 良好的记账对经营小生意至关重要。

e.en: She uses software to simplify her monthly {bookkeeping} tasks.
e.zh: 她用软件来简化每月的记账工作。

e.en: The doctor handed me a {booklet} explaining the procedure.
e.zh: 医生递给我一本说明手术流程的小册子。

e.en: Each guest received a welcome {booklet} at the front desk.
e.zh: 每位客人在前台都领到了一本欢迎手册。

e.en: They printed thousands of {booklets} for the conference attendees.
e.zh: 他们为参会者印制了成千上万本小册子。

e.en: The clinic offers free {booklets} on healthy eating habits.
e.zh: 诊所免费提供有关健康饮食习惯的小册子。

e.en: The teacher emailed a summer {booklist} to all parents.
e.zh: 老师把暑期书单邮件发给了所有家长。

e.en: Check the course {booklist} before the semester starts.
e.zh: 开学前请查看课程书单。

bookmaker.t: n. 赌注登记人；出版商

e.en: The {bookmaker} set the odds at three to one.
e.zh: 博彩商把赔率定为三比一。

e.en: Online {bookmaker} sites have changed the gambling industry.
e.zh: 网络博彩商改变了整个博彩行业。

e.en: The old {bookman} knew every rare title in the shop.
e.zh: 那位老书商熟知店里每一本珍本书。

e.en: As a true {bookman}, he collected first editions for decades.
e.zh: 作为一位真正的爱书人,他收藏初版书已有几十年。

bookmark.t:
n. 书签（纸质、网页）
v. 收藏网页

e.en: Don't forget to {bookmark} this page for later reference.
e.zh: 别忘了把这个页面收藏起来,以备日后参考。

e.en: She used a feather as a {bookmark} in her novel.
e.zh: 她把一根羽毛当作小说里的书签。

bookmarked.t: v. 已加入书签（过去式）

e.en: I {bookmarked} the recipe so I could find it tonight.
e.zh: 我把那份食谱收藏了,这样今晚就能找到。

e.en: She has {bookmarked} dozens of articles to read later.
e.zh: 她已经收藏了几十篇文章准备稍后阅读。

bookmarking.t:
n. 添加书签
v. 收藏（网页）

e.en: Social {bookmarking} sites let users share useful links easily.
e.zh: 社交书签网站让用户轻松分享有用的链接。

e.en: He's {bookmarking} every tutorial he plans to watch.
e.zh: 他正在把所有打算看的教程都加入书签。

e.en: My browser {bookmarks} got messy after years of saving links.
e.zh: 几年下来我的浏览器书签变得很乱。

e.en: She organized her {bookmarks} into folders by topic.
e.zh: 她按主题把书签整理到不同的文件夹里。

e.en: The {bookmobile} visits our neighborhood every Tuesday afternoon.
e.zh: 流动图书车每周二下午都会开到我们小区。

e.en: Children lined up eagerly when the {bookmobile} arrived.
e.zh: 流动图书车一到,孩子们就兴奋地排起了队。

books.t:
n. 书（复数）
v. 预订（第三人称）

e.en: She owns hundreds of {books} on history and philosophy.
e.zh: 她拥有几百本历史和哲学方面的书。

e.en: He {books} all his trips through a travel app.
e.zh: 他所有的旅行都通过一个旅行应用预订。

e.en: The local {bookseller} recommended a fantastic mystery novel.
e.zh: 本地的书商推荐了一本超棒的悬疑小说。

e.en: She works as a {bookseller} at the corner shop.
e.zh: 她在街角的小店当书店店员。

e.en: Independent {booksellers} are making a comeback in many cities.
e.zh: 独立书商正在许多城市重新兴起。

e.en: Online {booksellers} dominate the market these days.
e.zh: 如今网上书商占据了市场的主导地位。

e.en: My {bookshelf} is packed with novels and travel guides.
e.zh: 我的书架上塞满了小说和旅行指南。

e.en: He built a custom {bookshelf} that fits the alcove perfectly.
e.zh: 他做了一个定制书架,正好嵌进那个壁龛里。

e.en: The wall is lined with floor-to-ceiling {bookshelves}.
e.zh: 墙边摆着一整排顶天立地的书架。

e.en: Dust covered the top of the old {bookshelves}.
e.zh: 那些旧书架的顶部积满了灰尘。

e.en: There's a charming {bookshop} just around the corner.
e.zh: 街角就有一家很有情调的书店。

e.en: She runs an independent {bookshop} in the old town.
e.zh: 她在老城区经营着一家独立书店。

e.en: Many small {bookshops} struggle to compete with online retailers.
e.zh: 许多小书店难以与网上零售商竞争。

e.en: London is full of cozy second-hand {bookshops}.
e.zh: 伦敦到处都是温馨的二手书店。

e.en: He browsed the {bookstall} at the train station for magazines.
e.zh: 他在火车站的书报摊上翻找杂志。

e.en: A small {bookstall} sells used paperbacks near the park.
e.zh: 公园附近有个小书摊在卖旧平装书。

e.en: I spent the afternoon browsing at my favorite {bookstore}.
e.zh: 我整个下午都在最喜欢的书店里翻书。

e.en: The new {bookstore} downtown also serves great coffee.
e.zh: 市中心新开的那家书店还卖很棒的咖啡。

e.en: Independent {bookstores} are thriving again in college towns.
e.zh: 独立书店在大学城里重新红火起来。

e.en: Most {bookstores} now host author readings and book clubs.
e.zh: 现在大多数书店都会举办作者朗读会和读书俱乐部。

e.en: She's been a total {bookworm} since elementary school.
e.zh: 她从小学起就是个十足的书虫。

e.en: My brother is such a {bookworm} he reads at parties.
e.zh: 我弟弟是个超级书虫,连聚会上也在看书。

e.en: His apartment has a cozy, {booky} atmosphere with shelves everywhere.
e.zh: 他公寓到处都是书架,弥漫着书香气息。

e.en: The cafe has a quiet, {booky} vibe perfect for studying.
e.zh: 那家咖啡馆安静有书卷气,特别适合学习。

boolean.t:
adj. 布尔型的
n. 布尔值（真/假）

e.en: This function returns a {boolean} value of true or false.
e.zh: 这个函数返回一个真或假的布尔值。

e.en: Use a {boolean} flag to track whether the user is logged in.
e.zh: 用一个布尔标志来跟踪用户是否已登录。

boom.t:
n. 繁荣；轰鸣声
v. 激增；发出隆隆声

e.en: Tech startups experienced a huge {boom} during the last decade.
e.zh: 过去十年里科技初创公司经历了一场大繁荣。

e.en: We heard a loud {boom} when the fireworks started.
e.zh: 烟花一开始,我们就听到一声巨响。

e.en: He carried an old {boombox} on his shoulder down the street.
e.zh: 他扛着一台旧手提音箱沿街走着。

e.en: The {boombox} blasted hip-hop from the apartment window.
e.zh: 那台手提音箱从公寓窗口大声播放着嘻哈音乐。

boomer.t: n. 婴儿潮一代（尤指 1946–64 出生者）

e.en: My uncle is a classic {boomer} who loves classic rock.
e.zh: 我叔叔是个典型的婴儿潮一代,特别喜欢经典摇滚。

e.en: Each {boomer} grew up during a period of great prosperity.
e.zh: 每一个婴儿潮一代都是在繁荣时期长大的。

boomerang.t:
n. 回旋镖
v. 反噬；自食其果

e.en: The {boomerang} flew in a wide arc and returned to him.
e.zh: 回旋镖划出一个大弧线后又飞回到他手中。

e.en: His harsh comments {boomerang} back to hurt his reputation.
e.zh: 他的刻薄言论反弹回来,损害了他的名声。

booming.t: adj. 迅速发展的；轰鸣的

e.en: The local economy is {booming} thanks to new tech jobs.
e.zh: 由于新增的科技岗位,当地经济正蓬勃发展。

e.en: His {booming} voice filled the entire auditorium.
e.zh: 他洪亮的嗓音响彻整个礼堂。

e.en: The neighborhood saw a small housing {boomlet} last spring.
e.zh: 去年春天这个街区出现了一波小型房产热潮。

e.en: A brief {boomlet} in crypto investments faded by summer.
e.zh: 加密货币投资的一波小热潮到夏天就消退了。

booms.t:
n. 繁荣期（复数）
v. 激增（第三人称）

e.en: The economy {booms} whenever consumer confidence rises sharply.
e.zh: 每当消费者信心大幅上升,经济就会蓬勃发展。

e.en: Loud {booms} from the construction site shook the windows.
e.zh: 工地传来的巨响震得窗户都在抖。

e.en: Austin became a tech {boomtown} over the past decade.
e.zh: 过去十年里,奥斯汀变成了一座科技新兴城市。

e.en: The oil discovery turned the village into a {boomtown}.
e.zh: 石油的发现把这个小村庄变成了一座新兴繁荣城。

e.en: Cheap solar panels are a real {boon} to homeowners.
e.zh: 便宜的太阳能板对房主来说真是一大福音。

e.en: The new highway has been a {boon} for local businesses.
e.zh: 新建的高速公路对当地企业是一大利好。

e.en: Their cabin is way out in the {boondocks} with no Wi-Fi.
e.zh: 他们的小木屋在偏远乡下,连无线网络都没有。

e.en: He grew up in the {boondocks}, far from any city.
e.zh: 他在远离城市的偏远乡下长大。

boondoggle.t: n. 浪费时间与钱的项目

e.en: Critics called the new stadium a costly {boondoggle} for taxpayers.
e.zh: 批评人士称这座新体育场是浪费纳税人钱的形象工程。

e.en: The project turned into a {boondoggle} that wasted years of effort.
e.zh: 这个项目变成了一场浪费多年精力的无用工程。

bondi.t: n. 邦迪（澳大利亚悉尼海滩名）

e.en: We surfed all afternoon at {Bondi} Beach in Sydney.
e.zh: 我们整个下午都在悉尼的邦迪海滩冲浪。

e.en: The {Bondi} to Coogee coastal walk has stunning ocean views.
e.zh: 从邦迪到库吉的海岸步道海景非常壮观。

bonding.t:
n. 联结；情感联结
v. 黏合

e.en: Family camping trips are great for {bonding} with the kids.
e.zh: 全家露营旅行是和孩子增进感情的好方式。

e.en: Hydrogen {bonding} gives water its unusual properties.
e.zh: 氢键赋予了水许多独特的性质。

bonds.t: n. 债券；纽带（bond 的复数）

e.en: Treasury {bonds} are considered one of the safest investments.
e.zh: 国债被视为最安全的投资之一。

e.en: The pandemic strengthened the {bonds} between many neighbors.
e.zh: 疫情让许多邻居之间的关系变得更加紧密。

e.en: The defendant called a {bondsman} to post bail overnight.
e.zh: 被告连夜联系保释担保人帮他交保释金。

e.en: A local {bondsman} handles most cases at the county jail.
e.zh: 当地一位担保人承接县监狱的大部分保释案。

bone.t:
n. 骨头
v. 剔骨

e.en: The dog buried a {bone} in the backyard again.
e.zh: 那只狗又把一根骨头埋到了后院里。

e.en: She broke a {bone} in her wrist while skating.
e.zh: 她滑冰时摔断了手腕的一根骨头。

boned.t:
adj. 已剔骨的
v. 剔骨（过去式）

e.en: The chef {boned} the chicken before stuffing it.
e.zh: 厨师在填馅之前先把鸡剔了骨头。

e.en: This {boned} corset gives the dress its structured shape.
e.zh: 这件带骨胸衣让裙子呈现出挺括的轮廓。

e.en: Anglers travel to the Bahamas to catch {bonefish} on flats.
e.zh: 钓友们专程飞往巴哈马在浅滩钓北梭鱼。

e.en: A spooked {bonefish} can dart away in a split second.
e.zh: 受惊的北梭鱼一瞬间就能窜得无影无踪。

e.en: What a {bonehead} move to lock the keys inside.
e.zh: 把钥匙锁在车里真是蠢到家了。

e.en: Don't be a {bonehead} and skip your morning meds.
e.zh: 别犯傻,早上的药可不能漏吃。

e.en: That was a {boneheaded} decision to invest everything in crypto.
e.zh: 把全部身家投到加密货币上真是个愚蠢的决定。

e.en: He apologized for his {boneheaded} comment during the meeting.
e.zh: 他为开会时那句蠢话道了歉。

e.en: I ordered {boneless} chicken wings with extra sauce.
e.zh: 我点了无骨鸡翅,多加酱汁。

e.en: The {boneless} cut cooks faster and is easier to slice.
e.zh: 无骨肉块煮得更快,也更容易切片。

e.en: Gardeners add {bonemeal} to soil for extra phosphorus.
e.zh: 园丁会在土壤里加入骨粉来补充磷元素。

e.en: Sprinkle {bonemeal} around the roses before spring rain.
e.zh: 在春雨来临前往玫瑰花周围撒一些骨粉。

e.en: Forgetting his wife's birthday was a real {boner}.
e.zh: 忘记妻子的生日真是犯了个大错。

e.en: The reporter pulled a {boner} by misnaming the senator.
e.zh: 那位记者把参议员的名字搞错了,出了大糗。

e.en: Old {bones} ache more on cold winter mornings.
e.zh: 上了年纪的骨头在冬日清晨更容易酸痛。

e.en: Archaeologists uncovered dinosaur {bones} near the riverbed.
e.zh: 考古学家在河床附近发现了恐龙骨骼。

e.en: Herbalists once brewed {boneset} tea to fight fevers.
e.zh: 草药师过去会用泽兰煮茶来退烧。

e.en: {Boneset} grows wild along damp meadow edges.
e.zh: 泽兰在潮湿的草甸边缘野生生长。

boney.t: adj. 多骨的；瘦骨嶙峋的

e.en: The stray cat looked thin and {boney} after winter.
e.zh: 那只流浪猫熬过冬天后看起来又瘦又骨感。

e.en: He extended a {boney} finger toward the dusty book.
e.zh: 他朝那本布满灰尘的书伸出一根瘦骨嶙峋的手指。

e.en: Old planes end up in the desert {boneyard} in Arizona.
e.zh: 老旧飞机最终都被送到亚利桑那的飞机坟场。

e.en: The shipyard's {boneyard} is full of rusting tankers.
e.zh: 造船厂的废船场里堆满了生锈的油轮。

e.en: We roasted marshmallows around the beach {bonfire} all night.
e.zh: 我们围着海滩篝火烤了一整晚棉花糖。

e.en: The village holds a {bonfire} on the autumn equinox.
e.zh: 村里在秋分那天会燃起一堆篝火。

bong.t: n. 水烟筒（吸食大麻用具）

e.en: Police confiscated a {bong} during the dorm room search.
e.zh: 警方在搜查宿舍时没收了一支水烟枪。

e.en: The clock tower's deep {bong} echoed across the square.
e.zh: 钟楼低沉的钟声在广场上回响。

e.en: He tapped a quick rhythm on the {bongo} drums.
e.zh: 他在邦戈鼓上敲出一段快速的节奏。

e.en: Street musicians played a {bongo} beat near the fountain.
e.zh: 街头艺人在喷泉边敲打着邦戈鼓的节拍。

e.en: The pub was filled with laughter and easy {bonhomie}.
e.zh: 酒吧里充满了笑声和轻松融洽的气氛。

e.en: His natural {bonhomie} made every guest feel welcome.
e.zh: 他天生的好脾气让每位客人都倍感温暖。

boniface.t: n. 旅店老板；博尼费斯（人名）

e.en: The cheerful {boniface} greeted travelers at the country inn.
e.zh: 乡村客栈那位热情的店主迎接着每位旅客。

e.en: Saint {Boniface} is honored as the apostle of Germany.
e.zh: 圣博尼法斯被尊为德国的使徒。

e.en: Japanese broth gets its umami from dried {bonito} flakes.
e.zh: 日式高汤的鲜味来自干鲣鱼片。

e.en: Anglers landed several {bonito} off the coast today.
e.zh: 钓友们今天在海岸边钓上了好几条鲣鱼。

e.en: The waiter greeted us with a cheerful {bonjour}.
e.zh: 服务员愉快地对我们说了一句你好。

e.en: She practiced saying {bonjour} before her trip to Paris.
e.zh: 她在去巴黎前练习说你好这句法语。

e.en: Be careful not to {bonk} your head on the cabinet.
e.zh: 小心别把头撞到柜子上。

e.en: Marathon runners often {bonk} around the thirty-kilometer mark.
e.zh: 马拉松选手常在三十公里左右出现体力崩溃。

e.en: That last episode was a total {bonker} of a finale.
e.zh: 最后那集结局简直疯狂到爆。

e.en: He's a real {bonker} when it comes to vintage cars.
e.zh: 一谈到老爷车,他就是个十足的狂热分子。

e.en: {Bonn} served as West Germany's capital until reunification.
e.zh: 波恩在两德统一之前一直是西德的首都。

e.en: Beethoven was born in {Bonn} in 1770.
e.zh: 贝多芬于1770年出生在波恩。

e.en: She wished her colleagues {bonne} chance before the launch.
e.zh: 产品发布前她祝同事们好运。

e.en: The waiter said {bonne} nuit as we left the bistro.
e.zh: 我们离开小餐馆时服务员道了一声晚安。

bonnet.t: n. 软帽；（英）汽车引擎盖

e.en: The baby wore a pink {bonnet} to shield her eyes.
e.zh: 小宝宝戴着粉色的小帽子遮挡阳光。

e.en: Steam poured from under the car's {bonnet} on the highway.
e.zh: 高速公路上汽车引擎盖下冒出阵阵蒸汽。

bonny.t: adj. 漂亮的；健康可爱的

e.en: What a {bonny} baby you have there!
e.zh: 你这宝宝长得真俊俏!

e.en: They strolled through the {bonny} hills of Scotland.
e.zh: 他们漫步在苏格兰秀丽的山间。

e.en: The lawyer took the immigration case pro {bono}.
e.zh: 那位律师免费接下了这起移民案件。

e.en: {Bono} performed a surprise set at the charity gala.
e.zh: 波诺在慈善晚会上即兴表演了一段。

e.en: The {bonobo} shares about ninety-eight percent of human DNA.
e.zh: 倭黑猩猩与人类约百分之九十八的DNA相同。

e.en: Researchers study how the {bonobo} resolves conflicts peacefully.
e.zh: 研究人员研究倭黑猩猩如何和平化解冲突。

e.en: He spent years shaping the tiny {bonsai} on his desk.
e.zh: 他花了好几年时间修剪桌上那盆小盆景。

e.en: A well-pruned {bonsai} can live for over a century.
e.zh: 一盆修剪得当的盆景可以活上一百多年。

e.en: Everyone on the team got a year-end {bonus} this year.
e.zh: 今年团队每个人都拿到了年终奖。

e.en: Free shipping is a nice {bonus} when buying online.
e.zh: 网购时免运费是个不错的额外福利。

e.en: Executives received record {bonuses} despite layoffs at the company.
e.zh: 尽管公司裁员,高管们却拿到了创纪录的奖金。

e.en: Sign-up {bonuses} attract many new credit card customers.
e.zh: 开卡奖励吸引了许多新的信用卡客户。

e.en: The old man's {bony} hands trembled as he wrote.
e.zh: 那位老人写字时瘦削的双手微微颤抖。

e.en: This fish is too {bony} for my picky kids.
e.zh: 这条鱼刺太多,我那挑食的孩子吃不了。

e.en: That stunt was completely {bonzo}, even by his standards.
e.zh: 那个特技就连按他的标准也疯狂得离谱。

e.en: The crowd went {bonzo} when the band returned for an encore.
e.zh: 乐队返场加演时观众全都疯狂了。

boo.t:
int. 嘘（倒喝彩）
n. 宝贝（爱称）

e.en: The audience started to {boo} when the singer went off-key.
e.zh: 歌手跑调时观众开始嘘声四起。

e.en: He jumped out and yelled {boo} to scare his sister.
e.zh: 他跳出来大喊一声哇,把妹妹吓了一跳。

e.en: I made a total {boob} of myself at karaoke last night.
e.zh: 昨晚K歌时我彻底出了大丑。

e.en: Don't be a {boob} — read the instructions before assembling.
e.zh: 别犯傻,组装前先看说明书。

e.en: The thief triggered a {booby} trap and dropped the loot.
e.zh: 小偷触发了机关陷阱,赃物掉了一地。

e.en: The blue-footed {booby} dives spectacularly for fish.
e.zh: 蓝脚鲣鸟会以壮观的姿态扎入水中捕鱼。

boogaloo.t: n. 布加洛舞（一种舞曲）

e.en: The dancers broke into a funky {boogaloo} on stage.
e.zh: 舞者在台上跳起了一段动感十足的布加洛舞。

e.en: Latin {boogaloo} fused soul with mambo in the sixties.
e.zh: 拉丁布加洛在六十年代将灵魂乐与曼波融合在一起。

e.en: The toddler picked a {booger} and showed it to grandma.
e.zh: 小娃娃挖出一颗鼻屎给奶奶看。

e.en: Wipe that {booger} off your sleeve before the photo.
e.zh: 拍照前把袖子上的鼻屎擦掉。

boogeyman.t: n. 妖怪；吓唬小孩的怪物

e.en: Inflation has become the {boogeyman} of every campaign speech.
e.zh: 通胀已成了每场竞选演讲里的可怕妖怪。

e.en: He told the kids the {boogeyman} hides under messy beds.
e.zh: 他告诉孩子们妖怪会躲在乱糟糟的床底下。

boogie.t:
n. 布基舞
v. 跳舞，狂欢

e.en: Let's {boogie} on the dance floor all night long.
e.zh: 咱们整晚在舞池里尽情跳舞吧。

e.en: The kids started to {boogie} when the music came on.
e.zh: 音乐一响,孩子们就开始扭动起舞。

booing.t:
n. 喝倒彩
v. 发嘘声（现在分词）

e.en: The crowd was {booing} loudly after the missed penalty.
e.zh: 罚球失误后,观众大声发出嘘声。

e.en: Fans kept {booing} the referee throughout the match.
e.zh: 球迷整场比赛都在向裁判喝倒彩。

boonies.t: n. 偏远地区；穷乡僻壤

e.en: They moved out to the {boonies} to escape the city noise.
e.zh: 他们搬到了偏远乡下，逃离城市的喧嚣。

e.en: Cell service is terrible way out here in the {boonies}.
e.zh: 在这种偏远地方，手机信号差得很。

boor.t: n. 粗鲁的人；没教养的人

e.en: He acted like a complete {boor} at the dinner party.
e.zh: 他在晚宴上表现得像个粗鲁无礼的人。

e.en: Nobody wants to sit next to that loud {boor} on the plane.
e.zh: 飞机上没人想坐在那个吵闹粗鲁的人旁边。

e.en: His {boorish} comments embarrassed everyone at the meeting.
e.zh: 他粗鲁的言论让会议上所有人都很尴尬。

e.en: She apologized for her brother's {boorish} behavior at the wedding.
e.zh: 她为弟弟在婚礼上粗鲁的举止道歉。

boost.t:
v. 提升；推动
n. 促进；增长

e.en: Coffee gives me the {boost} I need every morning.
e.zh: 每天早上咖啡给我所需要的提神效果。

e.en: The new ad campaign should {boost} our sales significantly.
e.zh: 新的广告活动应该会大幅提升我们的销量。

boosted.t: v. 提升（boost 的过去式）

e.en: The promotion {boosted} her confidence at work.
e.zh: 这次升职大大提升了她在工作中的自信心。

e.en: Streaming has {boosted} the popularity of indie musicians.
e.zh: 流媒体让独立音乐人的人气大大提升。

booster.t:
n. 助推器；增效剂
n. 支持者

e.en: She got her flu vaccine {booster} last week.
e.zh: 她上周打了流感疫苗的加强针。

e.en: His best friend has always been his biggest {booster}.
e.zh: 他最好的朋友一直是他最坚定的支持者。

boosterism.t: n. 极力鼓吹；吹捧宣传

e.en: The mayor's speech was full of empty {boosterism} about the city.
e.zh: 市长的演讲充满了对这座城市空洞的吹捧。

e.en: Local {boosterism} helped attract new businesses to downtown.
e.zh: 当地的大力宣传帮助吸引了新企业入驻市中心。

boosting.t:
v. 提升中
n. 增强（机器学习方法）

e.en: The company is {boosting} salaries to retain top engineers.
e.zh: 公司正在提高薪资以留住顶尖工程师。

e.en: Regular exercise is great for {boosting} your mood.
e.zh: 经常锻炼对提升心情非常有效。

boosts.t: v./n. 提升（boost 的复数或第三人称）

e.en: A good night's sleep {boosts} your immune system.
e.zh: 一夜好眠能增强你的免疫系统。

e.en: The app got several {boosts} in downloads after the update.
e.zh: 应用更新后下载量获得了几次大幅提升。

boot.t:
v. 启动（电脑）
n. 靴子

e.en: My laptop takes forever to {boot} up these days.
e.zh: 我的笔记本电脑现在开机慢得要命。

e.en: She slipped on her left {boot} before heading outside.
e.zh: 她穿上左脚的靴子，然后走出门去。

bootable.t: adj. 可引导启动的（系统/磁盘）

e.en: You'll need a {bootable} USB drive to install the operating system.
e.zh: 你需要一个可启动的 U 盘来安装操作系统。

e.en: The technician created a {bootable} disk for system recovery.
e.zh: 技术员制作了一张用于系统恢复的可启动盘。

booted.t:
v. 已启动（boot 的过去式）
adj. 穿靴的

e.en: He {booted} up his computer and checked his email.
e.zh: 他启动了电脑，查看了邮件。

e.en: The bouncer {booted} the rowdy customer out of the bar.
e.zh: 保安把那个吵闹的顾客赶出了酒吧。

e.en: Grandma knitted a tiny pink {bootee} for the new baby.
e.zh: 奶奶为新生宝宝织了一只粉色小婴儿鞋。

e.en: One {bootee} fell off in the stroller during the walk.
e.zh: 散步时有一只婴儿软鞋掉在了婴儿车里。

booth.t: n. 小隔间；展位；电话亭

e.en: Let's grab a quiet {booth} at the back of the diner.
e.zh: 我们去餐厅后面找个安静的卡座吧。

e.en: She voted at the polling {booth} early in the morning.
e.zh: 她一大早就到投票站投了票。

e.en: The conference had dozens of company {booths} showcasing new products.
e.zh: 会议上有几十个公司展位在展示新产品。

e.en: All the {booths} at the diner were packed on Sunday morning.
e.zh: 周日早上餐厅所有的卡座都坐满了。

e.en: She wore a stylish ankle {bootie} with her dress.
e.zh: 她穿着一双时髦的短靴搭配连衣裙。

e.en: The baby kicked off one {bootie} during her nap.
e.zh: 宝宝午睡时踢掉了一只小袜套。

e.en: He knelt down to tie a loose {bootlace} before the hike.
e.zh: 徒步之前他蹲下系紧了松开的鞋带。

e.en: My {bootlace} snapped just as I was leaving the house.
e.zh: 我刚要出门，鞋带就断了。

e.en: The ferry from Liverpool stops near {Bootle} on the Mersey.
e.zh: 从利物浦出发的渡轮在默西河边的布特尔附近停靠。

e.en: She grew up in {Bootle} before moving to London.
e.zh: 她在布特尔长大，后来搬到了伦敦。

bootleg.t:
adj. 盗版的；非法的
n. 走私货

e.en: He bought a {bootleg} copy of the concert online.
e.zh: 他在网上买了一份盗版的演唱会录像。

e.en: The market was full of {bootleg} designer handbags.
e.zh: 市场上到处都是仿冒的名牌手袋。

bootlegged.t: v. 非法贩卖；盗录（过去式）

e.en: Fans {bootlegged} the live show and shared it online.
e.zh: 粉丝们偷录了现场演出，并把它发到了网上。

e.en: The album was widely {bootlegged} before its official release.
e.zh: 这张专辑在正式发行前就被广泛盗版了。

e.en: His grandfather was a {bootlegger} during Prohibition.
e.zh: 他的祖父在禁酒令时期是个私酒贩子。

e.en: The {bootlegger} sold pirated DVDs out of his car trunk.
e.zh: 那个盗版商从车后备箱里卖盗版 DVD。

e.en: After hours of arguing, his efforts proved {bootless}.
e.zh: 争论了几个小时后，他的努力被证明是徒劳的。

e.en: It's {bootless} to complain when no one is listening.
e.zh: 在没人听的时候抱怨是毫无用处的。

e.en: The old {bootmaker} hand-stitched every pair in his shop.
e.zh: 那位老靴匠在店里手工缝制每一双靴子。

e.en: She ordered custom riding boots from a famous {bootmaker}.
e.zh: 她从一位著名的靴匠那里定制了一双骑马靴。

boots.t:
n. 靴子（复数）
v. 启动（第三人称）

e.en: His muddy {boots} left footprints all across the kitchen floor.
e.zh: 他沾满泥的靴子在厨房地板上留下了一串脚印。

e.en: She bought new winter {boots} for the hiking trip.
e.zh: 她为徒步旅行买了一双新的冬季靴子。

bootstrap.t:
v. 自举；引导启动
n. 靴襻；自助程序

e.en: They had to {bootstrap} the startup with their own savings.
e.zh: 他们不得不靠自己的积蓄白手起家创办这家公司。

e.en: The script will {bootstrap} the entire development environment automatically.
e.zh: 这个脚本会自动初始化整个开发环境。

bootstrapping.t: n. 自举；引导启动；自助创业

e.en: She's {bootstrapping} her company without any outside investors.
e.zh: 她正在不依靠外部投资者地白手起家创办公司。

e.en: The framework handles {bootstrapping} the application on startup.
e.zh: 这个框架会在启动时负责初始化应用程序。

booty.t:
n. 战利品；赃物
n. 屁股（俚）

e.en: The pirates buried their {booty} on a deserted island.
e.zh: 海盗们把他们的战利品埋在了一座荒岛上。

e.en: Kids counted their Halloween candy {booty} after trick-or-treating.
e.zh: 孩子们要完糖后清点了他们万圣节的糖果战利品。

booze.t:
n. 酒（口语）
v. 狂饮

e.en: They stocked up on {booze} for the weekend party.
e.zh: 他们为周末派对囤了一堆酒。

e.en: He decided to quit {booze} for a healthier lifestyle.
e.zh: 为了更健康的生活方式，他决定戒酒。

e.en: Her uncle is a real {boozer} who drinks every night.
e.zh: 她叔叔是个真正的酒鬼，每晚都喝酒。

e.en: They met up at the local {boozer} after work.
e.zh: 他们下班后在当地的小酒馆碰面。

e.en: They had a {boozy} brunch with bottomless mimosas on Sunday.
e.zh: 他们周日吃了顿酒精满满、无限续杯的早午餐。

e.en: The party turned into a {boozy} night of karaoke.
e.zh: 这场派对变成了一个酒气熏天的卡拉 OK 之夜。

bop.t:
n. 波普爵士乐
v. 轻击；跳舞

e.en: She likes to {bop} along to her favorite playlist.
e.zh: 她喜欢跟着她最爱的歌单晃动身体。

e.en: That new song is a total {bop} — I love it!
e.zh: 那首新歌真是首神曲——我超喜欢！

bophuthatswana.t: n. 博普塔茨瓦纳（南非旧部族区）

e.en: {Bophuthatswana} was a former homeland in apartheid-era South Africa.
e.zh: 博普塔茨瓦纳是南非种族隔离时期的一个前黑人家园。

e.en: Sun City was the famous resort in {Bophuthatswana} during the 1980s.
e.zh: 太阳城是上世纪 80 年代博普塔茨瓦纳著名的度假胜地。

bopper.t: n. 爱跳舞的人；波普乐手

e.en: The mall was full of teen {bopper} fans waiting for the singer.
e.zh: 商场里挤满了等待那位歌手的少女追星族。

e.en: She was a typical teeny {bopper} obsessed with boy bands.
e.zh: 她是个典型的迷恋男子团体的少女追星族。

e.en: She added fresh {borage} flowers to the summer salad.
e.zh: 她在夏日沙拉里加了几朵新鲜的琉璃苣花。

e.en: {Borage} grows easily in the herb garden and attracts bees.
e.zh: 琉璃苣在香草园里很好种，还能吸引蜜蜂。

e.en: The cleaner contains a small amount of {borate} for stain removal.
e.zh: 这种清洁剂含有少量硼酸盐用于去除污渍。

e.en: Scientists tested the lake water for {borate} concentrations.
e.zh: 科学家们检测了湖水中的硼酸盐浓度。

e.en: She uses {borax} as a natural laundry booster.
e.zh: 她用硼砂作为天然的洗衣增效剂。

e.en: Mix {borax} with sugar to make a homemade ant trap.
e.zh: 把硼砂和糖混在一起就能自制蚂蚁诱捕剂。

bordeaux.t: n. 波尔多（法国城市/葡萄酒）

e.en: They opened a fine bottle of {Bordeaux} for the anniversary dinner.
e.zh: 他们为周年纪念晚餐开了一瓶上好的波尔多葡萄酒。

e.en: We spent a week touring vineyards in {Bordeaux} last summer.
e.zh: 去年夏天我们花了一周时间游览波尔多的葡萄园。

e.en: The old building was rumored to have once been a {bordello}.
e.zh: 据传这栋老建筑曾经是一家妓院。

e.en: The novel is set in a 19th-century New Orleans {bordello}.
e.zh: 这部小说的背景设定在 19 世纪新奥尔良的一家妓院。

border.t:
n. 边界；边框
v. 接壤；毗邻

e.en: They crossed the {border} into Canada early Sunday morning.
e.zh: 他们周日清晨越过边境进入了加拿大。

e.en: A small fence {border} separates the two backyards.
e.zh: 一道小栅栏边界把两家的后院隔开了。

bordered.t:
adj. 有边框的
v. 接壤（过去式）

e.en: The garden is {bordered} by tall hedges on three sides.
e.zh: 这座花园三面都有高高的树篱环绕。

e.en: His comments {bordered} on outright rudeness.
e.zh: 他的评论近乎彻头彻尾的无礼。

e.en: His ancestors were Scottish {borderer} families famous for cattle raids.
e.zh: 他的祖先是以劫掠牛群闻名的苏格兰边境家族。

e.en: The {borderer} clans fought for centuries along the Anglo-Scottish frontier.
e.zh: 边境氏族在英格兰和苏格兰边界沿线斗争了几个世纪。

e.en: France is one of several countries {bordering} Germany.
e.zh: 法国是与德国接壤的几个国家之一。

e.en: Her excitement was {bordering} on hysteria after the announcement.
e.zh: 宣布消息后，她的兴奋几乎到了歇斯底里的程度。

borderland.t: n. 边境地区；交界地带

e.en: They grew up in the {borderland} between Texas and Mexico.
e.zh: 他们在德克萨斯州和墨西哥的边境地带长大。

e.en: His research focuses on the cultural {borderland} between two nations.
e.zh: 他的研究关注两国之间的文化交界地带。

borderless.t: adj. 无边界的；无边框的

e.en: The internet has created a truly {borderless} global marketplace.
e.zh: 互联网创造了一个真正无国界的全球市场。

e.en: She loves the {borderless} layout of the new photo app.
e.zh: 她喜欢新照片应用那种无边框的布局。

borderline.t:
adj. 边缘的；勉强的
n. 分界线

e.en: His test score was {borderline}, so he had to retake it.
e.zh: 他的考试成绩处于及格边缘，所以不得不补考。

e.en: That joke was {borderline} offensive to a lot of people.
e.zh: 那个笑话对很多人来说几乎到了冒犯的程度。

borders.t:
n. 边界（复数）
v. 接壤（第三人称）

e.en: The country shares {borders} with five other nations.
e.zh: 这个国家与其他五个国家接壤。

e.en: Climate change knows no {borders} and affects everyone.
e.zh: 气候变化无国界，影响着每一个人。

bore.t:
v. 使厌烦；钻孔
n. 讨厌的人

e.en: That three-hour meeting was a complete {bore}.
e.zh: 那场三小时的会议简直无聊透顶。

e.en: Long flights {bore} me unless I have a good book.
e.zh: 长途飞行让我感到无聊，除非有本好书。

e.en: The {boreal} forests of Canada store huge amounts of carbon.
e.zh: 加拿大的北方针叶林储存着大量的碳。

e.en: Many migratory birds nest in the {boreal} regions each summer.
e.zh: 许多候鸟每年夏天都在北方地区筑巢。

e.en: The kids got {bored} after only ten minutes of the museum.
e.zh: 孩子们在博物馆里待了十分钟就觉得无聊了。

e.en: I'm so {bored} — there's nothing good on TV tonight.
e.zh: 我无聊死了——今晚电视上没什么好节目。

e.en: Out of pure {boredom}, I started reorganizing my closet.
e.zh: 纯粹是因为无聊，我开始整理衣柜。

e.en: Long meetings often trigger a deep sense of {boredom}.
e.zh: 冗长的会议常常让人感到深深的厌倦。

e.en: The endless {boredoms} of quarantine pushed many to learn new hobbies.
e.zh: 隔离期间无尽的乏味让许多人去学新爱好。

e.en: He described the small {boredoms} of office life with humor.
e.zh: 他幽默地描写了办公室生活中那些琐碎的无聊。

e.en: The team visited {Boreham} for a weekend training camp.
e.zh: 球队前往博勒姆进行周末集训。

e.en: {Boreham} is a quiet village in Essex, England.
e.zh: 博勒姆是英格兰埃塞克斯郡的一个安静村庄。

e.en: Engineers drilled a {borehole} to test the soil quality.
e.zh: 工程师钻了一个钻孔以检测土壤质量。

e.en: The village relies on a deep {borehole} for clean water.
e.zh: 这个村庄依靠一口深井获取清洁饮用水。

e.en: The emerald ash {borer} has destroyed millions of trees.
e.zh: 翠绿色的白蜡窄吉丁已毁掉了数百万棵树。

e.en: He used a {borer} to make precise holes in the metal.
e.zh: 他用钻孔器在金属上打出精确的孔。

bores.t:
v. bore 的第三人称单数
n. 讨厌的人（复数）

e.en: That long lecture really {bores} the entire class.
e.zh: 那场冗长的讲座让全班都觉得无聊。

e.en: The carpenter {bores} small holes for the screws.
e.zh: 木匠为螺丝钻出小孔。

borg.t: n. 博格（姓氏；《星际迷航》博格人）

e.en: In Star Trek, the {Borg} assimilate other species into their collective.
e.zh: 在《星际迷航》中，博格人将其他种族同化进集体意识。

e.en: Björn {Borg} dominated tennis in the late 1970s.
e.zh: 比约·博格在七十年代末统治了网球界。

borgia.t: n. 博尔吉亚（意大利家族姓氏）

e.en: The {Borgia} family wielded enormous power in Renaissance Italy.
e.zh: 博尔吉亚家族在文艺复兴时期的意大利权势滔天。

e.en: A new drama series explores the scandals of the {Borgia} popes.
e.zh: 一部新剧探讨了博尔吉亚教皇们的丑闻。

e.en: Pharmacists sometimes recommend {boric} acid for minor eye irritation.
e.zh: 药剂师有时会推荐用硼酸缓解轻微眼部刺激。

e.en: {Boric} acid powder is a common household pest control.
e.zh: 硼酸粉是常见的家用杀虫剂。

boring.t:
adj. 无聊的；乏味的
n. 钻孔

e.en: The movie was so {boring} that I fell asleep halfway through.
e.zh: 这部电影太无聊了，我看到一半就睡着了。

e.en: Crews are {boring} a tunnel beneath the river.
e.zh: 工人们正在河底下钻挖一条隧道。

e.en: He explained the rules {boringly}, putting everyone to sleep.
e.zh: 他枯燥地解释规则，听得大家昏昏欲睡。

e.en: The food was {boringly} predictable, just rice and chicken again.
e.zh: 食物乏味得毫无新意，又是米饭加鸡肉。

e.en: {Borland} once dominated the developer tools market in the 1990s.
e.zh: 宝兰公司曾在九十年代主导开发者工具市场。

e.en: Many old-school programmers learned C++ using {Borland} compilers.
e.zh: 许多老派程序员是用宝兰编译器学的 C++。

born.t:
adj. 出生的；天生的
v. bear 的过去分词

e.en: She was {born} in a small town near the coast.
e.zh: 她出生在沿海附近的一个小镇。

e.en: He's a {born} leader who inspires everyone around him.
e.zh: 他是个天生的领导者，能激励身边每个人。

borne.t: v. bear 的过去分词（承受、生育）

e.en: The costs were {borne} entirely by the local government.
e.zh: 这些费用完全由地方政府承担。

e.en: Mosquito-{borne} diseases spread quickly during the rainy season.
e.zh: 蚊媒疾病在雨季迅速传播。

e.en: The rainforests of {Borneo} are home to wild orangutans.
e.zh: 婆罗洲的雨林是野生猩猩的家园。

e.en: We took a riverboat trip deep into {Borneo} last summer.
e.zh: 去年夏天我们乘船深入婆罗洲腹地。

e.en: The old farmhouse still has its original {borning} room.
e.zh: 那座老农舍仍保留着原来的产房。

e.en: In colonial homes, the {borning} room was used for childbirth.
e.zh: 在殖民时期的家中，产房专门用来分娩。

e.en: The {Borns} family hosted Thanksgiving dinner this year.
e.zh: 今年感恩节晚餐由博恩斯一家主办。

e.en: Max {Borns} contributions to physics earned him a Nobel Prize.
e.zh: 马克斯·玻恩对物理学的贡献为他赢得了诺贝尔奖。

e.en: Japanese {boro} textiles are patched together from old indigo cloth.
e.zh: 日本的襤褸织物是用旧蓝染布拼缝而成的。

e.en: Middlesbrough fans affectionately call their team the {Boro}.
e.zh: 米德尔斯堡球迷亲切地称他们的球队为 Boro。

e.en: {Boron} is an essential micronutrient for healthy plant growth.
e.zh: 硼是植物健康生长所必需的微量元素。

e.en: Rocket fuels sometimes contain {boron} for higher energy output.
e.zh: 火箭燃料有时含硼以提供更高能量。

e.en: Brooklyn is the most populous {borough} in New York City.
e.zh: 布鲁克林是纽约市人口最多的行政区。

e.en: The {borough} council voted to expand the bike lanes.
e.zh: 区议会投票通过扩建自行车道。

e.en: Can I {borrow} your charger for a few minutes?
e.zh: 我能借你的充电器用几分钟吗？

e.en: Many writers {borrow} ideas from earlier works.
e.zh: 许多作家会借鉴早期作品中的灵感。

borrowed.t:
adj. 借来的
v. borrow 的过去式

e.en: I {borrowed} a book from the library yesterday afternoon.
e.zh: 我昨天下午从图书馆借了一本书。

e.en: The song {borrowed} its melody from an old folk tune.
e.zh: 这首歌的旋律借鉴了一首古老的民谣。

e.en: Each {borrower} must show valid ID at the loan desk.
e.zh: 每位借阅者都必须在借书台出示有效证件。

e.en: Rising interest rates make life harder for every {borrower}.
e.zh: 利率上升让每个借款人的日子都更难过。

borrowing.t:
n. 借贷；借用词
v. borrow 的现在分词

e.en: Government {borrowing} has reached a record high this quarter.
e.zh: 本季度政府借款已达到历史新高。

e.en: She's {borrowing} my laptop while hers is being repaired.
e.zh: 她的笔记本送修期间正借用我的。

borrows.t: v. borrow 的第三人称单数

e.en: He always {borrows} my umbrella and forgets to return it.
e.zh: 他总是借我的伞，然后忘了还。

e.en: This design {borrows} heavily from Scandinavian minimalism.
e.zh: 这个设计大量借鉴了北欧极简主义风格。

borscht.t: n. 罗宋汤（俄式甜菜汤）

e.en: My grandmother makes the best {borscht} with fresh beets.
e.zh: 我外婆用新鲜甜菜做的罗宋汤最好喝。

e.en: A bowl of hot {borscht} is perfect for cold winter nights.
e.zh: 一碗热腾腾的罗宋汤最适合寒冷的冬夜。

e.en: He spent two years in a {borstal} as a teenager.
e.zh: 他十几岁时在少年管教所待了两年。

e.en: The old {borstal} system was abolished in Britain in 1982.
e.zh: 英国旧的少年感化院制度在1982年被废除。

e.en: The {borzoi} ran across the field with elegant, sweeping strides.
e.zh: 那只俄罗斯猎狼犬以优雅的大步跑过田野。

e.en: A {borzoi} needs daily exercise and plenty of open space.
e.zh: 俄罗斯猎狼犬需要每天运动和宽阔的空间。

e.en: My new {Bosch} dishwasher is incredibly quiet during operation.
e.zh: 我新买的博世洗碗机运转时非常安静。

e.en: Hieronymus {Bosch} painted surreal religious scenes in vivid detail.
e.zh: 希罗尼穆斯·博斯绘制了细节生动的超现实宗教画作。

e.en: My {Bose} headphones cancel out almost all airplane noise.
e.zh: 我的 Bose 耳机几乎能消除所有飞机噪音。

e.en: Satyendra Nath {Bose} contributed foundational work to quantum statistics.
e.zh: 萨特延德拉·纳特·玻色为量子统计学奠定了基础工作。

e.en: {Bosnia} declared independence from Yugoslavia in 1992.
e.zh: 波斯尼亚于1992年宣布从南斯拉夫独立。

e.en: We hiked through stunning mountain trails in central {Bosnia}.
e.zh: 我们在波斯尼亚中部徒步走过令人惊叹的山间小径。

bosnian.t:
adj. 波斯尼亚的
n. 波斯尼亚人

e.en: She speaks fluent {Bosnian} and three other Balkan languages.
e.zh: 她说一口流利的波斯尼亚语，还会另外三种巴尔干语言。

e.en: The restaurant serves authentic {Bosnian} cuisine in downtown Chicago.
e.zh: 那家餐厅在芝加哥市中心提供地道的波斯尼亚美食。

bosom.t:
n. 胸部；内心
adj. 知心的

e.en: She held the puppy close to her {bosom} for warmth.
e.zh: 她把小狗紧紧抱在胸前取暖。

e.en: They have been {bosom} friends since elementary school.
e.zh: 他们从小学起就是知心好友。

e.en: The character was described as a tall, {bosomy} woman in red.
e.zh: 那个角色被描述为一位身材高挑、丰满的红衣女子。

e.en: The portrait depicted a {bosomy} opera singer in full costume.
e.zh: 那幅肖像描绘了一位身着盛装、丰满的歌剧女演员。

e.en: The Higgs {boson} was finally detected at CERN in 2012.
e.zh: 希格斯玻色子最终在2012年于欧洲核子研究中心被探测到。

e.en: Every {boson} carries one of the fundamental forces of nature.
e.zh: 每种玻色子都承载着自然界的一种基本作用力。

boss.t:
n. 老板；上司
v. 指挥

e.en: My {boss} approved the vacation request without any questions.
e.zh: 我老板没问任何问题就批准了我的休假申请。

e.en: The final {boss} in this game is incredibly difficult to beat.
e.zh: 这款游戏的最终 BOSS 极难打败。

bosses.t:
n. boss 的复数
v. 指挥（第三人称单数）

e.en: Good {bosses} listen carefully to feedback from their teams.
e.zh: 好的上司会认真倾听团队的反馈。

e.en: You'll face three {bosses} before reaching the final level.
e.zh: 在到达最终关卡前你会遇到三个 BOSS。

e.en: Her {bossiness} sometimes annoys her quieter coworkers.
e.zh: 她颐指气使的态度有时会惹恼那些比较安静的同事。

e.en: The toddler's adorable {bossiness} kept everyone laughing all afternoon.
e.zh: 那个小孩可爱的霸道劲儿让大家笑了一下午。

bossy.t: adj. 爱指挥人的；专横的

e.en: Don't be so {bossy} — let everyone share their ideas.
e.zh: 别那么霸道，让大家都说说自己的想法。

e.en: My older sister is incredibly {bossy} when planning family trips.
e.zh: 我姐姐在策划家庭旅行时特别爱发号施令。

e.en: {Boston} is famous for its rich history and Ivy League schools.
e.zh: 波士顿以悠久的历史和常春藤名校闻名。

e.en: We caught a Red Sox game while visiting {Boston} last weekend.
e.zh: 上周末我们去波士顿旅行时看了红袜队的比赛。

bostonian.t:
n. 波士顿人
adj. 波士顿的

e.en: As a true {Bostonian}, she swears the chowder is unmatched.
e.zh: 作为一个地道的波士顿人，她坚称这里的浓汤无与伦比。

e.en: His {Bostonian} accent gave away his hometown immediately.
e.zh: 他的波士顿口音立刻暴露了他的家乡。

bosun.t: n. 水手长（boatswain 的缩写）

e.en: The {bosun} blew his whistle to signal the morning watch.
e.zh: 水手长吹响哨子，宣告晨班开始。

e.en: Every sailor respected the experienced {bosun} on board.
e.zh: 船上每个水手都敬重这位经验丰富的水手长。

e.en: James {Boswell} wrote the famous biography of Samuel Johnson.
e.zh: 詹姆斯·鲍斯威尔撰写了塞缪尔·约翰逊的著名传记。

e.en: Every great leader needs a loyal {Boswell} to record their words.
e.zh: 每位伟人都需要一个忠实的鲍斯威尔来记录他们的言论。

bosworth.t: n. 博斯沃思（地名/姓氏）

e.en: Richard III was killed at the Battle of {Bosworth} in 1485.
e.zh: 理查三世于1485年在博斯沃思战役中阵亡。

e.en: Tourists visit the {Bosworth} battlefield to learn medieval history.
e.zh: 游客们参观博斯沃思战场以了解中世纪历史。

bot.t: n. 机器人程序；自动程序（robot 的缩写）

e.en: A customer service {bot} answered my question within seconds.
e.zh: 一个客服机器人在几秒钟内就回答了我的问题。

e.en: Most of the spam messages came from a single {bot} account.
e.zh: 大多数垃圾消息都来自同一个机器人账号。

boule.t:
n. 晶棒（单晶培育体）
n. 议会（古希腊）

bounce.t:
v. 弹跳；反弹
n. 跳回

bounced.t: v. 弹起（bounce 的过去式）

bounces.t: v. 弹跳（第三人称单数）

bouncing.t:
v. 弹跳中
adj. 活泼健康的

e.en: The toddler loves jumping on the {bouncy} castle at parties.
e.zh: 那个小孩很喜欢在派对上的充气城堡里蹦跳。

e.en: She has a {bouncy} personality that lifts everyone's mood.
e.zh: 她性格活泼,能让大家心情变好。

bound.t:
adj. 必定的；受束缚的
n. 界限

e.en: This train is {bound} for Shanghai and leaves at noon.
e.zh: 这趟列车开往上海,中午发车。

e.en: He is {bound} by contract to finish the project.
e.zh: 他受合同约束必须完成这个项目。

e.en: Healthy relationships require clear personal {boundaries}.
e.zh: 健康的关系需要清晰的个人界限。

e.en: The fence marks the {boundaries} of our property.
e.zh: 这道栅栏标出了我们房产的边界。

e.en: The river forms a natural {boundary} between the two countries.
e.zh: 这条河是两国之间的天然分界线。

e.en: Setting a {boundary} with coworkers is not rude.
e.zh: 和同事划定界限并不是失礼。

e.en: The garden is {bounded} by a low stone wall.
e.zh: 花园四周由一道矮石墙围着。

e.en: Our budget for the trip is strictly {bounded}.
e.zh: 我们这次旅行的预算有严格上限。

e.en: It is my {bounden} duty to protect my family.
e.zh: 保护家人是我义不容辞的责任。

e.en: She felt a {bounden} obligation to repay the favor.
e.zh: 她觉得有不可推卸的义务要回报这份恩情。

e.en: That charming {bounder} cheated several investors out of money.
e.zh: 那个迷人的无赖骗走了好几位投资者的钱。

e.en: The novel's villain is a classic Victorian {bounder}.
e.zh: 小说里的反派是个典型的维多利亚式恶棍。

bounding.t:
v. 跳跃
adj. 限定的

e.en: The dog came {bounding} across the field to greet me.
e.zh: 那只狗欢快地跳跃着穿过田野来迎接我。

e.en: Draw a {bounding} box around the detected object.
e.zh: 在检测到的物体周围画一个边界框。

e.en: Children seem to have {boundless} energy on weekends.
e.zh: 孩子们周末的精力似乎用不完。

e.en: Her curiosity about science is truly {boundless}.
e.zh: 她对科学的好奇心真是无穷无尽。

boundlessly.t: adv. 无限地；无边无际地

e.en: He is {boundlessly} optimistic about the startup's future.
e.zh: 他对这家初创公司的未来抱有无限乐观。

e.en: The desert stretched {boundlessly} toward the horizon.
e.zh: 沙漠一望无际地延伸到地平线。

e.en: The {boundlessness} of the ocean always humbles me.
e.zh: 海洋的无边无际总让我感到自身渺小。

e.en: Poets often write about the {boundlessness} of love.
e.zh: 诗人常常书写爱的无垠。

e.en: We enjoyed a {bounteous} feast on Thanksgiving evening.
e.zh: 感恩节晚上我们享用了一顿丰盛的大餐。

e.en: The farmers thanked the gods for a {bounteous} harvest.
e.zh: 农民们感谢神明赐予丰收。

e.en: This year's apple crop has been especially {bountiful}.
e.zh: 今年的苹果收成特别丰盛。

e.en: She is known for her {bountiful} generosity to charities.
e.zh: 她以对慈善事业的慷慨大方而闻名。

e.en: The garden produced {bountifully} after the spring rains.
e.zh: 春雨过后,花园里果实累累。

e.en: He gave {bountifully} to the local food bank every month.
e.zh: 他每个月都慷慨地向当地食物银行捐赠。

e.en: The sheriff offered a {bounty} for the outlaw's capture.
e.zh: 警长悬赏捉拿那名逃犯。

e.en: We shared the garden's {bounty} with our neighbors.
e.zh: 我们把花园的丰收成果分享给邻居。

bouquet.t:
n. 花束
n. 酒香

e.en: He brought her a beautiful {bouquet} of red roses.
e.zh: 他给她带来了一束漂亮的红玫瑰。

e.en: This wine has a rich {bouquet} of berries and oak.
e.zh: 这款酒散发着浓郁的浆果和橡木香气。

e.en: The florist arranged dozens of wedding {bouquets} that morning.
e.zh: 那天早上花艺师准备了几十束婚礼花束。

e.en: Fans threw {bouquets} onto the stage after the performance.
e.zh: 演出结束后粉丝们把花束扔到了舞台上。

e.en: He poured himself a glass of {bourbon} after work.
e.zh: 下班后他给自己倒了一杯波本威士忌。

e.en: Kentucky is famous worldwide for its {bourbon} distilleries.
e.zh: 肯塔基州以其波本酒厂闻名世界。

bourbons.t: n. 波旁酒（复数）；波旁王朝成员

e.en: The bar stocks over fifty different {bourbons} from Kentucky.
e.zh: 这家酒吧备有五十多种产自肯塔基的波本酒。

e.en: Premium {bourbons} have surged in price over recent years.
e.zh: 高端波本酒近几年价格大幅上涨。

bourgeois.t:
adj. 资产阶级的；中产的
n. 中产者

e.en: He criticized their lifestyle as shallow and {bourgeois}.
e.zh: 他批评他们的生活方式肤浅而市侩。

e.en: The novel mocks {bourgeois} values of nineteenth-century Paris.
e.zh: 这部小说讽刺了十九世纪巴黎的资产阶级价值观。

e.en: She was raised a proper {bourgeoise} in a quiet suburb.
e.zh: 她在安静的郊区被培养成一位地道的资产阶级女士。

e.en: The play depicts a {bourgeoise} struggling against rigid expectations.
e.zh: 这出戏描绘了一位资产阶级女性挣扎于种种刻板期待。

e.en: Marx wrote extensively about the rise of the {bourgeoisie}.
e.zh: 马克思详细论述了资产阶级的崛起。

e.en: The film satirizes the urban {bourgeoisie} and their habits.
e.zh: 这部电影讽刺了城市中产阶级及其生活习惯。

bourget.t: n. 布尔热（法国地名/姓氏）

e.en: The Paris air show takes place at Le {Bourget} airport.
e.zh: 巴黎航展在勒布尔歇机场举办。

e.en: Lindbergh landed at {Bourget} field after crossing the Atlantic.
e.zh: 林德伯格飞越大西洋后降落在布尔歇机场。

bourgogne.t: n. 勃艮第（法国产酒区）

e.en: We toured vineyards across {Bourgogne} during our French holiday.
e.zh: 在法国度假期间我们游览了勃艮第的葡萄园。

e.en: This {Bourgogne} pairs beautifully with roasted duck.
e.zh: 这款勃艮第葡萄酒与烤鸭非常搭配。

e.en: Death is the undiscovered {bourn} from which none return.
e.zh: 死亡是无人能从中归来的未知国度。

e.en: A small {bourn} ran along the edge of the meadow.
e.zh: 一条小溪沿着草地边缘流过。

bourne.t: n. 归宿；终点（文学用语）

e.en: Hamlet calls death the {bourne} from which no traveler returns.
e.zh: 哈姆雷特把死亡称作旅人无法归返的彼岸。

e.en: They followed the winding {bourne} down to the village.
e.zh: 他们沿着蜿蜒的小溪走到了村庄。

bournemouth.t: n. 伯恩茅斯（英国城市）

e.en: We spent a sunny weekend on the beach in {Bournemouth}.
e.zh: 我们在伯恩茅斯的海滩度过了一个阳光明媚的周末。

e.en: {Bournemouth} is popular with tourists for its long sandy coastline.
e.zh: 伯恩茅斯因其漫长的沙质海岸线深受游客欢迎。

e.en: Shares plunged sharply on the Paris {bourse} this morning.
e.zh: 今早巴黎证券交易所股价大幅下跌。

e.en: The {bourse} reopened after a brief technical halt.
e.zh: 该证券交易所在短暂技术中断后重新开市。

bout.t: n. 一阵（发作）；一场比赛

e.en: She's recovering from a nasty {bout} of the flu.
e.zh: 她正在从一场严重的流感中恢复。

e.en: The boxing {bout} ended with a knockout in round three.
e.zh: 那场拳击比赛在第三回合以击倒结束。

boutique.t:
n. 精品店
adj. 小而精的

e.en: She runs a small {boutique} selling handmade jewelry downtown.
e.zh: 她在市中心经营一家卖手工首饰的小精品店。

e.en: They booked a charming {boutique} hotel near the beach.
e.zh: 他们在海滩附近订了一家迷人的精品酒店。

e.en: The groom wore a white rose {boutonniere} on his lapel.
e.zh: 新郎在西装翻领上别着一朵白玫瑰胸花。

e.en: Each usher received a matching {boutonniere} before the ceremony.
e.zh: 每位引宾员在仪式前都拿到了配套的胸花。

bouts.t: n. 几次发作；数场比赛

e.en: He suffers from occasional {bouts} of insomnia during exam season.
e.zh: 考试季他偶尔会出现失眠的情况。

e.en: The wrestler won three consecutive {bouts} this week.
e.zh: 那名摔跤手本周连胜三场比赛。

bovary.t: n. 包法利（《包法利夫人》人物）

e.en: Madame {Bovary} remains one of the greatest novels ever written.
e.zh: 《包法利夫人》仍是有史以来最伟大的小说之一。

e.en: Emma {Bovary} dreams of a more romantic life beyond marriage.
e.zh: 爱玛·包法利渴望婚姻之外更浪漫的人生。

e.en: The vet specializes in {bovine} health and dairy herd management.
e.zh: 那位兽医专攻牛只健康和奶牛群管理。

e.en: He stared back with a calm, {bovine} expression.
e.zh: 他用一种平静而呆滞的表情回望着。

bovis.t: n. 牛型（如牛型分枝杆菌）

e.en: Mycobacterium {bovis} can spread from cattle to humans through milk.
e.zh: 牛分枝杆菌可通过牛奶从牛传染给人。

e.en: Researchers tested the herd for {bovis} infection last week.
e.zh: 研究人员上周对牛群进行了牛分枝杆菌感染检测。

bovril.t: n. 保卫尔（浓缩牛肉汁品牌）

e.en: Grandpa always drank a hot mug of {Bovril} on cold nights.
e.zh: 爷爷在寒冷的夜里总要喝一杯热腾腾的保卫尔牛肉汁。

e.en: Football fans queued for steaming cups of {Bovril} at halftime.
e.zh: 球迷们在中场休息时排队买热腾腾的保卫尔牛肉汁。

bovver.t: n. 流氓闹事；街头斗殴

e.en: The lads wore heavy {bovver} boots and leather jackets.
e.zh: 那群小伙子穿着厚重的战斗靴和皮夹克。

e.en: Don't go looking for {bovver} on a Friday night.
e.zh: 周五晚上别去自找麻烦。

bow.t:
v. 鞠躬；低头
n. 弓；蝴蝶结

e.en: The performers stepped forward to take a {bow} after the show.
e.zh: 演出结束后演员们走上前鞠躬致谢。

e.en: He drew back the {bow} and released the arrow smoothly.
e.zh: 他拉开弓,平稳地射出了箭。

bowden.t: n. 鲍登（姓氏）；鲍登线（机械拉索）

e.en: The brake uses a {Bowden} cable to transmit force.
e.zh: 这个刹车通过鲍登线缆来传递力。

e.en: My 3D printer has a {Bowden} extruder mounted on the frame.
e.zh: 我的3D打印机装有固定在机架上的鲍登挤出机。

bowdlerize.t: v. 删改（删除书中被认为不雅的内容）

e.en: Editors often {bowdlerize} classic books for younger readers.
e.zh: 编辑常常为年轻读者删改经典作品中的不雅内容。

e.en: Don't {bowdlerize} the playwright's intended meaning.
e.zh: 不要删改剧作家原本想表达的意思。

bowed.t:
adj. 弯曲的；弓形的
v. 鞠躬（过去式）

e.en: She {bowed} politely before accepting the award on stage.
e.zh: 她在台上接受奖项前礼貌地鞠了一躬。

e.en: The old shelves had {bowed} under years of heavy books.
e.zh: 那些旧书架因长年承载厚重书籍而弯曲变形。

e.en: The doctor recommended a high-fiber diet for healthy {bowel} function.
e.zh: 医生建议高纤维饮食以保持肠道健康。

e.en: He scheduled a routine {bowel} screening for next month.
e.zh: 他预约了下个月的常规肠道检查。

e.en: They sat in a shaded {bower} of climbing roses.
e.zh: 他们坐在攀缘玫瑰搭成的荫凉花架下。

e.en: A wooden {bower} sheltered the bench at the garden's end.
e.zh: 花园尽头的长椅上方有一座木制凉棚。

e.en: The male {bowerbird} builds elaborate structures to attract mates.
e.zh: 雄性园丁鸟会搭建精致的求偶亭来吸引配偶。

e.en: A satin {bowerbird} decorates its nest with bright blue objects.
e.zh: 缎蓝园丁鸟会用亮蓝色物品来装饰它的求偶亭。

bowhunter.t: n. 使用弓箭狩猎的人

e.en: The {bowhunter} waited silently in his tree stand at dawn.
e.zh: 那名弓猎人黎明时分静静地守在树上的猎台上。

e.en: Every {bowhunter} in the state must complete a safety course.
e.zh: 该州所有弓猎人都必须完成一门安全课程。

e.en: He took up {bowhunting} after retiring from the army.
e.zh: 他从军队退役后开始玩弓箭狩猎。

e.en: {Bowhunting} season opens in early September each year.
e.zh: 弓箭狩猎季每年九月初开放。

bowie.t: n. 鲍伊（人名）；鲍伊猎刀

e.en: He carried a sharp {bowie} knife strapped to his belt.
e.zh: 他腰带上挂着一把锋利的鲍伊刀。

e.en: David {Bowie} reinvented his image throughout his music career.
e.zh: 大卫·鲍伊在整个音乐生涯中不断重塑自己的形象。

bowing.t:
n. 鞠躬；弯腰
n. (乐器) 运弓法

e.en: The students were {bowing} respectfully to their teacher.
e.zh: 学生们正在恭敬地向老师鞠躬。

e.en: Her {bowing} technique on the violin has improved noticeably.
e.zh: 她小提琴的运弓技巧明显有了进步。

bowl.t:
n. 碗；碗状物
v. 投球（保龄球等）

e.en: She poured cereal into a small ceramic {bowl}.
e.zh: 她把麦片倒进一只小陶瓷碗里。

e.en: Let's {bowl} a few games at the new alley tonight.
e.zh: 今晚我们去新开的保龄球馆打几局吧。

e.en: He {bowled} a perfect strike on his very first throw.
e.zh: 他第一球就打出了完美的全中。

e.en: The audience was {bowled} over by her stunning performance.
e.zh: 她精彩的表演让观众完全为之倾倒。

bowlegged.t: adj. 罗圈腿的；弓形腿的

e.en: The old cowboy walked with a {bowlegged} stride.
e.zh: 那位老牛仔走起路来罗圈腿一摇一晃。

e.en: Her {bowlegged} puppy waddled across the kitchen floor.
e.zh: 她那只罗圈腿的小狗摇摇摆摆地穿过厨房。

bowler.t:
n. 投球手（板球等）
n. 圆顶礼帽

e.en: He wore a black {bowler} hat to the wedding.
e.zh: 他戴着一顶黑色的圆顶礼帽去参加婚礼。

e.en: The {bowler} took five wickets in the cricket match.
e.zh: 那位投球手在板球比赛中拿下了五个三柱门。

e.en: She ate a whole {bowlful} of noodles for lunch.
e.zh: 她午饭吃了满满一碗面条。

e.en: He served me a generous {bowlful} of strawberries.
e.zh: 他给我盛了满满一大碗草莓。

bowline.t: n. 称人结（一种绳结）；张帆索

e.en: Every sailor should know how to tie a {bowline}.
e.zh: 每个水手都应该会打单套结。

e.en: He secured the boat to the dock with a {bowline}.
e.zh: 他用单套结把船系在了码头上。

e.en: We're going {bowling} with friends on Friday night.
e.zh: 周五晚上我们要和朋友去打保龄球。

e.en: The new {bowling} alley has neon lights and arcade games.
e.zh: 新开的保龄球馆有霓虹灯和街机游戏。

bowls.t:
n. 草地滚球（运动）
n. 碗（复数）

e.en: Stack the clean {bowls} on the top shelf.
e.zh: 把洗好的碗摞在最上层架子上。

e.en: My grandfather plays lawn {bowls} every Sunday afternoon.
e.zh: 我爷爷每个星期天下午都打草地滚球。

e.en: The skilled {bowman} hit the bullseye three times.
e.zh: 那位熟练的弓箭手连中三次靶心。

e.en: Medieval armies relied heavily on the {bowman}.
e.zh: 中世纪的军队非常依赖弓箭手。

e.en: They bought a small {bowrider} for weekend lake trips.
e.zh: 他们买了一艘小型敞舱艇周末去湖上玩。

e.en: The {bowrider} can comfortably seat eight passengers.
e.zh: 这艘敞舱艇可以舒适地坐下八个人。

bows.t:
n. 船头；弓（复数）
v. 鞠躬（第三人称单数）

e.en: She {bows} politely whenever she meets her teacher.
e.zh: 她每次遇到老师都会礼貌地鞠躬。

e.en: The archer carried two wooden {bows} on his back.
e.zh: 那位弓箭手背上背着两把木弓。

e.en: The sailor climbed out onto the {bowsprit} to fix the rigging.
e.zh: 水手爬到艏斜桅上去修理索具。

e.en: Salt spray coated the ship's wooden {bowsprit}.
e.zh: 海水的浪花覆盖了船的木制艏斜桅。

e.en: He pulled the {bowstring} back and aimed carefully.
e.zh: 他拉开弓弦,仔细瞄准。

e.en: The {bowstring} snapped under the strain of the shot.
e.zh: 弓弦在射击的张力下断裂了。

e.en: The village {bowyer} crafted longbows from yew wood.
e.zh: 村里的弓匠用紫杉木制作长弓。

e.en: A skilled {bowyer} can shape a bow in two weeks.
e.zh: 一位熟练的弓匠两周就能做好一把弓。

box.t:
n. 盒子；箱子
v. 装箱；拳击

e.en: Please put the books back in the {box}.
e.zh: 请把书放回箱子里。

e.en: You can {box} up the leftovers and take them home.
e.zh: 你可以把剩菜打包带回家。

e.en: The freight train pulled fifty empty {boxcar} units.
e.zh: 那列货运火车拉着五十节空的棚车车厢。

e.en: Hobos used to ride in a {boxcar} across the country.
e.zh: 以前流浪汉常坐棚车穿越全国。

boxed.t:
adj. 盒装的
v. 装入盒中（过去式）

e.en: All the gifts were neatly {boxed} and labeled.
e.zh: 所有礼物都整齐地装盒并贴好了标签。

e.en: He {boxed} professionally for over a decade.
e.zh: 他从事职业拳击十多年。

boxer.t:
n. 拳击手
n. 拳师犬

e.en: The young {boxer} trained six hours every day.
e.zh: 那位年轻的拳击手每天训练六个小时。

e.en: Their {boxer} loves to chase tennis balls in the yard.
e.zh: 他们家的拳师犬喜欢在院子里追网球。

boxers.t: n. 平角内裤；拳击手（复数）

e.en: He prefers {boxers} over briefs for everyday wear.
e.zh: 他平时更喜欢穿平角内裤而不是三角裤。

e.en: Two heavyweight {boxers} faced off in the championship.
e.zh: 两位重量级拳击手在冠军赛中对决。

boxes.t:
n. 盒子（复数）
v. 装箱；拳击（第三人称单数）

e.en: We still have unpacked {boxes} from the move.
e.zh: 搬家后我们还有几个箱子没拆封。

e.en: Tick all the {boxes} on the application form.
e.zh: 在申请表上把所有方框都打勾。

e.en: She brought a {boxful} of homemade cookies to the party.
e.zh: 她带了一盒自制饼干来参加派对。

e.en: I found a {boxful} of old photos in the attic.
e.zh: 我在阁楼上找到一盒老照片。

boxing.t:
n. 拳击运动
n. 装箱

e.en: He's been taking {boxing} lessons to stay in shape.
e.zh: 他一直在学拳击来保持身材。

e.en: The {boxing} match ended in a stunning knockout.
e.zh: 那场拳击比赛以一记惊人的击倒结束。

boxings.t: n. 装箱物；拳击比赛（复数）

e.en: The carpenter installed wooden {boxings} around the pipes.
e.zh: 木匠在管道周围装了木制护板。

e.en: Decorative {boxings} hide the cables along the wall.
e.zh: 装饰性的护套把墙上的电线藏了起来。

e.en: The new building has a plain, {boxlike} appearance.
e.zh: 那栋新楼外观朴素,像个方盒子。

e.en: He drove a small, {boxlike} car from the eighties.
e.zh: 他开着一辆八十年代的方方正正的小车。

e.en: They trimmed the {boxwood} hedges into perfect spheres.
e.zh: 他们把黄杨树篱修剪成了完美的球形。

e.en: The chess pieces were carved from polished {boxwood}.
e.zh: 那些象棋子是用抛光的黄杨木雕成的。

boxy.t: adj. 方方正正的；盒状的

e.en: She wore a {boxy} blazer over her summer dress.
e.zh: 她在夏裙外面套了一件宽松方正的西装外套。

e.en: Old SUVs had a very {boxy} silhouette.
e.zh: 老款SUV的车身轮廓非常方正。

e.en: The little {boy} waved at his grandmother through the window.
e.zh: 那个小男孩透过窗户向奶奶挥手。

e.en: Oh {boy}, this is going to be an exciting trip!
e.zh: 哎呀,这趟旅行一定会很精彩!

boyar.t: n. 波雅尔（俄国旧贵族）

e.en: Each {boyar} held vast estates under the Russian tsar.
e.zh: 每位大贵族在俄国沙皇治下都拥有大片庄园。

e.en: The {boyar} class lost power after Peter the Great's reforms.
e.zh: 彼得大帝改革后,大贵族阶层失去了权力。

boycott.t:
v. 抵制，拒绝购买或参与
n. 抵制行动

e.en: Activists called for a {boycott} of the company's products.
e.zh: 活动人士呼吁抵制该公司的产品。

e.en: Several countries plan to {boycott} the upcoming summit.
e.zh: 几个国家计划抵制即将召开的峰会。

e.en: She introduced her new {boyfriend} to her parents.
e.zh: 她把新男朋友介绍给了父母。

e.en: My {boyfriend} and I are planning a trip to Japan.
e.zh: 我和男朋友正在计划去日本旅行。

boyfriends.t: n. 男朋友（boyfriend 的复数）

e.en: All her {boyfriends} have been musicians or artists.
e.zh: 她交往过的男朋友都是音乐家或艺术家。

e.en: The two friends rarely talk about their {boyfriends}.
e.zh: 那两位朋友很少谈论各自的男朋友。

boyhood.t: n. 男孩时期，少年时代

e.en: He spent his {boyhood} on a farm in Iowa.
e.zh: 他童年时光是在爱荷华州的一个农场度过的。

e.en: The novel describes his {boyhood} adventures by the river.
e.zh: 这部小说描写了他童年时在河边的冒险经历。

boyish.t: adj. 男孩般的，孩子气的

e.en: She loved his {boyish} smile and tousled hair.
e.zh: 她喜欢他孩子气的笑容和凌乱的头发。

e.en: He retains a {boyish} enthusiasm even in his fifties.
e.zh: 即使五十多岁,他仍保有男孩般的热情。

boyishly.t: adv. 男孩般地，孩子气地

e.en: He grinned {boyishly} when she walked into the room.
e.zh: 她走进房间时,他孩子气地咧嘴一笑。

e.en: The actor still dresses {boyishly} despite his age.
e.zh: 尽管年纪不小,那位演员仍穿得像个少年。

boyishness.t: n. 男孩气，孩子般的稚气

e.en: His charm comes from a certain lingering {boyishness}.
e.zh: 他的魅力来自某种始终未褪的少年气。

e.en: There's a playful {boyishness} in everything he does.
e.zh: 他做的每件事都带着一种顽皮的孩子气。

boyne.t: n. 博因河（爱尔兰河流）

e.en: The Battle of the {Boyne} was fought in 1690.
e.zh: 博因河战役发生于1690年。

e.en: We took a scenic walk along the River {Boyne}.
e.zh: 我们沿着博因河散步,风景优美。

boyo.t: n. 小伙子（爱尔兰/威尔士口语）

e.en: Come here, {boyo}, and help me carry this.
e.zh: 小伙子,过来帮我搬一下这个。

e.en: The Welsh shopkeeper greeted him warmly as {boyo}.
e.zh: 那位威尔士店主亲切地叫他「小伙」。

boys.t: n. 男孩们（boy 的复数）

e.en: The {boys} are playing soccer in the park.
e.zh: 那些男孩们正在公园里踢足球。

e.en: Come on {boys}, let's get the car loaded up.
e.zh: 伙计们,来吧,我们把车装好。

boyz.t: n. 男孩们（boys 的俚语拼写）

e.en: The hip-hop group called themselves the {Boyz} from Brooklyn.
e.zh: 那个嘻哈组合自称布鲁克林来的「Boyz」。

e.en: His shirt had {Boyz} printed in bold yellow letters.
e.zh: 他的衬衫上用粗黄色字母印着「Boyz」。

boz.t: n. 博兹（狄更斯早期笔名）

e.en: Charles Dickens originally wrote under the pen name {Boz}.
e.zh: 查尔斯·狄更斯最初用笔名「博兹」发表作品。

e.en: His early sketches were collected as Sketches by {Boz}.
e.zh: 他早期的随笔结集为《博兹特写集》。

e.en: Some {bozo} parked his truck across two spaces.
e.zh: 哪个蠢货把卡车横跨两个车位停着。

e.en: Don't be a {bozo} and forget your passport again.
e.zh: 别再当傻瓜了,又忘记带护照。

bpd.t:
n. 边缘型人格障碍（缩写）
n. 桶/日（石油产量单位）

e.en: The oil field produces about 50,000 {bpd} of crude.
e.zh: 该油田每天约产5万桶原油。

e.en: Therapy can help people manage symptoms of {BPD}.
e.zh: 心理治疗可以帮助患者控制边缘型人格障碍的症状。

bpi.t: n. 位每英寸（bits per inch，数据密度）

e.en: Older floppy disks had a much lower {bpi} rating.
e.zh: 旧式软盘的位每英寸密度要低得多。

e.en: Engineers measured the tape's storage in {bpi}.
e.zh: 工程师用每英寸位数来衡量磁带的存储密度。

e.en: She bought a new sports {bra} for her morning runs.
e.zh: 她买了一件新的运动文胸用来晨跑。

e.en: Finding a comfortable {bra} can be surprisingly difficult.
e.zh: 找到一件舒适的文胸出乎意料地难。

brabant.t: n. 布拉班特（比利时/荷兰地区）

e.en: The province of {Brabant} lies in central Belgium.
e.zh: 布拉班特省位于比利时中部。

e.en: Medieval {Brabant} was famous for its fine tapestries.
e.zh: 中世纪的布拉班特以其精美的挂毯闻名。

brabham.t: n. 布拉汉姆（F1 车队/姓氏）

e.en: Jack {Brabham} won three Formula One world championships.
e.zh: 杰克·布拉汉姆赢得了三届一级方程式世界冠军。

e.en: The vintage {Brabham} race car was sold at auction.
e.zh: 那辆老款布拉汉姆赛车在拍卖会上售出。

brac.t: n. 布拉奇（克罗地亚岛屿）

e.en: The shelves were cluttered with bric-a-{brac} from her travels.
e.zh: 架子上摆满了她旅行带回来的小摆设。

e.en: She collected antique bric-a-{brac} at every flea market.
e.zh: 她在每个跳蚤市场都会收集古董小玩意儿。

brace.t:
v. 使稳固，做好准备
n. 支架，括号

e.en: {Brace} yourself for some shocking news.
e.zh: 做好心理准备,有些令人震惊的消息。

e.en: He wore a knee {brace} after the surgery.
e.zh: 手术后他戴着一个护膝支架。

e.en: She wore a silver {bracelet} her grandmother gave her.
e.zh: 她戴着奶奶送给她的一条银手链。

e.en: The fitness {bracelet} tracks his steps and heart rate.
e.zh: 那只健身手环记录他的步数和心率。

e.en: She stacked five thin gold {bracelets} on her wrist.
e.zh: 她在手腕上叠戴了五条细细的金手链。

e.en: The market sold colorful beaded {bracelets} for tourists.
e.zh: 市场上卖着色彩缤纷的串珠手链给游客。

bracero.t: n. 短工，墨西哥入美合同工

e.en: His grandfather came to California as a {bracero} in 1955.
e.zh: 他祖父1955年作为合同短工来到了加利福尼亚。

e.en: The {bracero} program brought millions of Mexican workers north.
e.zh: 短工计划带来了数百万墨西哥工人北上。

e.en: The nurse measured his {brachial} blood pressure carefully.
e.zh: 护士仔细测量了他的肱动脉血压。

e.en: A nerve injury affected his {brachial} plexus.
e.zh: 一处神经损伤影响了他的臂丛神经。

e.en: The {brachialis} muscle helps flex the elbow joint smoothly.
e.zh: 肱肌帮助肘关节顺畅地弯曲。

e.en: My trainer said curls target the {brachialis} more than biceps.
e.zh: 教练说弯举锻炼的更多是肱肌而非二头肌。

e.en: The fossil shop sold a tiny {brachiopod} for ten dollars.
e.zh: 化石店里一只小腕足动物化石卖十美元。

e.en: Each {brachiopod} has two shells unlike a true clam.
e.zh: 每只腕足动物都有两片壳,与真正的蛤蜊不同。

bracing.t:
adj. 令人神清气爽的
n. 支撑结构

e.en: A {bracing} walk along the cliffs cleared my head.
e.zh: 沿着悬崖走一段令人精神一振的路,让我清醒了。

e.en: The engineers added steel {bracing} to strengthen the old bridge.
e.zh: 工程师们加装了钢支撑来加固这座旧桥。

bracingly.t: adv. 令人振奋地，清爽地

e.en: The morning air felt {bracingly} cold against my face.
e.zh: 清晨的空气吹在脸上,凉得令人精神一振。

e.en: She spoke {bracingly} to the team before the final match.
e.zh: 决赛前她以振奋人心的话语对队员讲话。

e.en: We pushed through tall {bracken} on the hillside trail.
e.zh: 我们在山坡小径上拨开高高的蕨丛前行。

e.en: The deer hid quietly in a patch of {bracken}.
e.zh: 那头鹿静静地藏在一片蕨丛之中。

bracket.t:
n. 括号；等级区间
v. 把……归为一类

e.en: Our income falls into the lowest tax {bracket} this year.
e.zh: 我们今年的收入处于最低的税级。

e.en: He mounted a metal {bracket} to hold the new shelf.
e.zh: 他装了一个金属托架来固定新书架。

bracketed.t: v. 加括号；归类（bracket 的过去式）

e.en: The editor {bracketed} the uncertain dates in the manuscript.
e.zh: 编辑用方括号把手稿中不确定的日期标了出来。

e.en: Two tall trees {bracketed} the entrance to the garden.
e.zh: 两棵高大的树夹在花园入口的两侧。

bracketing.t: n. 括号标注；(摄影) 包围曝光

e.en: Photographers use exposure {bracketing} to capture tricky lighting.
e.zh: 摄影师用包围曝光来拍摄复杂光线。

e.en: She kept {bracketing} her doubts in the margins of the report.
e.zh: 她不断在报告页边把自己的疑问括起来。

brackets.t: n. 括号；区间（bracket 的复数）

e.en: Put your citations in square {brackets} at the end.
e.zh: 把引用资料放在末尾的方括号里。

e.en: The shelf came with two metal {brackets} and screws.
e.zh: 这块搁板配了两个金属支架和螺丝。

brackish.t: adj. 微咸的（水）；令人不快的

e.en: Mangroves thrive in the {brackish} water near the estuary.
e.zh: 红树林在河口附近的微咸水中茂盛生长。

e.en: The well turned {brackish} after the summer storms.
e.zh: 夏季暴风雨过后那口井的水变得有些咸了。

brackley.t: n. 布拉克利（英国地名）

e.en: We stopped for lunch in {Brackley} on the way north.
e.zh: 我们北上途中在布拉克利停下吃了午饭。

e.en: {Brackley} is a small market town in Northamptonshire.
e.zh: 布拉克利是北安普敦郡的一个小集镇。

bracknell.t: n. 布拉克内尔（英国城镇）

e.en: Many tech companies have offices in {Bracknell}, England.
e.zh: 许多科技公司在英国布拉克内尔设有办事处。

e.en: She commutes from {Bracknell} into central London daily.
e.zh: 她每天从布拉克内尔通勤到伦敦市中心。

e.en: The red part of a poinsettia is actually a {bract}.
e.zh: 一品红的红色部分其实是苞片。

e.en: Each tiny flower sits above a green {bract}.
e.zh: 每朵小花都长在一片绿色苞片之上。

brad.t:
n. 无头钉，角钉
n. 布拉德（男名）

e.en: Use a small {brad} to attach the trim without splitting it.
e.zh: 用一颗小钉子固定饰条,以免木头开裂。

e.en: The carpenter drove a {brad} through the thin molding.
e.zh: 木工把一颗细钉敲入薄薄的线条板。

bradford.t: n. 布拉德福德（英国城市/姓氏）

e.en: {Bradford} is famous for its curry houses and old mills.
e.zh: 布拉德福德以咖喱餐馆和古老的纺织厂闻名。

e.en: She moved to {Bradford} for university last September.
e.zh: 她去年九月搬到布拉德福德上大学。

bradycardia.t: n. 心动过缓（心率过慢）

e.en: The patient's monitor showed signs of {bradycardia} overnight.
e.zh: 患者的监护仪在夜间显示出心动过缓的迹象。

e.en: Trained athletes often have {bradycardia} due to strong hearts.
e.zh: 训练有素的运动员常因心脏强健而出现心动过缓。

e.en: Sheep grazed peacefully on the grassy {brae} above the loch.
e.zh: 羊群在湖上方青草坡上安静地吃草。

e.en: We climbed the steep {brae} to watch the sunset.
e.zh: 我们爬上陡峭的山坡观看日落。

braemar.t: n. 布雷马（苏格兰地名）

e.en: The royal family attends the {Braemar} Gathering each September.
e.zh: 王室每年九月都会出席布雷马高地运动会。

e.en: We rented a cottage near {Braemar} for the weekend.
e.zh: 我们在布雷马附近租了一间小屋过周末。

e.en: The {Braer} oil spill of 1993 polluted Shetland's coast.
e.zh: 1993 年布雷尔号漏油事件污染了设得兰群岛海岸。

e.en: Documentary footage shows the tanker {Braer} breaking apart.
e.zh: 纪录片画面显示油轮布雷尔号正在解体。

brag.t:
v. 吹嘘，自夸
n. 自吹自擂

e.en: He likes to {brag} about his new sports car.
e.zh: 他喜欢炫耀自己的新跑车。

e.en: It's not polite to {brag} about your test scores.
e.zh: 炫耀考试成绩是不礼貌的。

e.en: His speech was full of {braggadocio} but short on facts.
e.zh: 他的演讲充满吹嘘,却没什么事实依据。

e.en: The rapper's {braggadocio} is part of the genre's appeal.
e.zh: 这位说唱歌手的自吹自擂是这种音乐风格魅力的一部分。

braggart.t: n. 吹牛的人，爱自夸的人

e.en: Nobody believed the {braggart} when he told fishing stories.
e.zh: 那个爱吹牛的人讲钓鱼故事时没人相信他。

e.en: He's a harmless {braggart} who exaggerates every accomplishment.
e.zh: 他是个无害的吹牛大王,把每件成就都夸大其词。

bragging.t:
n. 吹嘘
v. 自夸（brag 的现在分词）

e.en: Stop {bragging} about your salary at every dinner party.
e.zh: 别在每次聚餐时炫耀你的工资。

e.en: Winning the championship gave him serious {bragging} rights.
e.zh: 赢得冠军让他有了十足的吹牛资本。

brags.t: v. 吹嘘（brag 的第三人称单数）

e.en: She always {brags} about her son's grades on social media.
e.zh: 她总在社交媒体上炫耀儿子的成绩。

e.en: He {brags} that he can run a marathon without training.
e.zh: 他吹嘘说自己不训练也能跑马拉松。

brahman.t:
n. 婆罗门（印度种姓）
n. 梵（印度教最高存在）

e.en: In Hindu philosophy, {Brahman} is the ultimate universal reality.
e.zh: 在印度教哲学中,梵是终极的宇宙实在。

e.en: The rancher prefers {Brahman} cattle for the hot climate.
e.zh: 牧场主偏爱适合炎热气候的婆罗门牛。

brahmin.t:
n. 婆罗门
n. 上流知识分子

e.en: He came from a respected {Brahmin} family in Kerala.
e.zh: 他出身于喀拉拉邦一个受人尊敬的婆罗门家庭。

e.en: The university was run by Boston {Brahmin} families for decades.
e.zh: 这所大学几十年来都由波士顿的名门世家掌管。

brahms.t: n. 勃拉姆斯（德国作曲家）

e.en: The orchestra performed a moving symphony by {Brahms} last night.
e.zh: 乐团昨晚演奏了一首勃拉姆斯感人的交响曲。

e.en: She practiced a {Brahms} lullaby on the piano.
e.zh: 她在钢琴上练习一首勃拉姆斯的摇篮曲。

braid.t:
n. 辫子，编带
v. 编（发辫）

e.en: She wore her long hair in a single {braid}.
e.zh: 她把长发编成了一条辫子。

e.en: The dress was trimmed with gold {braid} along the sleeves.
e.zh: 这件连衣裙袖口缀着金色编织花边。

braided.t:
adj. 编成辫的
v. 编（braid 的过去式）

e.en: The little girl proudly showed off her newly {braided} hair.
e.zh: 小女孩自豪地展示她刚编好的辫子。

e.en: A {braided} leather belt hung on the closet door.
e.zh: 一条编织皮带挂在衣柜门上。

e.en: My sister is {braiding} my hair before the wedding.
e.zh: 婚礼前姐姐正在帮我编辫子。

e.en: Traditional {braiding} techniques have been passed down for generations.
e.zh: 传统的编发技艺已经世代相传。

braille.t: n. 盲文，布莱叶点字法

e.en: The elevator buttons include {braille} for blind passengers.
e.zh: 电梯按钮上有为盲人乘客准备的盲文。

e.en: She learned to read {braille} after losing her sight.
e.zh: 她在失明后学会了阅读盲文。

e.en: The student typed her notes on a portable {braillewriter}.
e.zh: 学生用一台便携式盲文打字机记笔记。

e.en: Each classroom for blind children had its own {braillewriter}.
e.zh: 每间盲童教室都配有一台盲文打字机。

brain.t:
n. 大脑，头脑
n. 智力，聪明人

e.en: Drinking enough water helps your {brain} stay focused.
e.zh: 喝足够的水有助于大脑保持专注。

e.en: She's the {brain} behind our company's new app.
e.zh: 她是我们公司新应用背后的智囊。

e.en: The fossil's {braincase} suggests a surprisingly intelligent species.
e.zh: 这具化石的颅腔显示该物种聪明得出乎意料。

e.en: Helmets are designed to protect the fragile {braincase}.
e.zh: 头盔的设计是为了保护脆弱的颅腔。

brainchild.t: n. 独创的点子或作品

e.en: The streaming service was the {brainchild} of two college friends.
e.zh: 这家流媒体服务是两位大学朋友的心血结晶。

e.en: This festival is the {brainchild} of a local artist.
e.zh: 这个节日是一位本地艺术家的创意。

brainiac.t: n. 绝顶聪明的人，学霸

e.en: My cousin is a total {brainiac} who finished college at sixteen.
e.zh: 我表弟是个十足的天才,十六岁就大学毕业了。

e.en: You don't have to be a {brainiac} to use this app.
e.zh: 用这个应用不需要你是个天才。

e.en: Scrolling videos for hours feels pretty {brainless} sometimes.
e.zh: 连续刷几个小时视频有时感觉挺无脑的。

e.en: That was a {brainless} decision to drive without insurance.
e.zh: 无保险就开车真是个愚蠢的决定。

e.en: The boxer took a hard hit to the {brainpan}.
e.zh: 那名拳击手脑壳被狠狠地击中了一拳。

e.en: Get that idea out of your {brainpan} right now.
e.zh: 赶紧把那种想法从你脑壳里赶出去。

e.en: Solving this puzzle takes serious {brainpower} and patience.
e.zh: 解开这道谜题需要相当的智力和耐心。

e.en: The startup pooled the {brainpower} of dozens of engineers.
e.zh: 这家初创公司汇集了数十名工程师的智慧。

brains.t:
n. 脑子，智慧
n. 智囊人物

e.en: She has the {brains} to lead any project successfully.
e.zh: 她有足够的智慧来成功领导任何项目。

e.en: Use your {brains} before you click that suspicious link.
e.zh: 点那个可疑链接之前先动动脑子。

e.en: The {brainstem} controls breathing, heart rate, and reflexes.
e.zh: 脑干控制着呼吸、心率和反射。

e.en: Damage to the {brainstem} can be life-threatening.
e.zh: 脑干受损可能危及生命。

brainstorm.t:
v. 集思广益
n. 头脑风暴，灵感

e.en: Let's {brainstorm} some names for the new product.
e.zh: 我们来给新产品集思广益取些名字。

e.en: The team had a quick {brainstorm} before the meeting.
e.zh: 团队在开会前快速进行了一次头脑风暴。

brainstorming.t: n. 头脑风暴，集思广益

e.en: We spent the morning {brainstorming} ideas for the campaign.
e.zh: 我们花了一上午为这场宣传活动集思广益。

e.en: Good {brainstorming} sessions welcome every idea, even silly ones.
e.zh: 好的头脑风暴会欢迎每个想法,哪怕是愚蠢的。

brainstormings.t: n. 头脑风暴（复数，罕用）

e.en: Several {brainstormings} were scheduled before the product launch.
e.zh: 产品发布前安排了几场头脑风暴会议。

e.en: Her notebook is filled with notes from past {brainstormings}.
e.zh: 她的笔记本里写满了过去几次头脑风暴的笔记。

brainstorms.t: v./n. 头脑风暴（第三人称单数/复数）

e.en: The designer often {brainstorms} ideas while walking outside.
e.zh: 那位设计师常常一边在外散步一边构思创意。

e.en: Our weekly {brainstorms} have produced some of our best features.
e.zh: 我们每周的头脑风暴催生了一些最棒的功能。

e.en: Many online stores use {Braintree} to process card payments.
e.zh: 许多网店使用 Braintree 来处理银行卡付款。

e.en: We took the commuter rail from Boston to {Braintree}.
e.zh: 我们坐通勤铁路从波士顿到布伦特里。

e.en: Cult leaders often try to {brainwash} their vulnerable followers.
e.zh: 邪教头目常试图给脆弱的信徒洗脑。

e.en: Don't let advertisers {brainwash} you into buying junk.
e.zh: 别让广告商把你洗脑,去买没用的东西。

brainwashed.t:
adj. 被洗脑的
v. 洗脑（过去式）

e.en: He felt completely {brainwashed} after years in that organization.
e.zh: 在那个组织里待了多年后,他感觉自己被彻底洗脑了。

e.en: The film shows how soldiers were {brainwashed} during captivity.
e.zh: 影片展示了士兵在被俘期间是如何被洗脑的。

brainwashes.t: v. 洗脑（第三人称单数）

e.en: Constant negative news {brainwashes} viewers into expecting disaster.
e.zh: 持续的负面新闻让观众被洗脑般地预期灾难。

e.en: The regime systematically {brainwashes} children through state textbooks.
e.zh: 该政权通过国家教科书系统地给孩子们洗脑。

e.en: Survivors described the cult's {brainwashing} techniques in chilling detail.
e.zh: 幸存者用令人毛骨悚然的细节描述了邪教的洗脑手法。

e.en: Critics accused the channel of {brainwashing} young viewers.
e.zh: 批评者指责该频道对年轻观众进行洗脑。

e.en: The cult's repeated {brainwashings} left members unable to think independently.
e.zh: 邪教反复的洗脑让成员无法独立思考。

e.en: Historians documented the regime's systematic {brainwashings} of young soldiers.
e.zh: 历史学家记录了该政权对年轻士兵的系统性洗脑。

brainwave.t:
n. 脑电波
n. 灵光一现

e.en: I just had a {brainwave} about how to fix the bug.
e.zh: 我刚灵光一闪,想到怎么修这个 bug 了。

e.en: Her sudden {brainwave} saved the project from disaster.
e.zh: 她突如其来的灵感把项目从灾难中拯救了出来。

e.en: His {brainy} younger sister won the math olympiad twice.
e.zh: 他聪明的妹妹两次赢得数学奥赛冠军。

e.en: The startup hired a {brainy} team of MIT graduates.
e.zh: 这家初创公司雇了一群麻省理工出身的高智商团队。

e.en: I like to {braise} short ribs in red wine for hours.
e.zh: 我喜欢用红酒把牛小排炖上几个小时。

e.en: You can {braise} the lamb shanks until they fall off the bone.
e.zh: 你可以把羊腿炖到肉一碰就脱骨。

e.en: The chef served {braised} beef with creamy mashed potatoes.
e.zh: 厨师端上了配奶油土豆泥的红烧牛肉。

e.en: Mom {braised} the pork belly in soy sauce all afternoon.
e.zh: 妈妈用酱油把五花肉炖了一整个下午。

braising.t:
n. 炖，焖煮
v. braise 的现在分词

e.en: {Braising} tough cuts of meat makes them incredibly tender.
e.zh: 炖煮粗硬的肉块能让它们变得非常软嫩。

e.en: She is {braising} lamb shanks for tonight's dinner party.
e.zh: 她正在为今晚的晚宴炖羊腿。

brass.t:
n. 黄铜
n. 铜管乐器

e.en: The door handles are made of polished {brass}.
e.zh: 门把手是用抛光黄铜做的。

e.en: The jazz band's {brass} section stole the entire show.
e.zh: 爵士乐队的铜管组抢尽了整场演出的风头。

brasserie.t: n. 供应酒食的小餐馆

e.en: We had steak frites at a small French {brasserie}.
e.zh: 我们在一家小法式餐酒馆吃了牛排薯条。

e.en: The {brasserie} on the corner serves until midnight.
e.zh: 街角那家餐酒馆营业到午夜。

brasses.t: n. 黄铜制品；铜管乐器（brass 复数）

e.en: The orchestra's {brasses} drowned out the strings.
e.zh: 乐团的铜管组盖过了弦乐声。

e.en: She polished the door {brasses} until they gleamed.
e.zh: 她把门上的铜件擦得锃亮。

brassica.t: n. 芸薹属植物（甘蓝、油菜等）

e.en: Cabbage and broccoli belong to the {brassica} family.
e.zh: 卷心菜和西兰花都属于芸薹属植物。

e.en: He grows several {brassica} varieties in the winter garden.
e.zh: 他在冬季菜园里种了好几种十字花科蔬菜。

e.en: The store sells lingerie, including a wide range of {brassiere} styles.
e.zh: 这家店出售内衣,包括各种款式的胸罩。

e.en: She bought a sports {brassiere} for her morning runs.
e.zh: 她买了一件运动文胸用于晨跑。

brassy.t:
adj. 黄铜色的
adj. 刺耳的；俗艳的

e.en: Her {brassy} laugh filled the entire room.
e.zh: 她那刺耳的笑声充满了整个房间。

e.en: The trumpet had a bright, {brassy} tone.
e.zh: 那把小号音色明亮而铜亮。

brat.t: n. 讨厌的小孩；熊孩子

e.en: Stop acting like a spoiled {brat} at dinner.
e.zh: 吃饭时别像个被宠坏的小屁孩一样。

e.en: The {brat} kicked the seat the entire flight.
e.zh: 那个熊孩子整趟航班都在踢椅背。

bratislava.t: n. 布拉迪斯拉发（斯洛伐克首都）

e.en: We took a day trip from Vienna to {Bratislava}.
e.zh: 我们从维也纳一日游去了布拉迪斯拉发。

e.en: {Bratislava} is the capital of Slovakia.
e.zh: 布拉迪斯拉发是斯洛伐克的首都。

brattish.t: adj. 像熊孩子一样讨人厌的

e.en: His {brattish} behavior at the party embarrassed his parents.
e.zh: 他在聚会上孩子气的行为让父母很尴尬。

e.en: She gave him a {brattish} smirk and walked off.
e.zh: 她调皮地咧嘴一笑就走开了。

bratty.t: adj. 像小屁孩一样任性讨厌的

e.en: The {bratty} kid refused to share his toys.
e.zh: 那个任性的小孩不肯分享玩具。

e.en: She rolled her eyes in a {bratty} way.
e.zh: 她翻了个白眼,一副傲娇任性的样子。

e.en: We grilled {bratwurst} and onions for dinner.
e.zh: 我们晚餐烤了德式香肠和洋葱。

e.en: The festival sold {bratwurst} with mustard on a bun.
e.zh: 集市上卖夹芥末的德式香肠面包。

braun.t: n. 博朗（德国家电品牌）

e.en: My new {Braun} shaver came with a charging dock.
e.zh: 我新买的博朗剃须刀附带一个充电底座。

e.en: She bought a {Braun} blender for the kitchen.
e.zh: 她为厨房买了一台博朗搅拌机。

e.en: The audience shouted "{Brava}!" as the soprano took her bow.
e.zh: 女高音谢幕时观众高喊"好啊!"。

e.en: "{Brava}, well done!" the coach called from the sidelines.
e.zh: "好样的,干得漂亮!"教练从场边喊道。

bravado.t: n. 故作勇敢；虚张声势

e.en: His {bravado} disappeared the moment the fight started.
e.zh: 打斗一开始,他那股虚张声势就消失了。

e.en: She masked her nerves with a show of {bravado}.
e.zh: 她用一副逞强的样子掩饰自己的紧张。

brave.t:
adj. 勇敢的
v. 勇敢面对

e.en: It was {brave} of her to speak up at the meeting.
e.zh: 她敢在会上发言,真有勇气。

e.en: They had to {brave} the storm to reach the cabin.
e.zh: 他们不得不冒着暴风雨赶到小屋。

e.en: She {bravely} admitted she had made a mistake.
e.zh: 她勇敢地承认自己犯了错。

e.en: The firefighters {bravely} entered the burning building.
e.zh: 消防员英勇地冲进了着火的大楼。

e.en: History books record the small {braveries} of ordinary people.
e.zh: 史书记载了普通人那些不起眼的勇敢之举。

e.en: Her diary listed countless quiet {braveries} from the war years.
e.zh: 她的日记记录了战时无数默默无闻的勇敢事迹。

e.en: He was awarded a medal for his {bravery} in combat.
e.zh: 他因在战斗中表现勇敢而获得奖章。

e.en: It takes real {bravery} to admit you were wrong.
e.zh: 承认自己错了需要真正的勇气。

e.en: "{Bravo}!" the crowd cheered after the final note.
e.zh: 最后一个音符落下后,人群高呼"好啊!"。

e.en: {Bravo} on landing the new job!
e.zh: 恭喜你拿到新工作,真棒!

e.en: The pianist gave a {bravura} performance of the concerto.
e.zh: 那位钢琴家以精湛技艺演奏了这首协奏曲。

e.en: Her closing speech was a piece of pure {bravura}.
e.zh: 她的结尾演讲堪称一场华丽的炫技。

brawl.t:
n. 斗殴
v. 大声争吵；打架

e.en: A {brawl} broke out in the parking lot after the game.
e.zh: 比赛结束后停车场爆发了一场斗殴。

e.en: The bouncers quickly broke up the bar {brawl}.
e.zh: 保安迅速制止了那场酒吧斗殴。

e.en: He was known as a street {brawler} in his youth.
e.zh: 他年轻时以街头斗殴闻名。

e.en: The bar hired bouncers to deal with any {brawler}.
e.zh: 酒吧雇了保安来对付任何闹事打架的人。

brawling.t:
n. 打架斗殴
adj. 吵闹的

e.en: Two drunks were {brawling} outside the pub.
e.zh: 两个醉汉在酒吧外打成一团。

e.en: Police arrested several fans for {brawling} after the match.
e.zh: 警方在赛后逮捕了几名斗殴的球迷。

e.en: The job needs brains as much as {brawn}.
e.zh: 这份工作既需要脑力,也需要体力。

e.en: He relied on his {brawn} to move the heavy crates.
e.zh: 他靠一身蛮力搬动那些沉重的板条箱。

brawny.t: adj. 肌肉发达的；强壮的

e.en: A {brawny} dockworker hoisted the crate onto his shoulder.
e.zh: 一个肌肉发达的码头工人把板条箱扛上肩。

e.en: His {brawny} arms were covered in tattoos.
e.zh: 他那粗壮的胳膊上布满了纹身。
