e.zh: 我的新牛仔裤接缝处都快撑破了。

e.en: The kids were {busting} with excitement on Christmas morning.
e.zh: 圣诞节早晨,孩子们兴奋得快要爆炸了。

bustle.t:
n. 喧嚣忙乱
v. 匆忙奔走

e.en: I love the {bustle} of the night market in Taipei.
e.zh: 我喜欢台北夜市的喧闹热闹。

e.en: Waiters {bustle} between tables during the dinner rush.
e.zh: 晚餐高峰期服务员在餐桌间忙碌穿梭。

bustled.t: v. 匆忙奔走（bustle 的过去式）

e.en: The chef {bustled} around the kitchen preparing the banquet.
e.zh: 厨师在厨房里忙忙碌碌地准备宴会。

e.en: Shoppers {bustled} through the mall on Black Friday.
e.zh: 黑色星期五购物者们在商场里熙熙攘攘。

bustles.t: v. 匆忙奔走（第三人称单数）

e.en: The café {bustles} with students every weekday morning.
e.zh: 这家咖啡馆每个工作日早上都挤满了学生。

e.en: Tokyo {bustles} with energy long after midnight.
e.zh: 东京在午夜过后依然充满活力,熙熙攘攘。

bustling.t: adj. 熙熙攘攘的、繁忙的

e.en: We stayed in a {bustling} neighborhood full of restaurants.
e.zh: 我们住在一个热闹的街区,周围全是餐馆。

e.en: The {bustling} market sells fresh seafood every morning.
e.zh: 这个熙熙攘攘的市场每天早上都卖新鲜海鲜。

busts.t:
n. 半身像；胸围
v. 打破、突袭

e.en: The museum displays marble {busts} of Roman emperors.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了罗马皇帝的大理石半身像。

e.en: Every startup {busts} eventually if it ignores customers.
e.zh: 任何忽视客户的初创公司最终都会倒闭。

e.en: The dress was designed for {busty} women who want comfort.
e.zh: 这件连衣裙是为追求舒适的丰满女性设计的。

e.en: She prefers tops that flatter her {busty} figure.
e.zh: 她喜欢能衬托她丰满身材的上衣。

busy.t: adj. 忙碌的；（电话）占线的

e.en: Sorry, I'm too {busy} to chat right now.
e.zh: 抱歉,我现在太忙了没法聊天。

e.en: The intersection gets {busy} during rush hour.
e.zh: 这个路口在高峰时段会变得很繁忙。

e.en: My neighbor is a {busybody} who watches everyone come and go.
e.zh: 我的邻居是个爱管闲事的人,总盯着人来人往。

e.en: Don't be a {busybody} about your coworker's personal life.
e.zh: 别对同事的私生活说三道四。

e.en: The {busyness} of modern life leaves little time for reflection.
e.zh: 现代生活的忙碌让人几乎没有时间反思。

e.en: She mistakes {busyness} for genuine productivity at work.
e.zh: 她把忙碌误认为是工作中真正的生产力。

busywork.t: n. 打发时间的琐碎工作

e.en: The teacher assigned {busywork} just to keep students quiet.
e.zh: 老师布置了些没意义的功课只是为了让学生安静。

e.en: Most of my Monday meetings feel like pointless {busywork}.
e.zh: 我周一的大部分会议都感觉像是毫无意义的应付差事。

but.t:
conj. 但是
prep. 除…之外

e.en: I wanted to come, {but} my flight was canceled.
e.zh: 我本来想来的,但是我的航班被取消了。

e.en: Everyone {but} Tom finished the assignment on time.
e.zh: 除了汤姆以外,大家都按时完成了作业。

e.en: Synthetic rubber tires are made primarily from {butadiene}.
e.zh: 合成橡胶轮胎主要是用丁二烯制成的。

e.en: The chemical plant produces {butadiene} for industrial use.
e.zh: 这家化工厂生产工业用的丁二烯。

e.en: Refill the lighter with {butane} from the canister.
e.zh: 用罐子里的丁烷给打火机充气。

e.en: Campers use {butane} stoves for cooking outdoors.
e.zh: 露营者使用丁烷炉在户外做饭。

e.en: She rocks a {butch} haircut and a leather jacket.
e.zh: 她留着帅气的短发,穿着皮夹克,很有男人味。

e.en: The character has a tough, {butch} attitude on screen.
e.zh: 这个角色在荧幕上展现出强硬阳刚的态度。

butcher.t:
n. 屠夫、肉贩
v. 屠宰；搞砸

e.en: The local {butcher} sells the freshest steaks in town.
e.zh: 当地的肉贩卖的牛排是镇上最新鲜的。

e.en: Please don't {butcher} my name when introducing me.
e.zh: 介绍我的时候请不要把我的名字念错得乱七八糟。

e.en: The translator {butchered} the original poem completely.
e.zh: 译者把原诗翻译得面目全非。

e.en: He {butchered} the chicken with skill and precision.
e.zh: 他熟练精准地把鸡肉切割好了。

butchering.t:
v. 屠宰（现在分词）
n. 屠宰业

e.en: The chef demonstrated {butchering} a whole pig on stage.
e.zh: 主厨在台上演示了如何分解一整头猪。

e.en: Stop {butchering} the lyrics and just hum the tune.
e.zh: 别再瞎唱歌词了,哼调子就行。

butchers.t:
n. 屠夫（复数）
v. 屠宰

e.en: Two {butchers} prepare cuts of meat behind the counter.
e.zh: 两位肉贩在柜台后面切割肉块。

e.en: That show always {butchers} historical facts for drama.
e.zh: 那部剧为了戏剧效果总是歪曲历史事实。

e.en: He learned the art of {butchery} from his grandfather.
e.zh: 他从祖父那里学会了屠宰的手艺。

e.en: Critics called the war an act of senseless {butchery}.
e.zh: 评论家称这场战争是毫无意义的屠杀。

bute.t: n. 保泰松（兽用止痛药）

e.en: The vet prescribed {bute} to ease the horse's joint pain.
e.zh: 兽医开了保泰松来缓解马的关节疼痛。

e.en: Racing officials banned {bute} on competition days.
e.zh: 赛马官方禁止在比赛日使用保泰松。

e.en: The {butler} answered the door and took our coats.
e.zh: 管家来开门并接过了我们的外套。

e.en: Bruce Wayne's loyal {butler} Alfred raised him after his parents died.
e.zh: 布鲁斯·韦恩忠诚的管家阿尔弗雷德在他父母去世后把他养大。

butlins.t: n. 巴特林度假村（英国连锁）

e.en: Our family spent every summer at {Butlins} in the eighties.
e.zh: 八十年代我们全家每个夏天都在巴特林度假村度过。

e.en: The kids loved the entertainment shows at {Butlins}.
e.zh: 孩子们很喜欢巴特林度假村的娱乐表演。

butt.t:
n. 屁股；烟蒂
v. 用头顶撞

e.en: She sat on her {butt} and refused to move.
e.zh: 她屁股坐在地上,死活不肯动。

e.en: He became the {butt} of every joke at the party.
e.zh: 他成了派对上所有笑话的笑柄。

butte.t: n. 孤山、孤峰（平顶小山）

e.en: The lone {butte} towered above the desert floor at sunset.
e.zh: 日落时分,孤零零的孤丘高耸于沙漠之上。

e.en: Hikers climbed the {butte} for panoramic views of the valley.
e.zh: 徒步者爬上孤丘,饱览山谷的全景。

butter.t:
n. 黄油
v. 涂黄油

e.en: Spread some {butter} on the toast while it's still warm.
e.zh: 趁吐司还热的时候抹点黄油上去。

e.en: This sauce is rich because of all the melted {butter}.
e.zh: 这款酱汁很浓郁,因为加了很多融化的黄油。

e.en: The Thanksgiving {Butterball} turkey fed twelve hungry guests.
e.zh: 那只感恩节的黄油球火鸡让十二位饥饿的客人都吃饱了。

e.en: The puppy is a chubby little {butterball} of fluff.
e.zh: 这只小狗是个圆滚滚毛茸茸的小胖墩。

e.en: A bright yellow {buttercup} bloomed at the edge of the field.
e.zh: 田边开着一朵亮黄色的毛茛花。

e.en: Wake up, {buttercup}, breakfast is getting cold.
e.zh: 快醒醒,小宝贝,早餐都要凉了。

buttered.t: v. 涂了黄油的（过去式/形容词）

e.en: She {buttered} her toast and added a drizzle of honey.
e.zh: 她给吐司涂了黄油,还淋了一些蜂蜜。

e.en: The waiter served warm {buttered} rolls before the meal.
e.zh: 服务员在用餐前端上了温热的涂黄油面包卷。

e.en: Whole milk has a higher {butterfat} content than skim.
e.zh: 全脂牛奶的乳脂含量比脱脂牛奶高。

e.en: Premium ice cream contains at least 14 percent {butterfat}.
e.zh: 优质冰淇淋的乳脂含量至少为14%。

e.en: The chef grilled a fresh {butterfish} with lemon and herbs.
e.zh: 厨师用柠檬和香草烤了一条新鲜的鲳鱼。

e.en: Fishermen caught several {butterfish} off the coast yesterday.
e.zh: 渔民昨天在海边捕到了几条鲳鱼。

e.en: The chef {butterflied} the chicken before grilling it.
e.zh: 厨师在烤鸡之前把鸡肉对半剖开摊平。

e.en: Try {butterflied} shrimp tossed with garlic and olive oil.
e.zh: 试试用蒜和橄榄油拌的对半剖开的虾。

e.en: Colorful {butterflies} fluttered around the lavender bushes.
e.zh: 五彩斑斓的蝴蝶在薰衣草丛中翩翩起舞。

e.en: I always get {butterflies} before public speaking.
e.zh: 每次公开演讲前我都会紧张得心里发慌。

e.en: A monarch {butterfly} landed gently on the flower.
e.zh: 一只帝王蝶轻轻落在花朵上。

e.en: She swims the {butterfly} stroke faster than anyone on the team.
e.zh: 她游蝶泳比队里任何人都快。

e.en: This pancake recipe calls for a cup of {buttermilk}.
e.zh: 这个煎饼配方需要一杯酪乳。

e.en: Soak the chicken in {buttermilk} overnight for tender meat.
e.zh: 把鸡肉在酪乳里浸泡一夜,肉质会更嫩。

e.en: Roast the {butternut} squash with olive oil and sage.
e.zh: 用橄榄油和鼠尾草烤胡桃南瓜。

e.en: Creamy {butternut} soup is perfect for chilly autumn nights.
e.zh: 奶香胡桃南瓜汤非常适合凉爽的秋夜。

e.en: Drizzle warm {butterscotch} sauce over vanilla ice cream.
e.zh: 把温热的奶油糖浆淋在香草冰淇淋上。

e.en: Grandma always kept {butterscotch} candies in her purse.
e.zh: 奶奶的包里总是放着奶油糖果。

e.en: The croissant had a flaky, {buttery} texture.
e.zh: 这个可颂酥脆松软,带着浓郁的黄油味。

e.en: Chardonnay often has a smooth, {buttery} finish.
e.zh: 霞多丽葡萄酒常常带有顺滑浓郁的黄油余味。

e.en: He pulled a muscle in his left {buttock} during the sprint.
e.zh: 他冲刺时拉伤了左臀的肌肉。

e.en: The doctor gave the injection in his upper {buttock}.
e.zh: 医生在他臀部上方注射了一针。

e.en: Squats are great for strengthening your {buttocks} and thighs.
e.zh: 深蹲对锻炼臀部和大腿很有效。

e.en: He slipped and landed hard on his {buttocks}.
e.zh: 他滑了一跤，重重地摔在屁股上。

button.t:
n. 按钮；纽扣
v. 扣上

e.en: Just click the green {button} to start the download.
e.zh: 点一下绿色按钮就能开始下载。

e.en: A {button} fell off my coat this morning.
e.zh: 今早我外套上掉了一颗扣子。

buttoned.t: v. 扣上（纽扣）的过去式

e.en: He {buttoned} his shirt up to the collar.
e.zh: 他把衬衫一直扣到领口。

e.en: She wore a neatly {buttoned} cardigan to the interview.
e.zh: 她面试时穿了一件扣得整整齐齐的开衫。

buttonhole.t:
n. 纽扣眼
v. 拉住搭话

e.en: He wore a small rose in his lapel {buttonhole}.
e.zh: 他西装翻领的扣眼里别着一朵小玫瑰。

e.en: The tailor sewed a new {buttonhole} on the jacket.
e.zh: 裁缝在外套上缝了一个新扣眼。

e.en: The remote has too many tiny {buttons} to remember.
e.zh: 这遥控器上的小按键多得记不住。

e.en: She sewed three pearl {buttons} onto the blouse.
e.zh: 她在衬衫上缝了三颗珍珠纽扣。

buttress.t:
n. 扶壁、支撑
v. 支持、加强

e.en: The cathedral's flying {buttress} keeps the wall from collapsing.
e.zh: 大教堂的飞扶壁防止墙体倒塌。

e.en: New data will {buttress} the team's argument in court.
e.zh: 新数据将为团队在法庭上的论点提供支撑。

butty.t: n. 夹心面包（英式俚语）

e.en: He grabbed a bacon {butty} from the corner shop.
e.zh: 他在街角小店买了个培根三明治。

e.en: Nothing beats a chip {butty} after a long shift.
e.zh: 漫长一班结束后，没什么比薯条三明治更香了。

e.en: The window seals are made of durable {butyl} rubber.
e.zh: 窗户密封条是用耐用的丁基橡胶做的。

e.en: Workers applied a {butyl} sealant around the roof edges.
e.zh: 工人在屋顶边缘涂上了丁基密封胶。

e.en: A quick-thinking {bystander} called the ambulance immediately.
e.zh: 一位反应敏捷的旁观者立刻叫了救护车。

e.en: She refused to be a silent {bystander} to the bullying.
e.zh: 她拒绝做欺凌事件的沉默旁观者。

byte.t: n. 字节（计算机存储单位）

e.en: Each {byte} stores eight bits of data in memory.
e.zh: 每个字节在内存中存储八个比特的数据。

e.en: The file is only a few hundred {bytes} in size.
e.zh: 这个文件只有几百字节大小。

e.en: We took a quiet {byway} to avoid the highway traffic.
e.zh: 我们走了一条安静的小路避开高速堵车。

e.en: The travel guide highlights scenic {byways} across the countryside.
e.zh: 这本旅游指南推荐了乡间多条风景小道。

e.en: His name became a {byword} for innovation in tech.
e.zh: 他的名字成了科技创新的代名词。

e.en: The brand is a {byword} for reliability among drivers.
e.zh: 这个品牌在车主中是可靠性的代名词。

byzantine.t:
adj. 错综复杂的
adj. 拜占庭的

e.en: The tax code is famously {byzantine} and hard to navigate.
e.zh: 税法以错综复杂著称,难以理清。

e.en: She studied {byzantine} mosaics during her trip to Istanbul.
e.zh: 她在伊斯坦布尔旅行时研究了拜占庭式马赛克。

e.en: Ancient {Byzantium} later became the city of Constantinople.
e.zh: 古代拜占庭后来成为君士坦丁堡。

e.en: The poem evokes the golden domes of {Byzantium}.
e.zh: 这首诗让人联想到拜占庭的金色穹顶。

bottle.t:
n. 瓶子
v. 装瓶

bottlebrush.t:
n. 瓶刷（清洗瓶子的刷子）
n. 瓶刷树

bottled.t:
adj. 瓶装的
v. 装瓶（bottle 的过去式）

bottleneck.t: n. 瓶颈；性能/进度制约点

bottlenose.t: n. 宽吻海豚（常指 bottlenose dolphin）

bottles.t:
n. 瓶子（复数）
v. 装瓶（第三人称单数）

bottling.t:
v. 装瓶（现在分词）
n. 瓶装（过程）

bottom.t:
n. 底部；最下方
adj. 最底下的

boudoir.t: n. 闺房；女子私人起居室

bouffant.t:
adj. 蓬松的（发型、裙摆）
n. 蓬蓬头

bougainvillaea.t: n. 三角梅；叶子花（热带攀援植物）

bougainville.t: n. 布干维尔（巴布亚新几内亚岛屿）

bought.t: v. 买（buy 的过去式和过去分词）

bouillabaisse.t: n. 马赛鱼汤（法式海鲜浓汤）

bouillon.t: n. 肉汤；清汤（法式高汤）

e.en: We spent the afternoon strolling through the {botanic} gardens.
e.zh: 我们整个下午都在植物园里漫步。

e.en: The city's {botanic} collection includes over five thousand species.
e.zh: 这座城市的植物收藏包括五千多种植物。

botanical.t:
adj. 植物的；植物学的
n. 植物制剂

e.en: This gin contains a unique blend of {botanical} ingredients.
e.zh: 这款金酒含有独特的植物成分混合配方。

e.en: She works as a researcher at the national {botanical} garden.
e.zh: 她在国家植物园担任研究员。

botanically.t: adv. 从植物学角度；在植物学上

e.en: Tomatoes are {botanically} fruits, even though we cook them as vegetables.
e.zh: 从植物学上讲，番茄是水果，尽管我们当蔬菜来烹饪。

e.en: The region is {botanically} diverse, with hundreds of native species.
e.zh: 该地区植物种类丰富，拥有数百种本土植物。

botanist.t: n. 植物学家；研究植物的人

e.en: The {botanist} discovered a new orchid species deep in the rainforest.
e.zh: 那位植物学家在雨林深处发现了一种新的兰花。

e.en: As a {botanist}, she travels the world studying rare plants.
e.zh: 作为植物学家，她环游世界研究稀有植物。

e.en: She studied {botany} before becoming a landscape designer.
e.zh: 她在成为景观设计师之前学过植物学。

e.en: The {botany} textbook explains plant cell structure in detail.
e.zh: 这本植物学教科书详细讲解了植物细胞结构。

botch.t:
v. 搞砸；拙劣地完成
n. 拙劣的活儿

botched.t:
adj. 搞砸的、拙劣完成的
v. botch 的过去式：把…弄糟

both.t:
adj./pron. 两者都、双方
conj. both…and… 既…又…

bother.t:
v. 打扰；费心
n. 麻烦

bothered.t:
adj. 烦恼的，困扰的
v. bother 的过去式

bothering.t: v. 打扰，使烦恼（bother 的现在分词）

bothers.t:
v. 打扰；使烦恼
n. 麻烦（bother 的复数/第三人称）

bothy.t: n. 山间简易小屋（苏格兰供登山者过夜）

botox.t: n. 肉毒杆菌素（除皱注射）

botswana.t: n. 博茨瓦纳（非洲南部国家）

botticelli.t: n. 波提切利（意大利文艺复兴画家）

botulism.t: n. 肉毒杆菌中毒（食物中毒的一种）

bottomland.t: n. 河谷低地；河边冲积地

bottomless.t: adj. 无底的；深不可测的

boucle.t: n. 圈圈呢（带环状纹理的粗纺面料）

boudin.t:
n. 血肠（法式香肠）
n. 条状物、卷状物

bottoms.t:
n. 底部；最低点
n. 裤装下身（如裤子）

botulinum.t:
adj. 肉毒杆菌的
n. 肉毒杆菌（产生肉毒素的梭状芽孢杆菌）

bibb.t: n. 毕布（生菜品种/姓氏）

bonnie.t:
adj. 漂亮的（苏格兰）
n. 邦妮（人名）

backslidden.t: vi. 堕落, 退步\nn. 堕落, 退步

bagmen.t: n. 推销员, 中间人

balconied.t: n. 阳台, 戏院楼厅

baldest.t: a. 秃头的, 光秃的, 单调的, 赤裸的\nvi. 变秃

balmiest.t: a. 芳香的, 温和的, 止痛的\n[化] 香脂气味的

balmier.t: a. 芳香的, 温和的, 止痛的\n[化] 香脂气味的

bandied.t: a. 向外弯曲的\nvt. 打来打去, 谈论, 往复投掷

barest.t: a. 赤裸的, 缺少的, 无遮蔽的, 坦率的\nvt. 使赤裸, 露出

barmier.t: a. 发酵的\n[机] 酵母的, 泡沫的

battier.t: a. 疯癫的, 古怪的, 蝙蝠的

bawdiest.t: a. 淫秽的, 言语猥亵的

beatified.t: vt. 赐福给, 行宣福礼

beefier.t: a. (牛)多肉的, 象牛肉的, 粗壮的, 结实的

begot.t: vt. 为某人之生父, 招致, 产生, 引起

bellied.t: n. 腹部, 食欲\nvt. 使鼓起\nvi. 鼓起, 匍匐前进

bespoken.t: vt. 预约, 订, 表示\nn. 预约

bade.t: n. 出价\nv. 命令, 吩咐, 请求, 表示, 宣布, 投标

biggest.t: a. 大的, 重要的\nadv. 大量地

bitchiest.t: a. 开下流玩笑的, 好挑剔的

bivouacking.t: n. 野营, 露营, 露营地\nvi. 露宿

bivouacked.t: n. 野营, 露营, 露营地\nvi. 露宿

blackest.t: n. 黑色, 黑颜料\na. 黑色的

blandest.t: a. 温和的, 乏味的, 冷漠的\n[医] 温和的, 淡的

bleakest.t: a. 萧瑟的, 荒凉的, 阴冷的

bloodiest.t: a. 血腥的, 嗜杀的, 有血的

bluntest.t: a. 钝的, 坦率的, 麻痹的

boing.t: n. 体臭, 汗臭, 狐臭, 暂时无法满足的订货, 戏院票房, 戏院售票处, 分支机构

boldest.t: a. 大胆的\nn. 粗体\n[计] 粗体

bondsmen.t: n. 奴隶\n[经] 保证人

bookmen.t: n. 学者, 文人, 书商

bossiest.t: a. 专横的, 浮雕装饰的

bouncier.t: a. 快活的, 精神饱满的, 有弹性的, 自大的

bowmen.t: n. 弓射手, 持弓的兵, 船首的划手

brer.t: [计] 总线请求\n[化] 生物试剂

brainiest.t: a. 脑筋好的, 聪明的

brakemen.t: n. 司闸员, 制动手

brashest.t: a. 性急的, 仓促的, 无礼的, 傲慢的\nn. 胃灼热, 骤雨, 碎石堆

bravest.t: a. 勇敢的, 美好的, 华丽的\nn. 勇敢者\nvt. 勇敢地面对

breastfed.t: vt.& vi. 用母乳喂养, 哺乳

breeziest.t: a. 有微风的, 通风好的, 活泼的

briefest.t: n. 摘要, 简报\na. 简短的, 短暂的\nvt. 对...作简报, 摘要, 节录

briskest.t: a. 强烈的, 寒冷而干燥的, 活泼的\nvt. 使活泼\nvi. 活跃起来

broadest.t: a. 宽广的, 辽阔的, 广大的, 显著的\nadv. 宽阔地\nn. 宽阔部分

bubbliest.t: a. 多泡的, 起泡的\nn. 香槟酒

bulkier.t: a. 庞大的\n[机] 庞大, 笨重

bulkiest.t: a. 庞大的\n[机] 庞大, 笨重

bumpier.t: a. 颠簸的, 崎岖不平的

bumpiest.t: a. 颠簸的, 崎岖不平的

burlier.t: a. 结实的, 粗壮的, 率直的

burliest.t: a. 结实的, 粗壮的, 率直的

bushier.t: a. 灌木一样的, 灌木茂密的, 浓密的

bustier.t: a. 大胸脯的, 胸部丰满的

b-complex.t: 维生素B族；B族复合维生素

e.en: She takes a {b-complex} supplement every morning.
e.zh: 她每天早上服用一种B族复合维生素补充剂。

e.en: {B-complex} vitamins help with energy metabolism.
e.zh: B族复合维生素有助于能量代谢。

b-girls.t: 霹雳舞女舞者；街舞女孩

e.en: The {b-girls} battled fiercely in the dance competition.
e.zh: 街舞女孩们在舞蹈比赛中激烈较量。

e.en: Several {b-girls} performed amazing power moves.
e.zh: 几位霹雳舞女舞者表演了精彩的力量动作。

e.en: He has a soft spot for cheesy {b-movies} from the 1950s.
e.zh: 他特别喜欢上世纪五十年代那些俗套的B级片。

e.en: The festival celebrates obscure {b-movies} and cult horror.
e.zh: 这个电影节专门致敬冷门B级片和邪典恐怖片。

e.en: She got her start acting in a forgotten {b-picture}.
e.zh: 她演艺生涯的起点是一部被遗忘的B级片。

e.en: The studio churned out a {b-picture} every other week.
e.zh: 那家制片厂几乎每两周就赶制一部B级片。

e.en: The {b-side} of the single became unexpectedly popular.
e.zh: 那张单曲的B面意外地走红了。

e.en: Fans love digging through old {b-sides} and rarities.
e.zh: 歌迷们喜欢翻找老唱片的B面和稀有曲目。

b-to-b.t: 企业对企业的（商业模式）

e.en: Their {b-to-b} sales team focuses on enterprise clients.
e.zh: 他们的B2B销售团队专注于企业客户。

e.en: The platform offers a {b-to-b} marketplace for suppliers.
e.zh: 该平台为供应商提供企业对企业的交易市场。

e.en: Whole grains are a good source of {b-vitamins}.
e.zh: 全谷物是B族维生素的良好来源。

e.en: The doctor recommended a supplement with {b-vitamins}.
e.zh: 医生推荐了一种含B族维生素的补充剂。

e.en: The toddler pointed at the field and shouted '{baa-lamb}!'
e.zh: 那个小孩指着田野喊道："小羊咩咩！"

e.en: Grandma read a story about a fluffy little {baa-lamb}.
e.zh: 奶奶讲了一个毛茸茸小羊羔的故事。

babassu.t: 巴巴苏棕榈（巴西产油棕榈）

e.en: The cosmetic uses {babassu} oil for its moisturizing properties.
e.zh: 这款化妆品使用巴巴苏油以发挥其保湿功效。

e.en: Local communities harvest {babassu} nuts for cooking oil.
e.zh: 当地社区采收巴巴苏果用以榨食用油。

babbittry.t: 市侩作风；庸俗市民习气

e.en: The novel satirizes the {babbittry} of small-town businessmen.
e.zh: 这部小说讽刺了小镇商人的市侩习气。

e.en: He despised the conformist {babbittry} of his suburban neighbors.
e.zh: 他鄙视郊区邻居那种随波逐流的市侩作风。

e.en: I tuned out the constant {babblement} from the next table.
e.zh: 我对邻桌没完没了的闲扯充耳不闻。

e.en: Her speech was dismissed as mere {babblement}.
e.zh: 她的发言被当作毫无意义的废话而被忽视。

e.en: The conference descended into a {babelism} of competing dialects.
e.zh: 会议最终演变为方言交杂的语言混乱。

e.en: Online forums often suffer from a kind of digital {babelism}.
e.zh: 网络论坛常常陷入一种数字时代的众声嘈杂。

babesiasis.t: 巴贝虫病（蜱传寄生虫感染）

e.en: The vet confirmed the dog had contracted {babesiasis} from a tick bite.
e.zh: 兽医确诊这只狗因蜱虫叮咬感染了巴贝虫病。

e.en: Cases of {babesiasis} have risen in the northeastern states.
e.zh: 东北部各州的巴贝虫病病例有所上升。

babiche.t: 生皮条（用于雪鞋等的鞣制兽皮带）

e.en: The snowshoes were laced with traditional {babiche}.
e.zh: 那双雪鞋是用传统的生皮条编结而成的。

e.en: He repaired the harness using strips of {babiche}.
e.zh: 他用一条条生皮带修补了那副挽具。

e.en: The bouquet was filled out with sprigs of {babies'-breath}.
e.zh: 那束花用满天星的细枝点缀得更加丰盈。

e.en: She tucked some {babies'-breath} into her hair for the wedding.
e.zh: 婚礼上她在头发里别了几枝满天星。

babiesbreath.t: 满天星（小白花，常用于花束陪衬）

e.en: The florist added {babiesbreath} to soften the arrangement.
e.zh: 花艺师加入满天星，让花束显得更柔和。

e.en: Tiny clusters of {babiesbreath} dotted the table centerpieces.
e.zh: 小簇的满天星点缀着餐桌中央的花饰。

e.en: The botanist examined the {baccate} fruit clusters on the shrub.
e.zh: 植物学家观察了灌木上一簇簇浆果状的果实。

e.en: Many tropical species produce {baccate} berries that birds disperse.
e.zh: 许多热带物种结出由鸟类传播的浆果状果实。

e.en: The old manuscript described a {baccated} vine climbing the wall.
e.zh: 古老的手稿描绘了一株结满浆果的藤蔓爬上墙壁。

e.en: Decorative carvings showed {baccated} branches around the doorway.
e.zh: 装饰雕刻在门口周围呈现出结满浆果的枝条。

e.en: The festival descended into outright {bacchanalianism} by midnight.
e.zh: 到了午夜，节日彻底沦为一场狂饮纵乐。

e.en: Critics condemned the party's {bacchanalianism} as excessive.
e.zh: 评论者谴责派对上的狂欢纵乐过于放纵。

e.en: The ancient mural depicted a wild {bacchant} dancing in the woods.
e.zh: 古老的壁画描绘了一位狂野的酒神信徒在林中起舞。

e.en: He behaved like a {bacchant} at the wedding feast.
e.zh: 他在婚宴上举止活像个狂欢纵酒之徒。

e.en: The statue of a {bacchante} stood in the museum garden.
e.zh: 博物馆花园里立着一尊酒神女祭司的雕像。

e.en: She danced with the abandon of a {bacchante}.
e.zh: 她跳舞时如酒神女祭司般纵情忘我。

e.en: The painting showed {bacchantes} crowned with ivy and grapes.
e.zh: 画中描绘了头戴常春藤与葡萄的酒神女祭司们。

e.en: Greek myths often feature wild {bacchantes} roaming the hills.
e.zh: 希腊神话中常出现在山野中游荡的酒神女祭司们。

e.en: The crowd reached a {bacchantic} frenzy as the music swelled.
e.zh: 音乐高涨时，人群达到了酒神信徒般的狂热。

e.en: His speech took on a {bacchantic} fervor.
e.zh: 他的演说带上了酒神般的狂热。

e.en: Robed {bacchants} marched through the village streets.
e.zh: 身披长袍的酒神信徒们穿行于村庄街道。

e.en: The poem describes {bacchants} singing under the full moon.
e.zh: 那首诗描绘了酒神信徒们在满月下歌唱。

e.en: The party turned into a {bacchic} celebration of wine and song.
e.zh: 派对变成了一场酒与歌的酒神式狂欢。

e.en: Ancient {bacchic} rites honored the god of wine.
e.zh: 古代的酒神祭典是为酒神而举行的。

e.en: Botanists classified the plant as a {bacciferous} species.
e.zh: 植物学家将该植物归为一种结浆果的物种。

e.en: Many {bacciferous} shrubs attract migrating birds.
e.zh: 许多结浆果的灌木能吸引迁徙的鸟类。

e.en: The seeds had a small, {bacciform} appearance under the microscope.
e.zh: 在显微镜下，那些种子呈现出小巧的浆果形状。

e.en: She sketched the {bacciform} fruit in her field notebook.
e.zh: 她在野外笔记本上画下了那种浆果形的果实。

e.en: Many {baccivorous} birds depend on autumn berry crops.
e.zh: 许多以浆果为食的鸟类依赖秋季的浆果作物。

e.en: The thrush is a typically {baccivorous} species.
e.zh: 画眉是一种典型以浆果为食的鸟类。

bachelor-at-arms.t: 学士见习骑士；初级武士

e.en: In medieval ranks, a {bachelor-at-arms} served under a senior knight.
e.zh: 在中世纪的等级中，初级武士隶属于资深骑士。

e.en: The young {bachelor-at-arms} polished his lord's armor each morning.
e.zh: 那位年轻的学士见习骑士每天清晨擦拭领主的盔甲。

e.en: He happily settled into a life of {bachelordom}.
e.zh: 他怡然自得地过起了单身汉的生活。

e.en: Friends teased him about his prolonged {bachelordom}.
e.zh: 朋友们取笑他长期的单身状态。

e.en: She lived as a confident {bachelorgirl} in the city.
e.zh: 她在城里过着自信独立的单身女子生活。

e.en: The novel celebrated the freedoms of the modern {bachelorgirl}.
e.zh: 这部小说颂扬了现代独立单身女子的自由。

bachelorism.t: 单身主义；单身生活习性

e.en: His friends joked about his unwavering {bachelorism}.
e.zh: 朋友们取笑他坚定不移的单身主义。

e.en: The article explored modern attitudes toward {bachelorism}.
e.zh: 这篇文章探讨了对单身主义的现代态度。

e.en: He enjoyed his {bachelorship} well into his forties.
e.zh: 他直到四十多岁仍享受着单身的身份。

e.en: After earning his {bachelorship}, he pursued a master's degree.
e.zh: 取得学士学位后，他继续攻读硕士。

e.en: The guide expected a small {bachsheesh} after the tour.
e.zh: 导游在游览结束后期待一笔小小的赏钱。

e.en: Travelers learned to carry coins for {bachsheesh}.
e.zh: 旅行者学会随身带些零钱用作小费。

e.en: The doctor diagnosed a {bacillary} infection in the patient's lungs.
e.zh: 医生诊断病人肺部出现杆菌感染。

e.en: Researchers studied the spread of {bacillary} dysentery.
e.zh: 研究人员研究了杆菌性痢疾的传播。

e.en: The hospital used a strong {bacillicide} to disinfect surfaces.
e.zh: 医院使用强效杀杆菌剂对表面进行消毒。

e.en: This cleaner acts as an effective {bacillicide}.
e.zh: 这种清洁剂是一种有效的杀杆菌剂。

e.en: Under the microscope, the cells appeared distinctly {bacilliform}.
e.zh: 在显微镜下，这些细胞显然呈杆状。

e.en: The virus has a {bacilliform} structure.
e.zh: 该病毒具有杆状结构。

bacillophobia.t: 杆菌恐惧症；细菌恐惧症

e.en: His {bacillophobia} made him wash his hands obsessively.
e.zh: 他的细菌恐惧症让他强迫性地反复洗手。

e.en: Therapy helped her manage severe {bacillophobia}.
e.zh: 治疗帮助她控制了严重的细菌恐惧症。

e.en: The nurse applied {bacitracin} ointment to the small cut.
e.zh: 护士在小伤口上涂了杆菌肽软膏。

e.en: {Bacitracin} is commonly used to prevent skin infections.
e.zh: 杆菌肽常用于预防皮肤感染。

back-alley.t: 后巷的；偷偷摸摸的；非法的

e.en: They met in a dim {back-alley} behind the restaurant.
e.zh: 他们在餐馆后面昏暗的小巷里碰面。

e.en: The film exposed dangerous {back-alley} medical procedures.
e.zh: 该影片揭露了危险的非法地下医疗手术。

babiroussa.t: 鹿豚（印尼苏拉威西的野猪）

e.en: The {babiroussa} has unusual curving tusks.
e.zh: 鹿豚长着不寻常的弯曲獠牙。

e.en: We spotted a {babiroussa} in the forest.
e.zh: 我们在森林里看到了一只鹿豚。

e.en: The {babirusa} is native to Indonesia.
e.zh: 鹿豚原产于印度尼西亚。

e.en: Zoologists study the rare {babirusa}.
e.zh: 动物学家研究这种稀有的鹿豚。

e.en: An old text mentioned the {babirussa}.
e.zh: 一本旧书提到了鹿豚。

e.en: The {babirussa} lives on Sulawesi.
e.zh: 鹿豚生活在苏拉威西岛。

e.en: He became a devoted {babist} in Persia.
e.zh: 他在波斯成为了虔诚的巴比教徒。

e.en: The {babist} movement arose in the 1840s.
e.zh: 巴比教运动兴起于1840年代。

babka.t: 巴布卡蛋糕（东欧甜面包）

e.en: She baked a chocolate {babka} for brunch.
e.zh: 她为早午餐烤了一个巧克力巴布卡蛋糕。

e.en: The bakery's {babka} sells out daily.
e.zh: 这家面包店的巴布卡蛋糕每天都会售罄。

e.en: Two {babkas} were cooling on the rack.
e.zh: 两个巴布卡蛋糕正在架子上冷却。

e.en: They sampled different {babkas} at the market.
e.zh: 他们在市场上品尝了不同的巴布卡蛋糕。

baboo.t: 先生（印度对男士的尊称）

e.en: The clerk addressed him as {baboo}.
e.zh: 那位文员称他为"先生"。

e.en: In old India a {baboo} was a respected gentleman.
e.zh: 在旧时印度，baboo是受人尊敬的先生。

baboonery.t: 愚蠢行为；狒狒般的胡闹

e.en: Stop this {baboonery} and act seriously.
e.zh: 别再胡闹了，认真点。

e.en: The classroom descended into pure {baboonery}.
e.zh: 教室里乱成了一团胡闹。

e.en: He gave a {baboonish} grin.
e.zh: 他咧嘴露出狒狒般的笑容。

e.en: Their {baboonish} antics annoyed the teacher.
e.zh: 他们粗野愚蠢的滑稽举动惹恼了老师。

e.en: She bought leather {babouche} in the souk.
e.zh: 她在集市里买了一双皮制摩洛哥拖鞋。

e.en: The colorful {babouche} caught her eye.
e.zh: 那双色彩鲜艳的摩洛哥拖鞋吸引了她的目光。

e.en: The {babu} stamped the documents.
e.zh: 那位文员在文件上盖了章。

e.en: He was a colonial-era {babu}.
e.zh: 他是殖民时代的印度文员。

e.en: The {babul} tree provides hardy wood.
e.zh: 金合欢树能提供坚硬的木材。

e.en: Goats grazed under the {babul}.
e.zh: 山羊在金合欢树下吃草。

e.en: She wore a {baby-blue} dress.
e.zh: 她穿着一条浅蓝色的连衣裙。

e.en: The nursery walls were {baby-blue}.
e.zh: 婴儿房的墙是婴儿蓝色的。

e.en: My father is a {baby-boomer}.
e.zh: 我父亲是婴儿潮一代。

e.en: Many {baby-boomers} are retiring now.
e.zh: 许多婴儿潮一代现在正在退休。

baby-bust.t: 婴儿低谷期；生育率骤降

e.en: The country faces a serious {baby-bust}.
e.zh: 该国面临严重的生育率骤降。

e.en: Economists worry about the {baby-bust} generation.
e.zh: 经济学家担忧低生育率一代。

e.en: She wore a cute {baby-doll} dress.
e.zh: 她穿了一条可爱的娃娃装。

e.en: He called her his {baby-doll}.
e.zh: 他叫她他的小娃娃。

e.en: The {baby-faced} actor played teen roles.
e.zh: 那位娃娃脸演员饰演青少年角色。

e.en: He's a {baby-faced} thirty-year-old.
e.zh: 他是个长着娃娃脸的三十岁男子。

e.en: She bought jars of {baby-food}.
e.zh: 她买了几瓶婴儿食品。

e.en: This {baby-food} is organic.
e.zh: 这款婴儿食品是有机的。

e.en: He warmed up the {baby-formula}.
e.zh: 他把婴儿配方奶粉加热了。

e.en: There's a shortage of {baby-formula}.
e.zh: 婴儿配方奶粉短缺。

e.en: They hired a {baby-minder} for the evening.
e.zh: 他们雇了一个保姆照看晚上。

e.en: The {baby-minder} arrived at six.
e.zh: 保姆六点到了。

e.en: Good {baby-minders} are hard to find.
e.zh: 好的保姆很难找。

e.en: The agency vets all its {baby-minders}.
e.zh: 中介对所有保姆都进行审核。

e.en: She earns extra money {baby-minding}.
e.zh: 她靠看护婴儿赚外快。

e.en: {Baby-minding} requires patience.
e.zh: 照看婴儿需要耐心。

e.en: The room had {baby-pink} walls.
e.zh: 房间的墙是浅粉色的。

e.en: She chose a {baby-pink} blanket.
e.zh: 她选了一条婴儿粉的毯子。

e.en: I {baby-sat} my niece last weekend.
e.zh: 上周末我照看了我的侄女。

e.en: She {baby-sat} for the neighbors often.
e.zh: 她经常给邻居家看小孩。

e.en: Can you {baby-sit} tonight?
e.zh: 你今晚能帮我看小孩吗？

e.en: Teenagers often {baby-sit} for extra cash.
e.zh: 青少年常常通过看小孩赚零花钱。

baby-sits.t: 照看小孩（第三人称单数）

e.en: She {baby-sits} every Friday night.
e.zh: 她每周五晚上都照看小孩。

e.en: He {baby-sits} for his cousin.
e.zh: 他帮他堂姐看小孩。

e.en: {Baby-sitting} pays well in this neighborhood.
e.zh: 在这个社区当临时保姆收入不错。

e.en: She enjoys {baby-sitting} on weekends.
e.zh: 她喜欢在周末照看小孩。

e.en: He spoke to the puppy in {baby-talk}.
e.zh: 他用儿语跟小狗说话。

e.en: Stop using {baby-talk} with me.
e.zh: 别用儿语跟我说话。

e.en: The toddler pushed his {baby-walker} around.
e.zh: 那幼儿推着学步车到处走。

e.en: Some doctors discourage using a {baby-walker}.
e.zh: 有些医生不建议使用学步车。

e.en: The post-war {babyboom} reshaped society.
e.zh: 战后的婴儿潮重塑了社会。

e.en: A small {babyboom} followed the lockdown.
e.zh: 封城之后出现了一波小型婴儿潮。

e.en: Hey, {babycakes}, come over here.
e.zh: 嘿，宝贝，过来这边。

e.en: He called her {babycakes} affectionately.
e.zh: 他亲昵地叫她宝贝。

e.en: She took a {babycare} class before delivery.
e.zh: 她在分娩前上了婴儿护理课程。

e.en: This brand specializes in {babycare} products.
e.zh: 这个品牌专做婴儿护理产品。

e.en: His {babyface} makes him look younger.
e.zh: 他的娃娃脸让他看起来更年轻。

e.en: The actor's {babyface} is his trademark.
e.zh: 那演员的娃娃脸是他的标志。

e.en: She dressed the baby in a soft {babygro}.
e.zh: 她给宝宝穿上了柔软的婴儿连体衣。

e.en: This {babygro} has tiny stars on it.
e.zh: 这件婴儿连体衣上有小星星。

e.en: She played with her wooden {babyhouse}.
e.zh: 她在玩她的木制玩具屋。

e.en: The {babyhouse} had tiny furniture inside.
e.zh: 那座玩具屋里有小巧的家具。

e.en: His complaints are pure {babyism}.
e.zh: 他的抱怨纯粹是孩子气。

e.en: Stop this {babyism} and grow up.
e.zh: 别再这么孩子气了，成熟点吧。

e.en: The couple remained {babyless} for years.
e.zh: 这对夫妇多年来一直没有孩子。

e.en: She felt sad about her {babyless} home.
e.zh: 她为没有孩子的家感到难过。

e.en: The crowd produced a {babylonish} clamor.
e.zh: 人群发出巴比伦式的嘈杂喧嚣。

e.en: He criticized the {babylonish} customs.
e.zh: 他批评那种巴比伦式的习俗。

e.en: They hired a trusted {babyminder}.
e.zh: 他们请了一位可靠的保姆。

e.en: The {babyminder} arrived early.
e.zh: 保姆早早地就到了。

e.en: They went on a {babymoon} to Hawaii.
e.zh: 他们去夏威夷度产前蜜月。

e.en: A {babymoon} is a pre-baby getaway.
e.zh: 产前蜜月是宝宝出生前的小度假。

babyproof.t: 对婴儿安全的；做防婴儿处理

e.en: They had to {babyproof} the entire house.
e.zh: 他们不得不把整个房子做防婴儿处理。

e.en: This cabinet is fully {babyproof}.
e.zh: 这个柜子已完全做了防婴儿处理。

babyproofing.t: 婴儿安全防护；居家防护处理

e.en: {Babyproofing} the kitchen took a weekend.
e.zh: 给厨房做婴儿安全防护花了一个周末。

e.en: They started {babyproofing} before the birth.
e.zh: 他们在孩子出生前就开始做安全防护了。

e.en: She slipped into {babytalk} with the dog.
e.zh: 她对狗狗用起了儿语。

e.en: Avoid {babytalk} when teaching kids.
e.zh: 教孩子时避免使用儿语。

e.en: The store sells organic {babywear}.
e.zh: 这家店出售有机婴儿服装。

e.en: She designs {babywear} for a living.
e.zh: 她以设计婴儿服装为生。

e.en: She cooked traditional {bacalao} for dinner.
e.zh: 她做了传统的咸鳕鱼当晚餐。

e.en: {Bacalao} is popular in Portuguese cuisine.
e.zh: 咸鳕鱼在葡萄牙菜中很受欢迎。

e.en: She {bad-mouthed} her former boss to anyone who'd listen.
e.zh: 她见人就说前老板的坏话。

e.en: He never {bad-mouthed} his teammates after losses.
e.zh: 输球之后他从不诋毁队友。

e.en: Stop {bad-mouthing} your colleagues behind their backs.
e.zh: 别在背后说同事的坏话了。

e.en: Constantly {bad-mouthing} the competition looks unprofessional.
e.zh: 老是贬低竞争对手显得很不专业。

e.en: He always {bad-mouths} his ex-girlfriend at parties.
e.zh: 他总是在派对上说前女友的坏话。

e.en: Anyone who {bad-mouths} the team gets benched.
e.zh: 谁要是说球队的坏话就会被换下场。

e.en: That guy is {bad-news}—stay away from him.
e.zh: 那家伙是个麻烦人物，离他远点。

e.en: Mixing alcohol with those pills is {bad-news}.
e.zh: 酒和那些药一起服用会出大事。

e.en: He made a {bad-taste} joke at the funeral.
e.zh: 他在葬礼上开了个很不得体的玩笑。

e.en: The advertisement was widely criticised as {bad-taste}.
e.zh: 那则广告被普遍批评为格调低下。

badass.t: 了不起的人；强悍的家伙

e.en: She's a total {badass} on the motorcycle.
e.zh: 她骑摩托车的样子真是又酷又猛。

e.en: That was a {badass} move in the final round.
e.zh: 决赛那一手实在是太牛了。

e.en: The squad is a bunch of real {badasses}.
e.zh: 这个小队都是些真正的硬汉。

e.en: Only {badasses} survive in this industry.
e.zh: 在这个行业里只有狠角色才能生存。

e.en: Locals harvest {badderlocks} from the rocky shore.
e.zh: 当地人在岩石海岸采集翅藻。

e.en: He added dried {badderlocks} to the soup for flavour.
e.zh: 他在汤里加了些干翅藻提味。

e.en: He's the {baddest} dude in the whole neighbourhood.
e.zh: 他是整个街区最狠的家伙。

e.en: This is the {baddest} guitar solo I've ever heard.
e.zh: 这是我听过最炸的吉他独奏。

e.en: The weather forecast looks {baddish} for the weekend.
e.zh: 周末的天气预报看起来不太妙。

e.en: She gave him a {baddish} review but not terrible.
e.zh: 她给了他一个不太好但也不算糟的评价。

e.en: The officers wore {badgeless} uniforms during the operation.
e.zh: 行动期间警官们穿着无徽章的制服。

e.en: He drove a {badgeless} sedan with tinted windows.
e.zh: 他开着一辆没有标识、贴着深色车窗的轿车。

e.en: The old man was short and {badger-legged}.
e.zh: 那老人个子矮，腿又短又弯。

e.en: A {badger-legged} dog waddled across the yard.
e.zh: 一只罗圈腿的狗摇摇晃晃地穿过院子。

e.en: They aren't rich, but they're not {badly-off} either.
e.zh: 他们不算富有，但也并不拮据。

e.en: Many pensioners are increasingly {badly-off} this winter.
e.zh: 今年冬天许多退休者的处境越来越艰难。

e.en: In old westerns, the {badman} always wore black.
e.zh: 在老式西部片里，坏蛋总是穿黑衣服。

e.en: He plays a charming {badman} in the new thriller.
e.zh: 他在这部新惊悚片里饰演一个迷人的反派。

e.en: He's a {badtempered} old man who shouts at children.
e.zh: 他是个爱冲孩子吼叫的坏脾气老头。

e.en: Don't talk to her now—she's {badtempered} before coffee.
e.zh: 现在别跟她说话，她没喝咖啡前脾气很差。

e.en: The speaker's {baffle-board} reduces unwanted vibrations.
e.zh: 扬声器的挡板可以减少不必要的振动。

e.en: Engineers added a {baffle-board} to dampen the engine noise.
e.zh: 工程师加装了一块挡板以减弱发动机噪音。

e.en: Under the microscope the spores looked oddly {bacteriform}.
e.zh: 显微镜下，这些孢子看起来奇怪地呈细菌状。

e.en: She described the {bacteriform} particles in her notes.
e.zh: 她在笔记中描述了那些形似细菌的颗粒。

e.en: The vet administered a {bacterin} to the calves.
e.zh: 兽医给小牛接种了细菌疫苗。

e.en: This {bacterin} protects livestock against several pathogens.
e.zh: 这种菌苗可保护牲畜免受多种病原体侵害。

e.en: Routine {bacterination} reduced losses on the farm.
e.zh: 常规细菌疫苗接种减少了农场的损失。

e.en: The herd underwent {bacterination} before the rainy season.
e.zh: 牛群在雨季前接受了菌苗接种。

e.en: Purple bacteria use {bacteriochlorophyll} to capture light energy.
e.zh: 紫色细菌利用细菌叶绿素来捕获光能。

e.en: Different forms of {bacteriochlorophyll} absorb different wavelengths.
e.zh: 不同形式的细菌叶绿素吸收不同波长的光。

e.en: Some bacteria secrete a {bacteriocin} to kill rivals.
e.zh: 有些细菌会分泌细菌素来杀死竞争对手。

e.en: This {bacteriocin} shows promise as a food preservative.
e.zh: 这种细菌素作为食品防腐剂前景看好。

e.en: Many lactic acid bacteria produce {bacteriocins} that inhibit pathogens.
e.zh: 许多乳酸菌会产生抑制病原体的细菌素。

e.en: Researchers screened dozens of {bacteriocins} for antimicrobial activity.
e.zh: 研究人员筛选了几十种细菌素的抗菌活性。

e.en: Inside the root nodule the rhizobia became {bacterioid} forms.
e.zh: 在根瘤内，根瘤菌转变为类菌体形态。

e.en: The slide showed clusters of tiny {bacterioid} cells.
e.zh: 载玻片上显示出一团团类菌体细胞。

e.en: The serum contained a {bacteriolysin} active against the strain.
e.zh: 血清中含有针对该菌株的溶菌素。

e.en: A specific {bacteriolysin} ruptures the bacterial cell wall.
e.zh: 特定的溶菌素能使细菌细胞壁破裂。

e.en: Antibodies can trigger {bacteriolysis} with the help of complement.
e.zh: 抗体可以借助补体引发细菌溶解。

e.en: The experiment measured the rate of {bacteriolysis} over time.
e.zh: 实验测量了细菌溶解随时间的速率。

e.en: Lysozyme has a strong {bacteriolytic} effect on many microbes.
e.zh: 溶菌酶对许多微生物有很强的溶菌作用。

e.en: They isolated a {bacteriolytic} enzyme from egg white.
e.zh: 他们从蛋清中分离出一种溶菌酶。

e.en: Certain protozoa are largely {bacteriophagous} in habit.
e.zh: 某些原生动物的食性主要以细菌为食。

e.en: The pond teemed with {bacteriophagous} organisms.
e.zh: 池塘里充满了以细菌为食的生物。

e.en: His {bacteriophobia} made him wash his hands constantly.
e.zh: 他的细菌恐惧症让他不停地洗手。

e.en: Mild {bacteriophobia} surged during the pandemic.
e.zh: 疫情期间，轻度的细菌恐惧症明显增加。

e.en: {Bacteriorhodopsin} pumps protons across the cell membrane when illuminated.
e.zh: 细菌视紫红质受光照后会在细胞膜上泵送质子。

e.en: Researchers engineered {bacteriorhodopsin} for use in optical devices.
e.zh: 研究人员改造细菌视紫红质，用于光学器件。

e.en: The hospital hired a skilled {bacterioscopist} to read slides.
e.zh: 医院聘请了一位熟练的细菌镜检者来判读载玻片。

e.en: As a {bacterioscopist}, she examined hundreds of samples weekly.
e.zh: 作为细菌镜检者，她每周检查数百份样本。

e.en: Diagnosis was confirmed by {bacterioscopy} of the sputum.
e.zh: 通过痰液的细菌镜检确诊了病情。

e.en: {Bacterioscopy} remains a basic tool in clinical labs.
e.zh: 细菌镜检仍是临床实验室的基本手段。

e.en: The orchard suffered from a serious {bacteriosis} that year.
e.zh: 那年果园遭受了严重的细菌病害。

e.en: Early treatment can limit the spread of {bacteriosis}.
e.zh: 及早治疗可以限制细菌病的传播。

e.en: The drug achieves {bacteriostasis} rather than killing the cells.
e.zh: 该药物起到的是抑菌作用，而非杀灭细胞。

e.en: Refrigeration helps maintain {bacteriostasis} in the sample.
e.zh: 冷藏有助于在样品中维持抑菌状态。

e.en: They added a mild {bacteriostat} to the cosmetic cream.
e.zh: 他们在化妆乳霜中加入了一种温和的抑菌剂。

e.en: This {bacteriostat} prevents growth without killing the bacteria.
e.zh: 这种抑菌剂能阻止生长但不杀死细菌。

e.en: Tetracyclines are mainly {bacteriostatic} at normal doses.
e.zh: 四环素类药物在常规剂量下主要起抑菌作用。

e.en: The lotion contains a {bacteriostatic} agent for safety.
e.zh: 该乳液含有抑菌成分以确保安全。

e.en: Fecal {bacteriotherapy} has helped patients with stubborn infections.
e.zh: 粪菌细菌疗法帮助了患有顽固感染的患者。

e.en: Doctors are exploring {bacteriotherapy} as an alternative to antibiotics.
e.zh: 医生正在探索细菌疗法作为抗生素的替代方案。

e.en: The serum showed clear {bacteriotropic} activity in vitro.
e.zh: 该血清在体外表现出明显的趋菌活性。

e.en: Phagocytes are guided by {bacteriotropic} signals to the infection site.
e.zh: 吞噬细胞受趋菌信号引导而前往感染部位。

bacterise.t: 使感染细菌；用细菌处理

e.en: The technician had to {bacterise} the sample for the trial.
e.zh: 技术员必须用细菌处理样品以进行试验。

e.en: They {bacterise} the milk to study fermentation.
e.zh: 他们让牛奶感染细菌以研究发酵过程。

e.en: The urine test revealed significant {bacteriuria}.
e.zh: 尿液检查显示有明显的菌尿。

e.en: Asymptomatic {bacteriuria} is common in older women.
e.zh: 无症状菌尿在老年女性中很常见。

e.en: Soil {bacterization} can boost crop yields significantly.
e.zh: 土壤菌化处理可以显著提高作物产量。

e.en: Seed {bacterization} with rhizobia improved nodulation.
e.zh: 用根瘤菌对种子进行菌化处理改善了结瘤。

bacterize.t: 使感染细菌；用细菌处理

e.en: Farmers sometimes {bacterize} seeds before planting.
e.zh: 农民有时会在播种前对种子进行菌化处理。

e.en: They {bacterize} the soil to enhance nitrogen fixation.
e.zh: 他们用细菌处理土壤以增强固氮作用。

e.en: The {bacterized} seeds showed faster germination than controls.
e.zh: 经细菌处理的种子比对照组发芽更快。

e.en: They compared yields from {bacterized} and untreated plots.
e.zh: 他们比较了菌化处理与未处理地块的产量。

bacterizes.t: 使感染细菌（第三人称单数）

e.en: This procedure {bacterizes} the substrate within minutes.
e.zh: 该程序能在几分钟内使底物感染细菌。

e.en: The lab routinely {bacterizes} samples for fermentation studies.
e.zh: 实验室常规地对样品进行菌化以研究发酵。

e.en: {Bacterizing} the soil improved nodule formation in legumes.
e.zh: 对土壤进行菌化处理改善了豆科植物的根瘤形成。

e.en: He spent the morning {bacterizing} fresh culture plates.
e.zh: 他用一上午时间对新培养板进行菌化处理。

e.en: The root nodules were full of {bacteroid} cells.
e.zh: 根瘤里充满了类菌体细胞。

e.en: Each {bacteroid} fixes nitrogen for the host plant.
e.zh: 每个类菌体都为寄主植物固定氮。

e.en: The image showed several {bacteroidal} structures inside the cell.
e.zh: 图像显示细胞内有若干类菌体结构。

e.en: Researchers studied the {bacteroidal} forms in legume nodules.
e.zh: 研究人员研究了豆科植物根瘤中的类菌体形态。

e.en: The museum displayed a row of mammalian {bacula}.
e.zh: 博物馆陈列着一排哺乳动物的阴茎骨。

e.en: Researchers compared the {bacula} of related species.
e.zh: 研究人员比较了近缘物种的阴茎骨。

e.en: The crystals had a clearly {baculiform} appearance.
e.zh: 这些晶体明显呈杆状外观。

e.en: Under magnification the bacteria looked {baculiform}.
e.zh: 放大后这些细菌看起来呈杆状。

e.en: The schoolmaster relied on harsh {baculine} discipline.
e.zh: 那位校长依赖严厉的棍棒纪律。

e.en: He decried the {baculine} methods of an earlier era.
e.zh: 他谴责早期那种棍棒式的管教方法。

e.en: Many mammals possess a {baculum}, though humans do not.
e.zh: 许多哺乳动物有阴茎骨，但人类没有。

e.en: The shape of the {baculum} can help identify species.
e.zh: 阴茎骨的形状有助于识别物种。

e.en: They blamed the illness on {bad-air} from the swamp.
e.zh: 他们把这场病归咎于沼泽散发的污浊空气。

e.en: The miners complained about the {bad-air} underground.
e.zh: 矿工抱怨井下的空气污浊。

bad-boy.t: 坏小子；离经叛道的男子

e.en: He played the {bad-boy} role in the new film.
e.zh: 他在新片中扮演坏小子的角色。

e.en: Their guitarist is the {bad-boy} of the band.
e.zh: 他们的吉他手是乐队里的坏小子。

bad-check.t: 空头支票；不能兑现的支票

e.en: He was arrested for passing a {bad-check} at the store.
e.zh: 他因在商店开具空头支票而被捕。

e.en: The landlord refused to accept another {bad-check}.
e.zh: 房东拒绝再接受一张空头支票。

e.en: The bank wrote off the loan as a {bad-debt}.
e.zh: 银行将这笔贷款作为坏账核销。

e.en: Rising {bad-debt} levels worried the company's investors.
e.zh: 不断上升的坏账水平令公司投资者担忧。

e.en: The court found that the insurer acted in {bad-faith}.
e.zh: 法院认定保险公司是出于恶意行事。

e.en: Negotiating in {bad-faith} can void the entire agreement.
e.zh: 以不诚信方式谈判可能会使整个协议无效。

e.en: She cultivated a {bad-girl} image on social media.
e.zh: 她在社交媒体上塑造了一个坏女孩形象。

e.en: The film cast her as a glamorous {bad-girl}.
e.zh: 这部电影让她饰演一个迷人的坏女孩。

e.en: The shortstop missed the grounder on a {bad-hop}.
e.zh: 游击手因为一个不规则反弹漏接了滚地球。

e.en: A nasty {bad-hop} struck him in the face.
e.zh: 一个棘手的不规则反弹球击中了他的脸。

e.en: The bank's profits were eroded by a {bad-loan} portfolio.
e.zh: 银行的利润被不良贷款组合所侵蚀。

e.en: Regulators urged lenders to clean up their {bad-loan} books.
e.zh: 监管机构敦促放贷机构清理不良贷款。

e.en: Breaking a mirror is said to bring {bad-luck}.
e.zh: 据说打破镜子会带来坏运气。

e.en: It was just {bad-luck} that the train was cancelled.
e.zh: 火车被取消只是倒霉而已。

e.en: Don't be so {bad-mannered} at the dinner table.
e.zh: 在饭桌上别这么没礼貌。

e.en: His {bad-mannered} reply embarrassed his parents.
e.zh: 他粗鲁的回答让父母感到难堪。

e.en: Please don't {bad-mouth} your colleagues behind their backs.
e.zh: 请不要在背后说同事的坏话。

e.en: He kept trying to {bad-mouth} his former employer.
e.zh: 他不停地诋毁他的前雇主。

e.en: The contract was full of {bafflegab} no one understood.
e.zh: 合同里满是没人看得懂的官话。

e.en: Cut the {bafflegab} and tell us plainly.
e.zh: 少说废话，直接告诉我们。

e.en: The engineer installed a {baffleplate} inside the tank.
e.zh: 工程师在罐内安装了一块挡板。

e.en: A loose {baffleplate} caused the strange noise.
e.zh: 挡板松动导致了奇怪的噪音。

e.en: He pulled out a {baffy} for the short approach.
e.zh: 他抽出一支短柄木杆准备短距离击球。

e.en: Old golfers still favor the trusty {baffy}.
e.zh: 老球手仍然偏爱那支可靠的短木杆。

e.en: A {bag-lady} sat shivering on the bench.
e.zh: 一个流浪老妇人在长椅上瑟瑟发抖。

e.en: He gave the {bag-lady} a warm meal.
e.zh: 他给那位流浪妇人买了一顿热饭。

e.en: Workers in sugar mills risk developing {bagassosis}.
e.zh: 糖厂工人有患蔗渣肺的风险。

e.en: Doctors diagnosed him with {bagassosis} after years of exposure.
e.zh: 医生在他多年接触后确诊为蔗渣肺。

e.en: Meet me at the {baggage-claim} after you land.
e.zh: 落地后到行李提取处见我。

e.en: Our suitcases never showed up at {baggage-claim}.
e.zh: 我们的行李箱一直没出现在提取处。

e.en: The {baggageman} loaded the trunks onto the train.
e.zh: 行李员把箱子搬上了火车。

e.en: A friendly {baggageman} helped her with the heavy case.
e.zh: 一位友善的行李员帮她搬那只沉重的箱子。

baggagemaster.t: 行李主管；行李房负责人

e.en: The {baggagemaster} kept careful records of every trunk.
e.zh: 行李主管对每只箱子都仔细登记。

e.en: Ask the {baggagemaster} where lost luggage is stored.
e.zh: 去问行李主管丢失的行李存在哪里。

e.en: He wore his {baggiest} jeans to the concert.
e.zh: 他穿了最宽松的牛仔裤去看演唱会。

e.en: That's the {baggiest} sweater I've ever seen.
e.zh: 那是我见过最松垮的毛衣。

e.en: The {bagginess} of his suit made him look thinner.
e.zh: 西装的宽松让他显得更瘦。

e.en: She noticed slight {bagginess} under her eyes.
e.zh: 她注意到眼下有些微浮肿松弛。

baghouse.t: 袋式除尘室；布袋除尘器

e.en: The factory's {baghouse} traps fine dust before release.
e.zh: 工厂的布袋除尘器在排放前捕集细尘。

e.en: Engineers redesigned the {baghouse} to improve filtration.
e.zh: 工程师重新设计了袋式除尘室以提高过滤效率。

e.en: She bought a {bagless} vacuum cleaner.
e.zh: 她买了一台无尘袋吸尘器。

e.en: The {bagless} design saves money on replacements.
e.zh: 无袋设计省下了更换尘袋的费用。

e.en: The novel describes a seedy {bagnio} in old London.
e.zh: 小说描写了旧伦敦一家肮脏的妓院。

e.en: Travelers once relaxed at a Turkish {bagnio}.
e.zh: 旅人们曾在土耳其浴室里放松休息。

e.en: Several {bagnios} lined the back alleys of the port.
e.zh: 港口的后巷里排着几家妓院。

e.en: Old prints depict crowded {bagnios} of the era.
e.zh: 老版画描绘了那个时代拥挤的浴室。

e.en: She served green mango with a side of {bagoong}.
e.zh: 她端上青芒果配一碟鱼虾酱。

e.en: {Bagoong} adds a salty kick to many Filipino dishes.
e.zh: 鱼虾酱为许多菲律宾菜增添咸鲜风味。

baguet.t: 长棍面包；长方形小宝石

e.en: He picked up a fresh {baguet} from the bakery.
e.zh: 他从面包店买了一根新鲜长棍面包。

e.en: The ring featured a tiny {baguet} diamond.
e.zh: 戒指上镶着一颗长方形小钻。

e.en: She dropped off her {bagwash} at the laundry.
e.zh: 她把袋装衣物送到洗衣店。

e.en: The shop offers cheap {bagwash} service by weight.
e.zh: 这家店提供按重量计价的袋装洗衣服务。

bagwig.t: 扎袋假发（旧时男士发型）

e.en: The portrait shows a gentleman in a powdered {bagwig}.
e.zh: 画像中绅士戴着扑了粉的扎袋假发。

e.en: He donned a {bagwig} for the costume ball.
e.zh: 他为化装舞会戴上了一顶扎袋假发。

bagwoman.t: 为黑帮收钱的女子；流浪女

e.en: The crooked official used a {bagwoman} to deliver bribes.
e.zh: 那个贪官利用一名女子传送贿款。

e.en: A weary {bagwoman} pushed her cart down the street.
e.zh: 一位疲惫的流浪妇人推着购物车走过街道。

e.en: A {bagworm} had stripped the cedar of its leaves.
e.zh: 一只蓑蛾幼虫把雪松的叶子啃光了。

e.en: Gardeners pick off each {bagworm} by hand.
e.zh: 园丁们一只只用手把袋蛾摘掉。

e.en: {Bagworms} can defoliate evergreens within weeks.
e.zh: 蓑蛾幼虫几周内就能把常绿树啃光叶子。

e.en: He sprayed the trees to control the {bagworms}.
e.zh: 他给树喷药以控制袋蛾虫害。

bahadur.t: 巴哈杜尔（南亚对勇士的尊称）

e.en: The old soldier was honored with the title {bahadur}.
e.zh: 那位老兵被授予巴哈杜尔的尊号。

e.en: Locals still call the hero a true {bahadur}.
e.zh: 当地人至今称这位英雄为真正的勇士。

e.en: The government announced a {bail-out} for the failing bank.
e.zh: 政府宣布对濒临倒闭的银行进行紧急救助。

e.en: Critics opposed the massive {bail-out} of the airlines.
e.zh: 批评者反对对航空公司的巨额财政援助。

e.en: The judge ruled that the offense was {bailable}.
e.zh: 法官裁定该罪行可以保释。

e.en: Not every charge is a {bailable} one.
e.zh: 并非每项指控都准予保释。

e.en: The {bailers} worked frantically to keep the boat afloat.
e.zh: 舀水的人疯狂地工作以使船不沉。

e.en: The court keeps a list of approved {bailers}.
e.zh: 法院保留一份获批保释人的名单。

e.en: He was appointed to the {bailiffship} of the district.
e.zh: 他被任命担任该地区的法警职务。

e.en: The {bailiffship} carried considerable authority in medieval towns.
e.zh: 在中世纪城镇中，执达员之职拥有相当大的权力。

bailment.t: 寄托；委托保管（法律术语）

e.en: The contract created a {bailment} of the equipment.
e.zh: 该合同对设备形成了一项寄托关系。

e.en: Under {bailment}, the holder must return the goods.
e.zh: 根据寄托关系，保管人必须归还货物。

e.en: The {bailor} retained ownership of the goods.
e.zh: 寄托人保留对货物的所有权。

e.en: A {bailor} may sue for damage to the property.
e.zh: 寄托人可就财产损坏提起诉讼。

e.en: The {bailors} demanded the return of their property.
e.zh: 寄托人要求归还他们的财产。

e.en: Several {bailors} signed identical contracts.
e.zh: 几位寄托人签署了相同的合同。

e.en: His uncle served as his {bailsman} in court.
e.zh: 他叔叔在法庭上担任他的保释人。

e.en: A reliable {bailsman} is hard to find.
e.zh: 可靠的担保人难寻。

e.en: Two {bailsmen} signed the bond together.
e.zh: 两位保释人共同签署了保证书。

e.en: The court verified the credentials of the {bailsmen}.
e.zh: 法院核查了保释人的资格。

e.en: Melt the chocolate gently in a {bain-marie}.
e.zh: 用水浴锅慢慢融化巧克力。

e.en: The custard sets perfectly when cooked in a {bain-marie}.
e.zh: 卡仕达酱在隔水加热锅中烹煮可凝固得恰到好处。

e.en: The steel was heat-treated to form {bainite}.
e.zh: 该钢材经热处理形成贝氏体。

e.en: {Bainite} offers a good balance of strength and toughness.
e.zh: 贝氏体在强度与韧性之间取得良好平衡。

e.en: Tourists are often expected to give {baksheesh} to local guides.
e.zh: 游客通常要给当地向导一些赏钱。

e.en: He slipped the doorman some {baksheesh} to let us in.
e.zh: 他塞给门卫一点小费让我们进去。

balance-of-payments.t: 国际收支；国际收支差额

e.en: The country's {balance-of-payments} deficit widened last quarter.
e.zh: 该国上季度的国际收支逆差扩大了。

e.en: Economists are watching the {balance-of-payments} figures closely.
e.zh: 经济学家正密切关注国际收支数据。

e.en: The election shifted the {balance-of-power} in parliament.
e.zh: 这次选举改变了议会中的势力均衡。

e.en: A small country can disrupt the regional {balance-of-power}.
e.zh: 一个小国可能打破地区的力量平衡。

e.en: The company's {balance-sheet} looks strong this year.
e.zh: 公司今年的资产负债表表现强劲。

e.en: Investors carefully review the {balance-sheet} before buying shares.
e.zh: 投资者购股前会仔细审阅资产负债表。

e.en: She used a {balance-transfer} to consolidate her credit-card debt.
e.zh: 她用余额代偿来合并信用卡债务。

e.en: The card offers zero interest on {balance-transfers} for a year.
e.zh: 这张卡余额转账一年内零利息。

e.en: The accountant insisted the books were {balanceable}.
e.zh: 会计坚称账目是可以平衡的。

e.en: These competing demands are barely {balanceable}.
e.zh: 这些相互冲突的需求几乎难以兼顾。

balanced-budget.t: 平衡预算；收支平衡的预算

e.en: The governor promised a {balanced-budget} next year.
e.zh: 州长承诺明年实现预算平衡。

e.en: Voters often demand a {balanced-budget} from politicians.
e.zh: 选民常常要求政客制定平衡预算。

e.en: Old golf-ball covers were often made from {balata}.
e.zh: 旧式高尔夫球的外壳常用巴拉塔胶制成。

e.en: {Balata} is harvested from the sap of a tropical tree.
e.zh: 巴拉塔胶是从一种热带树的树液中提取的。

e.en: A wrought-iron {balconet} decorated each upstairs window.
e.zh: 每扇楼上的窗户都饰有铁艺小阳台。

e.en: She bought a lacy {balconet} to wear under the dress.
e.zh: 她买了一件蕾丝半罩式胸罩搭配那条裙子。

e.en: That was a {bald-faced} lie and everyone knew it.
e.zh: 那是个赤裸裸的谎言，谁都看得出来。

e.en: He showed {bald-faced} contempt for the rules.
e.zh: 他对规则表现出公然的蔑视。

e.en: A {bald-headed} man waved at us from the porch.
e.zh: 一个秃头男人在门廊向我们挥手。

e.en: He rushed {bald-headed} into the argument without thinking.
e.zh: 他不假思索地一头扎进了争论。

e.en: A gilded {baldachin} stood over the cathedral altar.
e.zh: 镀金华盖矗立在大教堂祭坛上方。

e.en: Renaissance paintings often depict a {baldachin} above thrones.
e.zh: 文艺复兴时期的画作常描绘王座上方的华盖。

e.en: Driftwood collected along the {backshore} after the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨后浮木堆积在后滨地带。

e.en: Dunes form on the {backshore} above the high-tide line.
e.zh: 沙丘在高潮线以上的后滨形成。

e.en: The mill used a {backshot} water wheel for power.
e.zh: 这座磨坊使用背射式水轮提供动力。

e.en: A {backshot} wheel is more efficient than an undershot one.
e.zh: 背射式水轮比下射式更有效率。

e.en: The surveyor took a {backsight} to the previous station.
e.zh: 测量员对前一站进行了后视观测。

e.en: Adjust the rifle's {backsight} before firing.
e.zh: 开枪前先调整步枪的后照门。

e.en: The politicians {backslap} each other at every event.
e.zh: 政客们在每场活动上都互相拍背套近乎。

e.en: He gave his old friend a hearty {backslap}.
e.zh: 他用力拍了拍老朋友的背。

backslapped.t: 拍背祝贺过；亲热地拍打过

e.en: The coach {backslapped} every player after the win.
e.zh: 教练在获胜后拍了每位球员的背。

e.en: He was {backslapped} by colleagues at the celebration.
e.zh: 庆祝会上同事们都拍着他的背道贺。

backslapper.t: 爱拍背套近乎的人；过分亲热的人

e.en: He's a real {backslapper} at networking events.
e.zh: 他在社交活动上就是个超级爱拍背套近乎的人。

e.en: Voters distrust the smiling {backslapper} type of politician.
e.zh: 选民们不信任那种笑脸相迎、拍肩示好的政客。

e.en: There was a lot of {backslapping} after the deal closed.
e.zh: 交易达成后大家互相拍背庆贺了一番。

e.en: I dislike the {backslapping} atmosphere of these conventions.
e.zh: 我不喜欢这些大会上那种过分亲热的氛围。

e.en: He {backslid} into his old smoking habit.
e.zh: 他又回到了从前抽烟的旧习。

e.en: After months of progress, she {backslid} last week.
e.zh: 经过几个月的进步，她上周又倒退了。

e.en: The program tries to support {backsliders} without judgment.
e.zh: 这个项目努力不带评判地帮助那些故态复萌的人。

e.en: Reformed addicts often become the harshest critics of {backsliders}.
e.zh: 戒毒成功者往往是对故态复萌者最严厉的批评者。

e.en: The lever has a strong {backspring} mechanism.
e.zh: 这根杠杆装有强力的回弹机构。

e.en: The gymnast performed a graceful {backspring}.
e.zh: 体操运动员做了一个优雅的后弹动作。

e.en: Don't trust him; he'll {backstab} you for a promotion.
e.zh: 别信他；为了升职他会在背后捅你一刀。

e.en: Office politics is full of {backstab} maneuvers.
e.zh: 办公室政治充满了背后捅刀的伎俩。

backstabber.t: 背后捅刀的人；暗箭伤人者

e.en: Everyone knew she was a {backstabber} after the meeting.
e.zh: 那次会议后大家都知道她是个背后捅刀的人。

e.en: He turned out to be a {backstabber} I never suspected.
e.zh: 他竟是个我从未怀疑过的背后捅刀者。

e.en: This office is full of {backstabbers} chasing promotions.
e.zh: 这个办公室满是为了升职而背后捅刀的人。

e.en: Beware of smiling {backstabbers} in any workplace.
e.zh: 在任何职场都要提防笑里藏刀的人。

e.en: The grinding wheel sits on a sturdy {backstand}.
e.zh: 砂轮安装在坚固的后支架上。

e.en: He attached the belt sander to its {backstand}.
e.zh: 他把带式砂磨机装到了后支架上。

e.en: The sailor adjusted the {backstay} before tacking.
e.zh: 水手在转向前调整了后支索。

e.en: A broken {backstay} can bring down the mast.
e.zh: 后支索断裂可能会让桅杆倒下。

e.en: Engineers used {backstepping} to design the controller.
e.zh: 工程师采用反步法来设计这个控制器。

e.en: He kept {backstepping} away from the angry dog.
e.zh: 他不停地后退着躲开那条凶狗。

e.en: Use a {backstitch} to reinforce the seam.
e.zh: 用回针缝可以加固接缝。

e.en: She finished the hem with a neat {backstitch}.
e.zh: 她用整齐的回针把裙边收好。

e.en: The tailor {backstitched} the cuffs for durability.
e.zh: 裁缝用回针缝袖口以增加耐用度。

e.en: All seams were carefully {backstitched} by hand.
e.zh: 所有的接缝都被仔细地手工回针缝制。

e.en: Several {backstitches} secure the end of the seam.
e.zh: 几道回针固定住了接缝的末端。

e.en: She always {backstitches} at the start and finish.
e.zh: 她总是在开头和结尾打几道回针。

e.en: {Backstitching} makes the hem much stronger.
e.zh: 回针缝法能让裙边更加牢固。

e.en: She spent the afternoon {backstitching} the quilt.
e.zh: 她整个下午都在用回针缝那床被子。

e.en: Mayan weavers still use the traditional {backstrap} loom.
e.zh: 玛雅织工至今仍使用传统的腰机。

e.en: The bag has an adjustable {backstrap} for comfort.
e.zh: 这个包配有可调节的背带以提升舒适度。

e.en: The hunter prized the deer's tender {backstraps}.
e.zh: 猎人很珍视鹿那块鲜嫩的里脊肉。

e.en: The harness's {backstraps} kept slipping off her shoulders.
e.zh: 背带具的肩带不断从她肩上滑落。

e.en: The fighter jet has dramatically {backswept} wings.
e.zh: 这架战斗机有着明显后掠的机翼。

e.en: She wore her hair in a sleek {backswept} style.
e.zh: 她把头发梳成光滑的后掠造型。

e.en: {Backswimmers} hang upside down beneath the pond's surface.
e.zh: 仰泳蝽倒悬在池塘水面之下。

e.en: Children watched the {backswimmers} dart through the shallow water.
e.zh: 孩子们看着仰泳蝽在浅水里穿梭。

e.en: The soldier carried a short {backsword} at his hip.
e.zh: 那士兵腰间挂着一把短单刃剑。

e.en: Museums display the {backsword} as an early military weapon.
e.zh: 博物馆将单刃剑作为早期军用武器展出。

e.en: The ultrasonic signal reflected off the {backwall}.
e.zh: 超声波信号从后壁反射回来。

e.en: Posters covered the gym's {backwall}.
e.zh: 海报贴满了体育馆的后墙。

e.en: Apply a {backward-bias} voltage to the diode.
e.zh: 对二极管施加反向偏置电压。

e.en: Under {backward-bias}, current flow is minimal.
e.zh: 在反向偏置下，电流极小。

e.en: The new console is {backward-compatible} with old games.
e.zh: 这款新主机向后兼容旧游戏。

e.en: Make sure the API stays {backward-compatible} after the update.
e.zh: 确保更新后 API 仍然向后兼容。

e.en: His policies are too {backward-looking} for today's voters.
e.zh: 他的政策对当今选民来说过于守旧。

e.en: The report is mostly {backward-looking}, summarizing last year's results.
e.zh: 报告主要是回顾性的，总结了去年的成绩。

e.en: Oil futures slipped into {backwardation} last month.
e.zh: 上个月原油期货进入了现货溢价状态。

e.en: {Backwardation} often signals tight supply in the market.
e.zh: 现货溢价通常意味着市场供应紧张。

e.en: The leading boat tried to {backwind} its rival.
e.zh: 领先的船试图扰乱对手的风。

e.en: A jib can {backwind} the mainsail if trimmed wrong.
e.zh: 前帆若调整不当会扰乱主帆受风。

e.en: The old {backwoodsman} knew every trail in the forest.
e.zh: 那位老林区居民熟悉森林里的每一条小径。

e.en: He lived as a {backwoodsman}, far from any town.
e.zh: 他像个山野人一样住在远离城镇的地方。

e.en: The {backwoodsmen} hunted and trapped through the winter.
e.zh: 那些林区居民整个冬天都在打猎和设陷阱。

e.en: Stories about hardy {backwoodsmen} filled the pioneer histories.
e.zh: 拓荒史里满是关于坚韧山野人的故事。

e.en: The town has a charming {backwoodsy} feel.
e.zh: 这个小镇有种迷人的乡野气息。

e.en: His {backwoodsy} accent gave away his hometown.
e.zh: 他那乡野口音暴露了家乡所在。

e.en: The chair has a soft {backwrap} cushion.
e.zh: 这把椅子有一个柔软的后包裹靠垫。

e.en: She added a fleece {backwrap} for extra warmth.
e.zh: 她加了一层羊毛后包裹保暖。

e.en: Early modern science was shaped by {baconianism}.
e.zh: 早期现代科学深受培根主义的影响。

e.en: His essay defends {baconianism} as an empirical method.
e.zh: 他的论文将培根主义辩护为一种经验方法。

e.en: The soup had a rich, {bacony} flavor.
e.zh: 这道汤有着浓郁的培根味。

e.en: She loves anything {bacony} for breakfast.
e.zh: 她早餐爱吃一切带培根味的东西。

e.en: The patient developed {bacteraemia} after surgery.
e.zh: 病人术后出现了菌血症。

e.en: Blood cultures confirmed {bacteraemia} within hours.
e.zh: 血培养在数小时内证实了菌血症。

e.en: The {bacteremic} patient required immediate antibiotics.
e.zh: 这位菌血症患者需要立即使用抗生素。

e.en: Doctors monitor {bacteremic} infants very closely.
e.zh: 医生会密切监测患菌血症的婴儿。

e.en: The lab maintains a {bacteria-free} environment.
e.zh: 实验室保持无菌环境。

e.en: This filter promises {bacteria-free} drinking water.
e.zh: 这种滤水器承诺提供无菌饮用水。

e.en: Farmers spray a copper-based {bactericide} on the orchard.
e.zh: 农民在果园喷洒铜基杀菌剂。

e.en: The hospital uses a strong {bactericide} on surfaces.
e.zh: 医院用强效杀菌剂处理各种表面。

e.en: Researchers isolated a {bactericidin} from the soil sample.
e.zh: 研究人员从土壤样本中分离出一种杀菌素。

e.en: This {bactericidin} kills several drug-resistant strains.
e.zh: 这种杀菌素能杀死多种耐药菌株。

bait-and-switch.t: 先以低价或优惠引诱顾客，再推销高价货的伎俩

e.en: The store pulled a classic {bait-and-switch} on unwary shoppers.
e.zh: 这家店对粗心的顾客玩了典型的诱售把戏。

e.en: Regulators fined the dealer for {bait-and-switch} advertising.
e.zh: 监管机构因诱售广告对该经销商处以罚款。

baitandswitch.t: 诱售伎俩；以低价引诱再推销高价货

e.en: The dealership was sued for its {baitandswitch} practices.
e.zh: 这家车行因诱售行为被起诉。

e.en: He warned us not to fall for any {baitandswitch} schemes online.
e.zh: 他提醒我们别上网上诱售骗局的当。

e.en: She won first prize at the village {bake-off} with her apple pie.
e.zh: 她凭一只苹果派在村里的烘焙比赛中夺得头奖。

e.en: The charity organized a {bake-off} to raise funds for the shelter.
e.zh: 慈善机构举办了一场烘焙比赛为收容所筹款。

bake-oven.t: 烤面包的烤炉；砖砌烘炉

e.en: Grandma's old stone {bake-oven} stood in the corner of the kitchen.
e.zh: 奶奶那座旧石砌烘炉立在厨房的角落里。

e.en: They fired up the {bake-oven} early to prepare for the morning loaves.
e.zh: 他们一早就把烘炉点起来，准备烤早晨的面包。

e.en: The school held a {bake-sale} to raise money for new books.
e.zh: 学校举办糕点义卖，为购买新书筹集资金。

e.en: Parents brought cookies and brownies to the church {bake-sale}.
e.zh: 家长们带来曲奇和巧克力布朗尼参加教堂的烘焙义卖。

bakeapple.t: 云莓；北方寒地一种黄色野果

e.en: We picked {bakeapples} on the Newfoundland bog all afternoon.
e.zh: 我们整个下午都在纽芬兰沼泽地里采云莓。

e.en: She makes a tart jam from wild {bakeapples} every August.
e.zh: 她每年八月都用野生云莓做酸甜果酱。

e.en: She rolled out the pastry on a flour-dusted {bakeboard}.
e.zh: 她在撒了面粉的揉面板上把酥皮擀开。

e.en: The old wooden {bakeboard} was scarred from decades of kneading.
e.zh: 那块旧木揉面板因几十年的揉面而布满划痕。

bakehead.t: 旧时俚语：烧锅炉的工人；火夫

e.en: The {bakeheads} shoveled coal into the locomotive's firebox all night.
e.zh: 火夫们整夜把煤铲进火车头的炉膛。

e.en: He worked as a {bakehead} on the old steamships out of Liverpool.
e.zh: 他在利物浦出港的老式蒸汽船上当烧火工。

e.en: The smell of fresh bread drifted out of the village {bakehouse}.
e.zh: 新鲜面包的香味从村里的面包房里飘出来。

e.en: He apprenticed for three years at a small {bakehouse} in Vienna.
e.zh: 他在维也纳一家小面包房学了三年徒。

bakemeat.t: 古英语：肉馅饼；烘烤的肉食

e.en: The funeral feast was laid out with cold {bakemeats} and ale.
e.zh: 葬礼宴席上摆着凉肉馅饼和麦酒。

e.en: Shakespeare's Hamlet famously mentions the funeral {bakemeats}.
e.zh: 莎士比亚《哈姆雷特》中有名地提到了葬礼上的肉馅饼。

baken.t: 古旧用法：bake 的过去分词，已烘烤的

e.en: The loaves had {baken} slowly in the brick oven all morning.
e.zh: 面包在砖炉里慢慢烤了整整一上午。

e.en: The pies were {baken} to a perfect golden brown.
e.zh: 馅饼被烤成完美的金黄色。

e.en: She entered the annual {bakeoff} with her grandmother's apple pie.
e.zh: 她带着祖母传下来的苹果派参加了年度烘焙赛。

e.en: The {bakeoff} drew amateur bakers from every county.
e.zh: 这场烘焙赛吸引了各郡的业余烘焙爱好者。

baker-kneed.t: 旧时用语：膝外翻的；X 型腿的

e.en: The boy walked with a {baker-kneed} gait from childhood rickets.
e.zh: 男孩因幼年佝偻病走起路来呈 X 型腿。

e.en: Old medical texts described patients as {baker-kneed} when knock-kneed.
e.zh: 旧时的医学典籍把膝外翻的病人称作 baker-kneed。

baker-legged.t: 旧时用语：X 型腿的；两膝并拢的

e.en: He was teased for being {baker-legged} as a young boy.
e.zh: 他小时候因 X 型腿而被人取笑。

e.en: The term {baker-legged} simply means knock-kneed in old usage.
e.zh: baker-legged 这个旧词其实就是指 X 型腿。

bakeware.t: 烘焙器皿；烤盘烤模等用具

e.en: She bought a new set of nonstick {bakeware} for the holidays.
e.zh: 她为节日添了一套新的不粘烘焙器皿。

e.en: Glass {bakeware} won't react with acidic ingredients like tomatoes.
e.zh: 玻璃烘焙器皿不会和番茄等酸性食材发生反应。

e.en: Add a teaspoon of {baking-powder} to the flour before mixing.
e.zh: 搅拌前先在面粉里加一茶匙泡打粉。

e.en: The cake won't rise without enough {baking-powder}.
e.zh: 泡打粉不够蛋糕就发不起来。

e.en: Mix {baking-soda} with vinegar to unclog the kitchen drain.
e.zh: 用小苏打和醋混合疏通厨房下水道。

e.en: A pinch of {baking-soda} keeps the cookies soft and chewy.
e.zh: 一小撮小苏打能让饼干保持柔软有嚼劲。

bakkie.t: 南非英语：小型货卡；皮卡车

e.en: He loaded the firewood into the back of his {bakkie}.
e.zh: 他把木柴装到自己皮卡车的后斗里。

e.en: In South Africa nearly everyone calls a pickup truck a {bakkie}.
e.zh: 在南非几乎人人都把皮卡叫作 bakkie。

e.en: He criticized the {banalization} of serious art.
e.zh: 他批评了严肃艺术的平庸化。

e.en: Social media accelerates the {banalization} of tragedy.
e.zh: 社交媒体加速了悲剧的平庸化。

e.en: Repeated headlines tend to {banalize} violence.
e.zh: 反复的头条新闻往往会使暴力变得平淡无奇。

e.en: Don't {banalize} her achievement with cliches.
e.zh: 不要用陈词滥调贬低她的成就。

banana-skin.t: 香蕉皮；意外失误的诱因

e.en: He slipped on a {banana-skin} and fell.
e.zh: 他踩到香蕉皮滑倒了。

e.en: The minor poll was a {banana-skin} for the party.
e.zh: 这次小型投票成了该党的意外难关。

banausic.t: 庸俗实用的；只重实利的

e.en: He dismissed the job as {banausic} drudgery.
e.zh: 他认为那份工作是庸俗的苦差。

e.en: Her tastes were anything but {banausic}.
e.zh: 她的品味绝非平庸实用。

e.en: The case was reheard en {banc}.
e.zh: 该案由全体法官重新审理。

e.en: The court sat in {banc} to decide.
e.zh: 法院全席审理裁决此案。

e.en: She put a {band-aid} on the cut.
e.zh: 她在伤口上贴了一片创可贴。

e.en: That's just a {band-aid} solution to the problem.
e.zh: 那不过是解决问题的权宜之计。

band-limited.t: 频带受限的；有限带宽的

e.en: The signal is {band-limited} to four kilohertz.
e.zh: 该信号被限制在四千赫兹的频带内。

e.en: Engineers prefer {band-limited} waveforms for transmission.
e.zh: 工程师传输时偏好频带受限的波形。

e.en: Use a {band-pass} filter to isolate the tone.
e.zh: 用带通滤波器来分离这个音调。

e.en: The circuit acts as a {band-pass} stage.
e.zh: 该电路充当带通级。

e.en: He stuck a {bandaid} over the blister.
e.zh: 他在水泡上贴了一个创可贴。

e.en: The new policy is just a {bandaid}.
e.zh: 新政策只是个临时补救办法。

e.en: She wore colorful {bandeaux} in her hair.
e.zh: 她头发上戴着彩色束发带。

e.en: The shop sold silk {bandeaux} for dancers.
e.zh: 那家店出售供舞者用的丝质束发带。

bandelet.t: 小线脚；柱子上的小环带

e.en: A thin {bandelet} circled the column.
e.zh: 一道细小的环带环绕着柱子。

e.en: The architect added a {bandelet} above the cornice.
e.zh: 建筑师在檐口上方加了一道小环带。

e.en: He wore a {bandelier} of cartridges.
e.zh: 他斜挎着一条子弹带。

e.en: The soldier's {bandelier} gleamed in the sun.
e.zh: 士兵的子弹带在阳光下闪闪发亮。

banderilla.t: 斗牛短矛；带刺彩饰短矛

e.en: He thrust the {banderilla} into the bull.
e.zh: 他把短矛刺入公牛身上。

e.en: Each {banderilla} was decorated with bright paper.
e.zh: 每根短矛都装饰着鲜艳的彩纸。

e.en: The {banderillero} darted past the bull.
e.zh: 插矛斗牛士从公牛身旁迅速闪过。

e.en: Each {banderillero} placed his darts skillfully.
e.zh: 每位插矛斗牛士都熟练地刺下短矛。

e.en: A {banderol} fluttered above the tent.
e.zh: 一面小三角旗在帐篷上方飘扬。

e.en: The painting bore a Latin {banderol}.
e.zh: 画上有一条拉丁文铭文饰带。

e.en: A silk {banderole} hung from the lance.
e.zh: 一面丝质小旗挂在长矛上。

e.en: The angel held a {banderole} with text.
e.zh: 天使手持一条带文字的饰带。

bandersnatch.t: 凶猛怪兽（卡罗尔虚构生物）

e.en: Beware the frumious {bandersnatch}!
e.zh: 当心那只暴怒的凶猛怪兽！

e.en: The poem mentions a fearsome {bandersnatch}.
e.zh: 那首诗提到了一只可怕的怪兽。

e.en: A {bandicoot} scurried across the path.
e.zh: 一只袋狸窜过小路。

e.en: The {bandicoot} digs for insects at night.
e.zh: 袋狸在夜间挖掘昆虫为食。

bandido.t: 匪徒；强盗（西班牙语借词）

e.en: The {bandido} robbed the stagecoach at dawn.
e.zh: 那名匪徒在黎明时分抢劫了驿车。

e.en: Old westerns often feature a masked {bandido}.
e.zh: 老西部片中常出现戴面具的匪徒。

e.en: A gang of {bandidos} rode into town.
e.zh: 一伙匪徒骑马闯入小镇。

e.en: The {bandidos} hid in the mountains.
e.zh: 那些匪徒躲藏在山中。

bandier.t: 更弯曲的（腿）；更罗圈腿的

e.en: His legs grew {bandier} with age.
e.zh: 他的腿随着年龄增长更加弯曲。

e.en: The older horse looked {bandier} than before.
e.zh: 那匹老马看起来比以前更罗圈腿了。

e.en: He had the {bandiest} legs in town.
e.zh: 他是镇上腿最罗圈的人。

e.en: That cowboy is the {bandiest} I've seen.
e.zh: 那个牛仔是我见过腿最弯的。

banditti.t: 盗匪团伙；强盗们（古旧用法）

e.en: A band of {banditti} ambushed the travelers.
e.zh: 一伙强盗伏击了那些旅客。

e.en: The hills were infested with {banditti}.
e.zh: 那些山中盗匪横行。

e.en: A simple {bandlet} ran around the pillar.
e.zh: 一道简单的小环带绕着柱子。

e.en: The molding ended in a delicate {bandlet}.
e.zh: 线脚以一道精致的小环带结尾。

e.en: A fierce {bandog} guarded the yard.
e.zh: 一只凶猛的看门犬守着院子。

e.en: The {bandog} barked at every stranger.
e.zh: 那只看门犬对每个陌生人都狂吠。

ball-flower.t: 球花饰；哥特式建筑球形雕饰

e.en: The cathedral's arches are decorated with carved {ball-flower} ornaments.
e.zh: 大教堂的拱门上装饰着雕刻的球花饰。

e.en: Restorers carefully cleaned each medieval {ball-flower} on the facade.
e.zh: 修复人员仔细清洁了立面上每一个中世纪球花饰。

e.en: We took the kids to a {ball-game} on Saturday.
e.zh: 周六我们带孩子去看了场球赛。

e.en: Once the new manager arrived, it was a whole new {ball-game}.
e.zh: 新经理一来,情况就完全不同了。

e.en: The hammer has a smooth {ball-head} for shaping metal.
e.zh: 这把锤子有一个光滑的球形头部,用于敲打金属成形。

e.en: He tightened the screw using a {ball-head} hex key.
e.zh: 他用球头六角扳手把螺丝拧紧了。

e.en: Can you give me a {ball-park} figure for the cost?
e.zh: 你能给我一个大致的费用估算吗?

e.en: The fans cheered as they entered the {ball-park}.
e.zh: 球迷们走进棒球场时欢呼起来。

e.en: Please sign the form with a blue {ball-pen}.
e.zh: 请用蓝色圆珠笔签署表格。

e.en: My {ball-pen} ran out of ink during the exam.
e.zh: 考试时我的圆珠笔没墨了。

e.en: She prefers writing with a {ball-point} pen.
e.zh: 她更喜欢用圆珠笔写字。

e.en: The {ball-point} skipped on the glossy paper.
e.zh: 圆珠笔在光面纸上写不出字。

e.en: The lamp has a {ball-shaped} glass shade.
e.zh: 这盏灯有一个球形玻璃灯罩。

e.en: Children rolled the {ball-shaped} cookies in sugar.
e.zh: 孩子们把球形饼干在糖里滚了滚。

e.en: He tends to {ball-up} his socks before throwing them in the drawer.
e.zh: 他习惯把袜子团成球再扔进抽屉。

e.en: Don't let nerves {ball-up} your performance tomorrow.
e.zh: 别让紧张情绪搞砸了你明天的表现。

ballad-monger.t: 民谣贩子；二流民谣作者

e.en: The Elizabethan streets were full of {ballad-mongers} hawking printed verses.
e.zh: 伊丽莎白时代的街上满是叫卖印刷歌谣的民谣贩子。

e.en: Critics dismissed him as a mere {ballad-monger} rather than a true poet.
e.zh: 评论家把他贬为不过是个民谣贩子,而非真正的诗人。

e.en: Chopin's fourth {ballade} is technically demanding.
e.zh: 肖邦的第四叙事曲在技术上极具挑战性。

e.en: The medieval poet composed a {ballade} about lost love.
e.zh: 那位中世纪诗人创作了一首关于逝去爱情的叙事诗。

e.en: The song has a clearly {balladic} structure with repeated refrains.
e.zh: 这首歌具有明显的民谣式结构,带有反复出现的副歌。

e.en: Her novel adopts a {balladic} tone full of folk imagery.
e.zh: 她的小说采用了一种充满民间意象的民谣式语调。

e.en: He earned fame as a {balladist} of working-class life.
e.zh: 他作为一位描写工人阶级生活的民谣作者而闻名。

e.en: The festival honors a forgotten Scottish {balladist}.
e.zh: 这个节日纪念一位被遗忘的苏格兰民谣作者。

balladmonger.t: 民谣贩子；蹩脚歌谣作者

e.en: Shakespeare uses {balladmonger} as a term of mild contempt.
e.zh: 莎士比亚用"民谣贩子"一词带有轻微的轻蔑意味。

e.en: The square once swarmed with {balladmongers} selling broadsides.
e.zh: 这个广场曾挤满了兜售单页歌谣的民谣贩子。

e.en: She studies the oral tradition of Scottish {balladry}.
e.zh: 她研究苏格兰民谣的口头传统。

e.en: The book is a treasure of nineteenth-century American {balladry}.
e.zh: 这本书是十九世纪美国民谣的宝库。

ballas.t: 球状金刚石；工业用粒金刚石

e.en: The drill bit is tipped with industrial {ballas} for hardness.
e.zh: 这种钻头镶有工业用球状金刚石以增加硬度。

e.en: Miners separated the {ballas} from ordinary diamond rough.
e.zh: 矿工把球状金刚石从普通毛坯钻石中分拣出来。

e.en: Discharging untreated {ballast-water} can spread invasive species.
e.zh: 排放未经处理的压舱水会传播入侵物种。

e.en: The ship pumped out its {ballast-water} before loading cargo.
e.zh: 船舶在装货前排出了压舱水。

e.en: A worn {ballbearing} was making the wheel squeak.
e.zh: 一个磨损的滚珠轴承让车轮发出吱吱声。

e.en: The skateboard rolls smoothly thanks to its precision {ballbearings}.
e.zh: 这块滑板得益于精密的滚珠轴承,滚动十分顺畅。

e.en: The {ballboy} sprinted to retrieve the tennis ball.
e.zh: 那个球童飞奔去捡回网球。

e.en: He worked as a {ballboy} at Wimbledon as a teenager.
e.zh: 他十几岁时在温布尔顿当过球童。

e.en: The toilet keeps running because the {ballcock} is broken.
e.zh: 马桶一直在漏水,因为浮球阀坏了。

e.en: A plumber adjusted the {ballcock} to stop the overflow.
e.zh: 管道工调整了浮球阀,止住了溢水。

balled-and-burlapped.t: 带土球麻布包扎的（苗木）

e.en: The nursery sells mature trees {balled-and-burlapped} for transplanting.
e.zh: 这家苗圃出售带土球麻布包扎的成树以供移植。

e.en: Each shrub arrived {balled-and-burlapped} and ready to plant.
e.zh: 每棵灌木都带着土球用麻布包好,可以直接栽种。

e.en: The neighborhood {ballers} played pickup games every weekend.
e.zh: 街区里的球员们每个周末都打野球。

e.en: Those rappers act like real {ballers} in the music video.
e.zh: 那些说唱歌手在音乐录影带里摆出一副阔少派头。

e.en: She trained for years to become a professional {ballet-dancer}.
e.zh: 她训练了多年才成为一名专业芭蕾舞演员。

e.en: The {ballet-dancer} stretched carefully before rehearsal.
e.zh: 那位芭蕾舞演员在排练前仔细做了拉伸。

e.en: The goalkeeper leapt {balletically} to tip the ball over the bar.
e.zh: 门将如芭蕾舞般跃起,把球托过了横梁。

e.en: She moved {balletically} across the polished floor.
e.zh: 她如芭蕾舞般在光亮的地板上移动。

balletomane.t: 芭蕾迷；狂热的芭蕾爱好者

e.en: As a lifelong {balletomane}, she travels for every premiere.
e.zh: 作为终身的芭蕾迷,她会为每场首演而奔波。

e.en: The bookshop is a favorite haunt of London {balletomanes}.
e.zh: 这家书店是伦敦芭蕾迷们最爱光顾的地方。

balletomanes.t: 芭蕾迷们；芭蕾狂热爱好者

e.en: Russian {balletomanes} packed the theater for every performance.
e.zh: 俄罗斯的芭蕾迷们把每场演出的剧院都挤得水泄不通。

e.en: A small group of {balletomanes} waited at the stage door.
e.zh: 一小群芭蕾迷在舞台门口等候。

balletomania.t: 芭蕾狂热；对芭蕾的痴迷

e.en: Nineteenth-century Paris experienced a wave of {balletomania}.
e.zh: 十九世纪的巴黎经历了一阵芭蕾狂热。

e.en: Her {balletomania} began with a childhood trip to the Bolshoi.
e.zh: 她的芭蕾狂热始于童年时去大剧院的一次旅行。

ballflower.t: 球花饰；哥特式球形雕饰

e.en: The arch is enriched with rows of carved {ballflower}.
e.zh: 拱门上装饰着一排排雕刻的球花饰。

e.en: {Ballflower} ornament is typical of early-fourteenth-century English Gothic.
e.zh: 球花饰是十四世纪早期英国哥特建筑的典型装饰。

e.en: A quick {ballgirl} caught the foul ball mid-air.
e.zh: 一名敏捷的女球童在空中接住了界外球。

e.en: She started as a {ballgirl} at her local tennis club.
e.zh: 她最初在当地网球俱乐部当女球童。

ballhawk.t: 抢球高手；防守拦截能手

e.en: The young safety is a real {ballhawk} in the secondary.
e.zh: 这位年轻的安全卫真是后场的抢球高手。

e.en: Fans bring gloves hoping to {ballhawk} a home run souvenir.
e.zh: 球迷带着手套,希望抢到一个本垒打纪念球。

e.en: He mounted his camera on a sturdy {ballhead} tripod.
e.zh: 他把相机装在一个结实的球形云台三脚架上。

e.en: The lever locks the {ballhead} firmly in any position.
e.zh: 那个手柄能把球形云台牢牢锁定在任何位置。

ballin.t: 过着奢华生活（俚）；玩得很嗨

e.en: He's been {ballin} ever since he signed that contract.
e.zh: 自从签了那份合同,他就一直过着奢华生活。

e.en: The crew was {ballin} all weekend in Las Vegas.
e.zh: 那帮人整个周末在拉斯维加斯过得相当奢华。

ballism.t: 投掷症；舞蹈样不自主运动

e.en: The patient developed {ballism} after a small stroke.
e.zh: 这位患者在一次小中风后出现了投掷症。

e.en: Neurologists distinguish {ballism} from typical chorea by its violent amplitude.
e.zh: 神经科医生根据动作幅度剧烈,把投掷症与典型的舞蹈症区分开来。

e.en: Roman engineers wheeled the {ballistae} into position before dawn.
e.zh: 罗马工程师在黎明前把弩炮推到了阵位上。

e.en: Two massive {ballistae} guarded the city gate.
e.zh: 两台巨大的弩炮守卫着城门。

e.en: The treaty limits the number of long-range {ballistic-missiles}.
e.zh: 该条约限制了远程弹道导弹的数量。

e.en: Radar detected the launch of a {ballistic-missile} over the sea.
e.zh: 雷达探测到一枚弹道导弹越过海面发射。

e.en: A police {ballistician} matched the bullet to the suspect's gun.
e.zh: 一位警方弹道学家将子弹与嫌疑人的枪进行了比对。

e.en: The army hired a senior {ballistician} to redesign the artillery shells.
e.zh: 军方聘请了一位资深弹道学家重新设计炮弹。

e.en: The Roman elite practiced {balneation} as part of daily ritual.
e.zh: 罗马贵族把沐浴当作日常仪式的一部分。

e.en: Spa retreats revive the ancient art of {balneation}.
e.zh: 水疗度假村重现了古代的沐浴艺术。

e.en: She studied {balneology} to understand mineral water cures.
e.zh: 她研究浴疗学，以了解矿泉水疗法。

e.en: Modern {balneology} draws on chemistry and physiology.
e.zh: 现代浴疗学借助化学与生理学。

e.en: Doctors recommended {balneotherapy} for her arthritis.
e.zh: 医生推荐用浴疗法治她的关节炎。

e.en: The clinic offers {balneotherapy} in natural hot springs.
e.zh: 这家诊所在天然温泉中提供水疗服务。

e.en: The forest hosts many {balsamiferous} trees.
e.zh: 那片森林里有许多产香脂的树木。

e.en: Botanists prize {balsamiferous} species for their resin.
e.zh: 植物学家因树脂而珍视产香脂的物种。

e.en: Children pinched the {balsamine} pods to watch seeds fly out.
e.zh: 孩子们捏凤仙花的果荚，看种子飞出。

e.en: Pink {balsamine} blooms lined the garden path.
e.zh: 粉色凤仙花沿着花园小径盛开。

e.en: The air was sweet and {balsamous} after the rain.
e.zh: 雨后空气甘甜如香脂。

e.en: He breathed in the {balsamous} scent of pine.
e.zh: 他吸入了松树那香脂般的气味。

e.en: Yellow {balsamroot} carpeted the meadow in spring.
e.zh: 春天黄色的香脂菊铺满了草地。

e.en: Native peoples used {balsamroot} for medicine and food.
e.zh: 原住民将香脂菊用作药物和食物。

e.en: A {balsamy} fragrance filled the chapel.
e.zh: 小教堂里弥漫着香脂般的芬芳。

e.en: She loved the {balsamy} smell of the cedar chest.
e.zh: 她喜爱雪松箱那香脂般的气味。

balut.t: 鸭仔蛋；菲律宾受精鸭蛋

e.en: Tourists in Manila are often dared to try {balut}.
e.zh: 在马尼拉，游客常被怂恿去尝试鸭仔蛋。

e.en: He cracked the {balut} shell with practiced ease.
e.zh: 他熟练地敲开了鸭仔蛋的壳。

e.en: The proud parents cooed over their new {bambino}.
e.zh: 自豪的父母对着新生的小宝贝轻声逗弄。

e.en: Italian grandmothers spoil every {bambino} with sweets.
e.zh: 意大利的祖母们用糖果宠坏每一个小娃娃。

e.en: Stir-fried {bamboo-shoots} are common in Chinese cuisine.
e.zh: 炒竹笋在中国菜里很常见。

e.en: She added fresh {bamboo-shoot} to the soup.
e.zh: 她在汤里加了新鲜的竹笋。

e.en: The audience watched the magician's {bamboozlement} in awe.
e.zh: 观众敬畏地看着魔术师的蒙骗把戏。

e.en: His confident tone disguised the sheer {bamboozlement} of the scheme.
e.zh: 他自信的语气掩盖了这场骗局彻头彻尾的欺诈。

e.en: Critics claimed war had {barbarized} the soldiers.
e.zh: 批评家声称战争使士兵变得野蛮。

e.en: He {barbarized} the once-elegant language.
e.zh: 他把曾经优雅的语言变得粗鄙。

e.en: Constant violence {barbarizes} a society.
e.zh: 持续的暴力会使社会变得野蛮。

e.en: Her translation {barbarizes} the original poem.
e.zh: 她的翻译糟蹋了原诗的优美。

e.en: He accused the media of {barbarizing} public discourse.
e.zh: 他指责媒体使公共讨论变得粗俗。

e.en: Years of war were slowly {barbarizing} the region.
e.zh: 多年的战争正慢慢使该地区野蛮化。

e.en: A {barbed-wire} fence surrounded the camp.
e.zh: 营地周围围着带刺铁丝网。

e.en: He cut his hand on the {barbed-wire}.
e.zh: 他被带刺铁丝网划破了手。

e.en: The {barbershoppers} harmonized in four parts.
e.zh: 理发店式合唱团成员以四声部合唱。

e.en: Local {barbershoppers} performed at the festival.
e.zh: 当地的理发店式合唱团成员在节日上演出。

e.en: The colorful {barbet} perched on a high branch.
e.zh: 色彩鲜艳的拟啄木鸟栖息在高枝上。

e.en: She trains her {barbet} for waterfowl hunting.
e.zh: 她训练她的卷毛猎犬猎水禽。

e.en: The gun was mounted on a {barbette}.
e.zh: 火炮安装在炮座上。

e.en: Sailors manned the forward {barbette}.
e.zh: 水兵们操纵前部炮座。

e.en: Each {barbicel} hooks onto neighboring barbules.
e.zh: 每个羽小钩都钩住相邻的羽小枝。

e.en: The feather's {barbicel} structure aids flight.
e.zh: 羽毛的羽小钩结构有助于飞行。

e.en: Doctors once prescribed {barbital} as a sedative.
e.zh: 医生曾把巴比妥作为镇静剂开处方。

e.en: {Barbital} has largely been replaced by safer drugs.
e.zh: 巴比妥大多已被更安全的药物取代。

barbitone.t: 巴比妥（巴比妥的英式名称）

e.en: {Barbitone} was widely used in early sleep aids.
e.zh: 巴比妥曾广泛用于早期安眠药中。

e.en: The lab synthesized small amounts of {barbitone}.
e.zh: 实验室合成了少量巴比妥。

e.en: She decorated the mirror frame with {barbola} flowers.
e.zh: 她用立体浮雕花朵装饰镜框。

e.en: {Barbola} work was popular in the 1920s.
e.zh: 立体浮雕工艺在1920年代很流行。

e.en: The vase was decorated with {barbotine} flowers.
e.zh: 花瓶用陶瓷泥釉花朵装饰。

e.en: He learned to apply {barbotine} for relief effects.
e.zh: 他学会用泥釉做出浮雕效果。

e.en: The feather's {barbulation} interlocks tightly.
e.zh: 羽毛的羽小枝构造紧密交错。

e.en: Microscopes reveal intricate {barbulation} patterns.
e.zh: 显微镜下可见复杂的羽小枝构造。

e.en: Each {barbule} hooks into the next to form the vane.
e.zh: 每根羽小枝相互钩连形成羽片。

e.en: Damaged {barbule} rows make feathers look ragged.
e.zh: 羽小枝受损会使羽毛看起来凌乱。

e.en: The pianist played a gentle {barcarole}.
e.zh: 钢琴家演奏了一首轻柔的船歌。

e.en: Offenbach's {barcarole} is instantly recognizable.
e.zh: 奥芬巴赫的船歌一听便能认出。

e.en: The film's {bankrollers} pulled out at the last minute.
e.zh: 这部电影的金主在最后一刻撤资了。

e.en: Silicon Valley {bankrollers} backed the new startup.
e.zh: 硅谷的出资人支持了这家新创公司。

banksman.t: 井口管理员；吊车信号工

e.en: The {banksman} guided the crane operator carefully.
e.zh: 信号工小心地指挥着吊车司机。

e.en: Every site needs a trained {banksman}.
e.zh: 每个工地都需要一名训练有素的信号工。

e.en: The knight was promoted to {banneret} on the battlefield.
e.zh: 这名骑士在战场上被晋升为骑士领主。

e.en: A {banneret} led his own troops under a square banner.
e.zh: 骑士领主在方形旗帜下率领自己的部队。

bannerets.t: 中世纪小骑士领主（复数）

e.en: Several {bannerets} rode at the front of the column.
e.zh: 几名骑士领主骑马走在队伍最前面。

e.en: The king summoned his {bannerets} to council.
e.zh: 国王召集他的骑士领主们开会。

e.en: A tiny {bannerette} fluttered from the lance.
e.zh: 一面小三角旗在长矛上飘动。

e.en: Each car carried a colorful {bannerette}.
e.zh: 每辆车上都挂着一面彩色的小旗。

e.en: Her hair streamed {bannerlike} in the wind.
e.zh: 她的头发像旗帜一样在风中飘扬。

e.en: The leaves hung {bannerlike} from the branches.
e.zh: 叶子像旗帜一样从枝头垂下。

e.en: The clan's {bannerman} marched at the front.
e.zh: 氏族的旗手走在最前面。

e.en: He served as {bannerman} for the regiment.
e.zh: 他在团里担任旗手。

e.en: The Qing {bannermen} once dominated the empire's army.
e.zh: 清朝的八旗兵曾主宰着帝国的军队。

e.en: Loyal {bannermen} surrounded the chief.
e.zh: 忠诚的旗手们簇拥在首领周围。

e.en: A black {bannerol} hung above the tomb.
e.zh: 墓上方挂着一面黑色的丧旗。

e.en: Heralds carried a silk {bannerol}.
e.zh: 传令官拿着一面丝质小旗。

e.en: She screamed like a {banshie} in the night.
e.zh: 她在夜里像报丧女妖一样尖叫。

e.en: Old tales spoke of a wailing {banshie}.
e.zh: 古老的传说讲述着哀号的报丧女妖。

e.en: She decided to {bant} before the wedding.
e.zh: 她决定在婚礼前节食减肥。

e.en: Victorians used to {bant} on meat and wine.
e.zh: 维多利亚时代的人靠肉和酒来节食减肥。

e.en: The {banteng} is a wild ox native to Southeast Asia.
e.zh: 爪哇野牛是原产于东南亚的一种野牛。

e.en: Conservationists work to protect the endangered {banteng}.
e.zh: 环保人士致力于保护濒危的爪哇野牛。

e.en: He lost weight following the {banting} diet.
e.zh: 他通过班廷式节食法减肥。

e.en: {Banting} was popular in nineteenth-century England.
e.zh: 班廷减肥法在十九世纪的英格兰很流行。

e.en: The little {bantling} toddled across the room.
e.zh: 小娃娃摇摇晃晃地走过房间。

e.en: She cradled the sleeping {bantling} in her arms.
e.zh: 她把熟睡的小娃娃抱在怀里。

e.en: The {banty} rooster strutted across the yard.
e.zh: 那只矮脚公鸡在院子里大摇大摆地走着。

e.en: He's a {banty} little man who picks fights.
e.zh: 他是个爱挑衅的好斗小个子。

e.en: They relaxed in the wooden {banya} after skiing.
e.zh: 滑雪后他们在木制蒸汽浴室里放松。

e.en: A traditional {banya} uses birch branches for massage.
e.zh: 传统的俄式蒸汽浴室用桦树枝来按摩。

e.en: The cathedral's {baptistry} is famous for its mosaics.
e.zh: 这座大教堂的洗礼堂以马赛克闻名。

e.en: The child was carried into the {baptistry}.
e.zh: 孩子被抱进洗礼堂。

e.en: The priest deemed the convert {baptizable}.
e.zh: 神父认为这位皈依者可以受洗。

e.en: Only those who profess faith are considered {baptizable}.
e.zh: 只有公开信仰的人才被视为可以受洗。

e.en: The {baptizement} took place at dawn.
e.zh: 洗礼在黎明时举行。

e.en: Her {baptizement} marked a new chapter in her life.
e.zh: 她的洗礼标志着人生新篇章的开始。

e.en: We're hosting a backyard {bar-b-q} on Saturday.
e.zh: 我们周六要在后院办烧烤聚会。

e.en: He flipped burgers at the {bar-b-q}.
e.zh: 他在烧烤会上翻汉堡肉饼。

e.en: Every item is {bar-coded} for easy scanning.
e.zh: 每件商品都贴有条形码以便扫描。

e.en: The {bar-coded} tickets sped up entry.
e.zh: 带条形码的门票加快了入场速度。

e.en: The hospital is {bar-coding} all patient samples.
e.zh: 医院正在为所有病人样本贴上条形码。

e.en: {Bar-coding} reduced inventory errors dramatically.
e.zh: 条码化大幅减少了库存错误。

e.en: He installed {bar-end} shifters on his touring bike.
e.zh: 他在旅行自行车上装了车把末端变速器。

e.en: The {bar-end} mirror improved his visibility.
e.zh: 车把末端的后视镜提高了他的视野。

e.en: She played a gentle {barcarolle} on the piano.
e.zh: 她在钢琴上弹奏了一首轻柔的船歌。

e.en: The opera ends with a haunting {barcarolle}.
e.zh: 歌剧以一首萦绕心头的船歌结束。

e.en: A {barchan} slowly migrated across the desert floor.
e.zh: 一座新月形沙丘缓缓地在沙漠地面上移动。

e.en: Geologists studied the shape of the {barchan}.
e.zh: 地质学家研究了这座新月形沙丘的形状。

e.en: The {barchart} clearly shows monthly sales trends.
e.zh: 这张条形图清楚地显示了每月的销售趋势。

e.en: She added a {barchart} to her presentation.
e.zh: 她在演示文稿中加了一张柱状图。

e.en: The report included several colorful {barcharts}.
e.zh: 报告中包含几张彩色的条形图。

e.en: He compared the two {barcharts} side by side.
e.zh: 他把两张柱状图并排比较。

bardo.t: 中阴；藏传佛教中死后的过渡状态

e.en: The text describes the soul's journey through the {bardo}.
e.zh: 经文描述了灵魂穿越中阴的旅程。

e.en: Tibetan Buddhists meditate on the {bardo} states.
e.zh: 藏传佛教徒会冥想中阴的各种状态。

e.en: His {bardolatry} bordered on obsession.
e.zh: 他对莎士比亚的崇拜近乎痴迷。

e.en: Critics dismissed the lecture as pure {bardolatry}.
e.zh: 评论家将这场讲座斥为纯粹的莎翁崇拜。

bare-back.t: 不备马鞍地；裸背地骑乘

e.en: She rode {bare-back} along the beach.
e.zh: 她不备马鞍沿着海滩骑马。

e.en: Learning to ride {bare-back} takes great balance.
e.zh: 学习不用马鞍骑马需要极佳的平衡感。

e.en: The team operates on a {bare-bone} budget.
e.zh: 团队以最低限度的预算运作。

e.en: He gave only a {bare-bone} explanation.
e.zh: 他只给出了最基本的解释。

e.en: The men worked {bare-chested} in the heat.
e.zh: 男人们在酷热中赤裸上身地干活。

e.en: He ran {bare-chested} along the shore.
e.zh: 他赤着上身沿着岸边奔跑。

e.en: That was a {bare-faced} lie.
e.zh: 那是一个厚颜无耻的谎言。

e.en: His {bare-faced} cheek shocked everyone.
e.zh: 他的厚颜无耻让所有人震惊。

e.en: They fought {bare-fisted} in the alley.
e.zh: 他们在巷子里赤手空拳地打斗。

e.en: He won the {bare-fisted} boxing match.
e.zh: 他赢得了那场赤手拳击比赛。

e.en: The children ran {bare-footed} through the grass.
e.zh: 孩子们赤着脚在草地上奔跑。

e.en: She walked {bare-footed} on the warm sand.
e.zh: 她赤脚走在温暖的沙滩上。

bare-ground.t: 裸露地面的；无植被覆盖的

e.en: The {bare-ground} area eroded quickly in the rain.
e.zh: 那片裸露地面在雨中很快被侵蚀。

e.en: Farmers avoid leaving {bare-ground} during winter.
e.zh: 农民避免在冬天让土地裸露。

e.en: He caught the fish {bare-handed}.
e.zh: 他徒手抓住了那条鱼。

e.en: She fought off the attacker {bare-handed}.
e.zh: 她赤手空拳击退了袭击者。

e.en: He stood {bare-headed} in the cold rain.
e.zh: 他不戴帽子站在寒冷的雨中。

e.en: The soldiers marched {bare-headed} into the church.
e.zh: 士兵们不戴帽子走进教堂。

bare-knuckle.t: 赤手拳击的；不戴手套搏击的

e.en: He competed in a {bare-knuckle} fight.
e.zh: 他参加了一场赤手拳击比赛。

e.en: The campaign turned into a {bare-knuckle} brawl.
e.zh: 这场竞选演变成一场赤裸裸的混战。

bare-knuckled.t: 赤手拳击的；强硬激烈的

e.en: It was a {bare-knuckled} political debate.
e.zh: 那是一场激烈强硬的政治辩论。

e.en: He was a {bare-knuckled} fighter in his youth.
e.zh: 他年轻时是个赤手拳击手。

e.en: She went {bare-legged} despite the cold.
e.zh: 尽管天冷，她还是光着腿。

e.en: The girls played {bare-legged} on the lawn.
e.zh: 女孩们光着腿在草坪上玩耍。

e.en: The toddler ran {bare-naked} through the house.
e.zh: 那个小孩光着身子在屋里跑来跑去。

e.en: She told the {bare-naked} truth.
e.zh: 她说出了赤裸裸的真相。

e.en: We planted {bare-root} roses in the spring.
e.zh: 我们在春天种下了裸根玫瑰。

e.en: {Bare-root} trees are cheaper to ship.
e.zh: 裸根树苗运输成本更低。

bare-walled.t: 墙壁光秃的；没有装饰的

e.en: The {bare-walled} room felt cold and empty.
e.zh: 那间墙壁光秃的房间显得又冷又空。

e.en: They moved into a {bare-walled} apartment.
e.zh: 他们搬进了一间没有装饰的公寓。

bareboat.t: 光船租赁；不带船员的租船

e.en: They chartered a {bareboat} for the holiday.
e.zh: 他们假期租了一艘光船。

e.en: A {bareboat} charter requires sailing experience.
e.zh: 光船租赁需要驾船经验。

e.en: The startup ran a {barebones} operation.
e.zh: 那家初创公司以最基本的配置运营。

e.en: He gave a {barebones} summary of the meeting.
e.zh: 他对会议做了一个简略的总结。

barefeet.t: 赤脚（barefoot 的非标准复数形式）

e.en: The children ran with {barefeet} in the sand.
e.zh: 孩子们赤脚在沙地上奔跑。

e.en: She felt the cool grass beneath her {barefeet}.
e.zh: 她感受到赤脚下凉爽的草地。

e.en: They settled the dispute {barefisted}.
e.zh: 他们以赤手空拳的方式解决了争端。

e.en: He was a {barefisted} brawler in his youth.
e.zh: 他年轻时是个赤手打架的人。

e.en: He caught the snake {barehanded}.
e.zh: 他徒手抓住了那条蛇。

e.en: The shortstop fielded the ball {barehanded}.
e.zh: 游击手徒手接住了那个球。

e.en: The soldier wore a {bandoleer} across his chest.
e.zh: 士兵胸前斜挎着子弹带。

e.en: He kept extra rounds in his {bandoleer}.
e.zh: 他把备用子弹放在弹药带里。

e.en: The villagers feared the {bandolero} hiding in the hills.
e.zh: 村民害怕躲在山里的强盗。

e.en: He played a {bandolero} in the spaghetti western.
e.zh: 他在意式西部片中扮演一名土匪。

e.en: Victorian gentlemen used {bandoline} to slick back their hair.
e.zh: 维多利亚时代的绅士用发胶把头发梳到脑后。

e.en: She applied {bandoline} before pinning up her curls.
e.zh: 她在卷发别起之前先抹了定型胶。

bandora.t: 班多拉琴(文艺复兴低音弦乐器)

e.en: The musician strummed an antique {bandora}.
e.zh: 乐手拨弄着一把古老的班多拉琴。

e.en: A {bandora} provided the bass line of the consort.
e.zh: 班多拉琴在合奏中担任低音声部。

e.en: The {bandore} resembles a large flat-backed lute.
e.zh: 班多琴形似一种平背大鲁特琴。

e.en: He restored a sixteenth-century {bandore}.
e.zh: 他修复了一把十六世纪的班多琴。

e.en: He cut the planks with a {bandsaw}.
e.zh: 他用带锯切割木板。

e.en: The {bandsaw} hummed steadily in the workshop.
e.zh: 带锯在工坊里嗡嗡地稳定运转。

e.en: Old shortwave radios used {bandspreading} for fine tuning.
e.zh: 旧式短波收音机用频带扩展进行精调。

e.en: The {bandspreading} dial allows precise station selection.
e.zh: 频带扩展旋钮可精确选台。

e.en: Flip the {bandswitch} to the AM position.
e.zh: 把波段开关拨到调幅档。
