e.zh: 这部电影在票房上取得了轰动性的成功。

e.en: The engineer sketched a quick {blockdiagram} on the whiteboard.
e.zh: 工程师在白板上快速画了一张方块图。

e.en: A {blockdiagram} can clarify how the modules interact.
e.zh: 框图可以清晰展示各模块之间的交互。

e.en: His pure {blockheadism} cost the team the championship.
e.zh: 他纯粹的愚蠢使球队丢掉了冠军。

e.en: I have no patience for that kind of {blockheadism}.
e.zh: 我对那种笨头笨脑的行为毫无耐心。

blockiness.t: 块状感；方正笨重的样子

e.en: Compression caused noticeable {blockiness} in the video.
e.zh: 压缩让视频出现了明显的块状感。

e.en: The car's {blockiness} gives it a tough, rugged look.
e.zh: 这辆车方正的造型给人一种硬朗结实的感觉。

blockish.t: 像木头一样的；笨拙呆板的

e.en: He gave a {blockish} grunt and turned away.
e.zh: 他笨拙地哼了一声就转身走开。

e.en: The furniture was solid but rather {blockish}.
e.zh: 那家具结实却显得相当呆板笨重。

e.en: The building has a heavy, {blocklike} appearance.
e.zh: 这座建筑外观沉重，像个大方块。

e.en: Children stacked the {blocklike} cushions into a fort.
e.zh: 孩子们把方块状的靠垫堆成一座城堡。

blockout.t: 粗略布局；遮挡；初步排演

e.en: The director did a quick {blockout} of the scene before rehearsals.
e.zh: 导演在排练前对这场戏做了快速的初步走位。

e.en: We installed a {blockout} curtain to darken the room.
e.zh: 我们装了一块遮光帘让房间变暗。

e.en: Wrap the citation in a {blockquote} for clarity.
e.zh: 把引文用块引用包起来，看起来更清晰。

e.en: The article uses a {blockquote} to highlight the witness's words.
e.zh: 文章用块引用来突出证人的话。

e.en: He {bludged} a cigarette off his mate.
e.zh: 他向朋友讨了一支烟。

e.en: Stop {bludging} and finish your work.
e.zh: 别再偷懒了，把活干完。

e.en: Don't be such a {bludger} at work.
e.zh: 别在工作上当个懒鬼。

e.en: That {bludger} never pays for his drinks.
e.zh: 那个揩油鬼从来不付酒钱。

blue-baby.t: 青紫婴儿；先天性心脏病婴儿

e.en: The surgeon specialized in {blue-baby} operations.
e.zh: 这位外科医生专攻青紫婴儿手术。

e.en: He was born a {blue-baby} but recovered fully.
e.zh: 他出生时是青紫婴儿，但已完全康复。

e.en: Her hair was a glossy {blue-black}.
e.zh: 她的头发是亮泽的蓝黑色。

e.en: The crow's feathers shone {blue-black} in the sun.
e.zh: 乌鸦的羽毛在阳光下闪着蓝黑色的光。

e.en: The {blue-blackness} of the night sky was striking.
e.zh: 夜空的蓝黑色调令人惊艳。

e.en: He noted the {blue-blackness} of the bruise.
e.zh: 他注意到瘀伤呈蓝黑色。

e.en: She married into {blue-blood} aristocracy.
e.zh: 她嫁入了贵族世家。

e.en: His {blue-blood} lineage opened many doors.
e.zh: 他的贵族血统为他打开了许多大门。

blue-blooded.t: 出身贵族的；有贵族血统的

e.en: He came from a {blue-blooded} family.
e.zh: 他出身于贵族家庭。

e.en: The {blue-blooded} guests sipped champagne.
e.zh: 贵族出身的宾客们品着香槟。

e.en: A {blue-bottle} buzzed against the window.
e.zh: 一只青蝇在窗户上嗡嗡乱撞。

e.en: She picked a {blue-bottle} from the field.
e.zh: 她从田里摘了一朵矢车菊。

e.en: He invested mainly in {blue-chip} stocks.
e.zh: 他主要投资蓝筹股。

e.en: The firm has a {blue-chip} client list.
e.zh: 这家公司拥有一批优质客户。

e.en: That player is a real {blue-chipper}.
e.zh: 那名球员是真正的顶尖人才。

e.en: They scouted several {blue-chippers} this year.
e.zh: 今年他们物色了几位顶尖新秀。

e.en: The fund holds many {blue-chippers}.
e.zh: 该基金持有许多蓝筹股。

e.en: Coaches recruit {blue-chippers} from across the country.
e.zh: 教练们从全国各地招募顶尖新秀。

e.en: He grew up in a {blue-collar} neighborhood.
e.zh: 他在一个蓝领社区长大。

e.en: The factory hires mostly {blue-collar} workers.
e.zh: 这家工厂主要雇佣蓝领工人。

e.en: The town's {blue-collars} marched for higher wages.
e.zh: 镇上的蓝领工人为加薪而游行。

e.en: Many {blue-collars} lost jobs after the closure.
e.zh: 工厂关闭后许多蓝领工人失业了。

blue-eyed.t: 蓝眼睛的；天真的；得宠的

e.en: The {blue-eyed} child smiled shyly.
e.zh: 那个蓝眼睛的孩子腼腆地笑了。

e.en: He's the manager's {blue-eyed} boy.
e.zh: 他是经理的红人。

e.en: The lamp had a {blue-glass} shade.
e.zh: 那盏灯有一个蓝玻璃灯罩。

e.en: She collects antique {blue-glass} bottles.
e.zh: 她收藏古董蓝玻璃瓶。

blue-gold.t: 蓝金色；蓝金（喻指水资源）

e.en: Water is often called {blue-gold} today.
e.zh: 如今水常被称为蓝金。

e.en: The dress shimmered in {blue-gold} tones.
e.zh: 那件礼服闪烁着蓝金色调。

e.en: The lagoon shone a brilliant {blue-green}.
e.zh: 潟湖闪着鲜亮的蓝绿色。

e.en: She painted the wall a soft {blue-green}.
e.zh: 她把墙刷成柔和的蓝绿色。

e.en: His eyes were a cool {blue-grey}.
e.zh: 他的眼睛是冷调的蓝灰色。

e.en: The sky turned a stormy {blue-grey}.
e.zh: 天空变成暴风雨般的蓝灰色。

e.en: Please sign in {blue-ink} only.
e.zh: 请仅用蓝墨水签字。

e.en: She filled the pen with {blue-ink}.
e.zh: 她给钢笔灌上了蓝墨水。

e.en: A {blue-jeaned} crowd filled the concert.
e.zh: 一群穿蓝牛仔裤的人挤满了音乐会。

e.en: The {blue-jeaned} cowboy tipped his hat.
e.zh: 那个穿蓝牛仔裤的牛仔抬了抬帽檐。

e.en: He wore {blue-jeans} and a white shirt.
e.zh: 他穿着蓝牛仔裤和白衬衫。

e.en: Her favorite {blue-jeans} were faded.
e.zh: 她最爱的蓝牛仔裤已经褪色了。

e.en: {Blue-laser} discs hold more data.
e.zh: 蓝色激光光盘可以储存更多数据。

e.en: The device uses a {blue-laser} for cutting.
e.zh: 该装置使用蓝色激光进行切割。

e.en: Too much {blue-light} can disturb sleep.
e.zh: 过多的蓝光会扰乱睡眠。

e.en: A police car flashed its {blue-light}.
e.zh: 一辆警车闪着警灯。

blue-on-blue.t: 友军误击；自己人打自己人

e.en: The casualties were due to {blue-on-blue} fire.
e.zh: 伤亡是由于友军误击造成的。

e.en: They tried hard to avoid {blue-on-blue} incidents.
e.zh: 他们竭力避免友军误击事件。

e.en: The editor will {blue-pencil} your draft.
e.zh: 编辑会用蓝笔修改你的草稿。

e.en: Censors {blue-pencil} sensitive passages.
e.zh: 审查员会删改敏感段落。

blue-penciled.t: 被删改的；经编辑修订的

e.en: The article came back heavily {blue-penciled}.
e.zh: 文章被大幅删改后退了回来。

e.en: Several lines were {blue-penciled} by the censor.
e.zh: 几行字被审查员删改了。

blue-pencilled.t: 被删改的；经编辑修订的（英式）

e.en: The manuscript was thoroughly {blue-pencilled}.
e.zh: 这份手稿被彻底删改过。

e.en: His report came back {blue-pencilled}.
e.zh: 他的报告被删改后退了回来。

e.en: She spent the morning {blue-pencilling} drafts.
e.zh: 她整个上午都在删改草稿。

e.en: Heavy {blue-pencilling} ruined the writer's style.
e.zh: 过度删改毁了作者的风格。

blue-pencils.t: 删改；编辑（第三人称单数或复数）

e.en: The editor {blue-pencils} every submission.
e.zh: 编辑会删改每一份投稿。

e.en: He keeps a box of {blue-pencils} on his desk.
e.zh: 他桌上放着一盒蓝色铅笔。

e.en: They unveiled a {blue-print} for reform.
e.zh: 他们公布了一份改革蓝图。

e.en: The architect studied the {blue-print} carefully.
e.zh: 建筑师仔细研究了蓝图。

e.en: She won a {blue-ribbon} at the fair.
e.zh: 她在集市上赢得了头奖。

e.en: A {blue-ribbon} panel reviewed the case.
e.zh: 一个一流的专家小组审议了此案。

blue-ribboned.t: 获蓝绶带的；获头等奖的

e.en: The {blue-ribboned} cow was paraded proudly.
e.zh: 那头获头等奖的奶牛被自豪地展示。

e.en: He admired the {blue-ribboned} pie.
e.zh: 他欣赏那个获蓝绶带的派。

e.en: Finding a true {blue-rose} is nearly impossible.
e.zh: 找到真正的蓝玫瑰几乎不可能。

e.en: Their love was a {blue-rose} dream.
e.zh: 他们的爱情是一场蓝玫瑰般的梦。

e.en: It was a perfect {blue-skied} morning.
e.zh: 那是个晴空万里的清晨。

e.en: They hiked under a {blue-skied} afternoon.
e.zh: 他们在蓝天下的午后徒步。

e.en: The {blue-skinned} aliens greeted the captain.
e.zh: 蓝皮肤的外星人向船长致意。

e.en: Hindu art often depicts {blue-skinned} deities.
e.zh: 印度教艺术常描绘蓝皮肤的神祇。

blue-sky.t: 不切实际的；天马行空的

e.en: They held a {blue-sky} brainstorming session.
e.zh: 他们开了一场天马行空的头脑风暴会。

e.en: That's just {blue-sky} thinking right now.
e.zh: 目前这只是不切实际的空想。

e.en: The barrel was forged from {blue-steel}.
e.zh: 枪管由蓝钢锻造而成。

e.en: He flashed his best {blue-steel} pose.
e.zh: 他摆出最酷的冷峻造型。

e.en: She was dismissed as a mere {blue-stocking}.
e.zh: 她被人轻视为只会读书的女学究。

e.en: The salon attracted famous {blue-stocking} writers.
e.zh: 沙龙吸引了著名的女才子作家。

e.en: The jewelry rested on {blue-velvet} cushions.
e.zh: 珠宝放在蓝色天鹅绒垫上。

e.en: She wore a {blue-velvet} gown.
e.zh: 她穿着一件蓝色天鹅绒长裙。

e.en: He dreams of a {blue-water} sailing voyage.
e.zh: 他梦想进行一次远洋航行。

e.en: The navy expanded its {blue-water} capability.
e.zh: 海军扩展了远洋作战能力。

e.en: The {blue-whale} is the largest animal alive.
e.zh: 蓝鲸是现存最大的动物。

e.en: They spotted a {blue-whale} off the coast.
e.zh: 他们在海岸外发现了一头蓝鲸。

e.en: The river was full of {blueback} herring.
e.zh: 河里满是蓝背鲱鱼。

e.en: Anglers caught several {blueback} trout.
e.zh: 垂钓者钓到了几条蓝背鳟鱼。

e.en: A {bluebill} dove beneath the icy water.
e.zh: 一只潜鸭潜入冰冷的水中。

e.en: Hunters watched for {bluebill} on the lake.
e.zh: 猎人们在湖上等候蓝嘴鸭。

e.en: Flocks of {bluebills} flew overhead.
e.zh: 成群的蓝嘴鸭从头顶飞过。

e.en: The {bluebills} gathered on the marsh.
e.zh: 蓝嘴鸭聚集在沼泽地。

e.en: Students wrote essays in a {bluebook}.
e.zh: 学生们在蓝皮本上写论文。

e.en: Check the car's value in the {bluebook}.
e.zh: 在蓝皮书里查这辆车的估值。

bluebutton.t: 蓝纽扣花；一种海葵状海洋生物

e.en: The {bluebutton} drifts on the ocean surface.
e.zh: 蓝纽扣水母漂浮在海面上。

e.en: She pinned a {bluebutton} to her lapel.
e.zh: 她在翻领上别了一枚蓝纽扣。

bluecap.t: 戴蓝帽者；蓝山雀；矿井小精灵

e.en: Folklore tells of a {bluecap} helping miners underground.
e.zh: 民间传说讲述蓝帽精灵在井下帮助矿工。

e.en: A {bluecap} flitted between the branches.
e.zh: 一只蓝山雀在树枝间飞来飞去。

e.en: The {bluecaps} gathered at the village square.
e.zh: 那些戴蓝帽的人聚集在村广场。

e.en: Several {bluecaps} sang in the hedgerow.
e.zh: 几只蓝山雀在灌木篱中鸣叫。

e.en: He invested only in {bluechip} stocks.
e.zh: 他只投资蓝筹股。

e.en: The fund holds mostly {bluechip} companies.
e.zh: 该基金主要持有绩优大公司。

e.en: The town depends on {bluecollar} jobs.
e.zh: 这座小镇依赖蓝领工作。

e.en: He came from a {bluecollar} family.
e.zh: 他出身于一个蓝领家庭。

bluegown.t: 穿蓝袍者；旧时苏格兰受赐蓝袍的乞丐

e.en: The old {bluegown} begged at the gate.
e.zh: 那位穿蓝袍的老乞丐在门口乞讨。

e.en: Historians describe the {bluegown} tradition.
e.zh: 史学家描述了蓝袍乞丐的传统。

bluehead.t: 蓝头濑鱼；头部呈蓝色的鱼

e.en: The {bluehead} wrasse changes sex during its life.
e.zh: 蓝头濑鱼一生中会变换性别。

e.en: Divers spotted a {bluehead} on the reef.
e.zh: 潜水员在礁石上发现了一条蓝头鱼。

bluehearts.t: 蓝心草；一种紫蓝色野花

e.en: {Bluehearts} bloomed across the damp meadow.
e.zh: 蓝心草开满了潮湿的草地。

e.en: She picked a few {bluehearts} for her vase.
e.zh: 她摘了几枝蓝心草插瓶。

e.en: The sky had a {blueish} tint at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明时天空泛着微蓝。

e.en: Her eyes are a soft {blueish} gray.
e.zh: 她的眼睛是柔和的蓝灰色。

e.en: A young {bluejacket} stood at attention.
e.zh: 一名年轻水兵立正站着。

e.en: The {bluejacket} saluted the captain.
e.zh: 那位水兵向船长敬礼。

e.en: The {bluejackets} marched off the ship.
e.zh: 水兵们列队走下军舰。

e.en: Hundreds of {bluejackets} paraded through town.
e.zh: 数百名水兵列队穿过城镇。

e.en: A {bluejay} screeched from the oak tree.
e.zh: 一只冠蓝鸦在橡树上尖叫。

e.en: The noisy {bluejay} scared off smaller birds.
e.zh: 吵闹的冠蓝鸦把小鸟都吓跑了。

e.en: Several {bluejays} fought over the feeder.
e.zh: 几只冠蓝鸦在喂食器上争抢。

e.en: {Bluejays} are common in eastern forests.
e.zh: 冠蓝鸦在东部森林中很常见。

e.en: He wore old {bluejeans} and a t-shirt.
e.zh: 他穿着旧蓝牛仔裤和T恤。

e.en: Her favorite {bluejeans} were faded and torn.
e.zh: 她最爱的蓝牛仔裤已褪色破洞。

blueline.t: 蓝线；冰球场上的蓝色界线

e.en: He shot the puck from the {blueline}.
e.zh: 他从蓝线处射门。

e.en: The defender held the {blueline} steadily.
e.zh: 防守队员稳稳守住蓝线。

e.en: He's the team's top {blueliner} this season.
e.zh: 他是本赛季球队的头号防守队员。

e.en: The {blueliner} blocked another shot.
e.zh: 那名防守队员又挡下了一记射门。

bluenose.t: 假正经的人；古板卫道士

e.en: Don't be such a {bluenose} about jokes.
e.zh: 别对笑话那么道貌岸然。

e.en: The old {bluenose} disapproved of dancing.
e.zh: 那位古板的老人反对跳舞。

e.en: The {bluenosed} censors banned the film.
e.zh: 假正经的审查员禁了那部电影。

e.en: He gave a {bluenosed} sniff of disapproval.
e.zh: 他不以为然地哼了一声，颇为古板。

bluenoses.t: 假正经的人们；卫道士（复数）

e.en: The town {bluenoses} protested the play.
e.zh: 镇上的卫道士们抗议这出戏。

e.en: Local {bluenoses} called for a ban.
e.zh: 当地的假正经们呼吁禁演。

bluepencil.t: 用蓝铅笔删改；审查修订

e.en: The editor will {bluepencil} that paragraph.
e.zh: 编辑会把那一段删改掉。

e.en: Censors {bluepencil} anything controversial.
e.zh: 审查员会删掉一切有争议的内容。

bluepoint.t: 蓝点牡蛎；产自长岛的小牡蛎

e.en: He ordered a dozen {bluepoint} oysters.
e.zh: 他点了一打蓝点牡蛎。

e.en: {Bluepoint} oysters are mild and briny.
e.zh: 蓝点牡蛎味道清淡而带咸鲜。

bluescreen.t: 蓝屏；电脑死机蓝屏画面

e.en: My laptop suddenly hit a {bluescreen}.
e.zh: 我的笔记本电脑突然蓝屏了。

e.en: They filmed the actor against a {bluescreen}.
e.zh: 他们让演员在蓝幕前拍摄。

blueshift.t: 蓝移；光谱向蓝端的偏移

e.en: The galaxy shows a slight {blueshift}.
e.zh: 该星系显示出轻微的蓝移。

e.en: Astronomers measured the star's {blueshift}.
e.zh: 天文学家测量了那颗恒星的蓝移。

blueshifted.t: 发生蓝移的；光谱向蓝偏的

e.en: The approaching star appeared {blueshifted}.
e.zh: 接近中的恒星显示出蓝移。

e.en: Light from the source was clearly {blueshifted}.
e.zh: 来自该源的光明显发生了蓝移。

bluesky.t: 天马行空的；不切实际的构想

e.en: The team did some {bluesky} brainstorming.
e.zh: 团队进行了一番天马行空的头脑风暴。

e.en: That's a {bluesky} idea with no funding.
e.zh: 那只是个没有资金的空想方案。

e.en: The band plays gritty {bluesrock}.
e.zh: 这支乐队演奏粗犷的蓝调摇滚。

e.en: He grew up listening to {bluesrock}.
e.zh: 他是听着蓝调摇滚长大的。

e.en: Critics dismissed her work as mere {bluestockingism}.
e.zh: 评论家把她的作品贬为女学究气而已。

e.en: Victorian society scorned {bluestockingism}.
e.zh: 维多利亚社会鄙视女才子的做派。

bluet.t: 蓝雏菊；一种小型蓝色野花

e.en: A tiny {bluet} bloomed beside the path.
e.zh: 一朵小蓝雏菊在小径旁绽放。

e.en: She knelt to admire the delicate {bluet}.
e.zh: 她跪下欣赏那朵娇嫩的蓝雏菊。

e.en: A male {bluethroat} sang from the reeds.
e.zh: 一只雄性蓝喉歌鸲在芦苇丛中鸣叫。

e.en: We spotted a {bluethroat} during migration.
e.zh: 我们在迁徙季观察到一只蓝喉歌鸲。

e.en: {Bluethroats} breed in northern wetlands.
e.zh: 蓝喉歌鸲在北方湿地繁殖。

e.en: Several {bluethroats} flitted through the brush.
e.zh: 几只蓝喉歌鸲在灌木丛中飞来飞去。

e.en: {Bluetongue} can devastate sheep flocks.
e.zh: 蓝舌病可使羊群遭受重创。

e.en: A {bluetongue} lizard sunned itself on the rock.
e.zh: 一只蓝舌蜥在石头上晒太阳。

e.en: Pair the speaker via {bluetooth}.
e.zh: 通过蓝牙配对音箱。

e.en: My headphones connect over {bluetooth}.
e.zh: 我的耳机通过蓝牙连接。

e.en: {Bluets} carpeted the spring meadow.
e.zh: 蓝雏菊铺满了春天的草地。

e.en: She gathered a handful of {bluets}.
e.zh: 她采了一把蓝雏菊。

e.en: {Blueweed} crowded the roadside ditch.
e.zh: 蓝蓟挤满了路边的水沟。

e.en: Bees love the bright {blueweed} flowers.
e.zh: 蜜蜂喜爱鲜艳的蓝蓟花。

bluffest.t: 最直率的；最爽朗坦白的

e.en: He was the {bluffest} man in the regiment.
e.zh: 他是团里最爽朗直率的人。

e.en: Even her {bluffest} remarks felt kind.
e.zh: 即使她最直白的话也透着善意。

e.en: The bruise turned a deep {bluish-purple}.
e.zh: 瘀青变成了深蓝紫色。

e.en: She wore a {bluish-purple} silk scarf.
e.zh: 她戴了一条蓝紫色的丝巾。

e.en: You {blunderhead}, you locked the keys inside!
e.zh: 你这糊涂虫，把钥匙锁在里面了！

e.en: Only a {blunderhead} would forget the date.
e.zh: 只有笨蛋才会忘记日期。

e.en: Workers {blunge} the clay before molding.
e.zh: 工人在塑形前先把陶土搅拌成浆。

e.en: The potter learned to {blunge} the slip evenly.
e.zh: 陶工学会均匀地搅拌泥浆。

e.en: She broke a {blood-vessel} in her eye.
e.zh: 她眼里爆了一根血管。

e.en: These tiny {blood-vessels} carry oxygen everywhere.
e.zh: 这些细小的血管把氧气输送到全身。

bloodfin.t: 红鳍灯鱼（一种小型观赏鱼）

e.en: He keeps a school of {bloodfins} in his aquarium.
e.zh: 他在水族箱里养了一群红鳍灯鱼。

e.en: The {bloodfin} flashes silver and red as it swims.
e.zh: 红鳍灯鱼游动时闪着银红光。

bloodflower.t: 马利筋（一种红黄色花卉）

e.en: Butterflies love the bright {bloodflower}.
e.zh: 蝴蝶钟爱艳丽的马利筋。

e.en: She planted {bloodflowers} along the fence.
e.zh: 她沿着篱笆种了马利筋。

e.en: He could not escape his {bloodguiltiness}.
e.zh: 他无法摆脱自己的流血之罪。

e.en: The psalm pleads for cleansing from {bloodguiltiness}.
e.zh: 那首诗篇祈求洗净流血之罪。

e.en: The {bloodguilty} king feared divine retribution.
e.zh: 那位有流血之罪的国王害怕天谴。

e.en: He felt {bloodguilty} long after the war.
e.zh: 战后许久他仍觉自己沾染血罪。

e.en: This battle was {bloodier} than the last.
e.zh: 这场战斗比上一场更血腥。

e.en: Her bandage looked {bloodier} by the hour.
e.zh: 她的绷带每过一小时血迹就更多。

e.en: The novel's {bloodiness} shocked many readers.
e.zh: 这本小说的血腥震惊了不少读者。

e.en: Critics objected to the film's {bloodiness}.
e.zh: 评论家对影片的血腥提出异议。

e.en: Medieval {bloodletters} treated patients with leeches.
e.zh: 中世纪的放血者用水蛭给病人治疗。

e.en: History remembers him as a ruthless {bloodletter}.
e.zh: 历史把他记作一个冷酷的屠戮者。

e.en: The {bloodmobile} parks outside the office every Friday.
e.zh: 流动献血车每周五停在办公楼外。

e.en: She donated on the {bloodmobile} during lunch.
e.zh: 她午休时在献血车上捐了血。

e.en: The sunset turned the sky {bloodred}.
e.zh: 夕阳把天空染成血红色。

e.en: She wore a {bloodred} dress to the gala.
e.zh: 她穿了件血红色礼服去晚宴。

bloodsport.t: 血腥运动（如斗牛、猎狐等）

e.en: Many countries have banned {bloodsports}.
e.zh: 许多国家已禁止血腥运动。

e.en: Fox hunting is a controversial {bloodsport}.
e.zh: 猎狐是一种有争议的血腥运动。

e.en: Her ring had a polished {bloodstone}.
e.zh: 她的戒指上有一颗打磨过的血石。

e.en: Ancient warriors believed {bloodstone} could stop bleeding.
e.zh: 古代战士相信血石能止血。

e.en: Mosquitoes are annoying {bloodsucking} insects.
e.zh: 蚊子是讨厌的吸血昆虫。

e.en: He called the landlord a {bloodsucking} cheat.
e.zh: 他骂房东是个敲诈成性的吸血鬼。

e.en: The new villain is {bloodthirstier} than the last.
e.zh: 新反派比上一个更嗜血。

e.en: The crowd grew {bloodthirstier} with each round.
e.zh: 观众一轮比一轮更嗜血。

e.en: He plays the {bloodthirstiest} character in the show.
e.zh: 他在剧中扮演最嗜血的角色。

e.en: It was the {bloodthirstiest} reign of the dynasty.
e.zh: 那是该王朝中最嗜血的统治时期。

e.en: The mob howled {bloodthirstily} for revenge.
e.zh: 暴民嗜血地嚎叫着要报仇。

e.en: He cheered {bloodthirstily} at every knockout.
e.zh: 他对每次击倒都嗜血般地欢呼。

e.en: The table is made of polished {bloodwood}.
e.zh: 这张桌子由打磨过的血木制成。

e.en: Australian {bloodwood} trees ooze a deep red sap.
e.zh: 澳洲血木会渗出深红色树脂。

e.en: {Bloodwort} grows wild along the riverbank.
e.zh: 血根草沿着河岸野生。

e.en: Herbalists once used {bloodwort} to stop bleeding.
e.zh: 草药师曾用血根草来止血。

bloody-minded.t: 故意刁难的；执拗倔强的

e.en: Don't be so {bloody-minded}—just sign the form.
e.zh: 别这么故意作对，签个字就行。

e.en: She's too {bloody-minded} to admit she was wrong.
e.zh: 她固执得根本不肯认错。

bloodyminded.t: 故意刁难的；执拗倔强的

e.en: He's just being {bloodyminded} about the rules.
e.zh: 他只是在故意为难规则。

e.en: Stop being so {bloodyminded} and listen.
e.zh: 别再固执，听我说。

e.en: My laptop just went {blooey} again.
e.zh: 我的笔记本又罢工了。

e.en: The whole plan went {blooey} at the last minute.
e.zh: 整个计划在最后一刻泡汤了。

e.en: The engine went {blooie} on the highway.
e.zh: 发动机在高速公路上罢工了。

e.en: Everything went {blooie} after the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨后一切都乱套了。

e.en: An old {bloomary} once stood by the river.
e.zh: 河边曾有一座古老的块炼铁炉。

e.en: The {bloomary} produced lumps of wrought iron.
e.zh: 那座块炼铁炉打出一块块熟铁。

e.en: Iron was smelted in a small {bloomery}.
e.zh: 铁在一座小型块炼铁炉中冶炼。

e.en: Archaeologists found a Roman {bloomery} nearby.
e.zh: 考古学家在附近发现了一座罗马时期的块炼铁炉。

bloomy.t: 开花的；起白霉花的（如奶酪）

e.en: The garden looks {bloomy} in early spring.
e.zh: 早春的花园繁花盛开。

e.en: Brie has a soft {bloomy} rind.
e.zh: 布里干酪有一层柔软的白霉皮。

e.en: The orchard stood bare and {blossomless}.
e.zh: 果园光秃秃，毫无花朵。

e.en: Drought left the cherry trees {blossomless}.
e.zh: 干旱让樱桃树没了花。

e.en: The {blossomy} branches drooped over the path.
e.zh: 满枝繁花的枝条垂在小径上。

e.en: Her dress had a delicate {blossomy} pattern.
e.zh: 她的连衣裙上有精致的花朵图案。

e.en: His skin looked {blotchier} after the run.
e.zh: 他跑完步后皮肤显得更斑驳。

e.en: The wall got {blotchier} as the paint dried.
e.zh: 墙面随着油漆变干越来越斑驳。

e.en: She picked the {blotchiest} apples for sauce.
e.zh: 她挑了最斑驳的苹果做苹果酱。

e.en: It was the {blotchiest} watercolor in the show.
e.zh: 那是展览中最斑驳的水彩画。

e.en: Concealer can hide any {blotchiness}.
e.zh: 遮瑕膏可以掩盖肤色的斑驳。

e.en: The print's {blotchiness} ruined the photo.
e.zh: 印照的色斑毁了那张照片。

e.en: He kept a {blotless} record at school.
e.zh: 他在学校保持着无瑕的记录。

e.en: Her honor remained {blotless} after the trial.
e.zh: 经过审判她的名誉依然无瑕。

e.en: His {blottesque} brushwork suggested rather than defined.
e.zh: 他粗笔触的画风重在暗示而非勾勒。

e.en: The portrait had a charming {blottesque} quality.
e.zh: 这幅肖像有种迷人的斑点画风。

e.en: He got completely {blotto} at the party.
e.zh: 他在派对上喝得烂醉如泥。

e.en: By midnight half the guests were {blotto}.
e.zh: 到了半夜一半客人都醉成一团。

e.en: She wore a {blousy} top with jeans.
e.zh: 她穿了件宽松蓬松的上衣配牛仔裤。

e.en: His {blousy} shirt flapped in the wind.
e.zh: 他宽松的衬衫在风中飘动。

e.en: Politicians {bloviate} about issues they don't understand.
e.zh: 政客们对自己不懂的事情夸夸其谈。

e.en: He tends to {bloviate} whenever given a microphone.
e.zh: 他一拿到麦克风就喜欢高谈阔论。

e.en: The pottery factory bought a new {blunger} for mixing clay.
e.zh: 陶瓷厂购买了一台新的搅拌机来混合黏土。

e.en: He worked as a {blunger} at the ceramics plant.
e.zh: 他在陶瓷厂当混料工。

e.en: The workers spent the morning {blunging} clay for the kiln.
e.zh: 工人们整个上午都在为窑炉搅拌陶土。

e.en: {Blunging} produces a smooth slip used in pottery.
e.zh: 调和泥浆能产出制陶用的光滑泥釉。

e.en: The lights of the city shone {blurrily} through the rain.
e.zh: 城市的灯光透过雨幕朦胧地闪烁。

e.en: He spoke {blurrily} after waking from his nap.
e.zh: 他午睡醒来后说话含糊不清。

e.en: She gave him a {blushful} smile across the room.
e.zh: 她隔着房间向他露出羞涩的微笑。

e.en: The poet described the {blushful} dawn over the hills.
e.zh: 诗人描绘了山间泛着红晕的黎明。

e.en: He told a {blushless} lie to his boss.
e.zh: 他厚颜无耻地对老板撒了谎。

e.en: Her {blushless} confidence shocked the audience.
e.zh: 她毫不脸红的自信令观众震惊。

e.en: She gets {blushy} whenever he compliments her.
e.zh: 每当他称赞她时，她总会脸红。

e.en: The makeup gave her cheeks a {blushy} glow.
e.zh: 妆容让她的脸颊泛着红润的光泽。

e.en: They sailed home through {blusterous} winds.
e.zh: 他们在狂风中航行回家。

e.en: His {blusterous} speech failed to convince anyone.
e.zh: 他咆哮般的演讲未能说服任何人。

e.en: The {bo's'n} blew his whistle to summon the crew.
e.zh: 水手长吹响哨子召集船员。

e.en: Our {bo's'n} kept the deck spotless during the voyage.
e.zh: 我们的水手长在航行中将甲板擦得一尘不染。

e.en: The {bo'sun} ordered the sailors to trim the sails.
e.zh: 水手长命令船员调整船帆。

e.en: He served as {bo'sun} on a merchant ship for years.
e.zh: 他在一艘商船上当了多年水手长。

e.en: This movie is so {bo-ring} I want to leave.
e.zh: 这部电影太无聊了，我想离开。

e.en: "That class was {bo-ring}," she sighed.
e.zh: "那节课真无聊，"她叹了口气。

e.en: {Boa-constrictors} kill their prey by squeezing it.
e.zh: 蟒蛇通过挤压猎物来杀死它们。

e.en: Several {boa-constrictors} were on display at the reptile house.
e.zh: 爬行馆里展出了好几条蟒蛇。

e.en: The barn was clad in traditional {board-and-batten} siding.
e.zh: 那座谷仓覆有传统的板条相间式外墙。

e.en: They chose {board-and-batten} for the cottage's exterior.
e.zh: 他们为小屋的外墙选用了板条相间式装饰。

board-certified.t: 经委员会认证的（专科医师）

e.en: She is a {board-certified} cardiologist with twenty years of experience.
e.zh: 她是一位拥有二十年经验的认证心脏病专科医师。

e.en: Make sure your surgeon is {board-certified} before the operation.
e.zh: 手术前务必确认你的外科医生已通过专科委员会认证。

e.en: They had to {board-out} their dog while on vacation.
e.zh: 他们度假时不得不把狗送去寄养。

e.en: Some students {board-out} with local families during the term.
e.zh: 有些学生在学期内寄宿于当地家庭。

e.en: The flight is now {boardable} at gate twelve.
e.zh: 该航班现在可在十二号登机口登机。

e.en: Only ferries with ramps are easily {boardable} by wheelchair users.
e.zh: 只有带坡道的渡轮才方便轮椅使用者登船。

e.en: He rented a small room in a {boardhouse} near the docks.
e.zh: 他在码头附近的寄宿之家租了一间小屋。

e.en: The old {boardhouse} had been converted into apartments.
e.zh: 那栋旧寄宿之家已被改建成公寓。

e.en: Please show your passport and {boarding-card} at the gate.
e.zh: 请在登机口出示您的护照和登机牌。

e.en: I can't find my {boarding-card} anywhere.
e.zh: 我到处都找不到我的登机牌。

e.en: She runs a small {boarding-house} for university students.
e.zh: 她经营着一家专为大学生开设的小寄宿公寓。

e.en: The novel is set in a Victorian {boarding-house}.
e.zh: 这部小说以一座维多利亚时代的寄宿公寓为背景。

e.en: He was sent to a strict {boarding-school} at age ten.
e.zh: 他十岁时被送进一所管教严格的寄宿学校。

e.en: Many of the country's leaders attended elite {boarding-schools}.
e.zh: 该国许多领导人都曾就读于精英寄宿学校。

e.en: British {boarding-schools} have a long tradition of sport.
e.zh: 英国寄宿学校有着悠久的体育传统。

e.en: Several famous {boarding-schools} are located in this region.
e.zh: 这一地区坐落着几所著名的寄宿学校。

e.en: He took up {boardsailing} during his summer vacation.
e.zh: 他在暑假期间开始练习帆板运动。

e.en: The bay is famous for {boardsailing} competitions.
e.zh: 这个海湾以帆板比赛而闻名。

e.en: The overcooked steak felt {boardy} on the tongue.
e.zh: 煮过头的牛排在舌头上感觉硬得像木板。

e.en: Her stiff jacket had a {boardy} texture.
e.zh: 她那件僵硬的外套质感像木板一样。

e.en: The fisherman caught a small {boarfish} off the reef.
e.zh: 渔夫在礁石外捕到一条小野猪鱼。

e.en: {Boarfish} are recognized by their long snouts.
e.zh: 野猪鱼可以通过其长长的吻部辨认。

e.en: The duke kept a pack of {boarhounds} for hunting.
e.zh: 公爵养了一群猎野猪犬用于打猎。

e.en: A massive {boarhound} stood guard at the gate.
e.zh: 一只硕大的猎野猪犬守卫在大门旁。

e.en: His {boarish} manners offended every guest at the dinner.
e.zh: 他粗鲁的举止冒犯了晚宴上的每一位客人。

e.en: The villain was depicted with a {boarish} grin.
e.zh: 反派被描绘成一脸野猪般的狞笑。

boart.t: 工业用金刚石；黑金刚石

e.en: The drill bits were tipped with {boart} for cutting hard rock.
e.zh: 钻头镶嵌着工业金刚石，用于切割硬岩。

e.en: South African mines once supplied most of the world's {boart}.
e.zh: 南非矿山曾供应世界上大部分的工业金刚石。

e.en: She wore a black {boat-neck} sweater to the dinner.
e.zh: 她穿了一件黑色一字领毛衣去赴宴。

e.en: The dress has an elegant {boat-neck} cut.
e.zh: 这条裙子的一字领剪裁很优雅。

e.en: They cheered loudly during the annual {boat-race}.
e.zh: 在一年一度的划船比赛中他们大声欢呼。

e.en: The Oxford-Cambridge {boat-race} draws huge crowds.
e.zh: 牛津剑桥赛艇对抗赛吸引了大批观众。

boatable.t: 可通船的；可乘船航行的

e.en: The river is only {boatable} after heavy rain.
e.zh: 这条河只有大雨过后才可通船。

e.en: Most of the lake remains {boatable} year round.
e.zh: 这片湖大部分地方全年可以行船。

e.en: The merchant complained about the high {boatage}.
e.zh: 商人抱怨船运费太高。

e.en: They paid the {boatage} before unloading the cargo.
e.zh: 他们卸货前付清了船运费。

e.en: The {boatbill} hunts at night along quiet streams.
e.zh: 船嘴鹭夜间在安静的溪流边捕食。

e.en: We spotted a {boatbill} perched in the mangroves.
e.zh: 我们看到一只船嘴鹭栖息在红树林里。

e.en: His father was a respected {boatbuilder} on the coast.
e.zh: 他父亲是海岸上备受敬重的造船师。

e.en: The {boatbuilder} sketched the design on a napkin.
e.zh: 那位造船师在餐巾纸上画出了设计图。

e.en: She studied traditional {boatbuilding} in Maine.
e.zh: 她在缅因州学习传统造船工艺。

e.en: {Boatbuilding} requires patience and precise measurements.
e.zh: 造船需要耐心和精确的测量。

e.en: We stayed at a {boatel} moored on the canal.
e.zh: 我们住在停靠运河边的一家水上旅馆。

e.en: The {boatel} offered breakfast on its sun deck.
e.zh: 那家船屋酒店在日光甲板上提供早餐。

e.en: They returned with a {boatful} of fresh herring.
e.zh: 他们满载一船新鲜鲱鱼归来。

e.en: A {boatful} of tourists arrived at the island.
e.zh: 一船的游客抵达了这座岛。

e.en: Whole {boatfuls} of refugees crossed the strait that summer.
e.zh: 那年夏天整船整船的难民横渡了海峡。

e.en: They hauled in {boatfuls} of mackerel each morning.
e.zh: 他们每天清晨满船满船地捕获鲭鱼。

e.en: He used a {boathook} to pull the dinghy closer.
e.zh: 他用篙钩把小艇拉近。

e.en: The crewman grabbed the {boathook} from the deck.
e.zh: 船员从甲板上抓起篙钩。

e.en: Every {boatie} in town came to the regatta.
e.zh: 镇上所有的划船爱好者都来参加帆船赛了。

e.en: He's a real {boatie} and spends weekends on the lake.
e.zh: 他是个十足的船迷，周末都泡在湖上。

e.en: The bowl had a curious {boatlike} shape.
e.zh: 那个碗有一种奇特的船形外观。

e.en: Children played in a {boatlike} wooden cradle.
e.zh: 孩子们在一个船形的木制摇篮里玩耍。

e.en: His {boatmanship} impressed the entire crew.
e.zh: 他的驾船技术让全体船员折服。

e.en: Good {boatmanship} can save lives in rough weather.
e.zh: 高超的驾船技术在恶劣天气中能救命。

boatnik.t: 住船族；船上生活爱好者

e.en: The harbor is full of cheerful {boatnik} retirees.
e.zh: 港口里满是乐观的住船族退休老人。

e.en: As a lifelong {boatnik}, she rarely sleeps ashore.
e.zh: 作为终生的船上生活爱好者，她很少在岸上过夜。

e.en: The village held its summer {boatrace} on Saturday.
e.zh: 村里周六举行了夏季划船比赛。

e.en: He trained all year for the {boatrace}.
e.zh: 他为这场赛艇比赛训练了一整年。

e.en: The old {boatsman} knew every bend of the river.
e.zh: 那位年长的船夫熟悉河上每一个弯道。

e.en: A wiry {boatsman} rowed us across the lake.
e.zh: 一位精瘦的船夫划船把我们送过湖。

e.en: The {boatwright} carved each plank by hand.
e.zh: 造船匠手工刨削每一块船板。

e.en: She apprenticed with a master {boatwright} for years.
e.zh: 她跟随一位造船大师当了多年学徒。

e.en: Local {boatwrights} have built fishing vessels here for centuries.
e.zh: 当地的造船匠在这里造渔船已有几百年。

e.en: A guild of {boatwrights} once ruled this harbor.
e.zh: 造船匠行会曾经主宰这个港口。

e.en: They watched the {bob-sleigh} race on television.
e.zh: 他们在电视上观看雪橇比赛。

e.en: Our {bob-sleigh} sped down the icy track.
e.zh: 我们的雪橇沿着冰道飞驰而下。

boba.t: 珍珠（珍珠奶茶里的粉圆）

e.en: She ordered a milk tea with extra {boba}.
e.zh: 她点了一杯多加珍珠的奶茶。

e.en: The chewy {boba} settled at the bottom of the cup.
e.zh: 软糯的珍珠沉在杯底。

e.en: The market stalls erupted in {bobbery} after the announcement.
e.zh: 消息一公布，市场摊位上一片喧闹。

e.en: There was a great {bobbery} at the back of the hall.
e.zh: 大厅后面闹哄哄的一片骚动。

bobbinet.t: 机制网眼布；筒管花边布

e.en: Her veil was made of fine ivory {bobbinet}.
e.zh: 她的面纱是用精致的象牙色机制网眼布做的。

e.en: The factory specialized in cotton {bobbinet} for curtains.
e.zh: 那家工厂专门生产做窗帘用的棉质网眼布。

e.en: Grandfather seemed quite {bobbish} after his nap.
e.zh: 祖父午睡过后看上去精神十足。

e.en: She felt {bobbish} despite the long journey.
e.zh: 尽管长途跋涉，她仍然精神奕奕。

bobby-dazzler.t: 出众的人或物；耀眼的家伙

e.en: That new sports car is a real {bobby-dazzler}.
e.zh: 那辆新跑车真是个耀眼的尤物。

e.en: Her wedding dress was an absolute {bobby-dazzler}.
e.zh: 她的婚纱真是惊艳无比。

bobby-socker.t: （四十年代追星的）青春期少女

e.en: The theater was packed with screaming {bobby-socker} fans.
e.zh: 剧院里挤满了尖叫的追星少女。

e.en: His mother had been a {bobby-socker} in the forties.
e.zh: 他母亲在四十年代是个追星少女。

bobby-soxer.t: 穿短袜的青春期少女；少女追星族

e.en: Sinatra was worshipped by every {bobby-soxer} in town.
e.zh: 镇上每个少女追星族都崇拜辛纳特拉。

e.en: The diner was the {bobby-soxer} hangout after school.
e.zh: 放学后那家餐厅是少女们的聚集地。

e.en: She rolled down her white {bobbysock} above the saddle shoe.
e.zh: 她把白色翻边短袜卷在鞍形鞋上方。

e.en: A single pink {bobbysock} lay on the bedroom floor.
e.zh: 卧室地板上躺着一只粉色翻边短袜。

e.en: Girls in {bobbysocks} crowded the soda fountain.
e.zh: 穿着翻边短袜的女孩挤满了汽水店。

e.en: She paired her saddle shoes with crisp white {bobbysocks}.
e.zh: 她把鞍形鞋配上崭新的白色翻边短袜。

e.en: Every {bobbysoxer} in the audience screamed his name.
e.zh: 观众席里每个少女追星族都尖声呼喊他的名字。

e.en: Her diary read like a typical {bobbysoxer}'s in 1945.
e.zh: 她的日记读起来就像1945年典型少女追星族的日记。

e.en: A glass {bobeche} caught the wax from each candle.
e.zh: 一个玻璃烛盘接住每根蜡烛滴下的蜡油。

e.en: She polished the silver {bobeche} before the dinner party.
e.zh: 她在晚宴前擦亮了银烛盘。

e.en: He watched the {bobfloat} dip beneath the surface.
e.zh: 他看着浮漂没入水面之下。

e.en: A red {bobfloat} bobbed at the end of the line.
e.zh: 鱼线末端漂着一个红色的浮漂。

bog-standard.t: 普普通通的；最基本款的

e.en: He drives a {bog-standard} family sedan.
e.zh: 他开的是一辆最普通的家用轿车。

e.en: It's a {bog-standard} office job with no surprises.
e.zh: 那是一份毫无新意的普通办公室工作。

bogan.t: 澳式俚语，指粗俗没文化的人

e.en: He dresses like a total {bogan}.
e.zh: 他穿得活像个十足的乡巴佬。

e.en: The pub was full of loud {bogans} watching the football.
e.zh: 酒吧里挤满了大声看球的粗人。

bogans.t: 澳式俚语，指粗俗没文化的人（复数）

e.en: A bunch of {bogans} were arguing outside the bottle shop.
e.zh: 一群粗汉在酒铺外面吵架。

e.en: The film stereotypes Australians as {bogans}.
e.zh: 那部电影把澳大利亚人都刻画成了粗人。

bogey-man.t: 吓唬小孩的怪物；想象中的恶人

e.en: Parents used the {bogey-man} to scare children into behaving.
e.zh: 父母用妖怪吓唬孩子让他们听话。

e.en: Inflation has become the politicians' favourite {bogey-man}.
e.zh: 通货膨胀成了政客们最爱拿来吓人的话题。

boggart.t: 英国民间传说中的家宅恶灵

e.en: The old farmhouse was said to be haunted by a {boggart}.
e.zh: 据说那座旧农舍闹家宅妖怪。

e.en: In the novel, a {boggart} takes the shape of your worst fear.
e.zh: 在那本小说里，博格特会变成你最害怕的样子。

e.en: The project got {bogged-down} in legal disputes.
e.zh: 这个项目陷在法律纠纷里动弹不得。

e.en: Don't get {bogged-down} in the small details.
e.zh: 别在小细节上纠缠不清。

e.en: The trail gets {boggier} after heavy rain.
e.zh: 大雨过后那条小径会更泥泞。

e.en: This part of the field is {boggier} than the other.
e.zh: 田地的这一头比另一头更湿软泥泞。

boggiest.t: 最泥泞的；沼泽化最严重的

e.en: We avoided the {boggiest} stretch of the moor.
e.zh: 我们绕开了荒原上最泥泞的那一段。

e.en: He picked the {boggiest} spot to pitch his tent.
e.zh: 他偏偏挑了最泥泞的地方搭帐篷。

e.en: The {bogginess} of the ground made walking difficult.
e.zh: 地面泥泞使得行走困难。

e.en: Drainage was installed to reduce the field's {bogginess}.
e.zh: 为了减少田地的泥泞，安装了排水设施。

e.en: The {bogland} stretched for miles under the grey sky.
e.zh: 灰色的天空下，沼泽地绵延数英里。

e.en: Ancient bodies have been preserved in the Irish {bogland}.
e.zh: 古代尸体在爱尔兰的沼泽地里得以保存。

e.en: Ireland's {boglands} are protected as fragile habitats.
e.zh: 爱尔兰的沼泽地作为脆弱的生境受到保护。

e.en: Peat is harvested from these {boglands} for fuel.
e.zh: 人们从这些沼泽地采挖泥炭作燃料。

bodice-ripping.t: 色情言情小说式的；煽情浪漫的

e.en: She loves cheesy {bodice-ripping} romance novels.
e.zh: 她喜欢那种俗套的煽情浪漫小说。

e.en: The film has a {bodice-ripping} subplot set in the 18th century.
e.zh: 这部电影有一条设定在18世纪的香艳浪漫副线。

bodily-kinesthetic.t: 身体动觉的；肢体运动智能的

e.en: Dancers tend to have strong {bodily-kinesthetic} intelligence.
e.zh: 舞者往往有很强的身体动觉智能。

e.en: The school nurtures {bodily-kinesthetic} skills through sports.
e.zh: 学校通过体育培养学生的肢体动觉能力。

bodkin.t: 穿带锥；细长发针；尖头小刀

e.en: She threaded the ribbon through with a {bodkin}.
e.zh: 她用穿带锥把丝带穿了过去。

e.en: Hamlet speaks of ending life with a bare {bodkin}.
e.zh: 哈姆雷特说要用一把短匕首结束生命。

e.en: The sewing kit included several {bodkins} of different sizes.
e.zh: 针线盒里有几把大小不一的穿带锥。

e.en: Victorian ladies kept ivory {bodkins} in their workboxes.
e.zh: 维多利亚时代的女士在针线盒里放着象牙穿带锥。

e.en: Old fence posts of {bodock} can last a century.
e.zh: 用美洲桑橙木做的老栅栏柱能用上一个世纪。

e.en: He carved the bow from a piece of {bodock}.
e.zh: 他用一块奥赛奇橙木雕了一张弓。

e.en: The soldiers were brought home in {body-bags}.
e.zh: 那些士兵的遗体装在运尸袋里被运回国。

e.en: Paramedics zipped the corpse into a {body-bag}.
e.zh: 急救人员把尸体拉链封进装尸袋里。

e.en: The factory closure was a {body-blow} to the town.
e.zh: 工厂关闭对这个小镇是一记沉重打击。

e.en: He landed a vicious {body-blow} in the third round.
e.zh: 他在第三回合打出一记凶狠的躯干重击。

body-builder.t: 健美运动员；练肌肉的人

e.en: The {body-builder} flexed his enormous biceps.
e.zh: 那名健美运动员鼓起了硕大的二头肌。

e.en: She trains six days a week to become a {body-builder}.
e.zh: 她每周训练六天，立志成为健美运动员。

e.en: He took up {body-building} after a back injury.
e.zh: 背伤之后他开始练健美。

e.en: {Body-building} requires strict diet and discipline.
e.zh: 健美运动需要严格的饮食和自律。

body-centred.t: 以身体为中心的；体心的

e.en: Iron has a {body-centred} cubic crystal structure.
e.zh: 铁具有体心立方晶体结构。

e.en: Her therapy uses a {body-centred} approach to trauma.
e.zh: 她的治疗采用以身体为中心的方法处理创伤。

body-check.t: 身体阻挡；用身体撞挡（冰球）

e.en: He delivered a hard {body-check} along the boards.
e.zh: 他沿着挡板给了对手一记狠狠的身体阻挡。

e.en: Illegal {body-checks} draw a two-minute penalty.
e.zh: 违规的身体冲撞会被判两分钟处罚。

e.en: The mirrors are painted in matching {body-color}.
e.zh: 后视镜被喷成与车身同色。

e.en: She chose silver as the {body-color} of her new car.
e.zh: 她为新车选了银色作为车身色。

e.en: She wore a black {body-con} dress to the party.
e.zh: 她穿着一条黑色紧身裙去参加派对。

e.en: {Body-con} styles emphasize the wearer's curves.
e.zh: 紧身贴体款式凸显穿着者的身材曲线。

body-conscious.t: 在意身材的；贴身显形的

e.en: Many teenagers become very {body-conscious}.
e.zh: 许多青少年开始非常在意自己的身材。

e.en: The dress has a {body-conscious} silhouette.
e.zh: 这条裙子有贴身显形的剪裁。

e.en: Rugby is a sport with heavy {body-contact}.
e.zh: 橄榄球是一项身体接触激烈的运动。

e.en: The referee penalized illegal {body-contact}.
e.zh: 裁判处罚了违规的身体接触。

e.en: His {body-fat} percentage is below ten.
e.zh: 他的体脂率在百分之十以下。

e.en: Strength training helps reduce {body-fat}.
e.zh: 力量训练有助于降低体脂。

e.en: The virus spreads through {body-fluids}.
e.zh: 这种病毒通过体液传播。

e.en: Always wear gloves when handling {body-fluids}.
e.zh: 接触体液时务必戴手套。

e.en: Two {body-guards} escorted the singer to her car.
e.zh: 两名保镖护送那位歌手上车。

e.en: The president travels with armed {body-guards}.
e.zh: 总统出行时由武装保镖随行。

e.en: The lizard's tail is twice its {body-length}.
e.zh: 那只蜥蜴的尾巴是身长的两倍。

e.en: She bought a {body-length} mirror for the bedroom.
e.zh: 她给卧室买了一面全身镜。

e.en: Children learn the names of each {body-part} in school.
e.zh: 孩子们在学校学习各个身体部位的名称。

e.en: The factory makes replacement {body-parts} for cars.
e.zh: 这家工厂生产汽车的车身备件。

e.en: She got her first {body-piercing} at sixteen.
e.zh: 她十六岁时第一次穿了体环。

e.en: The shop offers tattoos and {body-piercing}.
e.zh: 这家店提供纹身和身体穿孔服务。

e.en: He learned {body-popping} from old hip-hop videos.
e.zh: 他通过看老的嘻哈视频学会了机械舞。

e.en: {Body-popping} requires sharp muscle control.
e.zh: 跳机械舞需要敏锐的肌肉控制。

e.en: The dress flatters her {body-shape}.
e.zh: 这条连衣裙很衬她的体型。

e.en: Different exercises suit different {body-shapes}.
e.zh: 不同的体型适合不同的运动。

body-shop.t: 汽车钣金车间；车身修理店

e.en: He took the dented car to a {body-shop}.
e.zh: 他把那辆撞凹的车送去了钣金店。

e.en: The {body-shop} repainted the whole hood.
e.zh: 修车厂把整个引擎盖重新喷漆了。

e.en: The medication dose depends on {body-size}.
e.zh: 用药剂量取决于体型大小。

e.en: Predators select prey of suitable {body-size}.
e.zh: 捕食者会挑选体型合适的猎物。

body-slamming.t: 摔角式重摔；用身体撞翻

e.en: He was arrested for {body-slamming} a reporter.
e.zh: 他因把记者重摔在地而被捕。

e.en: The wrestler is famous for {body-slamming} his opponents.
e.zh: 这名摔角手以重摔对手而闻名。

e.en: They spent the afternoon {body-surfing} at the beach.
e.zh: 他们整个下午都在海滩上玩徒手冲浪。

e.en: {Body-surfing} doesn't require any board at all.
e.zh: 徒手冲浪根本不需要冲浪板。

e.en: Normal {body-temperature} is around 37 degrees Celsius.
e.zh: 正常体温在摄氏37度左右。

e.en: The nurse took his {body-temperature} every hour.
e.zh: 护士每小时给他量一次体温。

e.en: Babies have a higher proportion of {body-water} than adults.
e.zh: 婴儿的体内水分比例比成年人高。

e.en: Dehydration occurs when {body-water} drops too low.
e.zh: 体内水分降得过低就会脱水。

e.en: Push-ups use your own {body-weight} as resistance.
e.zh: 俯卧撑利用自身体重作为阻力。

e.en: He lost ten percent of his {body-weight} in six months.
e.zh: 他在六个月里减掉了百分之十的体重。

bodyboard.t: 趴板冲浪板；玩趴板冲浪

e.en: She rented a {bodyboard} for the afternoon.
e.zh: 她下午租了一块趴板冲浪板。

e.en: The kids love to {bodyboard} in the shallows.
e.zh: 孩子们喜欢在浅水区玩趴板冲浪。

e.en: He delivered a clean {bodycheck} at the blue line.
e.zh: 他在蓝线处完成了一次干净的身体阻挡。

e.en: Players are taught to {bodycheck} legally.
e.zh: 球员被教导要合规地使用身体阻挡。

e.en: The scale also estimates {bodyfat} percentage.
e.zh: 这台体重秤还能估算体脂率。

e.en: Athletes try to keep {bodyfat} low in season.
e.zh: 运动员在赛季中会尽量保持低体脂。

e.en: The festival featured elaborate {bodypaint} designs.
e.zh: 那个节日上有精美的人体彩绘图案。

e.en: She uses {bodypaint} instead of costumes for her performance.
e.zh: 她在表演中用人体彩绘代替服装。

e.en: In the 19th century, {bodysnatchers} sold corpses to anatomists.
e.zh: 19世纪时，盗尸者把尸体卖给解剖学家。

e.en: The novel features a notorious {bodysnatcher}.
e.zh: 小说中出现了一个臭名昭著的盗尸贼。

e.en: She wore a black {bodysuit} under her jeans.
e.zh: 她在牛仔裤里搭了一件黑色紧身连体衣。

e.en: The dancers performed in matching {bodysuits}.
e.zh: 舞者们身穿同款紧身连体衣表演。

e.en: He learned to {bodysurf} as a child in California.
e.zh: 他小时候在加州学会了徒手冲浪。

e.en: You can {bodysurf} with just a pair of fins.
e.zh: 只要一双脚蹼就能玩徒手冲浪。

e.en: They {bodysurfed} all morning at Bondi.
e.zh: 他们整个上午都在邦迪海滩玩徒手冲浪。

e.en: She {bodysurfed} the wave right onto the sand.
e.zh: 她借着浪头徒手冲上了沙滩。

e.en: Experienced {bodysurfers} read the swell instinctively.
e.zh: 经验丰富的徒手冲浪者能本能地判断浪势。

e.en: He's a lifelong {bodysurfer} from Hawaii.
e.zh: 他是一位来自夏威夷的终身徒手冲浪爱好者。

e.en: {Bodysurfing} is harder than it looks.
e.zh: 徒手冲浪比看上去难。

e.en: He spent the summer {bodysurfing} in Malibu.
e.zh: 他整个夏天都在马里布玩徒手冲浪。

bodysurfs.t: 徒手冲浪（第三人称单数）

e.en: She {bodysurfs} every weekend in summer.
e.zh: 夏天她每个周末都去玩徒手冲浪。

e.en: He {bodysurfs} better than most board riders.
e.zh: 他徒手冲浪比大多数玩冲浪板的还厉害。

e.en: {Boehmite} is an important component of bauxite ore.
e.zh: 勃姆石是铝土矿的重要组成成分。

e.en: The catalyst is supported on a {boehmite} substrate.
e.zh: 该催化剂以勃姆石为载体。

e.en: Please set the title in {bold-face} type.
e.zh: 请把标题设为粗体字。

e.en: The editor decided to {bold-face} the key terms.
e.zh: 编辑决定把关键词以粗体印刷。

e.en: He told a {bold-faced} lie without flinching.
e.zh: 他面不改色地撒了个厚颜无耻的谎。

e.en: The headline appeared in {bold-faced} letters.
e.zh: 标题以粗体字母印出。

e.en: Don't {bollix} up the schedule again.
e.zh: 别再把日程表搞砸了。

e.en: He managed to {bollix} the entire project.
e.zh: 他竟然把整个项目弄得一团糟。

bolometer.t: 测辐射热计；辐射热测量仪

e.en: The {bolometer} measured tiny changes in radiation.
e.zh: 测辐射热计测量了辐射的微小变化。

e.en: Astronomers use a {bolometer} to detect infrared light.
e.zh: 天文学家用测辐射热计来探测红外光。

bolometric.t: 测辐射热的；辐射热测量的

e.en: They recorded the star's {bolometric} luminosity.
e.zh: 他们记录了这颗恒星的辐射热光度。

e.en: The {bolometric} correction was applied to the data.
e.zh: 测辐射热修正值已应用到数据上。

e.en: That excuse is pure {boloney}.
e.zh: 那个借口纯属胡说八道。

e.en: Don't feed me that {boloney} again.
e.zh: 别再跟我说那种废话了。

bolshevise.t: 使布尔什维克化；使共产化

e.en: Critics feared the party would {bolshevise} the unions.
e.zh: 批评者担心该党会使工会布尔什维克化。

e.en: They tried to {bolshevise} the rural villages.
e.zh: 他们试图使乡村地区共产化。

e.en: The teenager was being {bolshy} again.
e.zh: 那个少年又开始顶撞人了。

e.en: Don't get {bolshy} with the manager.
e.zh: 别跟经理对着干。

e.en: He carried an old {bolt-action} rifle.
e.zh: 他扛着一支旧式的栓动步枪。

e.en: The hunter prefers a {bolt-action} weapon.
e.zh: 这位猎人偏爱栓动式武器。

e.en: The cottage was his rural {bolt-hole}.
e.zh: 那座小屋是他乡间的避难所。

e.en: Every fugitive needs a {bolt-hole}.
e.zh: 每个逃亡者都需要一个藏身之处。

e.en: The rich keep {bolt-holes} abroad.
e.zh: 富人在国外都有避难所。

e.en: Foxes dig several {bolt-holes} in the field.
e.zh: 狐狸在田野里挖了好几个藏身洞。

e.en: The wrench slipped off the {bolthead}.
e.zh: 扳手从螺栓头上滑了下来。

e.en: He tightened the rusty {bolthead}.
e.zh: 他拧紧了那颗生锈的螺栓头。

e.en: The cabin became her weekend {bolthole}.
e.zh: 那间小屋成了她周末的避难所。

e.en: He fled to his secret {bolthole}.
e.zh: 他逃到了自己秘密的藏身处。

e.en: The sailor stitched the {boltrope} along the sail.
e.zh: 水手沿着帆边缝上了帆边索。

e.en: A frayed {boltrope} weakens the sail.
e.zh: 磨损的帆边索会削弱整张帆。

e.en: A {bomb-disposal} unit arrived at the scene.
e.zh: 一支拆弹小组抵达了现场。

e.en: He works in {bomb-disposal} for the army.
e.zh: 他在军队负责拆弹工作。

e.en: The {bomb-dropping} aircraft circled the target.
e.zh: 那架投弹飞机在目标上空盘旋。

e.en: He described the {bomb-dropping} mission in detail.
e.zh: 他详细描述了那次投弹任务。

e.en: The pilot opened the {bomb-hatch} over the target.
e.zh: 飞行员在目标上空打开了投弹舱口。

e.en: A faulty {bomb-hatch} grounded the plane.
e.zh: 故障的炸弹舱门让飞机停飞。

bomb-site.t: 轰炸现场；废墟般的地方

e.en: His bedroom looked like a {bomb-site}.
e.zh: 他的卧室乱得像轰炸现场。

e.en: Children played near the old {bomb-site}.
e.zh: 孩子们在旧轰炸废墟附近玩耍。

e.en: He played the {bombardon} in the brass band.
e.zh: 他在铜管乐队里吹低音号。

e.en: The {bombardon} produced a deep, resonant tone.
e.zh: 低音号发出深沉而洪亮的音色。

bloviating.t: 夸夸其谈；高谈阔论；空洞地长篇大论

e.en: The senator kept {bloviating} about his achievements.
e.zh: 那位参议员一直在夸夸其谈自己的成就。

e.en: Stop {bloviating} and answer the question directly.
e.zh: 别再高谈阔论了，直接回答问题。

bloviator.t: 夸夸其谈、自吹自擂的人

e.en: He's a famous {bloviator} on cable news.
e.zh: 他是有线电视新闻里有名的夸夸其谈者。

e.en: Don't waste time listening to that {bloviator}.
e.zh: 别浪费时间听那个吹牛大王说话。

blow-back.t: 反弹；意外的不良后果；负面回应

e.en: The new policy caused political {blow-back} from voters.
e.zh: 这项新政策遭到了选民的强烈反弹。

e.en: He worried about the {blow-back} from his decision.
e.zh: 他担心自己的决定带来不良后果。

blow-by.t: 赛车中的超越动作；活塞漏气

e.en: The driver executed a clean {blow-by} on the straight.
e.zh: 车手在直道上漂亮地完成了超车。

e.en: Engineers measured the {blow-by} in the engine cylinder.
e.zh: 工程师测量了发动机气缸里的漏气量。

blow-by-blow.t: 详尽细致的；逐一描述的

e.en: She gave a {blow-by-blow} account of the meeting.
e.zh: 她详细叙述了会议的每一个细节。

e.en: Fans wanted a {blow-by-blow} description of the fight.
e.zh: 粉丝们想听比赛每一招的详细描述。

blow-cock.t: 蒸汽锅炉的排污阀；放气阀

e.en: The engineer opened the {blow-cock} to release pressure.
e.zh: 工程师打开排污阀释放压力。

e.en: Steam hissed out of the {blow-cock} loudly.
e.zh: 蒸汽从排污阀里大声喷出。

blow-down.t: 锅炉排污；泄压；树木被风吹倒

e.en: Operators performed a {blow-down} of the boiler.
e.zh: 操作员对锅炉进行了排污操作。

e.en: The hurricane caused massive {blow-down} in the forest.
e.zh: 飓风在森林中造成大量树木倒伏。

blow-dried.t: 用吹风机吹干头发的过去式

e.en: She {blow-dried} her hair before the party.
e.zh: 她在派对前用吹风机把头发吹干了。

e.en: He {blow-dried} the puppy after its bath.
e.zh: 他给小狗洗澡后用吹风机把它吹干。

blow-dries.t: 用吹风机吹干头发的第三人称单数

e.en: She {blow-dries} her hair every single morning.
e.zh: 她每天早上都用吹风机吹头发。

e.en: The salon {blow-dries} hair for free today.
e.zh: 今天理发店免费提供吹干头发的服务。

blow-dry.t: 用吹风机吹干头发；做头发造型

e.en: Please {blow-dry} my hair after washing it.
e.zh: 请在洗完后帮我把头发吹干。

e.en: I want a quick {blow-dry} before dinner.
e.zh: 我想在晚餐前快速吹一下头发。

e.en: She bought a new {blow-dryer} yesterday afternoon.
e.zh: 她昨天下午买了一个新的吹风机。

e.en: The hotel room had no {blow-dryer} provided.
e.zh: 酒店房间里没有提供吹风机。

blow-drying.t: 用吹风机吹干头发的动作

e.en: She is {blow-drying} her hair upstairs now.
e.zh: 她现在正在楼上用吹风机吹头发。

e.en: He hates {blow-drying} his thick curly hair.
e.zh: 他讨厌用吹风机吹自己又厚又卷的头发。

blow-drys.t: 用吹风机吹干头发的第三人称单数变体

e.en: She {blow-drys} her hair every weekday morning.
e.zh: 她每个工作日早上都用吹风机吹头发。

e.en: He {blow-drys} his hair after every workout.
e.zh: 他每次健身后都把头发吹干。

blow-hard.t: 爱吹牛的人；自大狂；夸夸其谈者

e.en: That politician is just a loud {blow-hard}.
e.zh: 那个政客只是个爱吹牛的大嗓门。

e.en: Don't trust the {blow-hard} at the bar.
e.zh: 别相信酒吧里那个吹牛大王。

blow-hole.t: 鲸鱼的呼吸孔；通气孔；喷气孔

e.en: The whale exhaled through its {blow-hole} loudly.
e.zh: 鲸鱼通过呼吸孔大声呼气。

e.en: Water sprayed up from the rocky {blow-hole}.
e.zh: 水从礁石的喷气孔里喷涌而出。

blow-in.t: 新来的人；外来户；不速之客

e.en: The locals still call him a {blow-in}.
e.zh: 当地人仍然把他当作外来户。

e.en: Every {blow-in} eventually adapts to village life.
e.zh: 每个外来人最终都会适应乡村生活。

blow-job.t: 口交；粗俗的性行为用语

e.en: Crude slang like {blow-job} is inappropriate at work.
e.zh: 口交这种粗俗用语在工作场合不合适。

e.en: The novel bluntly mentions a {blow-job} scene.
e.zh: 那本小说直白地提到了口交场景。

blow-outs.t: 爆胎；停电；大型聚会的复数形式

e.en: Two {blow-outs} forced the team to retire.
e.zh: 两次爆胎迫使车队退出比赛。

e.en: They threw lavish {blow-outs} every single weekend.
e.zh: 他们每个周末都举办奢华的派对。

blow-over.t: 风暴平息；事过境迁；被风吹倒

e.en: Wait for the storm to {blow-over} first.
e.zh: 先等风暴过去吧。

e.en: This scandal will {blow-over} in due time.
e.zh: 这桩丑闻迟早会平息下来。

blow-period.t: 炼钢转炉的吹炼期；吹风时段

e.en: The {blow-period} in steelmaking lasts about twenty minutes.
e.zh: 炼钢的吹炼期大约持续二十分钟。

e.en: Engineers monitored temperature carefully during the {blow-period}.
e.zh: 工程师在吹炼期仔细监控温度。

blow-pipe.t: 吹管；吹箭筒；玻璃工的吹管

e.en: The hunter used a {blow-pipe} with poison darts.
e.zh: 猎人使用带毒针的吹管。

e.en: The glassblower heated his {blow-pipe} carefully.
e.zh: 吹玻璃工人小心地加热他的吹管。

blow-ups.t: 爆炸；放大照片；发火的复数

e.en: She had two {blow-ups} with her boss.
e.zh: 她和老板大吵了两次。

e.en: The gallery displayed {blow-ups} of historical photos.
e.zh: 画廊展出了历史照片的放大版。

blowball.t: 蒲公英的绒球；带绒毛的种子球

e.en: The children blew the {blowball} of a dandelion.
e.zh: 孩子们吹散了蒲公英的绒球。

e.en: A fluffy {blowball} drifted across the meadow.
e.zh: 一团蓬松的蒲公英绒球飘过草地。

blowby.t: 活塞漏气；气体从活塞处漏过

e.en: The mechanic detected excessive {blowby} in the engine.
e.zh: 技师检测到发动机有过多的漏气。

e.en: Worn piston rings often cause {blowby} problems.
e.zh: 活塞环磨损常常导致漏气问题。

blowcase.t: 化工用的压送容器；液体输送罐

e.en: The factory uses a {blowcase} to transfer acid.
e.zh: 工厂使用压送罐输送酸液。

e.en: Engineers maintained the {blowcase} once a week.
e.zh: 工程师每周维护一次压送容器。

blowfly.t: 丽蝇；麻蝇；产卵于腐肉的苍蝇

e.en: A fat {blowfly} buzzed around the kitchen.
e.zh: 一只肥大的丽蝇在厨房里嗡嗡飞。

e.en: The {blowfly} laid eggs on the meat.
e.zh: 丽蝇在肉上产了卵。

blowing-in.t: 高炉点火开工；启动鼓风

e.en: The {blowing-in} ceremony marked the furnace's start.
e.zh: 开炉仪式标志着高炉正式启动。

e.en: Workers prepared for the {blowing-in} of furnace.
e.zh: 工人们为高炉点火做准备。

blowing-out.t: 高炉停炉熄火；吹熄；呼出

e.en: The {blowing-out} of the furnace took days.
e.zh: 高炉停炉花了好几天的时间。

e.en: After {blowing-out}, the workers cleaned the equipment.
e.zh: 停炉之后，工人们清理了设备。

e.en: The plumber lit his {blowlamp} to solder pipes.
e.zh: 管道工点燃喷灯焊接水管。

e.en: He aimed the {blowlamp} at the frozen pipe.
e.zh: 他把喷灯对准结冰的水管。

e.en: The workshop had several {blowlamps} hanging on hooks.
e.zh: 车间里有几把喷灯挂在钩子上。

e.en: Old {blowlamps} typically use kerosene as fuel.
e.zh: 老式喷灯通常使用煤油作燃料。

blowmobile.t: 运送熔融玻璃的搬运车

e.en: The {blowmobile} carried molten glass to the workshop.
e.zh: 搬运车把熔融玻璃运送到车间。

e.en: Workers loaded the {blowmobile} very carefully.
e.zh: 工人们非常小心地装载搬运车。

blown-glass.t: 吹制玻璃；人工吹制的玻璃器皿

e.en: She collects beautiful {blown-glass} ornaments from Italy.
e.zh: 她收藏来自意大利的精美吹制玻璃饰品。

e.en: Venetian {blown-glass} is famous all over the world.
e.zh: 威尼斯的吹制玻璃举世闻名。

blown-up.t: 充气的；放大的；被炸毁的

e.en: He showed a {blown-up} photo of his daughter.
e.zh: 他给我看了他女儿的放大照片。

e.en: The {blown-up} balloon floated to the ceiling.
e.zh: 那个充足气的气球飘到了天花板。

blowpit.t: 造纸厂的喷放槽；纸浆排放池

e.en: Pulp drained from the {blowpit} into channels.
e.zh: 纸浆从喷放槽流入沟槽。

e.en: The mill's {blowpit} needed regular cleaning.
e.zh: 工厂的喷放槽需要定期清洗。

blowsier.t: 更加邋遢的；更加红脸粗俗的

e.en: Her hair grew {blowsier} as the day progressed.
e.zh: 随着时间推移，她的头发越来越蓬乱。

e.en: She looked {blowsier} than usual that afternoon.
e.zh: 那天下午她看上去比平常更邋遢。

blowsiest.t: 最邋遢的；最红脸粗俗的

e.en: She wore the {blowsiest} dress at the party.
e.zh: 她穿着派对上最邋遢的一条裙子。

e.en: His aunt was the {blowsiest} woman at church.
e.zh: 他姑妈是教堂里最红脸蓬头的女人。

blowtank.t: 造纸厂的喷放罐；蒸煮排放罐

e.en: The {blowtank} stored cooked pulp under high pressure.
e.zh: 喷放罐在高压下储存熟浆。

e.en: Operators inspected the {blowtank} every shift.
e.zh: 操作员每个班次都检查喷放罐。

blowtube.t: 吹管；吹箭筒；玻璃工的吹管

e.en: He shaped the molten glass on a {blowtube}.
e.zh: 他用吹管塑形熔融玻璃。

e.en: The hunter blew a dart through the {blowtube}.
e.zh: 猎人用吹管吹出一支飞镖。

blowup.t: 爆炸；发火争吵；放大照片

e.en: There was a huge {blowup} between the partners.
e.zh: 合伙人之间发生了激烈的争吵。

e.en: She framed a {blowup} of the family photo.
e.zh: 她把家庭合照的放大版裱了起来。

blowups.t: 爆炸或发火争吵的复数形式

e.en: These {blowups} hang in the museum lobby today.
e.zh: 这些放大照片今天挂在博物馆大厅。

e.en: He's known for sudden {blowups} during meetings.
e.zh: 他以会议上突然发火而出名。

blowwave.t: 用吹风机做出的波浪发型

e.en: She got a {blowwave} before the wedding.
e.zh: 她在婚礼前做了波浪吹风造型。

e.en: A good {blowwave} usually lasts about a week.
e.zh: 一次好的吹风造型通常能维持约一周。

e.en: It's a {blowy} day at the beach.
e.zh: 今天海滩上风很大。

e.en: The {blowy} weather completely ruined our picnic.
e.zh: 刮风的天气彻底毁了我们的野餐。

blowze.t: 邋遢红脸的女人；蓬头垢面的女子

e.en: The poet described her as a country {blowze}.
e.zh: 诗人把她描绘成乡下的红脸村妇。

e.en: Old novels sometimes call a wench a {blowze}.
e.zh: 老小说有时把女子称作红脸蓬头女。

blowzed.t: 脸色红润粗糙的；蓬头乱发的

e.en: Her cheeks were {blowzed} from the strong wind.
e.zh: 她的脸颊被强风吹得通红。

e.en: He returned home {blowzed} and very tired.
e.zh: 他回家时脸色泛红、十分疲惫。

blowzier.t: 更加蓬头垢面的；更红脸粗俗的

e.en: She looked {blowzier} after the long hike.
e.zh: 长途徒步后她显得更加蓬头垢面。

e.en: The wind made her hair even {blowzier}.
e.zh: 风让她的头发更加蓬乱。

blowziest.t: 最蓬头垢面的；最红脸粗俗的

e.en: She was the {blowziest} of the three sisters.
e.zh: 她是三姐妹中最蓬头垢面的那一个。

e.en: He wore his {blowziest} shirt to the picnic.
e.zh: 他穿着最邋遢的一件衬衫去野餐。

blowzy.t: 邋遢的；红脸粗野的；蓬头垢面的

e.en: The {blowzy} woman laughed loudly at the bar.
e.zh: 那个邋遢的女人在酒吧大声地笑。

e.en: Her hair looked {blowzy} after the windy walk.
e.zh: 刮风走完路后她的头发显得很蓬乱。

e.en: The store is running a {bogo} deal on shoes.
e.zh: 这家店的鞋子在搞买一送一活动。

e.en: I love {bogo} offers because they save real money.
e.zh: 我喜欢买一送一的优惠，因为能真正省钱。

e.en: Children were warned that the {bogyman} would come for them.
e.zh: 孩子们被警告说妖怪会来抓他们。

e.en: Politicians often invent a {bogyman} to scare voters.
e.zh: 政客常编造一个吓人的怪物来恐吓选民。

e.en: {Bohrium} is a synthetic element with atomic number 107.
e.zh: 𨨏是一种原子序数为107的人工合成元素。

e.en: Only a few atoms of {bohrium} have ever been produced.
e.zh: 人类迄今只制造出了少数几个𨨏原子。

e.en: He resented being called a {bohunk} at the factory.
e.zh: 他讨厌在工厂里被人叫做东欧苦力。

e.en: The slur {bohunk} was common in early industrial America.
e.zh: 在早期工业化的美国，“东欧佬”这种蔑称很常见。

bohunks.t: 东欧移民工人（蔑称，复数）

e.en: The mill bosses lumped the immigrants together as {bohunks}.
e.zh: 工厂老板把移民们一律称作“东欧苦力”。

e.en: Older novels still use the offensive word {bohunks}.
e.zh: 一些老小说里仍能见到“东欧佬”这种冒犯性的词。

e.en: We had a hearty {boil-up} after the long hike.
e.zh: 长途徒步之后我们煮了一大锅丰盛的炖菜。

e.en: A traditional Maori {boil-up} includes pork and watercress.
e.zh: 传统毛利大锅菜里有猪肉和西洋菜。

e.en: These pouches are {boilable}, so reheating is easy.
e.zh: 这些袋子是可水煮的，加热很方便。

e.en: Choose a {boilable} fabric for hospital laundry.
e.zh: 医院床单要选耐煮的布料。

e.en: The hotel's {boiler-room} is in the basement.
e.zh: 酒店的锅炉房在地下室。

e.en: Police shut down a stock-fraud {boiler-room} yesterday.
e.zh: 警方昨天捣毁了一个股票诈骗的电话窝点。

e.en: The mechanic zipped up his greasy {boilersuit}.
e.zh: 机修工拉上了他那件油污的连身工作服。

e.en: She wore a denim {boilersuit} to the festival.
e.zh: 她穿着一件牛仔连身工装去参加音乐节。

e.en: The old salt {boilery} still stands by the coast.
e.zh: 那座古老的盐场至今仍矗立在海边。

e.en: Workers tended the fires inside the sugar {boilery}.
e.zh: 工人们在制糖熬煮房里看守着炉火。

boiling-on-grain.t: 带麦芽糟同煮（酿酒工艺）

e.en: Some craft brewers swear by {boiling-on-grain} for richer flavor.
e.zh: 有些精酿酒师推崇带麦糟同煮以获得更浓郁的风味。

e.en: Modern breweries rarely use {boiling-on-grain} because it's inefficient.
e.zh: 现代酒厂很少使用带麦糟同煮的方式，因为效率太低。

e.en: The pot caused a messy {boilover} on the stove.
e.zh: 那口锅在炉子上沸溢得一塌糊涂。

e.en: Fans were stunned by the championship {boilover}.
e.zh: 球迷们被这场冠军赛的爆冷结果惊呆了。

e.en: Use {boilproof} bags for sterilizing the equipment.
e.zh: 使用耐沸煮的袋子给设备消毒。

e.en: The dye was advertised as completely {boilproof}.
e.zh: 这种染料宣称完全耐高温水煮。

e.en: The toy made a funny {boink} when squeezed.
e.zh: 那个玩具一捏就发出滑稽的砰的一声。

e.en: He bragged crudely about whom he had {boinked}.
e.zh: 他粗俗地吹嘘自己跟谁上过床。

boblet.t: 双人小型雪橇；二人雪橇

e.en: The {boblet} sped down the icy track.
e.zh: 双人小型雪橇飞速冲下冰道。

e.en: She trains with a {boblet} team.
e.zh: 她和一支双人雪橇队一起训练。

e.en: A {bobolink} sang in the meadow.
e.zh: 一只食米鸟在草地上歌唱。

e.en: Birdwatchers love spotting the {bobolink}.
e.zh: 观鸟者最喜欢寻找食米鸟。

e.en: We saw several {bobolinks} flying north.
e.zh: 我们看见几只食米鸟向北飞去。

e.en: Migrating {bobolinks} stop in our fields.
e.zh: 迁徙中的食米鸟在我们的田里停留。

bobotie.t: 南非风味咖喱肉末焗饭

e.en: She served warm {bobotie} for dinner.
e.zh: 晚餐她端上了热腾腾的南非咖喱焗肉。

e.en: {Bobotie} is a popular South African dish.
e.zh: 南非咖喱焗肉是当地的经典菜肴。

bobsledders.t: 雪橇运动员；连橇选手们

e.en: The {bobsledders} adjusted their helmets.
e.zh: 雪橇运动员们调整好头盔。

e.en: Olympic {bobsledders} train year-round.
e.zh: 奥运雪橇选手全年都在训练。

e.en: He won gold in the {bobsleigh} event.
e.zh: 他在雪橇项目中夺得金牌。

e.en: The {bobsleigh} hurtled around the curve.
e.zh: 雪橇飞速冲过弯道。

bobsleighs.t: 多辆雪橇；连橇运动用车

e.en: Several {bobsleighs} crashed during practice.
e.zh: 几辆雪橇在训练中翻车了。

e.en: The team owns three {bobsleighs}.
e.zh: 这支队伍拥有三辆雪橇。

bobstay.t: 船首斜桅下索；首斜桅支索

e.en: The {bobstay} keeps the bowsprit steady.
e.zh: 船首斜桅下索使首斜桅保持稳定。

e.en: Sailors checked the worn {bobstay}.
e.zh: 水手们检查了磨损的船首斜桅索。

e.en: The dog had a stubby {bobtail}.
e.zh: 那只狗长着粗短的截尾。

e.en: She owns an Old English {bobtail}.
e.zh: 她养着一只古英国短尾牧羊犬。

e.en: A {bobtailed} cat darted past us.
e.zh: 一只短尾猫从我们身边窜过。

e.en: He rode a {bobtailed} pony to school.
e.zh: 他骑着一匹短尾小马上学。

e.en: Engineers added a {bobweight} to the crankshaft.
e.zh: 工程师为曲轴加装了配重块。

e.en: The {bobweight} balances the rotating mass.
e.zh: 配重块平衡了转动部件的质量。

e.en: The judge wore a powdered {bobwig}.
e.zh: 法官戴着扑了粉的短假发。

e.en: His old {bobwig} sat on the dresser.
e.zh: 他那顶旧短假发放在梳妆台上。

bocaccio.t: 博卡乔鱼；太平洋长鳍石鲈

e.en: Fishermen caught a large {bocaccio} offshore.
e.zh: 渔民在近海捕获了一条大博卡乔鱼。

e.en: The {bocaccio} is a deep-water rockfish.
e.zh: 博卡乔鱼是一种深海石斑鱼类。

bocage.t: 树篱田园景观；瓷塑树丛装饰

e.en: Norman {bocage} stretched to the horizon.
e.zh: 诺曼底的树篱田园风光延伸至天际。

e.en: She admired a delicate porcelain {bocage}.
e.zh: 她欣赏了一件精致的瓷塑树丛饰。

bocardo.t: 逻辑学中的包卡多式三段论

e.en: Logicians study the {bocardo} syllogism form.
e.zh: 逻辑学家研究包卡多式三段论的形式。

e.en: He cited a classic {bocardo} argument.
e.zh: 他引用了一则经典的包卡多三段论。

e.en: Friends play {bocci} on summer weekends.
e.zh: 朋友们在夏日的周末玩意式滚球。

e.en: Our park has a small {bocci} court.
e.zh: 我们的公园里有一片小型滚球场。

boccia.t: 硬地滚球；残奥会精准运动

e.en: {Boccia} is a Paralympic precision sport.
e.zh: 硬地滚球是残奥会的精准运动项目。

e.en: She trained for {boccia} after her injury.
e.zh: 她在受伤之后开始训练硬地滚球。

boccie.t: 意式草地滚球；硬地滚球

e.en: Italians often play {boccie} after lunch.
e.zh: 意大利人常在午饭后玩意式滚球。

e.en: Grandpa loves a quiet game of {boccie}.
e.zh: 爷爷喜欢安静地玩一局意式滚球。

e.en: The salad came with fresh {bocconcini}.
e.zh: 沙拉里配有新鲜的小马苏里拉奶酪球。

e.en: We ordered {bocconcini} as an appetizer.
e.zh: 我们点了小奶酪球作为开胃菜。

bock.t: 博克啤酒；德式深色烈性啤酒

e.en: He ordered a cold German {bock}.
e.zh: 他点了一杯冰镇的德式博克啤酒。

e.en: The brewery released a seasonal {bock}.
e.zh: 这家酒厂推出了一款季节限定博克啤酒。

bocks.t: 几杯博克啤酒；多款博克黑啤

e.en: Two dark {bocks} stood on the bar.
e.zh: 吧台上摆着两杯黑色博克啤酒。

e.en: He preferred {bocks} to lighter lagers.
e.zh: 他喜欢博克啤酒甚于清淡的拉格。

boddhisattva.t: 菩萨；觉悟之士（异体拼写）

e.en: The temple housed a wooden {boddhisattva}.
e.zh: 寺庙里供奉着一尊木雕菩萨。

e.en: Pilgrims bowed before the gilded {boddhisattva}.
e.zh: 朝圣者在镀金菩萨像前躬身行礼。

bodeful.t: 不祥的；预示凶兆的（古语）

e.en: A {bodeful} silence filled the room.
e.zh: 房间里弥漫着不祥的寂静。

e.en: Her words felt strangely {bodeful}.
e.zh: 她的话听来透着诡异的凶兆感。

bodement.t: 预兆；凶兆；古语中的预言

e.en: The old man's {bodement} chilled them.
e.zh: 老人的预言让他们心中发寒。

e.en: Few heeded the witch's dark {bodement}.
e.zh: 没几个人理会女巫黑暗的凶兆预言。

bodgie.t: 澳洲俚语中的不良少年阿飞

e.en: The {bodgie} combed back his greasy hair.
e.zh: 那个不良少年把油亮的头发往后梳。

e.en: Her uncle was a {bodgie} in the fifties.
e.zh: 她叔叔在五十年代是个阿飞。

bodhi.t: 菩提；佛教中的觉悟与智慧

e.en: He sought {bodhi} through years of meditation.
e.zh: 他通过多年的冥想追寻菩提。

e.en: The Buddha attained {bodhi} under the tree.
e.zh: 佛陀在菩提树下证得觉悟。

bodhisatva.t: 菩萨；菩提萨埵（异体拼写）

e.en: She prayed to a compassionate {bodhisatva}.
e.zh: 她向慈悲的菩萨祈祷。

e.en: Statues of the {bodhisatva} lined the hall.
e.zh: 殿堂中列着一尊尊菩萨像。

bodhran.t: 爱尔兰传统单面皮手鼓

e.en: He played the {bodhran} at the Irish session.
e.zh: 他在爱尔兰民乐聚会上敲手鼓。

e.en: A small {bodhran} hung on the pub wall.
e.zh: 酒吧墙上挂着一面小爱尔兰手鼓。

bodice-ripper.t: 香艳历史言情小说；情色浪漫小说

e.en: She devoured another steamy {bodice-ripper}.
e.zh: 她又一口气读完了一部艳情言情小说。

e.en: Library shelves overflowed with {bodice-rippers}.
e.zh: 图书馆的书架上堆满了言情小说。

e.en: Her mourning gown was made of black {bombasine}.
e.zh: 她的丧服是用黑色邦巴辛绸做的。

e.en: The shop still stocked rolls of dusty {bombasine}.
e.zh: 那家店里还存着几卷蒙尘的邦巴辛绸。

e.en: His {bombastical} speeches bored everyone.
e.zh: 他那些夸夸其谈的演讲让所有人都觉得无聊。

e.en: The preacher had a {bombastical} style.
e.zh: 那位传教士风格十分浮夸。

e.en: He {bombastically} announced his retirement.
e.zh: 他夸张地宣布自己要退休。

e.en: She wrote {bombastically} about her travels.
e.zh: 她把自己的旅行写得天花乱坠。

e.en: The dress was cut from soft {bombazet}.
e.zh: 这件连衣裙用柔软的轻纺毛料裁成。

e.en: Victorian women favoured {bombazet} in summer.
e.zh: 维多利亚时代的女性夏天喜欢穿这种轻毛料。

bombazine.t: 邦巴辛绸；丝毛混纺黑绸

e.en: She wore a stiff {bombazine} mourning dress.
e.zh: 她穿着一件挺括的邦巴辛黑丧服。

e.en: The coffin was draped in black {bombazine}.
e.zh: 棺木上覆盖着黑色邦巴辛绸。

bombe.t: 半球形冰糕；外凸的家具造型

e.en: Dessert was a chocolate {bombe} with raspberries.
e.zh: 甜点是配覆盆子的巧克力炸弹冰糕。

e.en: They bought a {bombe} chest for the hallway.
e.zh: 他们给走廊买了一个外凸造型的抽屉柜。

e.en: They camped in a {bombed-out} church.
e.zh: 他们在一座被炸毁的教堂里露营。

e.en: He looked completely {bombed-out} after the exam.
e.zh: 考试结束后他看起来整个人都垮了。

e.en: Bees {bombilate} around the lavender.
e.zh: 蜜蜂在薰衣草丛间嗡嗡作响。

e.en: The old generator {bombilates} all night.
e.zh: 那台旧发电机整夜嗡嗡响个不停。

e.en: Mosquitoes {bombinate} near my ear.
e.zh: 蚊子在我耳边嗡嗡乱叫。

e.en: Rumours {bombinate} through the office.
e.zh: 流言在办公室里嗡嗡传开。

e.en: Flies {bombinated} above the rotting fruit.
e.zh: 苍蝇在腐烂的水果上方嗡嗡乱飞。

e.en: The wires {bombinated} in the wind.
e.zh: 电线在风中嗡嗡作响。

e.en: A lone bee {bombinates} by the window.
e.zh: 一只孤单的蜜蜂在窗边嗡嗡飞。

e.en: The transformer {bombinates} faintly.
e.zh: 那台变压器发出微弱的嗡嗡声。

e.en: A {bombinating} swarm filled the orchard.
e.zh: 一群嗡嗡作响的蜂群充满了果园。

e.en: He ignored the {bombinating} fluorescent light.
e.zh: 他没理会那盏嗡嗡作响的日光灯。

e.en: The hive's {bombination} grew louder.
e.zh: 蜂巢的嗡嗡声越来越响。

e.en: A low {bombination} came from the engine.
e.zh: 引擎传来低沉的嗡嗡声。

e.en: The aircraft carried a heavy {bombload}.
e.zh: 这架飞机携带着大量炸弹。

e.en: They reduced the {bombload} for longer range.
e.zh: 他们减少了载弹量以延长航程。

e.en: Surfers paddled out to the {bombora}.
e.zh: 冲浪者们划向那处暗礁巨浪区。

e.en: The {bombora} broke far from shore.
e.zh: 暗礁巨浪在离岸很远的地方拍碎。

e.en: The cabinet had a {bombous} front.
e.zh: 这个柜子的正面呈外凸造型。

e.en: She admired the {bombous} curve of the vase.
e.zh: 她欣赏那只花瓶外凸的曲线。

e.en: Children played on the old {bombsite}.
e.zh: 孩子们在旧轰炸废墟上玩耍。

e.en: His bedroom looked like a {bombsite}.
e.zh: 他的卧室乱得像个轰炸现场。

e.en: Postwar {bombsites} were slowly rebuilt.
e.zh: 战后被炸毁的废墟逐渐重建。

e.en: Their kitchens were both {bombsites}.
e.zh: 他们俩的厨房都乱得像炸过一样。

e.en: She stroked the {bombycine} fabric.
e.zh: 她抚摸着那块丝绸般的布料。

e.en: The robe had a {bombycine} sheen.
e.zh: 那件长袍泛着丝绸般的光泽。

e.en: He had a {bonapartean} ambition for empire.
e.zh: 他怀有拿破仑式的帝国野心。

e.en: The general's {bonapartean} pose was unmistakable.
e.zh: 那位将军摆出明显的拿破仑式姿态。

bonapartist.t: 拿破仑派的；波拿巴主义者

e.en: He came from an old {bonapartist} family.
e.zh: 他出身于一个老牌波拿巴派家族。

e.en: The {bonapartist} faction lost influence.
e.zh: 波拿巴派失去了影响力。

e.en: Each guest received a silver {bonbonniere}.
e.zh: 每位宾客都收到了一个银制糖果盒。

e.en: She kept mints in a porcelain {bonbonniere}.
e.zh: 她把薄荷糖放在瓷制糖果盒里。

e.en: He banged his {bonce} on the cupboard.
e.zh: 他把脑袋撞到了橱柜上。

e.en: Use your {bonce} for once!
e.zh: 你倒是动动脑子啊！

e.en: They tested the resin's {bondability} on metal.
e.zh: 他们测试了这种树脂在金属上的粘合性。

e.en: Surface roughness affects {bondability}.
e.zh: 表面粗糙度会影响粘合性能。

e.en: The two surfaces are easily {bondable}.
e.zh: 这两种表面很容易粘合在一起。

e.en: Only {bondable} employees handle the cash.
e.zh: 只有可担保的员工才能经手现金。

e.en: The novel describes life as a {bondmaid}.
e.zh: 这部小说描写了女奴的生活。

e.en: She was sold as a {bondmaid} at thirteen.
e.zh: 她十三岁就被卖为女奴。

e.en: In medieval times a {bondman} could not leave the estate.
e.zh: 中世纪时，农奴不能离开庄园。

e.en: He toiled like a {bondman} from dawn to dusk.
e.zh: 他像奴隶一样从早到晚劳作。

e.en: The lord owned dozens of {bondmen} on his estate.
e.zh: 领主在庄园里拥有数十名农奴。

e.en: The {bondmen} rebelled against their cruel master.
e.zh: 农奴们反抗了他们残暴的主人。

e.en: He was forced into {bondservice} to repay the debt.
e.zh: 他被迫做契约劳役以偿还债务。

e.en: The law abolished all forms of {bondservice}.
e.zh: 该法律废除了一切形式的奴役劳役。

e.en: He worked as a {bondslave} on the plantation.
e.zh: 他在种植园里做奴隶。

e.en: The {bondslave} dreamed of one day being free.
e.zh: 那名奴隶梦想着有朝一日能获得自由。

e.en: The mason placed a {bondstone} to tie the two walls together.
e.zh: 泥瓦匠放了一块丁石把两面墙连起来。

e.en: Each course included a {bondstone} for stability.
e.zh: 每一层石砌都加入一块丁石以保稳定。

e.en: She was sold as a {bondswoman} to a wealthy family.
e.zh: 她被卖给一户富贵人家做女奴。

e.en: The {bondswoman} secretly learned to read.
e.zh: 那名女奴偷偷学会了识字。

e.en: The {bondwoman} served the household for decades.
e.zh: 那位女奴为这家人服务了数十年。

e.en: She was once a {bondwoman} but later gained her freedom.
e.zh: 她曾是女奴，后来获得了自由。

e.en: The {bondwomen} gathered water at dawn.
e.zh: 女奴们在黎明时去打水。

e.en: Many {bondwomen} eventually escaped to the north.
e.zh: 许多女奴最终逃往了北方。

bone-chilling.t: 刺骨的；令人毛骨悚然的

e.en: A {bone-chilling} wind blew across the prairie.
e.zh: 刺骨的寒风吹过大草原。

e.en: She told a {bone-chilling} ghost story by the fire.
e.zh: 她在火炉旁讲了一个令人毛骨悚然的鬼故事。

e.en: He felt a {bone-deep} weariness after the long shift.
e.zh: 长班结束后他感到深入骨髓的疲惫。

e.en: Her love for music was {bone-deep}.
e.zh: 她对音乐的热爱深入骨髓。

e.en: The riverbed was {bone-dry} after the drought.
e.zh: 干旱过后河床完全干涸。

e.en: My throat is {bone-dry}; I need water.
e.zh: 我嗓子干透了，要喝水。

e.en: Her brother is {bone-idle} and never helps at home.
e.zh: 她哥哥懒得要命，从不帮忙做家务。

e.en: Don't be so {bone-idle}; get up and work.
e.zh: 别这么懒，起来干活吧。

e.en: He was {bone-lazy} and refused to lift a finger.
e.zh: 他懒到骨子里，连一根手指都不愿动。

e.en: Their {bone-lazy} dog slept all afternoon.
e.zh: 他们那条懒到骨子里的狗睡了一整个下午。

e.en: The village {bone-setter} fixed his dislocated shoulder.
e.zh: 村里的接骨师把他脱臼的肩膀复位了。

e.en: Traditional {bone-setter} techniques are still practiced today.
e.zh: 传统的正骨手法至今仍在沿用。

e.en: She has the elegant {bone-structure} of a model.
e.zh: 她有着模特般优雅的骨相。

e.en: The X-ray revealed her {bone-structure} clearly.
e.zh: X光片清楚地显示出她的骨骼结构。

bone-tired.t: 筋疲力尽的；累到骨头里

e.en: After the marathon I was {bone-tired}.
e.zh: 跑完马拉松后我累到骨头里。

e.en: She came home {bone-tired} every evening.
e.zh: 她每天晚上回到家都筋疲力尽。

e.en: {Boneblack} was once used to refine sugar.
e.zh: 骨炭曾被用来精炼糖。

e.en: The pigment is made from finely ground {boneblack}.
e.zh: 这种颜料由细磨的骨炭制成。

e.en: The shell had a hard, {bonelike} texture.
e.zh: 那个壳有着坚硬的骨状质地。

e.en: Scientists developed a {bonelike} material for implants.
e.zh: 科学家研发了一种用于植入的类骨材料。

boneshaker.t: 颠簸的旧车；早期自行车

e.en: His old van is a real {boneshaker} on rough roads.
e.zh: 他那辆旧货车在坑洼路上颠得要命。

e.en: Cyclists rode {boneshaker} bicycles in the 1860s.
e.zh: 19世纪60年代的骑行者骑着颠簸的早期自行车。

boneshakers.t: 颠簸的旧车；早期自行车

e.en: Those old buses were absolute {boneshakers}.
e.zh: 那些旧巴士颠得简直要散架。

e.en: Museums display vintage {boneshakers} from the 1800s.
e.zh: 博物馆展出着19世纪的早期自行车。

e.en: The {bongoist} kept the rhythm steady all night.
e.zh: 那位邦戈鼓手整晚都打着稳定的节奏。

e.en: She trained for years to become a skilled {bongoist}.
e.zh: 她苦练多年才成为一名熟练的邦戈鼓手。

e.en: He greeted everyone with easy {bonhommie}.
e.zh: 他以轻松友善的态度向大家打招呼。

e.en: There was a sense of {bonhommie} around the table.
e.zh: 餐桌周围洋溢着和睦融洽的气氛。

e.en: His {bonhomous} manner put guests at ease.
e.zh: 他和蔼可亲的态度让客人感到自在。

e.en: The host was famously {bonhomous} at parties.
e.zh: 那位主人在派对上以友善著称。

e.en: She roasted a {boniato} for dinner.
e.zh: 她烤了一个古巴白甘薯当晚餐。

e.en: The market sold fresh {boniato} from the Caribbean.
e.zh: 市场上卖着来自加勒比的新鲜古巴白甘薯。

e.en: This fish is {bonier} than the salmon we had yesterday.
e.zh: 这条鱼比我们昨天吃的三文鱼骨头多。

e.en: His face grew {bonier} after months of illness.
e.zh: 几个月的病痛后，他的脸变得更瘦骨嶙峋了。

e.en: That was the {boniest} fish I've ever eaten.
e.zh: 那是我吃过骨头最多的鱼。

e.en: He was the {boniest} kid in the class.
e.zh: 他是班上最瘦骨嶙峋的孩子。

e.en: The {boniness} of the fish made it hard to eat.
e.zh: 这鱼骨头多，不好吃。

e.en: He disliked the {boniness} of her thin shoulders.
e.zh: 他不喜欢她那瘦骨嶙峋的肩膀。

e.en: She read a trashy {bonkbuster} on the beach.
e.zh: 她在海滩上读了一本俗气的色情畅销小说。

e.en: The novel became a notorious 1980s {bonkbuster}.
e.zh: 这部小说成了上世纪80年代臭名昭著的色情畅销书。

e.en: She smiled {bonnily} at the children.
e.zh: 她对着孩子们漂亮地笑了笑。

e.en: The cottage was {bonnily} decorated for the holidays.
e.zh: 小屋为节日装饰得漂漂亮亮的。

e.en: Everyone admired the {bonniness} of the bride.
e.zh: 大家都赞叹新娘的美丽。

e.en: There was a quiet {bonniness} about the village.
e.zh: 那个村庄有一种宁静的美。

e.en: As a child he worked as a {boot-black} outside the train station.
e.zh: 他小时候在火车站外当擦鞋匠。

e.en: The old {boot-black} polished shoes for a few coins.
e.zh: 那位年迈的擦鞋匠为几枚硬币给人擦鞋。

e.en: She prefers {boot-cut} jeans over skinny ones.
e.zh: 她比起紧身牛仔裤更喜欢靴型裤。

e.en: These {boot-cut} trousers flatter most figures.
e.zh: 这种靴型长裤适合大多数身材。

e.en: The village {boot-maker} crafted footwear by hand.
e.zh: 村里的靴匠手工制作鞋靴。

e.en: He apprenticed with a famous {boot-maker} in Texas.
e.zh: 他曾在得州一位著名靴匠门下当学徒。

e.en: The {boot-up} sequence takes about thirty seconds.
e.zh: 开机过程大约需要三十秒。

e.en: A slow {boot-up} usually means the disk is failing.
e.zh: 开机变慢通常意味着硬盘快坏了。

e.en: A young {bootblack} offered to shine my shoes for a dollar.
e.zh: 一个小擦鞋匠提出花一美元给我擦鞋。

e.en: In old novels, the {bootblack} was a familiar street figure.
e.zh: 在旧时小说里，擦鞋匠是常见的街头人物。

e.en: The hotel {bootboy} carried our luggage upstairs.
e.zh: 旅馆的擦鞋小工把我们的行李搬上了楼。

e.en: He started as a {bootboy} before becoming the manager.
e.zh: 他从擦鞋杂役做起，后来成了经理。

e.en: She survived a brutal coding {bootcamp} last summer.
e.zh: 她去年夏天熬过了一场残酷的编程集训。

e.en: Marines must complete {bootcamp} before deployment.
e.zh: 海军陆战队员必须先完成新兵训练营才能派遣。

e.en: The downtown {bootery} carries handmade leather boots.
e.zh: 市中心那家鞋店出售手工皮靴。

e.en: She bought riding boots at a small {bootery}.
e.zh: 她在一家小靴店买了双骑马靴。

e.en: He ground out the cigarette with his {bootheel}.
e.zh: 他用靴跟把烟头碾灭。

e.en: The {bootheel} left a deep mark in the mud.
e.zh: 靴跟在泥地里留下了深深的印记。

e.en: He used a {bootjack} to pull off his muddy riding boots.
e.zh: 他用脱靴器把沾满泥的马靴脱下来。

e.en: An old wooden {bootjack} sat by the front door.
e.zh: 前门旁摆着一只旧木脱靴器。

e.en: He refused to {bootlick} the boss for a promotion.
e.zh: 他拒绝为升职去拍老板马屁。

e.en: Some employees {bootlick} shamelessly to get ahead.
e.zh: 有些员工为了上位毫不掩饰地阿谀奉承。

bootlicked.t: 拍马屁；逢迎过（bootlick的过去式）

e.en: He {bootlicked} every executive he met at the gala.
e.zh: 他在晚宴上对遇到的每位高管都极尽逢迎。

e.en: She {bootlicked} her way into a corner office.
e.zh: 她靠拍马屁混到了一间高管办公室。

e.en: Nobody respects a shameless {bootlicker}.
e.zh: 没人会尊重一个无耻的马屁精。

e.en: The office {bootlicker} agreed with every word the boss said.
e.zh: 办公室那个马屁精对老板的每句话都点头称是。

e.en: His {bootlicking} behavior disgusted his colleagues.
e.zh: 他阿谀奉承的样子让同事们反感。

e.en: She got the job through pure {bootlicking}.
e.zh: 她全凭拍马屁拿到了那份工作。

bootlicks.t: 拍马屁（bootlick的第三人称单数）

e.en: He {bootlicks} the manager every chance he gets.
e.zh: 他一有机会就拍经理的马屁。

e.en: She constantly {bootlicks} senior partners at the firm.
e.zh: 她在事务所里不断地讨好资深合伙人。

e.en: Detectives found a single {bootprint} in the snow.
e.zh: 侦探们在雪地上发现了一个靴印。

e.en: The astronaut's {bootprint} remains on the moon.
e.zh: 那位宇航员的靴印至今还留在月球上。

bootscraper.t: 刮泥器（用于刮去鞋底泥土）

e.en: There's a wrought-iron {bootscraper} beside the front step.
e.zh: 前门台阶旁有个铸铁刮泥器。

e.en: Use the {bootscraper} before coming inside.
e.zh: 进屋前请先用刮泥器把鞋底擦干净。

e.en: She slipped a wooden {boottree} into each riding boot.
e.zh: 她在每只马靴里塞了一个木制靴楦。

e.en: A {boottree} helps boots keep their shape.
e.zh: 靴楦能帮助靴子保持形状。

bootylicious.t: 性感诱人的（尤指臀部曲线）

e.en: The song made the word {bootylicious} famous worldwide.
e.zh: 那首歌让“bootylicious”这个词风靡全球。

e.en: She strutted onstage looking absolutely {bootylicious}.
e.zh: 她大摇大摆走上舞台，性感至极。

booyah.t: 耶！（表示得意或庆祝的感叹词）

e.en: {Booyah}! I finally beat the final boss.
e.zh: 耶！我终于打败了最终boss。

e.en: He pumped his fist and shouted {booyah} after the goal.
e.zh: 进球后他握拳高喊“耶！”

e.en: They threw a massive {booze-up} after finals.
e.zh: 期末考完后他们办了一场盛大的豪饮派对。

e.en: The wedding turned into an all-night {booze-up}.
e.zh: 婚礼演变成了一场通宵狂饮。

e.en: Office {booze-ups} were common before the pandemic.
e.zh: 疫情前办公室里的豪饮聚会很常见。

e.en: He's famous for hosting wild {booze-ups}.
e.zh: 他以举办疯狂的狂饮派对而出名。

e.en: Her uncle is a hopeless {boozehound}.
e.zh: 她叔叔是个无可救药的酒鬼。

e.en: The bar's regulars were all old {boozehounds}.
e.zh: 那家酒吧的常客全是些老酒鬼。

e.en: He grinned {boozily} at the bartender.
e.zh: 他醉醺醺地朝酒保咧嘴一笑。

e.en: She sang {boozily} along with the jukebox.
e.zh: 她醉醺醺地跟着点唱机哼唱。

e.en: The pharmacist mixed a {boracic} solution for the wound.
e.zh: 药剂师调配了硼酸溶液用于伤口。

e.en: Old first-aid kits often contained {boracic} powder.
e.zh: 过去的急救包里常装有硼酸粉。

e.en: Chemists synthesized a new {borane} compound for fuel research.
e.zh: 化学家为燃料研究合成了一种新的硼烷化合物。

e.en: {Borane} reacts vigorously with water.
e.zh: 硼烷与水反应剧烈。

borax-bead.t: 硼砂珠（化学定性分析中用以鉴别金属离子）

e.en: The {borax-bead} test reveals the presence of certain metals.
e.zh: 硼砂珠试验能显示某些金属的存在。

e.en: Students performed a classic {borax-bead} experiment in lab.
e.zh: 学生们在实验室做了一个经典的硼砂珠实验。

e.en: The doctor listened for {borborygmus} with her stethoscope.
e.zh: 医生用听诊器聆听肠鸣音。

e.en: His loud {borborygmus} embarrassed him during the meeting.
e.zh: 他响亮的肚鸣声让他在会议上很尴尬。

e.en: The lab uses {borosilicate} glass beakers.
e.zh: 实验室使用硼硅酸盐玻璃烧杯。

e.en: {Borosilicate} resists thermal shock well.
e.zh: 硼硅酸盐耐热冲击性好。

e.en: The reformer denounced every {boroughmonger} in parliament.
e.zh: 改革者谴责议会里每一个操纵选区的政客。

e.en: He was branded a {boroughmonger} by the press.
e.zh: 他被媒体冠以操纵选区者之名。

e.en: The act ended decades of {boroughmongering}.
e.zh: 这项法案结束了数十年操纵选区的行径。

e.en: Critics exposed his {boroughmongering} schemes.
e.zh: 评论者揭露了他操纵选区的伎俩。

e.en: She served hot {borsch} with sour cream.
e.zh: 她端上配酸奶油的热罗宋汤。

e.en: {Borsch} is a staple of Eastern European cuisine.
e.zh: 罗宋汤是东欧菜的主打。

e.en: Grandma's {borshch} simmered for hours.
e.zh: 奶奶的罗宋汤炖了好几个小时。

e.en: He ordered {borshch} at the Russian café.
e.zh: 他在俄式咖啡馆点了罗宋汤。

e.en: The {borsholder} kept order in the tithing.
e.zh: 村区小吏维持着十户区的秩序。

e.en: Each hamlet elected its own {borsholder}.
e.zh: 每个小村庄都选出自己的村区小吏。

bort.t: 工业用碎钻；劣质金刚石

e.en: The drill bit was tipped with {bort}.
e.zh: 钻头尖端镶嵌了工业碎钻。

e.en: Miners separated gem stones from {bort}.
e.zh: 矿工把宝石和工业碎钻分开。

e.en: The menu featured a beetroot {bortsch}.
e.zh: 菜单上有甜菜根罗宋汤。

e.en: He stirred sour cream into his {bortsch}.
e.zh: 他把酸奶油拌进罗宋汤里。

e.en: Cutting tools are coated with {bortz}.
e.zh: 切削工具上覆有工业碎钻。

e.en: {Bortz} has no jewelry value.
e.zh: 工业碎钻没有首饰价值。

e.en: Deer grazed at the edge of the {boscage}.
e.zh: 鹿群在树丛边缘吃草。

e.en: A path wound through the dim {boscage}.
e.zh: 一条小径穿过昏暗的丛林。

e.en: That's absolute {bosh} and you know it.
e.zh: 那完全是胡说，你心里清楚。

e.en: He dismissed her warning as {bosh}.
e.zh: 他把她的警告当成废话置之不理。

e.en: A nightingale sang in the {bosk}.
e.zh: 夜莺在小树林里歌唱。

e.en: They picnicked beside a shady {bosk}.
e.zh: 他们在荫凉的小树林旁野餐。

e.en: The estate ended in dense {boskage}.
e.zh: 庄园尽头是茂密的丛林。

e.en: Birds nested deep in the {boskage}.
e.zh: 鸟儿在丛林深处筑巢。

e.en: A neat {bosket} bordered the lawn.
e.zh: 一片整齐的小树丛环绕着草坪。

e.en: They hid behind the garden {bosket}.
e.zh: 他们躲在花园的矮树丛后面。

e.en: He admired the {boskiness} of the valley.
e.zh: 他赞叹山谷林木的茂密。

e.en: Spring brought a fresh {boskiness} to the park.
e.zh: 春天给公园带来了新的葱郁。

e.en: They walked through a {bosky} hollow.
e.zh: 他们走过一片林木茂盛的洼地。

e.en: The path was {bosky} and cool.
e.zh: 这条小路林荫蔽日，十分凉爽。

e.en: Cottonwoods filled the river {bosque}.
e.zh: 河边树林里满是棉白杨。

e.en: They camped in a shady {bosque}.
e.zh: 他们在荫凉的河边树林扎营。

e.en: A formal {bosquet} flanked the fountain.
e.zh: 喷泉两侧是规整的小树丛。

e.en: The {bosquet} was clipped into geometric shapes.
e.zh: 这片矮树林被修剪成几何形状。

e.en: The old {boss-eyed} cat ruled the alley.
e.zh: 那只独眼老猫称霸小巷。

e.en: He gave me a {boss-eyed} stare.
e.zh: 他斜着眼睛盯着我。

bossa.t: 巴萨诺瓦（巴西舞曲风格）

e.en: The band played a soft {bossa} groove.
e.zh: 乐队奏起轻柔的巴萨诺瓦节奏。

e.en: She loves classic {bossa} records.
e.zh: 她喜欢经典的巴萨诺瓦唱片。

e.en: The façade featured rough {bossage}.
e.zh: 建筑外立面有粗石饰面。

e.en: Stone {bossage} gave the wall a rugged look.
e.zh: 石质粗面让墙体显得粗犷。

e.en: Workers resented his petty {bossdom}.
e.zh: 员工厌恶他那种小老板的派头。

e.en: The party fell into corrupt {bossdom}.
e.zh: 该党陷入腐败的专横统治。

e.en: A {bosseyed} mongrel followed him home.
e.zh: 一只斜眼的杂种狗跟他回了家。

e.en: She squinted in a {bosseyed} way.
e.zh: 她斜着眼眯起来看。

e.en: Tighten the {bosshead} before clamping the flask.
e.zh: 夹烧瓶前先拧紧支架夹头。

e.en: The {bosshead} holds the rod in place.
e.zh: 支架夹头把支杆固定到位。

e.en: He {bossily} rearranged everyone's desks.
e.zh: 他专横地把大家的桌子重新摆放。

e.en: She spoke {bossily} to the new intern.
e.zh: 她颐指气使地对新实习生说话。

bossism.t: 政治寡头操纵；老板政治

e.en: The city long suffered from machine {bossism}.
e.zh: 这座城市长期受党魁政治之苦。

e.en: Reformers vowed to end {bossism}.
e.zh: 改革派誓言终结老板政治。

e.en: Ask the {bossman} before you leave early.
e.zh: 早走前先问问老板。

e.en: The {bossman} signed off on the deal.
e.zh: 头儿批准了这笔交易。

e.en: Don't be such a {bossyboots} at home.
e.zh: 在家别这么爱发号施令。

e.en: Her little brother is a real {bossyboots}.
e.zh: 她的小弟弟真是个爱指挥别人的家伙。

bosthoon.t: 粗鲁的乡巴佬（爱尔兰俚语）

e.en: Don't act like a {bosthoon} at dinner.
e.zh: 吃饭时别表现得像个乡巴佬。

e.en: The old man called him a right {bosthoon}.
e.zh: 那位老人骂他是个十足的粗鲁乡巴佬。

botanize.t: 采集植物标本；研究植物

e.en: They spent the summer {botanizing} in the Alps.
e.zh: 他们整个夏天都在阿尔卑斯山采集植物。

e.en: He likes to {botanize} on weekends.
e.zh: 他喜欢周末去采集和研究植物。

botanized.t: 采集了植物标本；研究过植物

e.en: She {botanized} along the riverbank for hours.
e.zh: 她沿着河岸采集植物好几个小时。

e.en: The professor {botanized} extensively in Borneo.
e.zh: 那位教授曾在婆罗洲广泛采集植物标本。

botanizer.t: 采集植物标本的人；植物研究者

e.en: The old {botanizer} pressed every flower he found.
e.zh: 那位年长的植物采集者把找到的每朵花都压制起来。

e.en: She became a passionate {botanizer} after college.
e.zh: 大学毕业后她成了一名热情的植物采集者。

botanizes.t: 采集植物标本；研究植物

e.en: He {botanizes} every Sunday in the woods.
e.zh: 他每个星期天都在树林里采集植物。

e.en: She {botanizes} whenever she travels abroad.
e.zh: 她出国旅行时总会去采集植物标本。

botanizing.t: 采集植物标本；研究植物

e.en: They went {botanizing} in the highlands.
e.zh: 他们去高地采集植物标本。

e.en: {Botanizing} requires patience and a good eye.
e.zh: 采集植物需要耐心和敏锐的眼力。

e.en: The whole project was a complete {botch-up}.
e.zh: 整个项目完全是一团糟。

e.en: His repair turned out to be a {botch-up}.
e.zh: 他修的活儿结果就是个烂摊子。

botchery.t: 拙劣的活计；蹩脚的修补

e.en: The renovation was sheer {botchery}.
e.zh: 那次翻修简直是粗制滥造。

e.en: I won't tolerate such {botchery} in my workshop.
e.zh: 我的工坊里容不下这种蹩脚活儿。

botchwork.t: 粗劣的工作；拙劣的修补

e.en: The carpenter's {botchwork} embarrassed the whole crew.
e.zh: 那木匠的烂活让整个施工队丢脸。

e.en: This report is just {botchwork}.
e.zh: 这份报告纯粹是粗制滥造。

e.en: The paint job looked {botchy} up close.
e.zh: 近看那油漆工活儿很粗糙。

e.en: He gave a rather {botchy} explanation.
e.zh: 他给出的解释相当蹩脚。

e.en: The hiker was bitten by a {botfly} in the jungle.
e.zh: 那位徒步者在丛林里被马蝇咬了。

e.en: {Botfly} larvae can burrow under the skin.
e.zh: 马蝇的幼虫会钻进皮肤下面。

e.en: This is a {both-way} street now.
e.zh: 这条路现在是双向通行的。

e.en: They installed a {both-way} radio system.
e.zh: 他们安装了一套双向无线电系统。

e.en: What a {botheration} this paperwork is!
e.zh: 这些文书工作真讨厌！

e.en: He apologized for the {botheration} he had caused.
e.zh: 他为造成的麻烦表示歉意。

e.en: The mineral formed a {botryoid} crust on the rock.
e.zh: 这种矿物在岩石上形成了葡萄状的外壳。

e.en: They examined the {botryoid} structure under a microscope.
e.zh: 他们在显微镜下观察那葡萄状的结构。

e.en: Hematite often occurs in {botryoidal} masses.
e.zh: 赤铁矿常以葡萄状团块形态出现。

e.en: The cave walls were covered in {botryoidal} formations.
e.zh: 洞壁上布满了葡萄状的矿物结构。

e.en: The plant has a {botryose} inflorescence.
e.zh: 这种植物具有总状花序。

e.en: Botanists classified it by its {botryose} structure.
e.zh: 植物学家按其总状结构进行了分类。

e.en: Take these empties to the {bottle-bank} on your way.
e.zh: 顺路把这些空瓶拿去废瓶回收箱。

e.en: There's a {bottle-bank} at the supermarket car park.
e.zh: 超市停车场那里有个废瓶回收箱。

e.en: She bought a new {bottle-cleaner} for the baby's bottles.
e.zh: 她为婴儿奶瓶买了一个新的洗瓶刷。

e.en: The {bottle-cleaner} reaches the bottom easily.
e.zh: 这个洗瓶器很容易就能伸到瓶底。

e.en: Their first child was {bottle-fed} from birth.
e.zh: 他们的第一个孩子从出生起就用奶瓶喂养。

e.en: {Bottle-fed} babies may need extra burping.
e.zh: 用奶瓶喂养的婴儿可能需要多拍嗝。

e.en: She decided to {bottle-feed} her newborn.
e.zh: 她决定用奶瓶喂养她的新生儿。

e.en: You can {bottle-feed} the lamb every four hours.
e.zh: 你可以每四小时用奶瓶喂一次小羊。

e.en: {Bottle-feeding} allows other family members to help.
e.zh: 用奶瓶喂养可以让其他家庭成员帮忙。

e.en: She switched to {bottle-feeding} after two months.
e.zh: 两个月后她改用奶瓶喂养。

e.en: He {bottle-feeds} the calves every morning.
e.zh: 他每天早上用奶瓶喂小牛。

e.en: She {bottle-feeds} her baby at night.
e.zh: 她晚上用奶瓶喂宝宝。

e.en: {Bottle-grass} grows wild along the path.
e.zh: 狗尾草沿着小路野生着。

e.en: The field was full of {bottle-grass}.
e.zh: 田地里长满了狗尾草。

e.en: She wore a {bottle-green} velvet dress.
e.zh: 她穿了一条墨绿色的天鹅绒连衣裙。

e.en: The car was painted a deep {bottle-green}.
e.zh: 那辆车被漆成了深墨绿色。

e.en: We saw a {bottle-nosed} dolphin near the boat.
e.zh: 我们在船边看到了一只瓶鼻海豚。

e.en: The {bottle-nosed} whale dove deep below the waves.
e.zh: 瓶鼻鲸潜入了深深的海浪下。

e.en: Do you have a {bottle-opener} handy?
e.zh: 你手边有开瓶器吗？

e.en: He keeps a {bottle-opener} on his keychain.
e.zh: 他把一个开瓶器挂在钥匙链上。

e.en: A huge {bottle-tree} stood at the edge of the farm.
e.zh: 农场边上立着一棵巨大的瓶子树。

e.en: The {bottle-tree} stores water in its swollen trunk.
e.zh: 瓶子树把水储存在膨大的树干中。

e.en: He started as a humble {bottle-washer} in the brewery.
e.zh: 他在啤酒厂从一个低微的洗瓶工做起。

e.en: She's chief cook and {bottle-washer} around here.
e.zh: 在这里她是又当大厨又打杂的。

e.en: He flicked the {bottlecap} off the table.
e.zh: 他把瓶盖从桌上弹了出去。

e.en: She collects vintage {bottlecap}s as a hobby.
e.zh: 她以收藏老式瓶盖为爱好。

e.en: The kittens were {bottlefed} until weaning.
e.zh: 那些小猫一直用奶瓶喂养直到断奶。

e.en: He was a {bottlefed} baby from week one.
e.zh: 他从第一周起就是个奶瓶喂养的宝宝。

e.en: They had to {bottlefeed} the orphaned puppies.
e.zh: 他们不得不用奶瓶喂养那些失去母亲的小狗。

e.en: Many parents choose to {bottlefeed} their infants.
e.zh: 许多父母选择用奶瓶喂养婴儿。

e.en: She {bottlefeeds} the lamb three times a day.
e.zh: 她一天用奶瓶喂三次小羊。

e.en: He {bottlefeeds} the baby while she rests.
e.zh: 她休息时由他用奶瓶喂宝宝。

e.en: She drank a whole {bottleful} of juice.
e.zh: 她喝下了整整一瓶果汁。

e.en: He poured a {bottleful} of oil into the pan.
e.zh: 他把一整瓶油倒进了锅里。

e.en: The bike has a built-in {bottleholder}.
e.zh: 这辆自行车自带一个水瓶架。

e.en: She fixed a new {bottleholder} to the stroller.
e.zh: 她在婴儿车上装了一个新的瓶架。

e.en: The greengrocer slipped a {bonsella} of fruit into our bag.
e.zh: 杂货商往我们的袋子里塞了一份赠送的水果。

e.en: She gave the porter a small {bonsella} for his help.
e.zh: 她给了搬运工一点小费以示感谢。

e.en: Our club hosts an annual {bonspiel} every January.
e.zh: 我们俱乐部每年一月举办一次冰壶锦标赛。

e.en: Curlers from across Canada attended the {bonspiel}.
e.zh: 来自加拿大各地的冰壶选手参加了这场比赛。

e.en: A herd of {bontebok} grazed quietly on the plain.
e.zh: 一群花斑羚在平原上安静地吃草。

e.en: The reserve was created to protect the {bontebok}.
e.zh: 这个保护区是为保护花斑羚而设立的。

e.en: A {bonxie} dived menacingly at the hikers.
e.zh: 一只大贼鸥气势汹汹地俯冲向徒步者。

e.en: Shetlanders affectionately call the great skua a {bonxie}.
e.zh: 设得兰人亲切地把大贼鸥称作 bonxie。

e.en: What a {bonza} day for the beach!
e.zh: 今天去海滩真是棒极了！

e.en: He landed a {bonza} job in Sydney last week.
e.zh: 上周他在悉尼找到了一份好工作。

e.en: An old {bonze} greeted us at the temple gate.
e.zh: 一位年长的和尚在寺庙门口迎接我们。

e.en: The {bonze} chanted softly before the shrine.
e.zh: 那位僧侣在神坛前轻声诵经。

e.en: That's a {bonzer} idea, mate!
e.zh: 兄弟，这主意妙极了！

e.en: We had a {bonzer} time at the barbecue.
e.zh: 我们在烧烤聚会上玩得很开心。

e.en: Their farm is way out in the {boo-ay}.
e.zh: 他们的农场远在荒郊野外。

e.en: We drove for hours into the {boo-ay}.
e.zh: 我们开了几个小时车进入偏远地区。

e.en: I made a silly {boo-boo} on the form.
e.zh: 我在表格上犯了个小错。

e.en: She kissed her son's {boo-boo} to make it better.
e.zh: 她亲了亲儿子的小伤口安慰他。

e.en: Everyone makes a few {boo-boos} at work.
e.zh: 每个人在工作中都会犯些小错。

e.en: The kids came home covered in {boo-boos}.
e.zh: 孩子们回家时身上有不少小擦伤。

e.en: Their public {boobery} made headlines for weeks.
e.zh: 他们公开的蠢事登上了几周头条。

e.en: I have no patience for such {boobery}.
e.zh: 我对这种愚蠢行为毫无耐心。

e.en: We watched a {boobie} dive headfirst for fish.
e.zh: 我们看着一只鲣鸟一头扎进水里抓鱼。

e.en: Don't be such a {boobie} about it.
e.zh: 别为这事犯傻了。

e.en: Mencken coined {booboisie} to mock the masses.
e.zh: 门肯造出 booboisie 一词来讽刺大众。

e.en: He sneered at the tastes of the {booboisie}.
e.zh: 他对愚民大众的品味嗤之以鼻。

e.en: Soldiers cleared a {booby-trap} from the road.
e.zh: 士兵们从路上排除了一个诡雷。

e.en: The drawer was rigged as a {booby-trap}.
e.zh: 这个抽屉被设成了陷阱机关。

booby-trapped.t: 装有诡雷的；设了陷阱的

e.en: The abandoned car was {booby-trapped}.
e.zh: 那辆废弃的汽车被装上了诡雷。

e.en: Rebels {booby-trapped} the bridge before retreating.
e.zh: 叛军在撤退前在桥上设置了诡雷。

e.en: They were charged with {booby-trapping} the warehouse.
