e.zh: 他们被控在仓库内设置诡雷。

e.en: {Booby-trapping} a vehicle is a serious crime.
e.zh: 在车上安装诡雷是严重罪行。

e.en: The forest path was full of {booby-traps}.
e.zh: 那条林间小路布满了陷阱。

e.en: Engineers defused the {booby-traps} one by one.
e.zh: 工兵逐一拆除了诡雷。

e.en: He gave a {boobyish} grin and nodded.
e.zh: 他憨憨地咧嘴一笑，点了点头。

e.en: Her {boobyish} reply embarrassed everyone.
e.zh: 她那愚蠢的回答让大家都很尴尬。

boobytrapped.t: 装有诡雷的；设了陷阱的

e.en: The vehicle had been {boobytrapped} overnight.
e.zh: 那辆车一夜之间被装上了诡雷。

e.en: We found a {boobytrapped} door at the entrance.
e.zh: 我们在入口处发现一扇装有陷阱的门。

e.en: The thieves split the {boodle} three ways.
e.zh: 三个小偷把赃款分成了三份。

e.en: He hid his {boodle} under the floorboards.
e.zh: 他把钱藏在地板下面。

e.en: The newspaper exposed the senator as a {boodler}.
e.zh: 报纸揭露这位参议员是个贪贿之徒。

e.en: Voters had no patience for another {boodler}.
e.zh: 选民们再也无法容忍又一个受贿政客。

e.en: He shook his {boody} on the dance floor.
e.zh: 他在舞池里扭着屁股跳舞。

e.en: The pirates buried their {boody} on the island.
e.zh: 海盗们把赃物埋在了岛上。

e.en: Stop being such a {boofhead} and listen!
e.zh: 别再傻乎乎的了，好好听！

e.en: Some {boofhead} parked across the driveway.
e.zh: 有个傻瓜把车停在了车道前。

e.en: She's afraid of the {boogey} under the bed.
e.zh: 她害怕床底下的妖怪。

e.en: Parents shouldn't scare kids with the {boogey}.
e.zh: 父母不该用妖怪吓唬孩子。

e.en: Fairy tales are full of menacing {boogeymen}.
e.zh: 童话故事里满是吓人的妖怪。

e.en: Politicians often invent new {boogeymen} to fear.
e.zh: 政客常常制造新的假想敌来恐吓民众。

boogie-woogie.t: 布吉伍吉（一种爵士钢琴风格）

e.en: He played some {boogie-woogie} on the old piano.
e.zh: 他在老钢琴上弹了几段布吉伍吉。

e.en: The bar was famous for its {boogie-woogie} nights.
e.zh: 那家酒吧以布吉伍吉之夜闻名。

e.en: Don't worry, the {boogieman} isn't real.
e.zh: 别担心，妖怪不是真的。

e.en: He uses inflation as a political {boogieman}.
e.zh: 他把通货膨胀当成政治上的吓人话题。

e.en: She loves dancing to {boogiewoogie}.
e.zh: 她喜欢随着布吉伍吉的节奏起舞。

e.en: The pianist broke into a lively {boogiewoogie}.
e.zh: 钢琴师弹起了一段欢快的布吉伍吉。

e.en: Let's {boogy} all night long!
e.zh: 咱们整晚跳舞吧！

e.en: The crowd started to {boogy} when the band played.
e.zh: 乐队一演奏，人群就跟着跳起了舞。

e.en: He told stories about the {boogyman} at midnight.
e.zh: 他在半夜里讲妖怪的故事。

e.en: The {boogyman} of inflation haunts every government.
e.zh: 通胀这个怪物困扰着每一届政府。

e.en: She cried {boohoo} when her toy broke.
e.zh: 玩具坏了，她哇哇大哭。

e.en: Stop your {boohoo} and tell me what happened.
e.zh: 别哭了，告诉我发生了什么。

e.en: He {boohooed} all the way home.
e.zh: 他一路嚎啕大哭回家。

e.en: She {boohooed} into her pillow for hours.
e.zh: 她把脸埋进枕头里痛哭了好几个小时。

e.en: The toddler kept {boohooing} for an hour.
e.zh: 那幼儿哭嚎了整整一个小时。

e.en: Stop {boohooing} and clean up the mess.
e.zh: 别哭了，赶紧把乱摊子收拾干净。

e.en: Her quiet {boohoos} filled the empty room.
e.zh: 她低声的啜泣声充满了空荡的房间。

e.en: The toddler's loud {boohoos} woke the neighbors.
e.zh: 幼儿响亮的哭声把邻居吵醒了。

boojum.t: 布吉姆（虚构怪物）；卜君树

e.en: Lewis Carroll invented the dreaded {boojum}.
e.zh: 刘易斯·卡罗尔创造了可怕的布吉姆。

e.en: A tall {boojum} grew in the desert garden.
e.zh: 一棵高大的卜君树长在沙漠花园里。

e.en: The {book-binder} repaired the leather cover.
e.zh: 装订工修复了那本书的皮革封面。

e.en: She apprenticed with a master {book-binder}.
e.zh: 她跟着一位装订大师当学徒。

e.en: The novel had a striking red {book-jacket}.
e.zh: 这本小说有一个抢眼的红色护封。

e.en: He removed the {book-jacket} before reading.
e.zh: 他读书前把护封取了下来。

e.en: Our {book-keeper} balances the accounts every month.
e.zh: 我们的簿记员每月对一次账。

e.en: She works as a part-time {book-keeper}.
e.zh: 她兼职做簿记员。

e.en: Good {book-keeping} is essential for any business.
e.zh: 良好的记账对任何企业都至关重要。

e.en: He took a course in {book-keeping} last year.
e.zh: 他去年上了一门簿记课。

book-learned.t: 只会读书的；纸上谈兵的

e.en: He's {book-learned} but lacks practical skills.
e.zh: 他书读得多，却缺乏实践能力。

e.en: A {book-learned} doctor is no substitute for experience.
e.zh: 光会读书的医生比不上有经验的。

e.en: Any {book-lover} would adore this old library.
e.zh: 任何爱书人都会喜爱这座古老的图书馆。

e.en: She's a true {book-lover} with thousands of titles.
e.zh: 她是个真正的书迷，藏书数千册。

border-line.t: 边界线；临界的；模棱两可的

e.en: She is a {border-line} case for the scholarship.
e.zh: 她是奖学金评选中的临界候选人。

e.en: The inspector drew a faint {border-line} on the chart.
e.zh: 检查员在图上画了一条淡淡的边界线。

e.en: The reinsurer requested an updated {bordereau} for the quarter.
e.zh: 再保险公司要求提供本季度的最新分保明细单。

e.en: Each {bordereau} listed every policy ceded that month.
e.zh: 每份明细单都列出了当月分出的每一张保单。

bordereaux.t: 分保明细单（bordereau 的复数）

e.en: Clerks file dozens of {bordereaux} every month.
e.zh: 职员们每月归档数十份分保明细单。

e.en: Insurers exchange {bordereaux} to keep their accounts accurate.
e.zh: 保险公司互换明细单以保持账目准确。

bordure.t: 盾边（纹章学中的盾牌边饰）

e.en: The shield bore a red {bordure} as a mark of cadency.
e.zh: 盾牌饰有红色盾边以表示分支身份。

e.en: Heralds described the {bordure} as ermine on azure.
e.zh: 纹章官将那道盾边描述为蓝底白貂纹。

e.en: Engineers measured the depth of the {bore-hole} carefully.
e.zh: 工程师仔细测量了钻孔的深度。

e.en: Muddy water seeped from the abandoned {bore-hole}.
e.zh: 浑浊的水从废弃的井眼里渗了出来。

e.en: Grandmother grew {borecole} in her winter garden.
e.zh: 奶奶在冬天的菜园里种羽衣甘蓝。

e.en: He served braised {borecole} alongside the roast.
e.zh: 他用炖煮的羽衣甘蓝来配烤肉。

boree.t: 澳洲相思树；金合欢的一种

e.en: Sheep sheltered beneath the {boree} during the heat.
e.zh: 炎热时羊群在相思树下躲阴。

e.en: Stockmen split the {boree} into fence posts.
e.zh: 牧民把金合欢木劈成围栏的柱子。

e.en: We walked down a quiet {boreen} to the cottage.
e.zh: 我们沿着一条安静的乡间小径走到小屋。

e.en: The {boreen} was lined with thick hawthorn hedges.
e.zh: 那条小径两旁是茂密的山楂树篱。

e.en: The mechanic used a {borescope} to inspect the cylinder.
e.zh: 技工用孔探仪检查了汽缸。

e.en: A flexible {borescope} can reach hidden cavities inside the engine.
e.zh: 软式内窥镜能伸进发动机内部的隐蔽空腔。

e.en: The gunner checked the {boresight} before firing.
e.zh: 炮手在开火前检查了瞄准基准。

e.en: Engineers aligned the antenna {boresight} with the satellite.
e.zh: 工程师将天线瞄轴对准了那颗卫星。

e.en: The technician was {boresighting} the rifle scope all morning.
e.zh: 技师整个上午都在校准步枪瞄准镜的瞄轴。

e.en: Careful {boresighting} saves a lot of ammunition at the range.
e.zh: 细心的瞄轴校准能在靶场上省下大量弹药。

e.en: The lecture was {boresome} from start to finish.
e.zh: 那场讲座从头到尾都令人厌烦。

e.en: I find office small talk rather {boresome}.
e.zh: 我觉得办公室里的闲聊相当无聊。

borewell.t: 机井；钻井（多见于印度英语）

e.en: Villagers depend on the {borewell} for drinking water.
e.zh: 村民们依靠这口机井取得饮用水。

e.en: The drought lowered the {borewell} water table sharply.
e.zh: 干旱使机井的地下水位急剧下降。

e.en: Titanium {boride} is prized for its extreme hardness.
e.zh: 二硼化钛因其极高的硬度而备受重视。

e.en: The coating is a thin layer of metal {boride}.
e.zh: 那层涂层是一薄层金属硼化物。

e.en: Several {borides} are used as cutting-tool inserts.
e.zh: 多种硼化物被用作切削刀具的镶片。

e.en: Researchers studied the magnetic properties of rare-earth {borides}.
e.zh: 研究人员研究了稀土硼化物的磁性。

bork.t: 阻挠（提名人选）；以舆论手段否决

e.en: Senators threatened to {bork} the next Supreme Court nominee.
e.zh: 参议员们威胁要阻挠下一位最高法院被提名人的任命。

e.en: The campaign {borked} her chances of confirmation.
e.zh: 那场运动使她的获任希望落空。

born-again.t: 重生的；皈依的；重新热衷的

e.en: She became a {born-again} Christian after college.
e.zh: 她大学毕业后成为重生的基督徒。

e.en: He spoke with the zeal of a {born-again} environmentalist.
e.zh: 他以皈依者般的热忱谈论环保。

bornagain.t: 重生的；皈依的（born-again 的连写形式）

e.en: He calls himself a {bornagain} runner since his surgery.
e.zh: 自从手术之后,他自称是个重生的跑者。

e.en: The {bornagain} fan watched every single game that season.
e.zh: 这位重新狂热起来的球迷那个赛季每场比赛都看。

e.en: Traditional medicine often uses {borneol} for its cooling effect.
e.zh: 传统医学常用冰片来清凉解热。

e.en: Pure {borneol} crystallizes into white flakes.
e.zh: 纯净的龙脑会结晶成白色薄片。

e.en: Miners extracted copper from veins of {bornite}.
e.zh: 矿工从斑铜矿矿脉中提取铜。

e.en: Polished {bornite} shows iridescent peacock colors.
e.zh: 抛光后的斑铜矿呈现孔雀般的彩虹光泽。

e.en: The plating bath contained sodium {borofluoride}.
e.zh: 电镀液中含有氟硼酸钠。

e.en: Chemists prepared a fresh copper {borofluoride} solution.
e.zh: 化学家配制了新鲜的氟硼酸铜溶液。

e.en: Sodium {borohydride} is a common reducing agent in organic synthesis.
e.zh: 硼氢化钠是有机合成中常用的还原剂。

e.en: The lab kept the {borohydride} in a tightly sealed container.
e.zh: 实验室把硼氢化物保存在密封严实的容器中。

e.en: Suzuki coupling requires a {boronic} acid partner.
e.zh: 铃木偶联反应需要一个硼酸搭档。

e.en: Researchers synthesized a new {boronic} ester for drug screening.
e.zh: 研究人员合成了一种新的硼酸酯用于药物筛选。

boroscope.t: 内窥镜；孔探仪（borescope 的异拼）

e.en: The inspector slid a {boroscope} into the engine housing.
e.zh: 检验员把内窥镜伸入发动机壳体中。

e.en: A medical {boroscope} can reveal tiny lesions in the airway.
e.zh: 医用内窥镜能发现气道内的微小病变。

bowdlerism.t: 删改文学作品中粗俗内容的做法

e.en: Critics accused the editor of {bowdlerism} for cutting all the bawdy passages.
e.zh: 批评者指责编辑删改原作中所有粗俗段落的做法。

e.en: Modern reprints often suffer from a kind of polite {bowdlerism}.
e.zh: 现代重印本常带有一种礼貌式的洁本删改。

e.en: The {bowdlerization} of Shakespeare for school editions has long been controversial.
e.zh: 为学校版本对莎士比亚作品进行洁本删改一直饱受争议。

e.en: She objected to the {bowdlerization} of the original folk tale.
e.zh: 她反对对这则原始民间故事进行删改净化。

bowdrill.t: 弓钻；用弓钻取火的工具

e.en: He learned to make fire with a {bowdrill} on his survival course.
e.zh: 他在野外求生课上学会用弓钻取火。

e.en: The archaeologist demonstrated an ancient {bowdrill} technique.
e.zh: 那位考古学家演示了一种古老的弓钻技术。

e.en: The villain was portrayed as a {bowelless} tyrant without pity.
e.zh: 那个反派被刻画成毫无怜悯之心的冷酷暴君。

e.en: Critics called the policy {bowelless} and cruel.
e.zh: 批评者称这项政策冷酷无情。

bower-bird.t: 园丁鸟（雄鸟会筑装饰巢吸引雌鸟）

e.en: The male {bower-bird} decorates his nest with bright objects to attract a mate.
e.zh: 雄性园丁鸟用鲜艳物品装饰巢穴以吸引配偶。

e.en: We watched a {bower-bird} arrange blue bottle caps in a neat pile.
e.zh: 我们看着一只园丁鸟把蓝色瓶盖整齐地堆成一摞。

boweries.t: 乡间庄园；树荫凉亭（复数）

e.en: The Dutch settlers built {boweries} along the river.
e.zh: 荷兰移民沿河建起了一座座农庄。

e.en: Old maps still show the original {boweries} on Manhattan.
e.zh: 旧地图上仍可见曼哈顿最初的几处荷兰式农庄。

e.en: They rested in a {bowery} corner of the garden.
e.zh: 他们在花园里绿树成荫的一角歇息。

e.en: The path led into a cool, {bowery} grove.
e.zh: 小径通向一片清凉、绿荫蔽日的小树林。

e.en: The angler caught a large {bowfin} in the swamp.
e.zh: 垂钓者在沼泽里钓到一条大弓鳍鱼。

e.en: The {bowfin} is considered a living fossil.
e.zh: 弓鳍鱼被视为活化石。

bowfront.t: 弧形前面的（家具或建筑）

e.en: She inherited a beautiful {bowfront} dresser from her grandmother.
e.zh: 她从祖母那里继承了一只漂亮的弧形前面五斗柜。

e.en: The townhouse has an elegant {bowfront} facade.
e.zh: 这栋联排别墅有着典雅的弧形外立面。

e.en: The crew rigged a {bowgrace} to protect the hull from drifting ice.
e.zh: 船员们装上船首护舷以保护船身不被浮冰撞坏。

e.en: Old whaling ships often carried a heavy {bowgrace}.
e.zh: 旧时的捕鲸船常装有厚重的船首护舷。

e.en: A {bowhead} whale can live for over two hundred years.
e.zh: 一头弓头鲸可以活两百多年。

e.en: Researchers tracked the migrating {bowhead} across the Arctic.
e.zh: 研究人员追踪迁徙中的弓头鲸穿越北极。

e.en: He likes to {bowhunt} deer in the autumn.
e.zh: 他喜欢在秋天用弓箭猎鹿。

e.en: You need a special permit to {bowhunt} on public land.
e.zh: 在公共土地上用弓箭狩猎需要特别许可证。

e.en: She tied the ribbon into a neat {bowknot}.
e.zh: 她把丝带打成一个整齐的蝴蝶结。

e.en: The package was finished with a red {bowknot}.
e.zh: 包裹上系着一个红色蝴蝶结作为收尾。

e.en: A huge {bowlder} blocked the trail after the landslide.
e.zh: 山体滑坡后一块巨石挡住了山路。

e.en: The geologist examined the glacial {bowlder}.
e.zh: 地质学家仔细查看那块冰川漂砾。

e.en: The old cowboy walked with a noticeable {bowleg}.
e.zh: 那位老牛仔走起路来明显是罗圈腿。

e.en: Vitamin D deficiency in childhood can cause {bowleg}.
e.zh: 儿童期缺乏维生素D会导致罗圈腿。

e.en: The {bowless} archer could no longer practice his craft.
e.zh: 失去弓的弓箭手再也无法练习技艺。

e.en: After the collision the boat was nearly {bowless}.
e.zh: 碰撞之后那条船几乎没了船首。

e.en: We met at the {bowling-alley} every Friday night.
e.zh: 我们每周五晚上都在保龄球馆碰头。

e.en: The new {bowling-alley} has twenty lanes.
e.zh: 这家新开的保龄球馆有二十条球道。

e.en: A bright {bowpot} stood on the parlor mantel.
e.zh: 客厅壁炉台上摆着一盆鲜艳的插花。

e.en: She arranged a fragrant {bowpot} for the guests.
e.zh: 她为客人摆好一束芬芳的插花。

e.en: The sailors began to {bowse} down the lashings.
e.zh: 水手们开始用绳索把绑带拉紧。

e.en: "{Bowse} away!" the bosun shouted to the crew.
e.zh: "用力拉！"水手长向船员喊道。

e.en: The probe detected a {bowshock} where the solar wind meets the planet's magnetosphere.
e.zh: 探测器在太阳风与行星磁层相遇处探测到弓形激波。

e.en: Astronomers study the {bowshock} produced by fast-moving stars.
e.zh: 天文学家研究高速运动恒星产生的弓形激波。

e.en: The enemy camp lay within a {bowshot} of the walls.
e.zh: 敌营离城墙不过一箭之遥。

e.en: He came within a {bowshot} before being seen.
e.zh: 他靠近到一箭之遥才被发现。

e.en: The {bowsman} kept lookout for rocks ahead.
e.zh: 船首水手警戒着前方的暗礁。

e.en: Our {bowsman} called the stroke for the rest of the crew.
e.zh: 我们的前桨手为其他船员喊出划桨节奏。

bowstrung.t: 用弓弦绞死；装上弓弦（bowstring过去式）

e.en: In the old tale the traitor was {bowstrung} by the sultan's guards.
e.zh: 在古老的故事里，叛徒被苏丹的卫兵用弓弦勒死。

e.en: He {bowstrung} the longbow with practiced ease.
e.zh: 他熟练自如地给长弓装上弓弦。

e.en: He wore a black {bowtie} to the gala.
e.zh: 他戴着一个黑色领结去参加晚会。

e.en: She straightened his crooked {bowtie} before the photo.
e.zh: 拍照前她帮他扶正了歪掉的领结。

e.en: The toddler pointed at the dog and said "{bowwow}!"
e.zh: 那个学步的孩子指着狗叫道"汪汪！"

e.en: He grew up calling every dog a {bowwow}.
e.zh: 他从小就把每只狗都叫做"汪汪"。

e.en: The kids were excited to see all the {bowwows} at the shelter.
e.zh: 孩子们兴奋地看着收容所里所有的小狗狗。

e.en: After the bankruptcy his career went to the {bowwows}.
e.zh: 破产后他的事业彻底完蛋了。

e.en: The old man walked on tired, {bowy} legs.
e.zh: 老人迈着疲惫弯曲的双腿走着。

e.en: She admired the {bowy} curve of the bridge.
e.zh: 她欣赏着那座桥优美的弓形曲线。

e.en: The shearer tied a {bowyang} below each knee to keep his trousers up.
e.zh: 剪羊毛工在每个膝盖下方系上裤腿绑带以免裤子滑落。

e.en: Old bushmen often wore a {bowyang} while working.
e.zh: 老一辈丛林人干活时常系着裤腿绑带。

e.en: The film was a huge {box-office} success.
e.zh: 这部电影取得了巨大的票房成功。

e.en: You can pick up the tickets at the {box-office}.
e.zh: 你可以在售票处取票。

e.en: They turned the tiny {box-room} into a nursery.
e.zh: 他们把那间小储藏室改成了婴儿房。

e.en: Old suitcases were stacked in the {box-room}.
e.zh: 旧手提箱堆放在小储藏室里。

e.en: The chess pieces were carved from polished {box-wood}.
e.zh: 这些象棋棋子是用抛光的黄杨木雕成的。

e.en: A neatly trimmed {box-wood} hedge surrounded the garden.
e.zh: 花园四周围着修剪整齐的黄杨木绿篱。

e.en: Children gathered {boxberry} along the woodland path.
e.zh: 孩子们沿着林间小径采摘白珠树果。

e.en: The leaves of the {boxberry} have a fresh, minty smell.
e.zh: 白珠树的叶子有一股清新的薄荷香气。

e.en: Cereal packs are usually made of recycled {boxboard}.
e.zh: 麦片包装盒通常用再生纸板制成。

e.en: The factory presses pulp into stiff {boxboard}.
e.zh: 工厂把纸浆压制成坚硬的箱板纸。

e.en: A spotted {boxfish} drifted past the coral.
e.zh: 一条带斑点的箱鲀从珊瑚旁漂过。

e.en: The {boxfish} has a hard, bony armor for protection.
e.zh: 箱鲀有一层坚硬的骨质外壳作保护。

e.en: The captain ordered the crew to {boxhaul} the ship clear of the reef.
e.zh: 船长命令船员急转掉头以避开礁石。

e.en: In tight waters they had no choice but to {boxhaul}.
e.zh: 在狭窄水域里他们只能急转掉头。

e.en: They {boxhauled} the brig just before she struck the rocks.
e.zh: 他们在双桅船撞礁前一刻急转掉头。

e.en: The frigate {boxhauled} smartly to escape the shoal.
e.zh: 那艘护卫舰利落地急转掉头逃离浅滩。

e.en: {Boxhauling} requires real skill in heavy seas.
e.zh: 在风浪大的海上急转掉头需要真本事。

e.en: The manual devotes a chapter to {boxhauling} a square-rigger.
e.zh: 这本手册用一整章讲解横帆船的急转掉头技术。

boxiness.t: 方方正正的样子；笨重感

e.en: The car's {boxiness} gives it a surprisingly roomy interior.
e.zh: 这辆车方正的造型让车内空间出奇地宽敞。

e.en: Designers softened the building's {boxiness} with curved windows.
e.zh: 设计师用弧形窗户柔化了这座建筑的方正感。

boxing-day.t: 节礼日（圣诞节后第一天）

e.en: Most British shops hold huge sales on {boxing-day}.
e.zh: 大多数英国商店在节礼日举行大减价。

e.en: We always visit my grandparents on {boxing-day}.
e.zh: 我们每年节礼日都去看望祖父母。

e.en: They watched the {boxing-match} on television.
e.zh: 他们在电视上观看那场拳击比赛。

e.en: The {boxing-match} ended in a knockout in the third round.
e.zh: 那场拳击比赛在第三回合以击倒告终。

e.en: The {boxkeeper} showed us to our seats at the opera.
e.zh: 包厢服务员把我们领到歌剧院的座位上。

e.en: A polite {boxkeeper} took our coats at the door.
e.zh: 一位有礼貌的包厢服务员在门口接过我们的外套。

boxman.t: 赌场监筹员；保险柜窃贼（俚）

e.en: The {boxman} watched every chip on the craps table.
e.zh: 赌场监筹员盯着掷骰子桌上的每一枚筹码。

e.en: Police arrested a notorious {boxman} after the bank job.
e.zh: 警方在那起银行案后逮捕了一名臭名昭著的撬保险柜惯犯。

e.en: The analyst drew a {boxplot} to compare the two distributions.
e.zh: 分析师画了一张箱形图来对比两个分布。

e.en: Outliers are easy to spot on a {boxplot}.
e.zh: 异常值在箱形图上很容易看出。

e.en: We stored old toys in the {boxroom} upstairs.
e.zh: 我们把旧玩具堆在楼上的小储藏室里。

e.en: The flat has two bedrooms and a tiny {boxroom}.
e.zh: 这套公寓有两间卧室和一间很小的杂物间。

e.en: Both {boxrooms} were already crammed with luggage.
e.zh: 两间小储藏室都已经塞满了行李。

e.en: Older houses often have several useful {boxrooms}.
e.zh: 老房子里常常有几间实用的小储藏室。

e.en: A thorny {boxthorn} hedge separated the two fields.
e.zh: 一道带刺的枸杞树篱把两块田地隔开。

e.en: Birds love the bright red berries of the {boxthorn}.
e.zh: 鸟儿很爱吃枸杞鲜红的浆果。

e.en: A neatly clipped {boxtree} stood beside the doorway.
e.zh: 门旁立着一棵修剪整齐的黄杨树。

e.en: The garden is famous for its ancient {boxtree} hedges.
e.zh: 这座花园以古老的黄杨树篱闻名。

boundry.t: 边界；界限（boundary 的拼写错误）

e.en: They argued over the property {boundary}.
e.zh: 他们为地界争执不下。

e.en: This idea pushes the {boundary} of physics.
e.zh: 这一想法突破了物理学的边界。

bouns.t: 奖金；红利（bonus 的拼写错误）

e.en: She got a year-end {bonus}.
e.zh: 她拿到了年终奖金。

e.en: Free shipping is a nice {bonus}.
e.zh: 免运费是个不错的额外好处。

e.en: The {bountied} outlaw fled to the hills.
e.zh: 那个被悬赏通缉的罪犯逃进了山里。

e.en: Every {bountied} wolf pelt fetched ten dollars.
e.zh: 每张悬赏的狼皮值十美元。

e.en: Old {Bourbonists} still toasted the exiled king.
e.zh: 老波旁派至今仍为流亡国王举杯。

e.en: He was branded a stubborn {Bourbonist}.
e.zh: 他被斥为顽固的波旁派分子。

e.en: He spoke in earnest, not in {bourd}.
e.zh: 他说得认真，并非戏言。

e.en: The minstrel mixed song with cheerful {bourd}.
e.zh: 游吟诗人把歌曲与欢快的戏言混在一起。

bourder.t: 开玩笑的人；戏谑者（古旧用法）

e.en: The court {bourder} kept the king laughing.
e.zh: 宫中的戏谑者总让国王发笑。

e.en: Don't trust a {bourder} with serious news.
e.zh: 别把正事托付给一个爱开玩笑的人。

e.en: The organ's {bourdon} rumbled through the nave.
e.zh: 管风琴的低音管在中殿轰然回响。

e.en: A bagpipe {bourdon} held the steady drone.
e.zh: 风笛的持续低音稳稳地嗡鸣着。

e.en: Critics decried the {bourgeoisification} of the movement.
e.zh: 批评者谴责该运动的资产阶级化。

e.en: Suburban life signaled the family's {bourgeoisification}.
e.zh: 郊区生活标志着这家人的资产阶级化。

e.en: Mass media tends to {bourgeoisify} radical art.
e.zh: 大众媒体往往会把激进艺术资产阶级化。

e.en: He refused to let success {bourgeoisify} him.
e.zh: 他不愿因成功而变得资产阶级化。

bourguignon.t: 勃艮第风味的（红酒炖煮的菜肴）

e.en: She ordered the beef {bourguignon}.
e.zh: 她点了勃艮第红酒炖牛肉。

e.en: His {bourguignon} sauce simmered for hours.
e.zh: 他的勃艮第酱汁慢炖了好几个小时。

bournless.t: 无边的；无尽的（古旧用法）

e.en: They sailed across the {bournless} ocean.
e.zh: 他们航行在无边的大海上。

e.en: Her ambition seemed {bournless}.
e.zh: 她的雄心似乎没有止境。

e.en: An old {bourtree} grew by the cottage door.
e.zh: 小屋门旁长着一棵老接骨木。

e.en: Children gathered berries from the {bourtree}.
e.zh: 孩子们从接骨木上采集果实。

e.en: Sailors {bouse} the line taut.
e.zh: 水手用滑车把绳索拉紧。

e.en: They had to {bouse} the cannon into place.
e.zh: 他们得用滑车把火炮拉到位。

boused.t: 用滑车拉紧（bouse 的过去式）

e.en: The crew {boused} the heavy cargo upward.
e.zh: 船员把沉重的货物用滑车拉了上去。

e.en: They {boused} the rigging tight before sunset.
e.zh: 他们在日落前把索具拉紧。

bouses.t: 用滑车拉紧（bouse 的第三人称单数）

e.en: The bosun always {bouses} the line first.
e.zh: 水手长总是先把绳索用滑车拉紧。

e.en: He {bouses} the tackle until it groans.
e.zh: 他把滑车拉紧到吱吱作响。

bousing.t: 用滑车拉紧（动名词/现在分词）

e.en: They were {bousing} the boat onto the davits.
e.zh: 他们正用滑车把小艇拉到吊艇柱上。

e.en: {Bousing} the cable required four men.
e.zh: 拉紧那根缆绳需要四个人。

boustrophedon.t: 牛耕式转行书写（左右行交替）

e.en: Early Greek inscriptions used {boustrophedon}.
e.zh: 早期希腊铭文采用牛耕式书写。

e.en: The tablet's text runs in {boustrophedon}.
e.zh: 这块石板上的文字以左右交替的方式书写。

bousy.t: 醉醺醺的（古旧用法，同 boozy）

e.en: A {bousy} sailor stumbled out of the tavern.
e.zh: 一个醉醺醺的水手跌跌撞撞走出酒馆。

e.en: His {bousy} laugh filled the room.
e.zh: 他醉醺醺的笑声充满了整个房间。

bouzouki.t: 布祖基琴（希腊弹拨乐器）

e.en: He plucked a melody on the {bouzouki}.
e.zh: 他用布祖基琴弹了一段旋律。

e.en: The taverna echoed with {bouzouki} music.
e.zh: 小酒馆里回荡着布祖基琴的乐声。

bouzoukia.t: 布祖基琴（复数）；希腊夜店

e.en: They danced all night at the {bouzoukia}.
e.zh: 他们在希腊夜店跳了一整夜舞。

e.en: Two {bouzoukia} hung on the wall.
e.zh: 墙上挂着两把布祖基琴。

bovarism.t: 包法利主义；自我浪漫化的幻想

e.en: Her {bovarism} drove her into endless debt.
e.zh: 她的包法利式幻想让她债台高筑。

e.en: Critics noted a streak of {bovarism} in him.
e.zh: 评论家注意到他身上有几分包法利式的自欺。

bovate.t: 牛犁地（古英格兰土地面积单位）

e.en: He held a {bovate} of land from the lord.
e.zh: 他从领主手中租得一份牛犁地。

e.en: The deed records two {bovates} in the village.
e.zh: 地契记载了村里的两份牛犁地。

bove.t: 在……上方（古旧用法，同 above）

e.en: Stars shone {bove} the silent moor.
e.zh: 群星在寂静的荒野上空闪烁。

e.en: A banner waved {bove} the gate.
e.zh: 一面旗帜在城门上方飘扬。

e.en: Cattle and antelope are {bovids}.
e.zh: 牛和羚羊都属于牛科动物。

e.en: The reserve protects several rare {bovids}.
e.zh: 保护区保护着几种珍稀牛科动物。

e.en: There was a placid {bovinity} in his stare.
e.zh: 他的目光中带着一种牛一般的迟钝。

e.en: The herd's {bovinity} fascinated the children.
e.zh: 牛群的憨厚模样让孩子们看得入神。

e.en: A {bow-backed} old man tended the garden.
e.zh: 一位驼背的老人在打理花园。

e.en: The {bow-backed} mare still pulled the cart.
e.zh: 那匹弓背的母马仍在拉车。

e.en: The {bow-legged} cowboy ambled to the bar.
e.zh: 那个罗圈腿的牛仔晃悠悠地走向吧台。

e.en: Years of riding left him {bow-legged}.
e.zh: 多年骑马让他成了 O 型腿。

bow-wave.t: 船首波；前进时推开的浪

e.en: Dolphins surfed the ship's {bow-wave}.
e.zh: 海豚在船首波上嬉戏。

e.en: A frothy {bow-wave} curled away from the hull.
e.zh: 船体两侧翻起白沫的船首波。

e.en: The puppy let out a tiny {bow-wow}.
e.zh: 小狗发出一声细细的汪汪声。

e.en: Look at the {bow-wow}, sweetie!
e.zh: 宝贝，快看那只小狗狗！

bowdlerise.t: 删改（书籍、影片中的不当内容）

e.en: Editors {bowdlerised} the novel for schools.
e.zh: 编辑为学校删改了这部小说。

e.en: He refused to let anyone {bowdlerise} his lyrics.
e.zh: 他不许任何人删改他的歌词。

e.en: His {brachydactylous} traits were inherited.
e.zh: 他短指的特征是遗传来的。

e.en: The puppy was noticeably {brachydactylous}.
e.zh: 那只小狗的脚趾明显短小。

e.en: She was diagnosed with {brachydactyly}.
e.zh: 她被诊断为短指畸形。

e.en: {Brachydactyly} can be detected at birth.
e.zh: 短指畸形可以在出生时发现。

e.en: He studied {brachygraphy} to take notes faster.
e.zh: 他学速记法以便更快做笔记。

e.en: Old manuscripts often used {brachygraphy}.
e.zh: 古抄本常使用简写法。

e.en: The poem's {brachylogy} made it powerful.
e.zh: 这首诗的简洁使它充满力量。

e.en: His writing favors {brachylogy} over flourish.
e.zh: 他的写作偏爱简练而非华丽。

e.en: {Brachymeiosis} occurs in some fungi.
e.zh: 短减数分裂出现在某些真菌中。

e.en: Researchers studied {brachymeiosis} in yeast.
e.zh: 研究人员研究酵母中的短减数分裂。

e.en: Humans have {brachyodont} teeth.
e.zh: 人类拥有短冠齿。

e.en: Carnivores typically possess {brachyodont} molars.
e.zh: 食肉动物通常长着短冠的臼齿。

e.en: The beetle is {brachypterous} and cannot fly.
e.zh: 这种甲虫翅膀短小，不能飞行。

e.en: Some {brachypterous} insects live underground.
e.zh: 一些短翅昆虫生活在地下。

e.en: {Brachystomatous} flies have short mouthparts.
e.zh: 短口蝇类的口器很短。

e.en: He classified the specimen as {brachystomatous}.
e.zh: 他把这只标本归类为短口类。

e.en: The species shows a {brachytelic} pattern.
e.zh: 该物种呈现缓慢进化的模式。

e.en: {Brachytelic} lineages persist over long periods.
e.zh: 缓慢进化的谱系能延续很久。

e.en: She underwent {brachytherapy} for cancer.
e.zh: 她接受了近距离放射治疗。

e.en: {Brachytherapy} delivers radiation inside the body.
e.zh: 近距离放疗在体内施放辐射。

e.en: Crabs are typical {brachyuran} crustaceans.
e.zh: 螃蟹是典型的短尾甲壳类动物。

e.en: The lab studies {brachyuran} behavior.
e.zh: 实验室研究短尾蟹的行为。

e.en: {Brachyurous} crustaceans include true crabs.
e.zh: 短尾的甲壳动物包括真螃蟹。

e.en: The species is {brachyurous} and burrows in sand.
e.zh: 该物种短尾，会在沙中挖洞。

e.en: Grandma made {braciola} for Sunday dinner.
e.zh: 奶奶为周日晚餐做了意式肉卷。

e.en: The {braciola} simmered in tomato sauce.
e.zh: 意式肉卷在番茄酱里慢炖。

e.en: He ordered {braciole} at the trattoria.
e.zh: 他在小餐馆点了意式肉卷。

e.en: The {braciole} was tender and flavorful.
e.zh: 这道意式肉卷鲜嫩入味。

brack.t: 瑕疵；爱尔兰葡萄干面包

e.en: She sliced the warm {brack} for tea.
e.zh: 她切开温热的葡萄干面包配茶。

e.en: The fabric had a small {brack}.
e.zh: 这块布有一处小瑕疵。

e.en: The plant has prominent {bracteal} leaves.
e.zh: 这种植物有明显的苞片叶。

e.en: Botanists noted the {bracteal} structure.
e.zh: 植物学家注意到苞片结构。

e.en: The flower is clearly {bracteate}.
e.zh: 这朵花明显带有苞片。

e.en: Vikings minted {bracteate} coins.
e.zh: 维京人铸造过薄片金币。

e.en: The species is {bracteolate} at each node.
e.zh: 该物种在每个节上都有小苞片。

e.en: Botanists labeled the stems {bracteolate}.
e.zh: 植物学家把茎标为有小苞片。

e.en: Each flower has a tiny {bracteole}.
e.zh: 每朵花都有一片小苞片。

e.en: The {bracteole} protects the bud.
e.zh: 小苞片保护着花蕾。

e.en: A delicate {bractlet} hugged the bud.
e.zh: 一片细小的小苞片紧贴着花蕾。

e.en: The {bractlet} is barely visible.
e.zh: 小苞片几乎看不见。

e.en: He pierced the wood with a {bradawl}.
e.zh: 他用木工锥在木头上钻孔。

e.en: A {bradawl} starts a screw hole cleanly.
e.zh: 用锥子开螺丝孔很干净。

e.en: The {bradenhead} sealed the well casing.
e.zh: 井口套管头封住了井管。

e.en: Workers inspected the {bradenhead} for leaks.
e.zh: 工人检查井口套管头是否漏气。

e.en: She fitted the horse with a {bradoon}.
e.zh: 她给马戴上了轻型嚼子。

e.en: A {bradoon} sits beside the curb bit.
e.zh: 轻型嚼子位于杠杆嚼子旁边。

e.en: He was treated for {bradyarrhythmia}.
e.zh: 他因缓慢性心律失常接受治疗。

e.en: {Bradyarrhythmia} can require a pacemaker.
e.zh: 缓慢性心律失常可能需要起搏器。

e.en: Several {bradyarrhythmias} were detected.
e.zh: 检测到了多种缓慢性心律失常。

e.en: Elderly patients often develop {bradyarrhythmias}.
e.zh: 老年患者常出现缓慢性心律失常。

e.en: The organ shows {bradyauxesis} relative to body size.
e.zh: 该器官相对体型呈慢生长。

e.en: {Bradyauxesis} affects limb proportions.
e.zh: 慢生长会影响四肢比例。

e.en: {Bradykinin} causes blood vessels to dilate.
e.zh: 缓激肽会使血管扩张。

e.en: Allergic reactions can release {bradykinin}.
e.zh: 过敏反应可释放缓激肽。

e.en: Patients with {bradypepsia} feel bloated.
e.zh: 消化迟缓的患者感到腹胀。

e.en: {Bradypepsia} can result from low stomach acid.
e.zh: 消化迟缓可能因胃酸不足引起。

e.en: The monitor flagged signs of {bradypnoea}.
e.zh: 监护仪显示出呼吸过缓的迹象。

e.en: {Bradypnoea} can indicate opioid overdose.
e.zh: 呼吸过缓可能提示阿片类药物过量。

e.en: {Bradyseism} slowly raised the coastal town.
e.zh: 地壳缓动慢慢抬升了沿海小镇。

e.en: Scientists monitor {bradyseism} near volcanoes.
e.zh: 科学家监测火山附近的地壳缓动。

e.en: Crocodiles are a {bradytelic} lineage.
e.zh: 鳄鱼属于演化缓慢的谱系。

e.en: {Bradytelic} groups change little over time.
e.zh: 演化缓慢的类群随时间变化甚微。

e.en: She packed a {braeburn} for lunch.
e.zh: 她带了一个布雷本苹果当午餐。

e.en: {Braeburn} apples are crisp and tart.
e.zh: 布雷本苹果脆爽带酸。

e.en: The geologist identified the sample as {braggite}.
e.zh: 地质学家确认样本是硫钯铂矿。

e.en: {Braggite} contains platinum and palladium.
e.zh: 硫钯铂矿含铂和钯。

e.en: His {braggy} tone annoyed everyone.
e.zh: 他爱吹嘘的口气惹恼了大家。

e.en: She tried not to sound {braggy}.
e.zh: 她尽量不显得在吹牛。

e.en: He shared the news in a {bragless} way.
e.zh: 他不张扬地分享了这个消息。

e.en: Her {bragless} success impressed the team.
e.zh: 她不事张扬的成功打动了团队。

e.en: Hindus revere {Brahma} as the creator.
e.zh: 印度教徒尊梵天为创世神。

e.en: A statue of {Brahma} stood in the temple.
e.zh: 庙里立着一尊梵天像。

e.en: He took a vow of {brahmacharya}.
e.zh: 他立下了禁欲修行的誓言。

e.en: {Brahmacharya} is one of the yamas in yoga.
e.zh: 梵行是瑜伽戒律之一。

book-maker.t: 赌注经纪人；接受赌注的庄家

e.en: The local {book-maker} took bets on every horse race.
e.zh: 当地的赌注经纪人为每场赛马接受下注。

e.en: The {book-maker} adjusted the odds before kickoff.
e.zh: 庄家在开赛前调整了赔率。

book-match.t: 对花拼接；木皮或石材的对称拼花

e.en: The cabinetmaker decided to {book-match} the walnut veneer.
e.zh: 家具师傅决定将胡桃木皮做对花拼接。

e.en: The marble slabs {book-match} perfectly across the wall.
e.zh: 大理石板在整面墙上严丝合缝地对花拼接。

book-phrase.t: 书面用语；带书卷气的措辞

e.en: He used a stiff {book-phrase} no one would say aloud.
e.zh: 他用了一句没人会大声说出口的书面用语。

e.en: Her speech was full of formal {book-phrases}.
e.zh: 她的演讲满是带书卷气的措辞。

e.en: The {book-seller} kept rare editions in a glass case.
e.zh: 这位书商把珍本放在玻璃柜里。

e.en: She works as a {book-seller} on weekends.
e.zh: 她周末在书店当售书员。

book-stall.t: 书摊；书亭；流动卖书摊位

e.en: We stopped at a {book-stall} near the station.
e.zh: 我们在车站附近的书摊停了一下。

e.en: The {book-stall} sold yellowed paperbacks for a dollar.
e.zh: 那个书摊以一美元一本卖泛黄的旧平装书。

book-stand.t: 阅读架；放书的小型支架

e.en: She propped the cookbook on a wooden {book-stand}.
e.zh: 她把食谱架在一个木制阅读架上。

e.en: A small {book-stand} sat by the entrance.
e.zh: 入口处放着一个小型的放书支架。

book-token.t: 图书礼券；英国常见的购书代金券

e.en: His aunt gave him a ten-pound {book-token} for Christmas.
e.zh: 圣诞节时姑妈送了他一张十英镑的图书礼券。

e.en: I redeemed the {book-token} at the campus bookshop.
e.zh: 我在校园书店兑换了那张购书代金券。

e.en: She is a complete {bookaholic} who can't pass a bookshop.
e.zh: 她是个不折不扣的书痴，路过书店从来不空手。

e.en: Most {bookaholics} have stacks of unread novels at home.
e.zh: 大多数嗜书如命的人家里都堆着没读完的小说。

e.en: The old {bookbindery} still uses hand-stitched spines.
e.zh: 这家老装订作坊仍采用手工缝订书脊。

e.en: He apprenticed at a small {bookbindery} in Paris.
e.zh: 他曾在巴黎一家小型图书装订厂学徒。

bookclub.t: 读书俱乐部；定期共读的书友会

e.en: Our {bookclub} meets the first Sunday of each month.
e.zh: 我们的读书俱乐部每月第一个星期天聚会。

e.en: Joining a {bookclub} pushed her to read more widely.
e.zh: 加入书友会促使她阅读更广。

bookcraft.t: 制书工艺；书籍制作技艺

e.en: He has dedicated his life to traditional {bookcraft}.
e.zh: 他把毕生献给了传统的制书工艺。

e.en: The museum exhibits early examples of {bookcraft}.
e.zh: 博物馆展示了早期的书籍制作技艺。

bookcrossing.t: 图书漂流；放书旅行活动

e.en: She left her novel on a park bench as part of {bookcrossing}.
e.zh: 她把小说留在公园长椅上参加图书漂流活动。

e.en: {Bookcrossing} lets strangers share books around the world.
e.zh: 图书漂流让世界各地的陌生人共享书籍。

booket.t: 小册子；袖珍读本（罕用古旧词）

e.en: She tucked a slim {booket} of poems into her bag.
e.zh: 她把一本薄薄的小诗册塞进包里。

e.en: The shop sold tiny {bookets} of folk songs.
e.zh: 那家店出售袖珍的民歌小册子。

e.en: We picked up several novels at the Frankfurt {bookfair}.
e.zh: 我们在法兰克福书展上买了好几本小说。

e.en: Publishers showcase new titles at every {bookfair}.
e.zh: 出版商在每届图书博览会推介新书。

bookful.t: 满腹书本知识的；书生气十足的

e.en: He spoke with a {bookful} air that annoyed his classmates.
e.zh: 他说话满口书生气，惹得同学不悦。

e.en: Her arguments are {bookful} but lack real experience.
e.zh: 她的论点书卷气十足，却缺乏实际经验。

bookholder.t: 阅读架；书托；夹书的支架

e.en: The reader propped her textbook on a metal {bookholder}.
e.zh: 读者把课本架在金属阅读架上。

e.en: A small {bookholder} freed both of his hands.
e.zh: 一个小书托解放了他的双手。

bookhunter.t: 觅书人；寻书者；旧书猎手

e.en: The veteran {bookhunter} scoured every flea market in town.
e.zh: 这位老练的觅书人把城里的跳蚤市场翻了个遍。

e.en: {Bookhunters} pay top prices for first editions.
e.zh: 旧书猎手愿出高价收购初版书。

e.en: Please complete the {bookingform} and return it by Friday.
e.zh: 请填写预订表格并在周五前交回。

e.en: Our online {bookingform} only takes two minutes.
e.zh: 我们的网上预约登记表只需两分钟即可填完。

bookkeepter.t: 簿记员；记账员（bookkeeper 的拼写变体）

e.en: She trained as a {bookkeepter} after leaving school.
e.zh: 离校后她受训成为簿记员。

e.en: Every small firm needs a reliable {bookkeepter}.
e.zh: 每家小公司都需要可靠的记账员。

bookland.t: 文契土地；古英格兰以特许书持有的地

e.en: Anglo-Saxon nobles often held land as {bookland}.
e.zh: 盎格鲁-撒克逊贵族常以文契方式持有土地。

e.en: {Bookland} could be transferred outside the family.
e.zh: 文契土地可在家族之外转让。

booklearned.t: 死读书的；只会书本知识的；书呆子气的

e.en: He was {booklearned} but useless on a real farm.
e.zh: 他满腹书本知识，但在真正的农场上毫无用处。

e.en: Her {booklearned} cousins looked down on practical work.
e.zh: 她那些死读书的表亲瞧不起实际的体力活。

booklore.t: 书本知识；书中所学的学问

e.en: His {booklore} amazed everyone at the dinner table.
e.zh: 他渊博的书本知识令餐桌上每个人惊叹。

e.en: Centuries of {booklore} are stored in this library.
e.zh: 这座图书馆储藏了数百年的书本学问。

booklouse.t: 书虱；以书页为食的微小昆虫

e.en: A {booklouse} can damage old paper if humidity is high.
e.zh: 湿度高时书虱会损坏旧纸张。

e.en: Tiny booklice crawled across the dusty {booklouse} colony.
e.zh: 细小的书虱在落满灰尘的虫群中爬行。

booklover.t: 爱书人；书迷；书籍爱好者

e.en: Any {booklover} would envy that home library.
e.zh: 任何爱书人都会羡慕那间家庭图书馆。

e.en: She gave the {booklover} a leather bookmark.
e.zh: 她送给这位书迷一枚皮质书签。

bookmaking.t: 接受赌注的行当；制书业

e.en: He was arrested for illegal {bookmaking} last year.
e.zh: 他去年因非法接受赌注被捕。

e.en: Traditional {bookmaking} requires careful binding by hand.
e.zh: 传统制书工艺需要手工精心装订。

bookmarklet.t: 浏览器书签小程序；脚本书签

e.en: Drag the {bookmarklet} to your toolbar to install it.
e.zh: 把这个书签小程序拖到工具栏即可安装。

e.en: A handy {bookmarklet} can highlight all links on a page.
e.zh: 一个好用的脚本书签可以标出页面上所有链接。

bookmatch.t: 对花拼接；木皮或石材的镜像拼花

e.en: We chose to {bookmatch} the marble for a symmetrical look.
e.zh: 我们选择对花拼接大理石以求对称美感。

e.en: The two veneer panels {bookmatch} along the centerline.
e.zh: 两块木皮沿中线对花拼接。

bookmatched.t: 对花拼接的；纹路镜像对称的

e.en: The countertop features {bookmatched} stone slabs.
e.zh: 台面采用对花拼接的石板。

e.en: Their guitar has a beautifully {bookmatched} maple top.
e.zh: 他们的吉他面板由对花拼接的枫木制成。

bookplate.t: 藏书票；标示书主的小贴片

e.en: Each volume bears the family's antique {bookplate}.
e.zh: 每一卷都贴有家族的古董藏书票。

e.en: She designs custom {bookplates} for collectors.
e.zh: 她为收藏家设计定制藏书票。

bookrack.t: 书架；书报架；放书的搁架

e.en: He set the magazine on the metal {bookrack}.
e.zh: 他把杂志放在金属书报架上。

e.en: A revolving {bookrack} stood beside the desk.
e.zh: 桌旁立着一个旋转书架。

bookrest.t: 阅读架；读书时撑书的小架

e.en: She used a small {bookrest} while studying for exams.
e.zh: 她备考时用一个小阅读架。

e.en: The wooden {bookrest} folded flat for travel.
e.zh: 那个木制阅读架可以折叠起来便于携带。

bookrunner.t: 主承销商；新股发行的簿记管理人

e.en: Goldman acted as the lead {bookrunner} on the IPO.
e.zh: 高盛担任此次首次公开募股的主承销商。

e.en: The {bookrunner} sets the offer price after demand checks.
e.zh: 簿记管理人在询价后确定发行价。

e.en: Online platforms have transformed {bookselling}.
e.zh: 网上平台改变了整个图书销售业。

e.en: She has worked in {bookselling} for thirty years.
e.zh: 她从事卖书行业已三十年。

bookstack.t: 书架；书库；图书馆中密集书堆区

e.en: He searched the {bookstack} for a missing volume.
e.zh: 他在书库中搜寻一本遗失的卷册。

e.en: Light filtered weakly into the deep {bookstacks}.
e.zh: 微弱的光线透入深处的密集书架。

e.en: The Bible lay open on a brass {bookstand}.
e.zh: 《圣经》摊开在一个黄铜阅读架上。

e.en: A folding {bookstand} keeps the recipe at eye level.
e.zh: 一个折叠书架把食谱保持在视线高度。

booksy.t: 书卷气十足的；爱卖弄学问的

e.en: His {booksy} manner put off most of his coworkers.
e.zh: 他那副书呆子气让大多数同事敬而远之。

e.en: She had a slightly {booksy} way of speaking.
e.zh: 她说话带着点卖弄学问的味道。

bookteller.t: 说书人；讲述书中故事的人（罕用）

e.en: The village {bookteller} knew every old legend by heart.
e.zh: 村里的说书人对每一则古老传说烂熟于心。

e.en: A traveling {bookteller} would visit each summer.
e.zh: 每年夏天都有一位云游的说书人来访。

bookwork.t: 书本作业；查阅资料的脑力工作；账目工作

e.en: She prefers fieldwork to {bookwork} any day.
e.zh: 她任何时候都更喜欢田野工作而不是书本作业。

e.en: Most of his shift involves {bookwork} and ledgers.
e.zh: 他大半个班次都在做账和处理书面工作。

boom-and-bust.t: 繁荣与萧条；经济上的大起大落

e.en: The mining town went through cycles of {boom-and-bust}.
e.zh: 这个矿业小镇经历了一轮又一轮的繁荣与萧条。

e.en: Tech investors are used to {boom-and-bust} markets.
e.zh: 科技投资者已习惯了大起大落的市场。

boomslang.t: 非洲树蛇；剧毒的后沟牙树栖蛇

e.en: A {boomslang} hung motionless from the acacia branch.
e.zh: 一条非洲树蛇一动不动地挂在金合欢树枝上。

e.en: The bite of a {boomslang} can be deadly without antivenom.
e.zh: 没有抗蛇毒血清，非洲树蛇咬伤可能致命。

boomsprinkler.t: 横臂式喷灌机；大型农田长臂洒水器

e.en: The farmer installed a {boomsprinkler} across the field.
e.zh: 农夫在田里架起一台横臂式喷灌机。

e.en: A long {boomsprinkler} watered both crop rows at once.
e.zh: 一台长臂喷灌机同时浇灌两行作物。

boomster.t: 看涨派；过分乐观看好经济的人

e.en: Every {boomster} on Wall Street predicted record growth.
e.zh: 华尔街的每个看涨派都预测会有创纪录的增长。

e.en: He's a confirmed {boomster} despite the warning signs.
e.zh: 尽管有警示信号，他仍是个坚定的乐观派。

boondagger.t: 美式旧俚语；指粗野彪悍的人（罕见用法）

e.en: The slang term {boondagger} appears in mid-century pulp fiction.
e.zh: 俚语 boondagger 一词出现在二十世纪中期的通俗小说里。

e.en: Few readers today recognize the word {boondagger}.
e.zh: 今天几乎没有读者认得 boondagger 这个旧俚语。

boondocker.t: 野外露营者；偏爱荒野扎营的人

e.en: Every {boondocker} carries water and a backup battery.
e.zh: 每个野外露营者都会带水和备用电池。

e.en: He's a serious {boondocker} who avoids campgrounds.
e.zh: 他是个正经的荒野露营者，从不去营地。

boondockers.t: 军用作战靴；耐磨的野营靴

e.en: The marines cleaned mud off their {boondockers}.
e.zh: 海军陆战队员擦掉作战靴上的泥。

e.en: His worn {boondockers} had hiked a thousand miles.
e.zh: 他那双磨损的野营靴已徒步走过一千英里。

boong.t: 澳洲土著（带强烈侮辱意味的蔑称，禁忌用语）

e.en: The novel uses the offensive word {boong} to show period prejudice.
e.zh: 小说使用带侮辱意味的 boong 一词来呈现当时的偏见。

e.en: Modern dictionaries flag {boong} as a derogatory slur.
e.zh: 现代词典将 boong 标注为带贬义的种族蔑称。

boongary.t: 树袋鼠；澳大利亚昆士兰一种树栖袋鼠

e.en: The {boongary} is a tree-kangaroo found in Queensland.
e.zh: boongary 是一种生活在昆士兰的树袋鼠。

e.en: Researchers tagged a young {boongary} for tracking.
e.zh: 研究人员给一只幼年树袋鼠装上追踪标记。

e.en: The coral grew in delicate {branch-like} formations.
e.zh: 珊瑚长成精致的枝状结构。

e.en: Lightning left {branch-like} scars across the sky.
e.zh: 闪电在天空划出枝状的痕迹。

e.en: The old {branch-line} closed in the 1960s.
e.zh: 那条旧支线铁路在1960年代关闭。

e.en: They took a {branch-line} train to the village.
e.zh: 他们乘支线列车到村里。

e.en: Tadpoles are {branchiate} until they mature.
e.zh: 蝌蚪在成熟前都是有鳃的。

e.en: Many {branchiate} animals live entirely underwater.
e.zh: 许多有鳃动物完全生活在水中。

branchiopod.t: 鳃足类动物（如水蚤、卤虫）

e.en: The brine shrimp is a small {branchiopod}.
e.zh: 卤虫是一种小型鳃足类动物。

e.en: Researchers studied {branchiopod} populations in the lake.
e.zh: 研究人员调查了湖中鳃足类动物的数量。

branchiopodous.t: 鳃足类的；属于鳃足亚纲的

e.en: These tiny {branchiopodous} crustaceans drift in fresh water.
e.zh: 这些微小的鳃足类甲壳动物漂浮在淡水中。

e.en: He specializes in {branchiopodous} species of arid lakes.
e.zh: 他专门研究干旱湖泊中的鳃足类物种。

branchiostegite.t: 鳃盖（甲壳动物保护鳃的甲壳部分）

e.en: The crab's {branchiostegite} shields its delicate gills.
e.zh: 螃蟹的鳃盖保护着脆弱的鳃。

e.en: A cracked {branchiostegite} can lead to infection.
e.zh: 鳃盖破裂可能导致感染。

e.en: The fish has prominent {branchiostegous} structures.
e.zh: 这种鱼有明显的鳃盖结构。

e.en: He sketched the {branchiostegous} flap in detail.
e.zh: 他细致地画出了鳃盖膜。

e.en: Tiny {branchlet} buds appeared after the rain.
e.zh: 雨后小枝上冒出了嫩芽。

e.en: She trimmed each dead {branchlet} from the bonsai.
e.zh: 她把盆景上每根枯小枝都剪掉。

e.en: Frost formed {branchlike} patterns on the window.
e.zh: 霜在窗上形成枝状的图案。

e.en: The nerve cells have {branchlike} extensions.
e.zh: 神经细胞有枝状的突起。

e.en: This is a critical {branchpoint} in the project.
e.zh: 这是项目的一个关键分支点。

e.en: Evolution shows clear {branchpoint} events in the fossil record.
e.zh: 化石记录显示进化中明显的分支点。

e.en: The garden was full of {branchy} old oaks.
e.zh: 花园里满是枝条繁茂的老橡树。

e.en: He chose a {branchy} stick for the campfire.
e.zh: 他挑了一根多枝的树枝生篝火。

e.en: She only buys {brand-name} clothes.
e.zh: 她只买名牌服装。

e.en: The store sells {brand-name} goods at a discount.
e.zh: 那家店折价出售名牌商品。

e.en: He baited the hook with a wriggling {brandling}.
e.zh: 他用一条扭动的红条蚯蚓挂钩。

e.en: {Brandling} worms thrive in the compost heap.
e.zh: 红条蚯蚓在堆肥堆里大量繁殖。

e.en: The company redesigned its {brandmark} last year.
e.zh: 公司去年重新设计了品牌标识。

e.en: A strong {brandmark} helps customers recognize the product.
e.zh: 鲜明的品牌标识能让顾客认出产品。

brandysnap.t: 白兰地脆饼（薄脆姜味卷饼）

e.en: She filled each {brandysnap} with whipped cream.
e.zh: 她在每个白兰地脆饼里挤上奶油。

e.en: Grandma's {brandysnap} recipe is a family secret.
e.zh: 奶奶的白兰地脆饼配方是家族秘方。

e.en: The neighbors {brangle} over the fence again.
e.zh: 邻居们又为篱笆争吵起来。

e.en: They had a noisy {brangle} in the tavern.
e.zh: 他们在酒馆里大声争吵了一番。

e.en: The siblings {brangled} all afternoon.
e.zh: 兄弟姐妹整个下午都在争吵。

e.en: They {brangled} over a trivial misunderstanding.
e.zh: 他们为一个小误会争吵不休。

e.en: He's known as a stubborn {brangler} in court.
e.zh: 他在法庭上以固执好争闻名。

e.en: Avoid that {brangler} if you want a quiet evening.
e.zh: 想要安静的夜晚就别招惹那个爱争吵的人。

e.en: Their constant {brangling} drove me crazy.
e.zh: 他们没完没了的争吵把我逼疯了。

e.en: The meeting ended in pointless {brangling}.
e.zh: 会议在无谓的争吵中结束。

brank.t: 昔日惩戒妇人的铁口箍（古词）

e.en: The museum displays an iron {brank} from the 1600s.
e.zh: 博物馆展出一件十七世纪的铁口箍。

e.en: Scolds were once forced to wear the {brank}.
e.zh: 过去爱骂人的妇女曾被迫戴上铁口箍。

branks.t: 旧时套头惩戒铁具；马笼头

e.en: The {branks} were a cruel medieval punishment.
e.zh: 这种铁口箍是中世纪的残酷刑具。

e.en: He fastened the {branks} on the pony.
e.zh: 他给小马套上笼头。

e.en: Geologists found {brannerite} in the abandoned mine.
e.zh: 地质学家在废弃矿井里发现了钛铀矿。

e.en: {Brannerite} is mined as a source of uranium.
e.zh: 钛铀矿被开采作为铀的来源。

e.en: The pub erupted in a wild {brannigan}.
e.zh: 酒馆里爆发了一场喧闹的争吵。

e.en: After the wedding, they had a real {brannigan}.
e.zh: 婚礼之后他们大闹了一场。

e.en: The bread had a coarse, {branny} texture.
e.zh: 这面包口感粗糙，带有麸皮感。

e.en: His skin was dry and slightly {branny}.
e.zh: 他的皮肤干燥，带些糠皮状屑。

e.en: A {brantail} flitted across the garden wall.
e.zh: 一只红尾鸲掠过花园的墙头。

e.en: Birdwatchers spotted a male {brantail} singing.
e.zh: 观鸟者看到一只雄性红尾鸲在鸣叫。

e.en: The path was loose and {brashy} underfoot.
e.zh: 这条小路脚下满是松散的碎石。

e.en: They cleared {brashy} debris from the slope.
e.zh: 他们清除了斜坡上的碎石残片。

brasier.t: 火盆；铜匠（brazier 的旧拼写）

e.en: A glowing {brasier} warmed the courtyard.
e.zh: 一只通红的火盆温暖了庭院。

e.en: The old {brasier} hammered out copper pots.
e.zh: 那位铜匠敲打出铜锅。

brahminic.t: 婆罗门的；与婆罗门有关的

e.en: The text describes ancient {brahminic} rituals in detail.
e.zh: 这部典籍详细描述了古代婆罗门的仪式。

e.en: He studied the {brahminic} traditions of northern India.
e.zh: 他研究了印度北部的婆罗门传统。

e.en: The scholar wore {brahminical} robes during the ceremony.
e.zh: 这位学者在仪式上身穿婆罗门式长袍。

e.en: She critiqued the {brahminical} hierarchy in her essay.
e.zh: 她在文章中批评了婆罗门式的等级制度。

e.en: The sailors used a {brail} to gather the sail quickly.
e.zh: 水手们用卷帆索迅速收起船帆。

e.en: He pulled the {brail} as the wind picked up.
e.zh: 风渐大时，他拉起了卷帆索。

e.en: The crew {brailed} the sails before the storm hit.
e.zh: 船员在暴风雨来临前收起了风帆。

e.en: They quickly {brailed} the canvas to slow the boat.
e.zh: 他们迅速收起帆布以减慢船速。

e.en: The fisherman lifted the catch with a long {brailer}.
e.zh: 渔夫用长柄捞网将鱼提起。

e.en: A skilled {brailer} can scoop up dozens of fish.
e.zh: 熟练的捞网工一次能舀起几十条鱼。

e.en: The crew began {brailing} the sail at dusk.
e.zh: 船员在黄昏时开始收帆。

e.en: {Brailing} the catch took most of the morning.
e.zh: 用网捞起渔获花了一上午的大部分时间。

e.en: The {braillist} transcribed the novel into raised dots.
e.zh: 这位盲文专家将小说转译成凸点文字。

e.en: She trained as a {braillist} to help blind students.
e.zh: 她受训成为盲文专家以帮助盲人学生。

e.en: Loosen the {brails} so the sail can drop.
e.zh: 松开卷帆索，让帆落下。

e.en: The old {brails} had frayed in the salty air.
e.zh: 旧卷帆索在咸湿的空气中已磨损。

e.en: The accident left him {brain-damaged} for life.
e.zh: 那场事故使他终身脑部受损。

e.en: Critics called the design {brain-damaged} and unusable.
e.zh: 评论者称这个设计脑残且无法使用。

e.en: Hours of study gave him a bad case of {brain-fag}.
e.zh: 长时间学习让他严重脑力疲劳。

e.en: She took a walk to relieve her {brain-fag}.
e.zh: 她出去散步以缓解用脑过度。

brain-picker.t: 善于汲取他人智慧的人

e.en: He's a notorious {brain-picker} at every meeting.
e.zh: 他在每次会议上都爱套别人的想法。

e.en: As a {brain-picker}, she gathered ideas from many experts.
e.zh: 作为一个善于取经的人，她从众多专家处汲取想法。

brain-picking.t: 向他人请教；汲取他人想法

e.en: Some {brain-picking} over coffee helped me solve the issue.
e.zh: 喝咖啡时向他请教让我解决了问题。

e.en: He invited me for a session of {brain-picking}.
e.zh: 他邀请我去聊聊以汲取我的想法。

e.en: She had a {brain-wave} and solved the puzzle instantly.
e.zh: 她灵机一动，立刻解开了谜题。

e.en: The device measures each {brain-wave} during sleep.
e.zh: 这台仪器测量睡眠中的每一段脑电波。

e.en: Every {brain-worker} needs regular breaks to stay sharp.
e.zh: 每个脑力劳动者都需要定期休息以保持敏锐。

e.en: The city is filled with {brain-workers} in finance and tech.
e.zh: 这座城市里满是金融和科技领域的脑力劳动者。

e.en: My sister is the family {brainbox}—she aces every exam.
e.zh: 我妹妹是家里的聪明人，每次考试都拿高分。

e.en: Use your {brainbox} and figure it out yourself.
e.zh: 动动你的脑子，自己想办法解决。

e.en: These apps are the {brainchildren} of two college friends.
e.zh: 这些应用是两位大学好友的智慧结晶。

e.en: Her latest {brainchildren} have impressed the whole industry.
e.zh: 她最新的几个创意让整个行业刮目相看。

e.en: The {braindamaged} interface frustrated every user.
e.zh: 这个愚蠢的界面让每个用户都很恼火。

e.en: Doctors confirmed the patient was {braindamaged}.
e.zh: 医生确认病人有脑损伤。

e.en: After exams she suffered serious {brainfag}.
e.zh: 考试结束后她严重脑力疲劳。

e.en: A nap is the best cure for {brainfag}.
e.zh: 小睡是治疗脑力疲劳的最佳方法。

e.en: Her {braininess} earned her a full scholarship.
e.zh: 她的聪明让她获得了全额奖学金。

e.en: The job demands more than just {braininess}.
e.zh: 这份工作需要的不只是聪明。

e.en: His {brainish} decision cost the team the match.
e.zh: 他冲动的决定让球队输掉了比赛。

e.en: Don't make a {brainish} move you'll regret.
e.zh: 别做出会让自己后悔的鲁莽举动。

e.en: They called him the {brainman} of the project team.
e.zh: 他们称他为项目组里的智囊。

e.en: Every startup needs at least one {brainman}.
e.zh: 每家初创公司都需要至少一位智囊。

e.en: The doctor ordered a {brainscan} after the fall.
e.zh: 摔倒后医生安排做了脑部扫描。

e.en: Her {brainscan} showed no sign of injury.
e.zh: 她的脑部扫描显示没有受伤迹象。

e.en: His {brainsick} jealousy ruined the friendship.
e.zh: 他疯狂的嫉妒毁掉了这段友谊。

e.en: The villain laughed with a {brainsick} grin.
e.zh: 反派露出疯狂的笑容大笑起来。

e.en: He muttered {brainsickly} to himself in the corner.
e.zh: 他在角落里疯疯癫癫地自言自语。

e.en: She stared {brainsickly} at the empty page.
e.zh: 她神思恍惚地盯着空白页。

e.en: The interview ended with a tricky {brainteaser}.
e.zh: 面试以一道棘手的脑筋急转弯结束。

e.en: Kids love this {brainteaser} about three doors.
e.zh: 孩子们很喜欢这道关于三扇门的益智题。

brainteasers.t: 益智题；脑筋急转弯（复数）

e.en: The book is full of math {brainteasers}.
e.zh: 这本书里满是数学益智题。

e.en: He solves {brainteasers} during his commute.
e.zh: 他在通勤路上做脑筋急转弯。

e.en: This job requires more {brainwork} than muscle.
e.zh: 这份工作更看重脑力而非体力。

e.en: Heavy {brainwork} leaves him exhausted by evening.
e.zh: 繁重的脑力劳动让他到傍晚就精疲力竭。

e.en: A typical {brainworker} spends hours at a desk.
e.zh: 典型的脑力劳动者每天伏案数小时。

e.en: The cafe is popular with local {brainworkers}.
e.zh: 这家咖啡馆很受当地脑力劳动者欢迎。

e.en: The jeweler appraised a rare {brait} from Africa.
e.zh: 珠宝商鉴定了一颗来自非洲的稀有钻石原石。

e.en: Each {brait} must be cut to reveal its brilliance.
e.zh: 每颗钻石原石都需切割才能显出光彩。

e.en: The fisherman caught a large {braize} off the coast.
e.zh: 渔夫在近海钓到一条大红鲷鱼。

e.en: Grilled {braize} is a local delicacy.
e.zh: 烤红鲷鱼是当地的美味。

e.en: The guard rode in the {brake-van} at the rear.
e.zh: 列车员坐在最后面的守车里。

e.en: An old {brake-van} sat rusting on the siding.
e.zh: 一节老旧的守车锈迹斑斑地停在岔道上。

e.en: The truck's {brakeage} failed on the steep hill.
e.zh: 卡车的制动装置在陡坡上失灵了。

e.en: Engineers improved the {brakeage} on the new model.
e.zh: 工程师改进了新型号的制动系统。

e.en: He rode a {brakeless} bike through the city.
e.zh: 他骑着一辆无刹车的自行车穿过城市。

e.en: The cart rolled {brakeless} down the slope.
e.zh: 小车没有刹车顺坡滑了下去。

brakesman.t: 制动员；矿井卷扬机操作工

e.en: The {brakesman} controlled the cage descending the mine.
e.zh: 制动员操控着下入矿井的笼子。

e.en: He worked as a {brakesman} for thirty years.
e.zh: 他做了三十年制动员。

e.en: He pushed the {brakestaff} forward to stop the wagon.
e.zh: 他推动制动杆使车厢停下。

e.en: The wooden {brakestaff} had cracked over time.
e.zh: 那根木制动杆已经年久开裂。

e.en: The conductor sat alone in the {brakevan}.
e.zh: 列车员独自坐在守车里。

e.en: A red lamp glowed at the rear of the {brakevan}.
e.zh: 守车后端亮着一盏红灯。

e.en: The old {brakie} told stories from the rails.
e.zh: 老制动员讲起铁路上的故事。

e.en: Every {brakie} learned to jump between cars.
e.zh: 每个制动员都学会在车厢之间跳跃。

e.en: They lost the trail in the {braky} hillside.
e.zh: 他们在长满灌木的山坡上迷了路。

e.en: Sheep grazed along the {braky} edges of the field.
e.zh: 羊群在田边长满灌木丛的地方吃草。

brale.t: 布氏硬度计金刚石压头

e.en: The technician calibrated the {brale} indenter.
e.zh: 技师校准了金刚石压头。

e.en: A worn {brale} produces inaccurate hardness readings.
e.zh: 磨损的金刚石压头会导致硬度读数不准。

e.en: They pushed through the {brambly} hedge.
e.zh: 他们穿过荆棘丛生的树篱。

e.en: The path turned narrow and {brambly}.
e.zh: 小路变得狭窄而荆棘丛生。

e.en: She showed off her {bran-new} car to everyone.
e.zh: 她向大家炫耀她崭新的汽车。

e.en: The shop sells {bran-new} appliances at a discount.
e.zh: 这家店折价出售全新的家电。

bran-pie.t: 麸皮抽奖盒（藏礼物的游戏）

e.en: Children dug into the {bran-pie} for hidden prizes.
e.zh: 孩子们在麸皮抽奖盒里翻找藏着的礼物。

e.en: Every fair had a {bran-pie} for the kids.
e.zh: 每个集市都为孩子准备了麸皮抽奖盒。

e.en: The {brass-hats} arrived in a black sedan.
e.zh: 那些高级军官乘黑色轿车抵达。

e.en: He's just another {brass-hat} from headquarters.
e.zh: 他不过是总部来的又一位大官。

e.en: The old {brass-smith} hammered a candlestick.
e.zh: 老黄铜匠敲打着一根烛台。

e.en: Her grandfather was a skilled {brass-smith}.
e.zh: 她祖父是个手艺高超的铜匠。

e.en: The {brass-visaged} swindler kept smiling.
e.zh: 那个厚颜无耻的骗子还在微笑。

e.en: He gave a {brass-visaged} denial in court.
e.zh: 他在法庭上厚着脸皮否认。

e.en: She plays in the {brass-wind} section.
e.zh: 她在铜管乐组演奏。

e.en: The march needed a louder {brass-wind} part.
e.zh: 这首进行曲需要更响亮的铜管乐部分。

e.en: The mint charged a small {brassage}.
e.zh: 造币厂收取少量铸币费。

e.en: Medieval kings collected {brassage} on every coin.
e.zh: 中世纪国王对每枚硬币征收铸币费。

e.en: He wore a black {brassard} of mourning.
e.zh: 他戴着黑色的丧礼臂章。

e.en: Medics are identified by a red {brassard}.
e.zh: 医务人员靠红色臂章来辨认。

e.en: The knight's {brassart} was dented in battle.
e.zh: 骑士的护臂甲在战斗中凹陷了。

e.en: Museum curators restored the rusted {brassart}.
e.zh: 博物馆馆员修复了生锈的护臂甲。

e.en: Her {brassbound} traditions ruled the household.
e.zh: 她那墨守成规的传统支配着整个家。

e.en: He carried a {brassbound} oak chest.
e.zh: 他提着一只包铜的橡木箱子。

e.en: The {brassfounder} poured molten metal carefully.
e.zh: 黄铜铸造工小心地浇注熔融金属。

e.en: Her father trained as a {brassfounder}.
e.zh: 她父亲学的是黄铜铸造。

e.en: The town was famous for {brassfounding}.
e.zh: 这个小镇以黄铜铸造闻名。

e.en: He learned {brassfounding} from his uncle.
e.zh: 他跟叔叔学会了黄铜铸造。

e.en: Cabbage and kale are {brassicaceous} plants.
e.zh: 卷心菜和羽衣甘蓝都是十字花科植物。

e.en: The garden featured several {brassicaceous} species.
e.zh: 这片菜园种了好几种十字花科植物。

brassie.t: 二号木杆；铜底高尔夫球杆

e.en: He chose a {brassie} for the long fairway.
e.zh: 他选了一支二号木杆来打长球道。

e.en: The old {brassie} hung above the fireplace.
e.zh: 那支老式高尔夫球杆挂在壁炉上方。

e.en: Her tone grew {brassier} with each insult.
e.zh: 她的语气随着每句辱骂越来越尖刻。

e.en: The trumpet sounded {brassier} than usual.
e.zh: 小号听起来比平时更刺耳。

e.en: That was the {brassiest} reply I'd heard.
e.zh: 那是我听过最厚脸皮的回答。

e.en: She wore the {brassiest} earrings in the room.
e.zh: 她戴着房间里最俗艳的耳环。

e.en: He {brassily} demanded a refund.
e.zh: 他厚着脸皮要求退款。

e.en: The horn blared {brassily} through the hall.
e.zh: 号声刺耳地响彻大厅。

e.en: I disliked the {brassiness} of his manner.
e.zh: 我不喜欢他那副厚脸皮的样子。

e.en: The trumpet's {brassiness} filled the room.
e.zh: 小号那刺耳的音色充满了房间。

e.en: She polished the {brassware} every Sunday.
e.zh: 她每个星期天都擦拭那些铜器。

e.en: The shop sold Indian {brassware} and silks.
e.zh: 那家店出售印度铜器和丝绸。

e.en: The {brasswind} ensemble rehearsed nightly.
e.zh: 铜管乐合奏团每晚排练。

e.en: He plays a {brasswind} instrument professionally.
e.zh: 他以演奏铜管乐器为业。

e.en: The dam {brast} under the flood's pressure.
e.zh: 水坝在洪水压力下轰然崩裂。

e.en: Their hearts {brast} with sudden grief.
e.zh: 他们的心因突来的悲痛而崩裂。

e.en: Miners installed a wooden {brattice} for ventilation.
e.zh: 矿工们安装了一块木质隔板以利通风。

e.en: The {brattice} directed fresh air to the face.
e.zh: 隔板把新鲜空气引向工作面。

e.en: The shaft was carefully {bratticed} for safety.
e.zh: 为安全起见，这条竖井装上了隔板。

e.en: They worked in a tightly {bratticed} tunnel.
e.zh: 他们在隔板密布的巷道里作业。

e.en: The old {brattices} had rotted through.
e.zh: 老旧的矿井隔板已经腐朽透了。

e.en: New {brattices} improved airflow underground.
e.zh: 新隔板改善了井下的通风。

e.en: His {brattiness} embarrassed the whole family.
e.zh: 他那副小屁孩样子让全家难堪。

e.en: She outgrew her teenage {brattiness}.
e.zh: 她终于摆脱了少年时的任性。

e.en: Cart wheels {brattle} over the cobblestones.
e.zh: 车轮在卵石路上咔嗒作响。

e.en: We heard the {brattle} of distant thunder.
e.zh: 我们听见远处雷声隆隆。

e.en: The audience shouted {bravissimo} after the aria.
e.zh: 咏叹调结束后观众高喊妙极了。

e.en: "{Bravissimo}!" cried the conductor at rehearsal.
e.zh: 指挥在排练时大喊："妙极了！"

e.en: It's a {braw} morning in the Highlands.
e.zh: 高地上是个晴朗美好的早晨。

e.en: She wore her {braw} new dress to church.
e.zh: 她穿着漂亮的新裙子去教堂。

e.en: The bairn is doing {brawly} at school.
e.zh: 那孩子在学校表现很好。

e.en: She sings {brawly} at every ceilidh.
e.zh: 她在每场盖尔聚会上都唱得动听。

e.en: He {brawnily} hauled the timber up the slope.
e.zh: 他强壮有力地把木料拖上斜坡。

e.en: The wrestler stood {brawnily} in the ring.
e.zh: 那名摔跤手魁梧地站在擂台上。

e.en: His {brawniness} impressed the recruiters immediately.
e.zh: 他强壮的体格立刻给招募者留下了印象。

e.en: Years of farm work gave her real {brawniness}.
e.zh: 多年的农活让她真正变得强壮。

e.en: The flock was vaccinated against {braxy}.
e.zh: 羊群已接种了羊快疫疫苗。

e.en: Highland shepherds dreaded outbreaks of {braxy}.
e.zh: 高地牧羊人最怕羊快疫爆发。

e.en: His {brazen-faced} lying shocked the jury.
e.zh: 他厚颜无耻的撒谎令陪审团震惊。

e.en: She gave a {brazen-faced} excuse for being late.
e.zh: 她为迟到找了个不要脸的借口。

e.en: Her {brazenfaced} demand stunned everyone present.
e.zh: 她那厚颜无耻的要求让在场所有人愣住。

e.en: He's a {brazenfaced} cheat who never apologizes.
e.zh: 他是个从不道歉的无耻骗子。

e.en: Dyers prized {brazil-wood} for its red pigment.
e.zh: 染工因其红色色素而珍视巴西红木。

e.en: Ships once carried {brazil-wood} across the Atlantic.
e.zh: 昔日船只把巴西红木运过大西洋。

e.en: The violin's bow is made of {brazilwood}.
e.zh: 这把小提琴的弓是用巴西红木制成的。

e.en: {Brazilwood} once fueled colonial trade routes.
e.zh: 巴西红木曾推动了殖民地贸易航线。

boxty.t: 博克斯蒂；爱尔兰土豆煎饼

e.en: Her grandmother taught her to make {boxty} every Christmas.
e.zh: 她外婆每年圣诞节都教她做爱尔兰土豆煎饼。

e.en: We ordered {boxty} with smoked salmon at the Dublin pub.
e.zh: 我们在都柏林酒馆点了配熏三文鱼的土豆煎饼。

boxwork.t: 箱状构造；网格状矿脉残留

e.en: The cave walls displayed delicate {boxwork} formations.
e.zh: 洞壁上呈现出精致的网格状矿脉构造。

e.en: Geologists study {boxwork} to track mineral weathering.
e.zh: 地质学家通过研究箱状构造来追踪矿物风化过程。

boy-meets-girl.t: 男孩邂逅女孩式的；俗套爱情故事的

e.en: The novel follows a classic {boy-meets-girl} plot.
e.zh: 这部小说遵循经典的男孩邂逅女孩式情节。

e.en: Hollywood keeps recycling the same {boy-meets-girl} formula.
e.zh: 好莱坞不停翻拍同样的男孩遇见女孩套路。

e.en: The {boyard} owned vast estates outside Moscow.
e.zh: 那位俄国贵族在莫斯科城外拥有大片庄园。

e.en: Peter the Great curtailed the power of the {boyard} class.
e.zh: 彼得大帝削弱了波雅尔贵族阶层的权力。

e.en: Hey {boychick}, come help me with these groceries.
e.zh: 嘿小伙子，过来帮我拎这些杂货。

e.en: That {boychick} is sharper than he looks.
e.zh: 那小子比看上去要精明。

boychik.t: 小子；小伙子（意第绪语借词）

e.en: My grandfather always called me {boychik}.
e.zh: 我爷爷总是叫我小伙子。

e.en: The {boychik} grew up to run the family deli.
e.zh: 那个小伙子长大后接手了家里的熟食店。

boys-and-girls.t: 男女混合的；男女皆有的

e.en: It's a {boys-and-girls} school with mixed classrooms.
e.zh: 那是一所男女合班的学校。

e.en: The chorus features a {boys-and-girls} ensemble.
e.zh: 合唱团由男女混合组成。

e.en: We picked fresh {boysenberries} from the garden.
e.zh: 我们从园子里摘了新鲜的博伊森莓。

e.en: The pie was packed with sweet {boysenberries}.
e.zh: 派里满是香甜的博伊森莓。

e.en: She ordered {boysenberry} ice cream for dessert.
e.zh: 她点了博伊森莓冰淇淋作甜点。

e.en: The jam was made from a single {boysenberry} variety.
e.zh: 那款果酱由单一品种的博伊森莓制成。

brabantine.t: 布拉班特的；属布拉班特地区的

e.en: They admired the {brabantine} lace at the antique fair.
e.zh: 他们在古董展上欣赏布拉班特蕾丝。

e.en: The painter showed clear {brabantine} influences.
e.zh: 那位画家明显受到布拉班特地区的影响。

brabble.t: 为琐事争吵；喋喋不休地拌嘴（古语）

e.en: They will {brabble} for hours over trifles.
e.zh: 他们会为琐事争吵几个小时。

e.en: Old men {brabble} on benches all afternoon.
e.zh: 老人们整下午都坐在长椅上瞎吵。

e.en: The neighbors {brabbled} over the fence again.
e.zh: 邻居们又隔着篱笆吵起来了。

e.en: They {brabbled} until dawn about politics.
e.zh: 他们就政治问题争论到天亮。

e.en: Their endless {brabblement} drove me from the room.
e.zh: 他们没完没了的争吵把我赶出了房间。

e.en: Court records noted the petty {brabblement}.
e.zh: 法庭记录中提到了那场琐碎的口角。

e.en: He was known as the village {brabbler}.
e.zh: 他在村里以好争吵著称。

e.en: Don't bother arguing with that {brabbler}.
e.zh: 别费劲跟那个爱抬杠的人争。

brabbles.t: 为琐事争吵（第三人称单数）

e.en: She {brabbles} with anyone who disagrees.
e.zh: 凡是不同意她的人她都要争上几句。

e.en: He {brabbles} like a child over change.
e.zh: 他像小孩似的为零钱争个不停。

e.en: The two clerks were {brabbling} all morning.
e.zh: 那两个职员吵了一上午。

e.en: Their {brabbling} made the meeting useless.
e.zh: 他们的争吵让会议毫无成效。

e.en: The eagle's {braccate} legs are covered in fine feathers.
e.zh: 那只鹰的腿上长满细密羽毛。

e.en: Owls are typically {braccate} down to the toes.
e.zh: 猫头鹰的羽毛通常一直延伸到脚趾。

e.en: The hunter brought his finest {brach} to the field.
e.zh: 猎人带着他最好的母猎犬来到原野。

e.en: Shakespeare mentions a {brach} in King Lear.
e.zh: 莎士比亚在《李尔王》中提到过母猎犬。

e.en: Gibbons {brachiate} effortlessly between branches.
e.zh: 长臂猿在树枝间轻松摆荡前进。

e.en: Children try to {brachiate} across the monkey bars.
e.zh: 孩子们试着用双臂荡过攀爬架。

brachiated.t: 以双臂攀荡前进（过去式）

e.en: The ape {brachiated} from tree to tree.
e.zh: 那只猿从一棵树荡到另一棵树。

e.en: He {brachiated} across the gym rings.
e.zh: 他用双臂荡过了体操吊环。

brachiates.t: 以双臂攀荡（第三人称单数）

e.en: A spider monkey {brachiates} faster than it walks.
e.zh: 蜘蛛猴用双臂攀荡比走路还快。

e.en: This species rarely {brachiates} on the ground.
e.zh: 这一物种很少在地面用双臂前进。

e.en: The orangutan was {brachiating} through the canopy.
e.zh: 那只红毛猩猩正在树冠间用双臂攀荡。

e.en: He hurt his shoulder while {brachiating}.
e.zh: 他在臂荡时伤到了肩膀。

e.en: They went {braching} on the moors at dawn.
e.zh: 他们拂晓时上沼地用母猎犬打猎。

e.en: Old hunters still recall the days of {braching}.
e.zh: 老猎人仍能忆起当年用母猎犬狩猎的日子。

e.en: The {brachiocephalic} artery branches off the aorta.
e.zh: 头臂动脉由主动脉分出。

e.en: Surgeons reviewed the {brachiocephalic} vein scan.
e.zh: 外科医生查看了头臂静脉的扫描图。

e.en: The museum's {brachiosaur} skeleton towered overhead.
e.zh: 博物馆的腕龙骨架高耸于头顶。

e.en: A {brachiosaur} could reach leaves twelve meters up.
e.zh: 腕龙能够吃到十二米高处的叶子。

e.en: The {brachiosaurus} was one of the tallest dinosaurs.
e.zh: 腕龙是最高的恐龙之一。

e.en: Children love the {brachiosaurus} model in the lobby.
e.zh: 孩子们喜欢大厅里那座腕龙模型。

e.en: Bernoulli solved the {brachistochrone} problem in 1696.
e.zh: 伯努利于1696年解决了最速降线问题。

e.en: The {brachistochrone} turns out to be a cycloid.
e.zh: 最速降线被证明是一段摆线。

e.en: The {brachium} extends from shoulder to elbow.
e.zh: 上臂从肩部延伸到肘部。

e.en: Anatomy texts label the {brachium} clearly.
e.zh: 解剖学课本对上臂有清晰的标注。

e.en: The crystal's {brachyaxis} is shorter than its macroaxis.
e.zh: 该晶体的短轴比长横轴更短。

e.en: Mineralogists measure the {brachyaxis} precisely.
e.zh: 矿物学家精确测量短轴的长度。

e.en: The skull belonged to a {brachycephal} from the region.
e.zh: 那颗头骨属于本地的一位短头型人。

e.en: Anthropologists classified him as a {brachycephal}.
e.zh: 人类学家将他归为短头型。

brachycephalic.t: 短头的；扁脸的（如哈巴狗）

e.en: Pugs are a {brachycephalic} breed prone to breathing issues.
e.zh: 哈巴狗是短头犬种，易有呼吸问题。

e.en: The vet warned about {brachycephalic} airway syndrome.
e.zh: 兽医提醒注意短头犬气道综合症。

e.en: Scholars debate the cause of European {brachycephalization}.
e.zh: 学者们争论欧洲人头骨短头化的成因。

e.en: {Brachycephalization} appears in skeletal records over time.
e.zh: 骨骼记录显示出头骨逐渐变短的趋势。

e.en: The skulls were uniformly {brachycephalous}.
e.zh: 那些头骨清一色都是短头型。

e.en: He described the population as {brachycephalous}.
e.zh: 他形容那一族群属于短头型。

e.en: The remains were classified as {brachycranial}.
e.zh: 那批遗骨被归类为短颅型。

e.en: {Brachycranial} indices vary widely by region.
e.zh: 短颅指数因地区而存在显著差异。

e.en: Fancy a quick {brekkie} before we head out?
e.zh: 出门前要不要快快吃个早饭？

e.en: She made bacon and eggs for {brekkie}.
e.zh: 她做了培根加蛋当早餐。

bremsstrahlung.t: 轫致辐射（带电粒子减速时发出的电磁辐射）

e.en: X-rays from the tube are produced mainly by {bremsstrahlung}.
e.zh: X 射线管发出的射线主要源于轫致辐射。

e.en: Electrons hitting the metal target emit {bremsstrahlung} radiation.
e.zh: 电子撞击金属靶时会发出轫致辐射。

bressummer.t: 承重横梁（建筑结构中支撑上方墙体的横梁）

e.en: The old shop front was held up by a heavy oak {bressummer}.
e.zh: 那家老店的门面由一根厚重的橡木承重横梁支撑。

e.en: They had to replace the rotting {bressummer} above the window.
e.zh: 他们不得不更换窗户上方那根腐朽的承重横梁。

brethren.t: 弟兄们；同道；教友（brother 的古旧复数）

e.en: The minister addressed his {brethren} from the pulpit.
e.zh: 牧师在讲坛上向众弟兄讲话。

e.en: He appealed to his fellow {brethren} in the union.
e.zh: 他向工会里的同道们发出呼吁。

bretzel.t: 椒盐脆饼（pretzel 的旧式拼法）

e.en: She ordered a warm {bretzel} from the street vendor.
e.zh: 她向街边小贩买了一个热乎乎的椒盐脆饼。

e.en: The bakery still spells it {bretzel} in the German style.
e.zh: 那家面包店仍按德式拼法写作 bretzel。

e.en: The vowel is marked with a {breve} to show it is short.
e.zh: 该元音上标有短音符号，表示读短音。

e.en: The choir held the {breve} for a full eight beats.
e.zh: 合唱团把那个二全音符整整唱满了八拍。

e.en: Several officers received {brevetcies} after the campaign.
e.zh: 战役结束后，数名军官获得了名誉军衔。

e.en: The records list all {brevetcies} awarded that year.
e.zh: 档案列出了那一年所有授予的名誉军衔。

brevetcy.t: 名誉军衔（高于实际职务的荣誉性军衔）

e.en: He was granted a {brevetcy} for gallantry in battle.
e.zh: 他因战斗中的英勇表现获授名誉军衔。

e.en: The {brevetcy} brought honor but no extra pay.
e.zh: 这一名誉军衔带来荣誉，却没有加薪。

e.en: The clerk prepared a {breviate} of the long report.
e.zh: 书记员把那份长篇报告整理成一份摘要。

e.en: She read the {breviate} before the meeting began.
e.zh: 她在会议开始前读了那份概要。

brevier.t: 小八号字（一种约八点大小的旧式印刷字号）

e.en: The footnotes were set in tiny {brevier} type.
e.zh: 脚注使用了细小的小八号铅字排印。

e.en: Old prayer books were often printed in {brevier}.
e.zh: 旧时的祈祷书常用小八号字印刷。

breviped.t: 短足的（指腿脚短小的鸟类或动物）

e.en: The naturalist described the bird as {breviped} and stout.
e.zh: 那位博物学家把这种鸟描述为短足而粗壮。

e.en: Many ground-dwelling species are {breviped} by nature.
e.zh: 许多地栖物种天生腿短。

e.en: The finch is a {brevirostrate} species adapted for cracking seeds.
e.zh: 这种雀是短喙物种，适合啄开种子。

e.en: Ornithologists noted the {brevirostrate} skull shape.
e.zh: 鸟类学家注意到那短喙型的头骨形态。

brevitoxin.t: 短裸甲藻毒素（一种引起赤潮中毒的神经毒素）

e.en: Shellfish near the red tide were contaminated with {brevitoxin}.
e.zh: 红潮附近的贝类被短裸甲藻毒素污染。

e.en: Researchers studied how {brevitoxin} affects nerve cells.
e.zh: 研究人员研究短裸甲藻毒素如何影响神经细胞。

e.en: The old {brew-house} has been turned into a museum.
e.zh: 那座老酿酒坊已被改建成博物馆。

e.en: Steam rose from the chimney of the village {brew-house}.
e.zh: 村里酿酒坊的烟囱里冒出蒸汽。

brew-kettle.t: 煮麦汁锅（酿酒用的大铜锅）

e.en: They poured the wort into the copper {brew-kettle}.
e.zh: 他们把麦汁倒进了那口铜制煮麦汁锅。

e.en: The {brew-kettle} bubbled all afternoon in the brewery.
e.zh: 煮麦汁锅在酒厂里咕嘟咕嘟煮了一整个下午。

brew-pub.t: 自酿啤酒馆（自家酿造并出售啤酒的小酒馆）

e.en: We met at a cozy {brew-pub} downtown.
e.zh: 我们约在市中心一家舒适的自酿啤酒馆见面。

e.en: The new {brew-pub} serves six house-made ales.
e.zh: 这家新开的自酿啤酒馆供应六款自制麦酒。

brew-up.t: 沏茶歇（英军俚语，指野外泡茶小憩）

e.en: The soldiers stopped for a quick {brew-up} by the road.
e.zh: 士兵们在路边停下来沏茶小歇。

e.en: Let's have a {brew-up} before we set off again.
e.zh: 我们再上路前先沏壶茶歇一歇吧。

e.en: The innkeeper offered us a strange dark {brewage}.
e.zh: 客栈老板给我们端来一种奇怪的深色酿酒。

e.en: Each monastery had its own secret {brewage}.
e.zh: 每座修道院都有自己秘制的酿造饮品。

e.en: The {brewhouse} dates back to the seventeenth century.
e.zh: 这座酿酒坊可追溯至十七世纪。

e.en: Tourists can tour the {brewhouse} every Saturday.
e.zh: 游客每周六可以参观这座啤酒厂。

brewis.t: 面包浸肉汤（一种古早的面包泡汤食物）

e.en: Grandma served us hot {brewis} on cold mornings.
e.zh: 奶奶在寒冷的早晨给我们端上热腾腾的面包浸汤。

e.en: Newfoundland fishermen ate salt cod with {brewis}.
e.zh: 纽芬兰的渔民把咸鳕鱼配着面包浸汤一起吃。

e.en: Grab me a cold {brewski} from the fridge.
e.zh: 从冰箱里给我拿瓶冰啤酒。

e.en: They cracked open a few {brewskis} after the game.
e.zh: 比赛结束后他们开了几瓶啤酒。

briard.t: 布里牧羊犬（一种法国长毛牧羊犬）

e.en: Their {briard} herded the sheep with practiced ease.
e.zh: 他们的布里牧羊犬熟练自如地驱赶着羊群。

e.en: The {briard} has a thick, shaggy coat.
e.zh: 布里牧羊犬有着厚实蓬乱的被毛。

briarean.t: 百手巨人般的；多手的（典出希腊神话 Briareus）

e.en: The factory had a {briarean} reach across many industries.
e.zh: 那家工厂的触角如百手巨人般伸入诸多行业。

e.en: He worked with {briarean} energy on a dozen projects.
e.zh: 他像百手巨人般精力充沛，同时操办十几个项目。

briarroot.t: 石南根（用于制作烟斗的木材）

e.en: His pipe was carved from a single piece of {briarroot}.
e.zh: 他的烟斗是用一整块石南根雕成的。

e.en: Fine {briarroot} comes mainly from the Mediterranean.
e.zh: 上等石南根主要产自地中海地区。

briarwood.t: 石南木（常用来做烟斗的硬木）

e.en: He smoked an old {briarwood} pipe by the fire.
e.zh: 他在火炉旁抽着一支旧石南木烟斗。

e.en: The shop sold pipes made of polished {briarwood}.
e.zh: 那家店出售用打磨过的石南木制成的烟斗。

e.en: They struggled through the {briary} hillside.
e.zh: 他们艰难地穿过那片荆棘丛生的山坡。

e.en: A {briary} hedge surrounded the abandoned cottage.
e.zh: 一道荆棘丛生的树篱围住了那座废弃的农舍。

bribability.t: 可被收买性；易受贿赂的程度

e.en: The report exposed the {bribability} of local officials.
e.zh: 该报告揭露了当地官员易被收买的程度。

e.en: Reformers worried about the {bribability} of the new judges.
e.zh: 改革者担心新任法官易受贿赂。

e.en: He insisted that no honest officer was {bribable}.
e.zh: 他坚持认为正直的警官是不会被收买的。

e.en: The smugglers searched for {bribable} guards at the border.
e.zh: 走私者在边境寻找可以贿赂的卫兵。

bribeable.t: 可被贿赂的（bribable 的异体拼写）

e.en: They assumed every customs agent was {bribeable}.
e.zh: 他们以为每个海关人员都可以被收买。

e.en: Few of the inspectors turned out to be {bribeable}.
e.zh: 事实证明几乎没有几个检查员是可以被贿赂的。

e.en: The wheat grew {breast-high} by midsummer.
e.zh: 到了仲夏，麦子长得齐胸高。

e.en: They waded through {breast-high} water to reach the boat.
e.zh: 他们涉过齐胸深的水走到船边。

e.en: The shipwright fitted a new {breasthook} into the bow.
e.zh: 造船工匠在船首装入了一块新的艏肘板。

e.en: A cracked {breasthook} can weaken the entire bow.
e.zh: 艏肘板开裂会削弱整个船首结构。

e.en: The statue depicted a {breastless} figure.
e.zh: 这尊雕像描绘了一个无胸的形象。

e.en: After surgery she felt self-conscious about being {breastless}.
e.zh: 术后她对自己失去乳房感到不自在。

e.en: She wore a silver {breastpin} on her lapel.
e.zh: 她在翻领上别了一枚银胸针。

e.en: The antique {breastpin} belonged to her grandmother.
e.zh: 那枚古董胸针是她祖母的遗物。

e.en: He leaned on the {breastrail} watching the harbor.
e.zh: 他倚着齐胸的栏杆望着港口。

e.en: The balcony's {breastrail} needed repainting.
e.zh: 阳台的护胸栏杆需要重新粉刷。

e.en: A massive oak {breastsummer} spans the shopfront.
e.zh: 一根巨大的橡木大梁横跨店面。

e.en: The {breastsummer} bears the weight of the upper floors.
e.zh: 这根承重梁支撑着楼上各层的重量。

breath-taking.t: 惊人的；令人叹为观止的

e.en: The view from the summit was {breath-taking}.
e.zh: 山顶的景色令人叹为观止。

e.en: Her performance showed {breath-taking} skill.
e.zh: 她的演出展现了惊人的技巧。

e.en: Police can {breathalyze} drivers at any checkpoint.
e.zh: 警察可以在任何检查点对司机进行酒精呼气检测。

e.en: They {breathalyze} every driver involved in a crash.
e.zh: 他们对每位发生事故的司机进行酒精检测。

e.en: He was {breathalyzed} after the minor collision.
e.zh: 小事故后他接受了酒精呼气检测。

e.en: All the drivers were {breathalyzed} at the roadblock.
e.zh: 路障处所有司机都被进行了酒精检测。

e.en: The officer routinely {breathalyzes} late-night drivers.
e.zh: 那名警官常规对深夜司机进行酒精检测。

e.en: She {breathalyzes} suspects before any arrest.
e.zh: 她在逮捕前会先对嫌疑人进行酒精检测。

breathalyzing.t: 正在进行酒精呼气检测

e.en: They spent the night {breathalyzing} drivers near the bar.
e.zh: 他们整晚在酒吧附近对司机进行酒精检测。

e.en: {Breathalyzing} every motorist would cause huge delays.
e.zh: 对每位司机都做酒精检测会造成严重延误。

e.en: Free divers train to extend their {breathhold}.
e.zh: 自由潜水员训练以延长闭气时间。

e.en: His {breathhold} record exceeded four minutes.
e.zh: 他的闭气纪录超过了四分钟。

e.en: She sang the lullaby {breathily}.
e.zh: 她带着气声唱起了摇篮曲。

e.en: He whispered {breathily} into the microphone.
e.zh: 他对着麦克风气声低语。

e.en: The diver checked his {breathing-pipe} before descending.
e.zh: 潜水员下潜前检查了呼吸管。

e.en: A blocked {breathing-pipe} can be fatal underwater.
e.zh: 呼吸管堵塞在水下可能致命。

e.en: The loan extension gave us some {breathing-space}.
e.zh: 贷款延期给了我们一些喘息空间。

e.en: Workers need {breathing-space} between shifts.
e.zh: 工人在轮班之间需要喘息时间。

breathing-spaces.t: 喘息时间；缓冲余地（复数）

e.en: The schedule offered few {breathing-spaces}.
e.zh: 日程几乎没有任何喘息空间。

e.en: Short {breathing-spaces} help prevent burnout.
e.zh: 短暂的喘息时间有助于防止过度疲劳。

e.en: Tectonic forces can {brecciate} the bedrock.
e.zh: 构造力可以使基岩形成角砾岩。

e.en: Heat and pressure {brecciate} the surrounding stone.
e.zh: 高温和压力会使周围岩石角砾化。

e.en: The cliff exposed a {brecciated} layer of limestone.
e.zh: 悬崖露出一层角砾化的石灰岩。

e.en: Geologists studied the {brecciated} rock samples.
e.zh: 地质学家研究了角砾岩化的岩石样本。

e.en: Faulting often {brecciates} the rocks along its plane.
e.zh: 断层活动常使断层面上的岩石角砾化。

e.en: Intense pressure {brecciates} the marble over time.
e.zh: 巨大压力日积月累使大理石角砾化。

e.en: The fault was actively {brecciating} the surrounding stone.
e.zh: 该断层正在使周围岩石角砾化。

e.en: {Brecciating} forces shaped the canyon walls.
e.zh: 角砾化作用塑造了峡谷的岩壁。

e.en: His honesty was {bred-in-the-bone}.
e.zh: 他的诚实是与生俱来的。

e.en: She has a {bred-in-the-bone} love of horses.
e.zh: 她对马有一种根深蒂固的喜爱。

e.en: The cloak's hem was edged with golden {brede}.
e.zh: 披风的下摆镶着金色刺绣。

e.en: She admired the intricate {brede} on the tapestry.
e.zh: 她欣赏挂毯上精美的刺绣。

e.en: The cook ladled hot {bree} into the bowls.
e.zh: 厨师把热腾腾的肉汤舀进碗里。

e.en: He warmed himself with a cup of {bree}.
e.zh: 他喝了一杯肉汤暖身子。

e.en: The hunter wore only a {breech-cloth} in the heat.
e.zh: 猎人在炎热中只穿一条缠腰布。

e.en: Museum displays included a beaded {breech-cloth}.
e.zh: 博物馆展出了一条饰珠缠腰布。

e.en: The army adopted {breech-loading} rifles in the 1860s.
e.zh: 军队在十九世纪六十年代采用了后膛装填步枪。

e.en: {Breech-loading} cannons fired far more quickly.
e.zh: 后膛装填的火炮射速快得多。

e.en: He cleaned the {breechblock} after every drill.
e.zh: 每次训练后他都清洁枪机。

e.en: A jammed {breechblock} rendered the rifle useless.
e.zh: 枪机卡住使步枪无法使用。

e.en: The warrior wore a deerskin {breechclout}.
e.zh: 那名战士穿着鹿皮缠腰布。

e.en: Children swam in nothing but a {breechclout}.
e.zh: 孩子们只穿着缠腰布游泳。

e.en: Several {breechclouts} hung drying by the fire.
e.zh: 几条缠腰布挂在火边晾干。

e.en: The dancers wore embroidered {breechclouts}.
e.zh: 舞者穿着刺绣的缠腰布。

e.en: The toddler ran {breechless} across the lawn.
e.zh: 那个小孩光着屁股跑过草坪。

e.en: Old satires depicted soldiers as {breechless} fools.
e.zh: 旧时讽刺画把士兵描绘成不穿裤子的蠢货。

e.en: He inherited a Civil War-era {breechloader}.
e.zh: 他继承了一支南北战争时期的后膛装填枪。

e.en: The {breechloader} fired three times faster than muzzle-loaders.
e.zh: 后膛装填枪比前装枪射速快三倍。

e.en: {Breechloading} weapons revolutionized infantry tactics.
e.zh: 后膛装填武器彻底改变了步兵战术。

e.en: He restored an antique {breechloading} shotgun.
e.zh: 他修复了一支古董后膛装填猎枪。

e.en: The keeper tended the {breeding-fire} all night.
e.zh: 饲养员整夜照看着育雏的炉火。

e.en: A steady {breeding-fire} kept the eggs warm.
e.zh: 持续的孵化炉火让蛋保持温暖。

e.en: Wetlands serve as {breeding-grounds} for many birds.
e.zh: 湿地是许多鸟类的繁殖地。

e.en: Slums became {breeding-grounds} for disease.
e.zh: 贫民窟成了疾病的温床。

e.en: He pulled on his old tweed {breeks}.
e.zh: 他套上了那条旧粗花呢裤子。

e.en: The shepherd's {breeks} were patched at the knees.
e.zh: 牧羊人的裤子膝盖处打了补丁。

e.en: The wall was built from {breeze-block}.
e.zh: 这堵墙是用煤渣砖砌成的。

e.en: He stacked the {breeze-block} beside the foundation.
e.zh: 他把煤渣砖堆在地基旁边。

e.en: They unloaded a pallet of {breeze-blocks}.
e.zh: 他们卸下了一托盘煤渣砖。

e.en: The shed was made of plain gray {breeze-blocks}.
e.zh: 棚屋是用普通灰色煤渣砖搭的。

e.en: The afternoon was hot and {breezeless}.
e.zh: 下午又热又无风。

e.en: Sailors hated the long {breezeless} doldrums.
e.zh: 水手们讨厌漫长无风的赤道无风带。

e.en: Today is much {breezier} than yesterday.
e.zh: 今天比昨天风大得多。

e.en: Her second novel has a {breezier} tone.
e.zh: 她的第二部小说语调更轻松。

e.en: I love the {breeziness} of her writing style.
e.zh: 我喜欢她写作风格的轻松活泼。

e.en: The coastal {breeziness} kept the city cool.
e.zh: 沿海的徐徐微风让这座城市凉爽宜人。

e.en: The anatomist marked the {bregma} on the skull.
e.zh: 解剖学家在颅骨上标出前囟点。

e.en: In infants the {bregma} remains soft for months.
e.zh: 婴儿的前囟点会保持柔软数月。

e.en: The {brehon} settled disputes under ancient Irish law.
e.zh: 那位古爱尔兰法官依古法裁决纠纷。

e.en: Each clan had its own respected {brehon}.
e.zh: 每个氏族都有自己受人尊敬的法官。

e.en: The {bribee} was later prosecuted alongside the briber.
e.zh: 受贿者后来与行贿者一同被起诉。

e.en: Investigators traced the money to an unnamed {bribee}.
e.zh: 调查人员追踪资金到一名不愿透露姓名的受贿者。

e.en: The {bribers} faced harsher penalties than the officials.
e.zh: 行贿者所受的惩罚比官员还重。

e.en: Several {bribers} were named in the leaked report.
e.zh: 泄露的报告中点名了几位行贿者。

e.en: Her shelves were crowded with dusty {bric-a-brac}.
e.zh: 她的架子上堆满了落灰的小摆设。

e.en: We sold the old {bric-a-brac} at the yard sale.
e.zh: 我们在庭院旧物拍卖中卖掉了那些零碎古玩。

e.en: The attic was full of grandmother's {bricabrac}.
e.zh: 阁楼里堆满了奶奶的小摆设。

e.en: He collects Victorian {bricabrac} from estate sales.
e.zh: 他从遗产拍卖中收集维多利亚时代的小古玩。

e.en: Many {brick-and-mortar} stores closed during the pandemic.
e.zh: 疫情期间许多实体店倒闭了。

e.en: They expanded from online into {brick-and-mortar} retail.
e.zh: 他们从线上扩展到了实体零售。

e.en: She wore a {brick-red} sweater that day.
e.zh: 她那天穿了一件砖红色的毛衣。

e.en: The walls were painted a warm {brick-red}.
e.zh: 墙壁被刷成温暖的砖红色。

e.en: Fine {brickdust} covered the demolition site.
e.zh: 细细的砖屑覆盖了拆除现场。

e.en: His boots were caked in {brickdust}.
e.zh: 他的靴子上结满了砖屑。

bricked-in.t: 用砖封砌的；砌砖封住的

e.en: The old fireplace had been {bricked-in} years ago.
e.zh: 那座旧壁炉多年前就被砖封住了。

e.en: They found a {bricked-in} doorway behind the wallpaper.
e.zh: 他们在墙纸后发现了一道被砖封死的门。

e.en: Workers toiled long hours at the {brickfield}.
e.zh: 工人们在砖窑场长时间辛苦劳作。

e.en: Smoke rose from the {brickfield} on the horizon.
e.zh: 地平线上的砖窑场升起阵阵浓烟。

e.en: A scorching {brickfielder} blew dust through Sydney.
e.zh: 一阵灼热的北风把尘土吹遍了悉尼。

e.en: The {brickfielder} pushed temperatures past forty degrees.
e.zh: 那阵热风把气温推到了四十度以上。

e.en: They began {bricking-up} the unused windows.
e.zh: 他们开始把不用的窗户砌砖封堵起来。

e.en: The {bricking-up} of the old door took a morning.
e.zh: 封堵那扇旧门花了一个上午。

e.en: The village still has an old {brickkiln} standing.
e.zh: 那个村子里还保留着一座旧砖窑。

e.en: Smoke billowed from the {brickkiln} all night.
e.zh: 砖窑里整夜冒着滚滚浓烟。

e.en: The ancient pottery was thin and {brickle}.
e.zh: 那古老的陶器又薄又脆。

e.en: Winter ice on the pond was {brickle} underfoot.
e.zh: 池塘上的冬冰踩上去十分易碎。

e.en: His grandfather was a {brickmaker} in the village.
e.zh: 他祖父在村里是个制砖工。

e.en: The {brickmaker} shaped clay from dawn till dusk.
e.zh: 那名制砖工从清晨到日暮都在塑泥。

e.en: {Brickmaking} was once a major local industry.
e.zh: 制砖业曾是当地的主要产业。

e.en: He learned {brickmaking} from his father.
e.zh: 他从父亲那里学会了制砖手艺。

e.en: The {brickmason} laid each row with care.
e.zh: 砌砖工小心地砌好每一层。

e.en: She apprenticed under a master {brickmason}.
e.zh: 她跟着一位老砖瓦匠学徒。

e.en: Online retailers eventually opened {bricks-and-mortar} shops.
e.zh: 网络零售商最终开起了实体店。

e.en: He prefers {bricks-and-mortar} bookstores to websites.
e.zh: 比起网店,他更喜欢实体书店。

e.en: The walls had a rough, {bricky} texture.
e.zh: 墙面有一种粗糙似砖的质感。

e.en: My uncle worked as a {bricky} for decades.
e.zh: 我叔叔做了几十年的砌砖工。

e.en: He won the frame with a clever {bricole}.
e.zh: 他用一记巧妙的反弹击球赢下了一局。

e.en: The {bricole} sent the ball into the corner pocket.
e.zh: 那次反弹击球把球打进了角袋。

e.en: The poem celebrates her {bridalty} and joy.
e.zh: 这首诗颂扬了她的新娘身份和喜悦。

e.en: Old verses speak of her radiant {bridalty}.
e.zh: 古老的诗篇述说着她光彩照人的新娘风采。

e.en: The {bride-cake} stood three tiers tall.
e.zh: 那个婚礼蛋糕足有三层高。

e.en: Guests took home slices of the {bride-cake}.
e.zh: 宾客们各自带回了一块婚礼蛋糕。

e.en: His family paid a substantial {bride-price}.
e.zh: 他家付了一笔可观的彩礼。

e.en: Customs around the {bride-price} vary by region.
e.zh: 各地关于聘礼的习俗各不相同。

e.en: The {bride-to-be} chose her dress yesterday.
e.zh: 准新娘昨天挑好了礼服。

e.en: Her friends threw a party for the {bride-to-be}.
e.zh: 朋友们为这位准新娘办了个聚会。

e.en: They cut the {bridecake} together to applause.
e.zh: 他们在掌声中一起切开了婚礼蛋糕。

e.en: The {bridecake} was decorated with sugar roses.
e.zh: 婚礼蛋糕上装饰着糖霜玫瑰。

e.en: Several {brides-to-be} attended the bridal expo.
e.zh: 几位准新娘参加了婚博会。

e.en: The shop caters to {brides-to-be} on a budget.
e.zh: 这家店面向预算有限的准新娘们。

e.en: His brother served as the chief {bridesman}.
e.zh: 他的哥哥担任了首席伴郎。

e.en: The {bridesman} gave a heartfelt toast.
e.zh: 伴郎致了一段感人的祝酒辞。

e.en: The {bridesmen} stood beside the groom in matching suits.
e.zh: 伴郎们身着同款西装站在新郎身旁。

e.en: All four {bridesmen} were childhood friends.
e.zh: 四位伴郎都是童年好友。

bridge-building.t: 建桥；增进沟通；化解隔阂

e.en: Diplomatic {bridge-building} eased tensions between the two states.
e.zh: 外交上的化解工作缓解了两国紧张局势。

e.en: He devoted his career to {bridge-building} engineering.
e.zh: 他一生致力于桥梁建造工程。

e.en: The gap between their views is {bridgeable}.
e.zh: 他们观点之间的分歧是可以弥合的。

e.en: Engineers said the canyon was barely {bridgeable}.
e.zh: 工程师说这道峡谷几乎无法架桥。

e.en: The carpenter cut notches into the {bridgeboard}.
e.zh: 木匠在楼梯斜梁上凿出了缺口。

e.en: A solid {bridgeboard} supports each step.
e.zh: 一根结实的斜梁支撑着每一级台阶。

e.en: She is known as a {bridgebuilder} between rival camps.
e.zh: 她以在敌对阵营之间架起桥梁而著称。

e.en: The veteran {bridgebuilder} has worked on dozens of spans.
e.zh: 那位资深造桥师参与过几十座桥的建设。

e.en: The {bridgeless} river forced travelers to ford it.
e.zh: 这条没有桥的河迫使旅人涉水而过。

e.en: For centuries the gorge remained {bridgeless}.
e.zh: 几个世纪以来,这道峡谷上始终没有桥。

e.en: He tugged the {bridle-rein} to steady his horse.
e.zh: 他拉了拉缰绳让马稳住。

e.en: The leather {bridle-rein} had cracked with age.
e.zh: 那条皮缰绳因年久而开裂。

e.en: The young mare is already {bridlewise}.
e.zh: 这匹小母马已经能听从缰绳指挥了。

e.en: A {bridlewise} horse responds to the slightest signal.
e.zh: 听话的马对最轻微的信号都有反应。

e.en: The rider adjusted the {bridoon} before mounting.
e.zh: 骑手在上马前调整了轻马衔。

e.en: A double bridle uses both a curb and a {bridoon}.
e.zh: 双缰马具同时使用衔铁和轻马嚼子。

briefless.t: 没案子的(律师);没委托业务的

e.en: The young {briefless} barrister waited for his first client.
e.zh: 那位年轻的无案律师在等待他的第一位客户。

e.en: He spent years as a {briefless} lawyer in chambers.
e.zh: 他在律所里做了多年没有案子的律师。

e.en: Fine pipes are carved from {brierroot}.
e.zh: 上等烟斗是用石楠根雕成的。

e.en: He polished the {brierroot} bowl with care.
e.zh: 他细心地打磨那只石楠根烟斗碗。

e.en: The pipe was carved from aged {brierwood}.
e.zh: 那只烟斗是用陈年石楠木雕成的。

e.en: {Brierwood} resists heat better than most timbers.
e.zh: 石楠木比多数木材更耐热。

e.en: They struggled through the {briery} thicket.
e.zh: 他们艰难地穿过荆棘丛生的灌木林。

e.en: A {briery} path led down to the stream.
e.zh: 一条满是荆棘的小径通向溪边。

e.en: Three {brigadier-generals} attended the briefing.
e.zh: 三位准将出席了简报会。

e.en: The {brigadier-generals} signed the joint statement.
e.zh: 几位准将签署了联合声明。

brigalow.t: 澳大利亚相思树；布里加洛树

e.en: They cleared a stand of {brigalow} for the pasture.
e.zh: 他们砍掉一片相思树以开辟牧场。

e.en: The {brigalow} thrives in dry inland soils.
e.zh: 这种相思树在干旱内陆土壤中生长良好。

e.en: The mountain passes were plagued by {brigandage}.
e.zh: 山口一带饱受土匪劫掠之苦。

e.en: He was hanged for {brigandage} on the highway.
e.zh: 他因在公路上行劫而被绞死。

e.en: The knight wore a heavy {brigandine} into battle.
e.zh: 骑士穿着厚重的铆钉布甲上阵。

e.en: Museum curators restored a fifteenth-century {brigandine}.
e.zh: 博物馆馆长修复了一件十五世纪的铆钉布甲。

e.en: He gave a {brigandish} grin from under his hat.
e.zh: 他从帽檐下露出一个土匪般的笑容。

e.en: Her {brigandish} swagger amused the crowd.
e.zh: 她那匪气十足的大摇大摆逗乐了众人。

e.en: The region descended into open {brigandism}.
e.zh: 这一地区陷入了公然的盗匪横行。

e.en: He denounced corporate {brigandism} in his speech.
e.zh: 他在演讲中谴责企业的强盗作风。

bright-eyed.t: 目光炯炯的；兴致勃勃的

e.en: The children arrived {bright-eyed} and excited.
e.zh: 孩子们目光闪亮、兴奋地来到这里。

e.en: She was {bright-eyed} on her first day at work.
e.zh: 上班第一天她兴致勃勃。

bright-line.t: 清晰明确的；界限分明的

e.en: The court drew a {bright-line} rule on free speech.
e.zh: 法院在言论自由问题上划定了一条明确界线。

e.en: There is no {bright-line} test for fairness.
e.zh: 对于公平并没有一条非黑即白的判定标准。

e.en: She wore a {brightly-coloured} scarf.
e.zh: 她戴着一条颜色鲜艳的围巾。

e.en: The market sold {brightly-coloured} fabrics.
e.zh: 市场上卖着色彩鲜艳的布料。

brightsome.t: 明亮的；光辉的（古旧用法）

e.en: A {brightsome} dawn lit the meadow.
e.zh: 明亮的黎明照亮了草地。

e.en: He sang in a {brightsome} mood.
e.zh: 他心情爽朗地唱着歌。

brightwork.t: （船上的）光亮金属件或抛光木器

e.en: The sailors polished the {brightwork} every morning.
e.zh: 水手们每天早上都擦亮船上的金属件。

e.en: Salt spray dulled the yacht's {brightwork}.
e.zh: 盐雾让游艇上抛光的部件失去了光泽。

e.en: She chose a {brilliant-cut} diamond for the ring.
e.zh: 她为这枚戒指挑了一颗明亮式切工的钻石。

e.en: The pendant featured a {brilliant-cut} sapphire.
e.zh: 吊坠上镶着一颗明亮式切工的蓝宝石。

e.en: He slicked his hair back with {brilliantine}.
e.zh: 他用发蜡把头发往后梳得油亮。

e.en: The barber kept a tin of {brilliantine} on the shelf.
e.zh: 理发师在架子上放着一罐亮发油。

e.en: Her eyes were {brimfull} of tears.
e.zh: 她的眼睛里满是泪水。

e.en: The bucket was {brimfull} of fresh milk.
e.zh: 桶里装满了新鲜牛奶。

e.en: He wore a small {brimless} cap.
e.zh: 他戴着一顶小小的无檐帽。

e.en: The waiter handed her a {brimless} hat.
e.zh: 侍者递给她一顶无檐的帽子。

e.en: A {brimstony} smell rose from the geyser.
e.zh: 间歇泉冒出一股硫磺味。

e.en: The preacher's {brimstony} sermon shook the room.
e.zh: 牧师那充满硫磺味的布道震撼了全场。

e.en: A {brinded} cow grazed by the river.
e.zh: 一头有斑纹的牛在河边吃草。

e.en: The poet praised the {brinded} hills at dusk.
e.zh: 诗人赞美黄昏时分斑驳的山色。

bringdown.t: 扫兴的事；令人失望的事

e.en: His bad mood was a real {bringdown}.
e.zh: 他的坏心情真是大煞风景。

e.en: The cancellation was a total {bringdown}.
e.zh: 取消活动让大家彻底扫兴。

e.en: Her gentle {bringing-up} showed in her manners.
e.zh: 她温和的教养在举止中显露无遗。

e.en: The {bringing-up} of children takes patience.
e.zh: 养育孩子需要耐心。

e.en: I love the {brininess} of fresh oysters.
e.zh: 我喜欢新鲜牡蛎的咸鲜味。

e.en: The soup had a pleasant {brininess}.
e.zh: 这汤带有怡人的咸鲜味。

e.en: The pond water tasted {brinish}.
e.zh: 池水尝起来微咸。

e.en: A {brinish} breeze blew off the marsh.
e.zh: 一阵带着咸味的风从沼泽吹来。

e.en: He was a notorious {brinkman} in negotiations.
e.zh: 他在谈判中是出了名的边缘策略高手。

e.en: Only a true {brinkman} would push that hard.
e.zh: 只有真正搞边缘政策的人才会逼到这种地步。

e.en: Cold War {brinksmanship} terrified the world.
e.zh: 冷战时期的边缘政策让世界胆战心惊。

e.en: His budget {brinksmanship} alarmed investors.
e.zh: 他在预算上的冒险策略让投资者惊慌。

e.en: She wore earrings set with diamond {briolettes}.
e.zh: 她戴着镶有水滴形钻石的耳环。

e.en: The pendant featured a single sapphire {briolette}.
e.zh: 吊坠上有一颗水滴形切割的蓝宝石。

e.en: He tossed another {briquet} on the grill.
e.zh: 他又往烤架上扔了一块煤砖。

e.en: The factory makes peat {briquets} for heating.
e.zh: 这家工厂生产用于取暖的泥炭煤砖。

e.en: Engineers measured the {brisance} of the new explosive.
e.zh: 工程师测量了新型炸药的爆裂力。

e.en: High {brisance} makes the charge ideal for demolition.
e.zh: 高猛度使这种装药非常适合爆破作业。

brisken.t: 使变得轻快；振奋（古旧用法）

e.en: The cool air seemed to {brisken} her step.
e.zh: 凉爽的空气似乎让她的步伐变得轻快。

e.en: A cup of tea will {brisken} you up.
e.zh: 一杯茶会让你精神一振。

e.en: He opened a tin of {brisling} for lunch.
e.zh: 他打开一罐小鲱鱼当午餐。

e.en: Norwegian {brisling} is canned in olive oil.
e.zh: 挪威的小鲱鱼用橄榄油装罐。

e.en: Ancient {bristlecone} pines cling to the high ridges.
e.zh: 古老的刺果松紧贴在高高的山脊上。

e.en: A {bristlecone} can live for thousands of years.
e.zh: 一棵刺果松可以活上数千年。

e.en: The cactus had {bristlelike} hairs along its stem.
e.zh: 这种仙人掌的茎上长着鬃毛状的细刺。

e.en: Tiny {bristlelike} fibers covered the leaf.
e.zh: 细小的刚毛状纤维覆盖着叶面。

e.en: A {bristletail} darted across the bathroom floor.
e.zh: 一只鬃尾虫从浴室地板上窜过。

e.en: Entomologists study {bristletails} as primitive insects.
e.zh: 昆虫学家把鬃尾虫作为原始昆虫来研究。

bristlier.t: 更多刚毛的；更易动怒的

e.en: His beard grew {bristlier} by the week.
e.zh: 他的胡子一周比一周更扎手。
