e.en: He teaches {bushcraft} to scouts every summer.
e.zh: 他每年夏天教童子军野外生存技能。

e.en: Good {bushcraft} can save your life in the wild.
e.zh: 过硬的野外技能能在荒野中救命。

e.en: Old records still mention a duty called {bushelage}.
e.zh: 旧档案仍提到一种叫蒲式耳税的税。

e.en: Farmers paid {bushelage} on every grain shipment.
e.zh: 农民每批谷物都要缴蒲式耳税。

e.en: She picked apples into a heavy {bushelbasket}.
e.zh: 她把苹果摘进一个沉甸甸的大筐里。

e.en: A {bushelbasket} of corn sat beside the door.
e.zh: 门旁放着一大筐玉米。

e.en: The seasoned {bushfighter} knew every jungle trail.
e.zh: 那名老练的丛林战士熟悉每一条丛林小径。

e.en: Each {bushfighter} carried only a light pack.
e.zh: 每个丛林战士都只背着轻装行囊。

e.en: Their unit specialized in tropical {bushfighting}.
e.zh: 他们的部队专攻热带丛林作战。

e.en: {Bushfighting} demands stealth and patience.
e.zh: 丛林作战需要隐蔽和耐心。

e.en: A {bushfire} swept across the dry hillside overnight.
e.zh: 一场丛林大火一夜之间席卷了干燥的山坡。

e.en: Firefighters battled the {bushfire} for several days.
e.zh: 消防员与这场丛林大火奋战了好几天。

e.en: The hunters went out at dawn to catch a {bushfowl}.
e.zh: 猎人黎明出发去捕一只林鸡。

e.en: A startled {bushfowl} darted through the underbrush.
e.zh: 一只受惊的林鸡从灌木丛中窜出。

e.en: The mason used a {bushhammer} to texture the stone.
e.zh: 石匠用凿毛锤给石材做出粗糙纹理。

e.en: Fine dust flew up with every {bushhammer} blow.
e.zh: 每一锤凿毛锤都扬起细尘。

e.en: {Bushido} guided every samurai's daily conduct.
e.zh: 武士道指导着每位武士的日常言行。

e.en: Loyalty stood at the heart of {bushido}.
e.zh: 忠诚是武士道的核心。

bushie.t: 澳洲乡下人；丛林居民（俚语）

e.en: He grew up as a {bushie} in the outback.
e.zh: 他在内陆地区长大,是个地道的丛林人。

e.en: Locals affectionately call him a true {bushie}.
e.zh: 当地人亲切地叫他真正的丛林佬。

e.en: He has the {bushiest} eyebrows I've ever seen.
e.zh: 他长着我见过最浓密的眉毛。

e.en: Pick the {bushiest} branches for the wreath.
e.zh: 挑最茂密的枝条来做花环。

e.en: His hair grew {bushily} around his ears.
e.zh: 他的头发在耳边长得蓬蓬松松。

e.en: The vine spread {bushily} over the wall.
e.zh: 藤蔓在墙上长得密密匝匝。

e.en: I love the {bushiness} of this fern.
e.zh: 我喜欢这株蕨类的茂密感。

e.en: Trim the hedge to reduce its {bushiness}.
e.zh: 修剪一下树篱,让它别那么蓬。

e.en: Late-night comedians repeated each new {bushism} on TV.
e.zh: 深夜喜剧节目把每个新的布什式口误都拿来重播。

e.en: That awkward phrase quickly became a famous {bushism}.
e.zh: 那句别扭的话很快成了著名的布什式口误。

e.en: Kangaroos hopped across the open {bushland}.
e.zh: 袋鼠在开阔的丛林地上跳跃。

e.en: The reserve protects native Australian {bushland}.
e.zh: 该保护区保护着澳洲本土的丛林地带。

e.en: His {bushmanship} impressed even the local guides.
e.zh: 他的丛林本领连当地向导都折服。

e.en: Years of {bushmanship} kept him alive out there.
e.zh: 多年的丛林本领让他在荒野中活了下来。

e.en: A {bushpig} rooted around in the muddy clearing.
e.zh: 一头丛林猪在泥泞的空地上拱来拱去。

e.en: Farmers worry about {bushpig} damage to their crops.
e.zh: 农民担心丛林猪糟蹋庄稼。

bushranger.t: 澳洲丛林大盗；丛林匪徒

e.en: Ned Kelly is the most famous Australian {bushranger}.
e.zh: 内德·凯利是澳洲最有名的丛林大盗。

e.en: The {bushranger} robbed the gold-carrying coach.
e.zh: 那名丛林大盗抢劫了运金马车。

e.en: He was hanged for {bushranging} during the gold rush.
e.zh: 他在淘金热期间因丛林劫掠被处以绞刑。

e.en: {Bushranging} thrived in colonial Australia.
e.zh: 丛林劫掠在殖民时期的澳洲十分猖獗。

e.en: A tiny {bushtit} flitted among the oak branches.
e.zh: 一只小巧的长尾山雀在橡树枝间飞来飞去。

e.en: We spotted a {bushtit} nest hanging from the limb.
e.zh: 我们发现树枝上挂着一个长尾山雀窝。

e.en: Lions roam freely on the South African {bushveld}.
e.zh: 狮群在南非的灌丛草原上自由游荡。

e.en: The {bushveld} stretches for hundreds of miles.
e.zh: 灌丛草原绵延数百英里。

e.en: His excuse for being late was complete {bushwa}.
e.zh: 他迟到的理由完全是胡扯。

e.en: Don't feed me that political {bushwa}.
e.zh: 少跟我灌输那些政治废话。

e.en: We went {bushwalking} in the national park last weekend.
e.zh: 我们上周末在国家公园丛林徒步。

e.en: {Bushwalking} is a popular pastime in Australia.
e.zh: 丛林徒步是澳洲很受欢迎的消遣。

bushy-tailed.t: 尾巴蓬松的；精神抖擞的

e.en: She arrived bright-eyed and {bushy-tailed} for her first day.
e.zh: 她神采奕奕地来报到上班第一天。

e.en: A {bushy-tailed} squirrel watched us from the fence.
e.zh: 一只尾巴蓬松的松鼠从篱笆上看着我们。

buoyage.t: 浮标系统；航道浮标布置

e.en: The harbor's {buoyage} guides ships safely to port.
e.zh: 港口的浮标系统引导船只安全入港。

e.en: Modern {buoyage} uses standardized colors and shapes.
e.zh: 现代航标系统采用统一的颜色和形状。

buoyance.t: 浮力；轻快活泼；活力充沛

e.en: The cork's {buoyance} kept the line afloat.
e.zh: 软木塞的浮力让钓线浮在水面上。

e.en: Her natural {buoyance} lifted everyone's spirits.
e.zh: 她天生的活泼劲儿鼓舞了大家。

e.en: I worked all day and got {bupkis}.
e.zh: 我忙了一整天，结果什么也没捞到。

e.en: He knows {bupkis} about cooking.
e.zh: 他对烹饪一窍不通。

buppie.t: 黑人雅皮士；黑人都市新贵

e.en: The cafe was full of stylish {buppies}.
e.zh: 咖啡馆里坐满了时髦的黑人雅皮士。

e.en: She's a typical {buppie} working downtown.
e.zh: 她是典型的黑人都市新贵，在市中心上班。

e.en: Anglers caught a large {burbot} through the ice.
e.zh: 钓友们凿冰钓上一条大江鳕。

e.en: The {burbot} is the only freshwater cod.
e.zh: 江鳕是唯一栖息于淡水的鳕科鱼类。

e.en: The ballad praised a young {burd}.
e.zh: 那首民谣歌颂一位年轻少女。

e.en: A small {burd} sang from the tower.
e.zh: 一只小鸟在塔楼上鸣唱。

e.en: She walked home {burdenless} after finishing the project.
e.zh: 项目完成后，她无忧无虑地回家了。

e.en: He longed for a {burdenless} life by the sea.
e.zh: 他向往海边那种了无牵挂的生活。

bureaucrat-capitalist.t: 官僚资本主义的；官僚资产阶级的

e.en: The pamphlet attacked the {bureaucrat-capitalist} elite.
e.zh: 这本小册子抨击官僚资本主义精英。

e.en: He criticized {bureaucrat-capitalist} reforms in the speech.
e.zh: 他在演讲中批判官僚资本主义式的改革。

bureaucratise.t: 使官僚化；变得官样文章

e.en: Reforms began to {bureaucratise} the small charity.
e.zh: 改革开始让这家小型慈善机构变得官僚化。

e.en: Critics fear new rules will further {bureaucratise} healthcare.
e.zh: 批评者担心新规会让医疗体系更趋官僚化。

bureaucratism.t: 官僚主义；繁文缛节作风

e.en: Complaints about hospital {bureaucratism} keep growing.
e.zh: 对医院官僚主义的投诉不断增加。

e.en: He blamed delays on rampant {bureaucratism}.
e.zh: 他把延误归咎于盛行的官僚主义。

bureaucratist.t: 官僚主义者；推崇官僚作风者

e.en: The reformer denounced every {bureaucratist} in the ministry.
e.zh: 改革者痛斥部里每一个官僚主义者。

e.en: Old {bureaucratists} resisted the open-door policy.
e.zh: 守旧的官僚主义者抵制开放政策。

bureaucratize.t: 使官僚化；让事务变得繁琐

e.en: Critics warn the policy will {bureaucratize} schools further.
e.zh: 批评者警告该政策将让学校更趋官僚化。

e.en: Mergers tend to {bureaucratize} small startups.
e.zh: 并购往往会让小型创业公司变得官僚化。

bureaucratizes.t: 使变得官僚化；动词第三人称单数

e.en: Each new department {bureaucratizes} the workflow further.
e.zh: 每增设一个部门都让工作流程更趋官僚化。

e.en: She argues regulation always {bureaucratizes} small business.
e.zh: 她认为监管总是把小企业拖入官僚作风。

buret.t: 滴定管；化学实验用量管

e.en: Fill the {buret} with the standard solution.
e.zh: 把标准溶液装入滴定管。

e.en: She read the {buret} carefully at eye level.
e.zh: 她平视刻度，仔细读取滴定管的读数。

burette.t: 滴定管；化学实验用玻璃量管

e.en: Add the acid drop by drop from the {burette}.
e.zh: 用滴定管把酸一滴一滴地加进去。

e.en: The lab needs a clean {burette} for titration.
e.zh: 实验室做滴定需要一支干净的滴定管。

burgage.t: 城镇土地保有权；中世纪市镇租地

e.en: Old records list every {burgage} in the town.
e.zh: 旧档案登记着镇上的每一份市镇租地。

e.en: He inherited a small {burgage} near the wall.
e.zh: 他继承了城墙附近一小块市镇租地。

e.en: The yacht flew its club {burgee} proudly.
e.zh: 游艇骄傲地悬挂着俱乐部的三角旗。

e.en: A blue {burgee} fluttered from the masthead.
e.zh: 一面蓝色三角旗在桅顶飘扬。

burghal.t: 自治市镇的；与城镇相关的

e.en: The charter laid out {burghal} rights and duties.
e.zh: 宪章规定了自治市的权利和义务。

e.en: Old maps show the {burghal} boundaries clearly.
e.zh: 古地图清晰标出市镇的边界。

burghership.t: 市民身份；自治市公民资格

e.en: He earned full {burghership} after twenty years.
e.zh: 他在二十年后获得了完整的市民身份。

e.en: {Burghership} brought tax privileges and trade rights.
e.zh: 市民身份带来税收优待和经商权利。

burglar-alarm.t: 防盗警报器；防盗报警系统

e.en: Our new {burglar-alarm} woke the whole street.
e.zh: 我们家新装的防盗警报器吵醒了整条街。

e.en: Always set the {burglar-alarm} before leaving.
e.zh: 出门前一定要打开防盗警报器。

burglarious.t: 入室盗窃的；行窃性质的

e.en: Police found {burglarious} tools in the van.
e.zh: 警方在那辆面包车里发现了行窃工具。

e.en: He was charged with {burglarious} intent.
e.zh: 他被控有入室行窃的意图。

burglariously.t: 以盗窃方式；入室行窃地

e.en: The thief entered the building {burglariously} at night.
e.zh: 窃贼夜里以入室盗窃的方式潜入大楼。

e.en: Goods taken {burglariously} must be returned.
e.zh: 通过盗窃手段取得的物品必须归还。

e.en: Thieves tried to {burglarise} the corner shop.
e.zh: 窃贼企图闯入街角的小店行窃。

e.en: Someone {burglarised} our flat last weekend.
e.zh: 上个周末有人闯进我们公寓盗窃。

burglarproof.t: 防盗的；不易被入室盗窃的

e.en: The store has {burglarproof} windows and doors.
e.zh: 这家商店装了防盗的窗户和门。

e.en: No safe is truly {burglarproof}.
e.zh: 没有哪个保险柜是真正防盗的。

e.en: The {burgomaster} welcomed the visiting delegation.
e.zh: 市长亲自欢迎来访代表团。

e.en: An old portrait of the city's first {burgomaster} hangs there.
e.zh: 那里挂着这座城市首任市长的旧画像。

burgonet.t: 轻便头盔；勃艮第式头盔

e.en: The knight's {burgonet} bore engraved patterns.
e.zh: 骑士的轻便头盔上刻有花纹。

e.en: Museums display many ornate {burgonets}.
e.zh: 博物馆陈列着许多装饰华丽的勃艮第头盔。

e.en: Sailors ate hot {burgoo} every morning.
e.zh: 水手每天早上喝热腾腾的厚粥。

e.en: The festival serves homemade Kentucky {burgoo}.
e.zh: 节日上供应自制的肯塔基浓肉粥。

burgoos.t: 厚粥的复数形式；多种浓肉粥

e.en: The cookbook lists three traditional {burgoos}.
e.zh: 食谱里列出了三种传统厚粥。

e.en: Different counties cook their own {burgoos}.
e.zh: 不同郡县各自烹制自家风味的厚粥。

e.en: The {burgrave} ruled the castle for decades.
e.zh: 这位城堡伯爵统治该城堡数十年。

e.en: An old chronicle lists every {burgrave} by name.
e.zh: 古老编年史一一列出每位城堡伯爵的名字。

burhel.t: 蓝羊；岩羊；喜马拉雅野生绵羊

e.en: Hikers spotted a {burhel} on the cliff.
e.zh: 徒步者在峭壁上发现了一只岩羊。

e.en: The {burhel} is hunted by snow leopards.
e.zh: 岩羊是雪豹捕猎的对象。

e.en: The old {burial-ground} sits behind the church.
e.zh: 古老的墓地坐落在教堂后面。

e.en: Archaeologists excavated a Bronze Age {burial-ground}.
e.zh: 考古学家发掘了一处青铜时代的墓地。

e.en: The dog became a famous {burier} of bones.
e.zh: 那只狗成了出名的埋骨头能手。

e.en: Workers acted as {buriers} after the storm.
e.zh: 风暴过后，工人充当掩埋者。

burinist.t: 雕刻师；用刻刀雕版的工匠

e.en: The {burinist} carved fine lines into the copper plate.
e.zh: 这位雕刻师在铜版上刻出精细的线条。

e.en: Old prints often bear the {burinist}'s signature.
e.zh: 古版画上常有雕刻师的签名。

e.en: The {burlesqueen} dazzled the audience with her costume.
e.zh: 那位滑稽脱衣舞女演员的服装令观众惊艳。

e.en: Famous {burlesqueens} of the era still inspire performers.
e.zh: 那个时代著名的滑稽脱衣舞女演员至今仍激励着表演者。

e.en: He moved {burlily} through the dense crowd.
e.zh: 他壮硕地穿过密集的人群。

e.en: The wrestler stood {burlily} in the ring.
e.zh: 摔跤手魁梧地站在擂台上。

e.en: His {burliness} made him an obvious choice for the role.
e.zh: 他的魁梧身材使他成为该角色的不二人选。

e.en: The coat couldn't quite hide his {burliness}.
e.zh: 外套也难以遮住他的壮硕身材。

burn-off.t: 烧除；燃烧清理；卡路里消耗

e.en: The farmers conducted a controlled {burn-off} to clear the land.
e.zh: 农民们进行了有控制的烧荒以清理土地。

e.en: Calorie {burn-off} during exercise varies by intensity.
e.zh: 运动中卡路里消耗因强度而异。

e.en: Please separate {burnable} waste from recyclables.
e.zh: 请将可燃垃圾与可回收物分开。

e.en: The shed contained mostly {burnable} materials.
e.zh: 棚子里大多是可燃材料。

e.en: After years of overtime, he felt completely {burned-out}.
e.zh: 多年加班后，他感到彻底身心俱疲。

e.en: We replaced the {burned-out} bulbs in the hallway.
e.zh: 我们换掉了走廊里烧坏的灯泡。

burnettize.t: 用氯化锌浸渍木材防腐

e.en: Workers {burnettize} the timber to prevent rot.
e.zh: 工人们用氯化锌处理木材以防腐烂。

e.en: The factory will {burnettize} all railroad ties.
e.zh: 工厂会对所有铁路枕木做防腐处理。

burnettized.t: 经氯化锌防腐处理过的

e.en: The {burnettized} planks lasted decades longer.
e.zh: 经氯化锌处理过的木板使用寿命延长了数十年。

e.en: All ties were {burnettized} before installation.
e.zh: 所有枕木在铺设前都经过了防腐处理。

burnettizing.t: 用氯化锌防腐处理木材

e.en: {Burnettizing} was once common for railway sleepers.
e.zh: 氯化锌防腐处理曾普遍用于铁路枕木。

e.en: The mill specialized in {burnettizing} timber.
e.zh: 这家厂专门从事木材防腐处理。

burning-in.t: 老化测试；摄影局部加深

e.en: The technician spent hours {burning-in} the new monitor.
e.zh: 技术员花了数小时对新显示器进行老化测试。

e.en: Photographers use {burning-in} to darken parts of a print.
e.zh: 摄影师用局部加深法使照片的某些部分变暗。

burnoose.t: 阿拉伯人的连帽长斗篷

e.en: The traveler wrapped himself in a thick {burnoose}.
e.zh: 旅行者裹紧了厚厚的连帽斗篷。

e.en: His {burnoose} flapped in the desert wind.
e.zh: 他的连帽斗篷在沙漠风中飘动。

burnoosed.t: 穿着阿拉伯连帽斗篷的

e.en: {Burnoosed} riders crossed the dunes at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明时分，披着连帽斗篷的骑手穿越沙丘。

e.en: A {burnoosed} merchant approached our caravan.
e.zh: 一位身披连帽斗篷的商人向我们的商队走来。

burnous.t: 阿拉伯人穿的连帽斗篷

e.en: She bought a wool {burnous} at the souk.
e.zh: 她在集市买了一件羊毛连帽斗篷。

e.en: His {burnous} kept out the morning chill.
e.zh: 他的连帽斗篷挡住了清晨的寒意。

e.en: The desert guide wore a faded {burnouse}.
e.zh: 沙漠向导穿着一件褪色的连帽斗篷。

e.en: She admired the embroidered {burnouse}.
e.zh: 她欣赏那件绣花连帽斗篷。

e.en: The {burnt-out} car still smoldered by the roadside.
e.zh: 那辆烧毁的汽车仍在路边冒烟。

e.en: After ten years in nursing, she felt {burnt-out}.
e.zh: 做了十年护士，她感到身心俱疲。

e.en: The dentist switched to a finer {burr-drill}.
e.zh: 牙医换上了更细的牙钻。

e.en: The jeweler used a tiny {burr-drill} to shape the setting.
e.zh: 珠宝匠用小磨钻为镶座成形。

burrhead.t: 短而硬的平头发型；寸头

e.en: He sported a {burrhead} from his army days.
e.zh: 他留着当兵时的平头。

e.en: The boy's {burrhead} stuck up in all directions.
e.zh: 男孩的短硬头发各处翘起。

e.en: {Burrobrush} thrives in the dry washes of the desert.
e.zh: 驴灌在沙漠干涸河床中生长茂盛。

e.en: The trail wound through patches of {burrobrush}.
e.zh: 小径蜿蜒穿过几丛驴灌。

e.en: The fishermen built a {burrock} across the stream.
e.zh: 渔夫们在溪流上筑了一道拦鱼小坝。

e.en: Eels gathered behind the {burrock}.
e.zh: 鳗鱼聚集在拦鱼坝后面。

e.en: The miller selected a hard {burrstone} for grinding wheat.
e.zh: 磨坊主选了一块坚硬的磨石用来磨小麦。

e.en: Quarries supplied {burrstone} to mills across the region.
e.zh: 采石场为该地区的磨坊供应磨石。

e.en: Her sweater came home {burry} from the hike.
e.zh: 她的毛衣徒步回来后沾满了带刺果实。

e.en: The dog's fur was {burry} after the long walk.
e.zh: 狗散完长步后毛上沾满了刺球。

bursae.t: 滑囊；关节滑膜囊的复数

e.en: Inflammation of the {bursae} causes painful joints.
e.zh: 滑囊发炎会引起关节疼痛。

e.en: Several {bursae} cushion the shoulder joint.
e.zh: 肩关节有几个滑囊起缓冲作用。

bursalogy.t: 滑囊学；研究滑囊的医学分支

e.en: {Bursalogy} is a niche field within orthopedics.
e.zh: 滑囊学是骨科中的一个小众领域。

e.en: The textbook devotes a chapter to {bursalogy}.
e.zh: 教科书有一章专讲滑囊学。

e.en: She holds the {bursarial} office at the college.
e.zh: 她在学院担任财务主管职务。

e.en: The {bursarial} accounts were audited yearly.
e.zh: 财务主管的账目每年都要审计。

bursarship.t: 财务主管的职位；司库职务

e.en: He resigned from the {bursarship} after a decade.
e.zh: 十年后他辞去了财务主管的职务。

e.en: The new {bursarship} carries broader responsibilities.
e.zh: 新设的司库职位职责更广。

e.en: The priest carried the corporal in a velvet {burse}.
e.zh: 神父将祭布装在天鹅绒圣物盒中。

e.en: Coins jingled in his leather {burse}.
e.zh: 他的皮钱袋里硬币叮当作响。

e.en: Surgeons sometimes {bursectomize} chronically inflamed tissue.
e.zh: 外科医生有时会切除慢性发炎的滑囊。

e.en: They had to {bursectomize} the affected knee.
e.zh: 他们不得不切除受影响膝盖的滑囊。

bursectomy.t: 滑囊切除术；切除发炎滑囊

e.en: The patient underwent a knee {bursectomy} last week.
e.zh: 该病人上周接受了膝部滑囊切除术。

e.en: {Bursectomy} relieved her chronic shoulder pain.
e.zh: 滑囊切除术缓解了她慢性的肩痛。

e.en: She gave him a polite {bursh-off} at the door.
e.zh: 她在门口礼貌地把他打发走了。

e.en: After the {bursh-off}, he never called again.
e.zh: 被冷漠拒绝后，他再也没打过电话。

e.en: Botanists describe the flower as {bursiculate}.
e.zh: 植物学家将这朵花描述为小袋状的。

e.en: Microscopy revealed {bursiculate} structures on the leaf.
e.zh: 显微观察显示叶片上有小囊状结构。

bursiform.t: 囊状的；袋状的；钱包状的

e.en: The fungus has a {bursiform} fruiting body.
e.zh: 这种真菌有囊状子实体。

e.en: Botanists noted the {bursiform} pods on the plant.
e.zh: 植物学家注意到这种植物长有囊状荚果。

e.en: Doctors examined the {bursine} fluid for infection.
e.zh: 医生检查滑囊液是否有感染。

e.en: {Bursine} swelling can limit joint movement.
e.zh: 滑囊肿胀会限制关节活动。

e.en: Their partnership ended in a noisy {burst-up}.
e.zh: 他们的合伙关系以一场吵闹的破裂告终。

e.en: The deal led to a complete {burst-up} of the firm.
e.zh: 这笔交易导致公司彻底瓦解。

e.en: Honesty became his {by-word} in business.
e.zh: 诚信成了他做生意的座右铭。

e.en: That town is a {by-word} for poverty.
e.zh: 那个小镇成了贫困的代名词。

by-your-leave.t: 经允许；冒昧（多用于否定）

e.en: He took the car without so much as a {by-your-leave}.
e.zh: 他连招呼都不打一声就把车开走了。

e.en: She entered with a polite {by-your-leave}.
e.zh: 她礼貌地打了声招呼便走进来。

bycatch.t: 兼捕渔获物；附带捕获的鱼类

e.en: Dolphins are often killed as {bycatch} in tuna nets.
e.zh: 海豚常常作为兼捕物死于金枪鱼网中。

e.en: New rules aim to reduce {bycatch} at sea.
e.zh: 新规旨在减少海上的兼捕渔获。

e.en: She waved and said {bye-bye} to her grandma.
e.zh: 她挥着手对外婆说再见。

e.en: {Bye-bye}, see you tomorrow!
e.zh: 再见，明天见！

e.en: The party lost the {bye-election} badly.
e.zh: 该党在补选中惨败。

e.en: A {bye-election} was held to fill the vacant seat.
e.zh: 为填补空缺席位举行了补选。

e.en: The {byeelection} drew low voter turnout.
e.zh: 这次补选投票率很低。

e.en: Reports referred to the contest as a {byeelection}.
e.zh: 报道将这场竞选称为补选。

e.en: A small {byland} jutted into the sea.
e.zh: 一小片半岛伸入海中。

e.en: They sailed past the rocky {byland}.
e.zh: 他们驶过那片岩石密布的半岛。

e.en: Profit was only a {bymotive} for the project.
e.zh: 利润对这个项目而言只是次要动机。

e.en: He admitted to a hidden {bymotive}.
e.zh: 他承认有一个隐藏的次要动机。

e.en: He earned the {byname} Rocket for his speed.
e.zh: 他因速度极快而得了个火箭的绰号。

e.en: The king's {byname} described his fierce temper.
e.zh: 那位国王的绰号正反映了他暴躁的脾气。

bypast.t: 过去的；以往的（古旧用法）

e.en: In {bypast} years the village thrived.
e.zh: 在过去的岁月里，这个村庄曾繁荣兴盛。

e.en: Memories of {bypast} times warmed her heart.
e.zh: 对往昔的回忆温暖了她的心。

e.en: They followed a quiet {bypath} through the woods.
e.zh: 他们沿着一条幽静的小径穿过树林。

e.en: A rocky {bypath} led to the hut.
e.zh: 一条多石的小路通向小屋。

e.en: Many {bypaths} branched off from the main road.
e.zh: 许多小径从主路分出。

e.en: Hikers explored the forest {bypaths}.
e.zh: 徒步者们探索着森林中的小径。

byplay.t: 穿插表演；舞台上的次要动作

e.en: Comic {byplay} between the actors stole the show.
e.zh: 演员之间的滑稽穿插抢尽了风头。

e.en: The {byplay} on stage made the audience laugh.
e.zh: 舞台上的穿插表演逗得观众大笑。

e.en: A romantic {byplot} added depth to the novel.
e.zh: 一条浪漫的副线让小说更有深度。

e.en: The film's {byplot} felt rushed.
e.zh: 这部电影的次要情节显得仓促。

e.en: The warrior wore a heavy iron {byrnie}.
e.zh: 那名战士身穿沉重的铁制锁子甲。

e.en: His {byrnie} clinked as he walked.
e.zh: 他走动时锁子甲叮当作响。

e.en: We took a quiet {byroad} to avoid traffic.
e.zh: 我们走了一条偏僻小路以避开车流。

e.en: The {byroad} wound through farmland.
e.zh: 那条小路蜿蜒穿过农田。

e.en: His poetry shows traces of {byronism}.
e.zh: 他的诗中带有拜伦主义的痕迹。

e.en: {Byronism} influenced many Romantic writers.
e.zh: 拜伦主义影响了许多浪漫派作家。

byssi.t: 足丝（贝类附着用纤维束的复数）

e.en: Mussels secrete {byssi} to anchor on rocks.
e.zh: 贻贝分泌足丝以附着在岩石上。

e.en: Researchers studied the strength of mussel {byssi}.
e.zh: 研究人员研究了贻贝足丝的强度。

e.en: Workers in cotton mills risk developing {byssinosis}.
e.zh: 棉纺厂工人有患棉尘肺的风险。

e.en: {Byssinosis} causes chronic breathing problems.
e.zh: 棉尘肺会导致慢性呼吸障碍。

byssus.t: 足丝（贝类用以附着的纤维束）

e.en: The mussel attaches to rocks using its {byssus}.
e.zh: 贻贝用足丝附着在岩石上。

e.en: Each strand of the {byssus} is remarkably strong.
e.zh: 足丝的每一根都异常坚韧。

byssuses.t: 足丝（贝类附着用纤维束的复数）

e.en: Different shellfish produce {byssuses} of varying strength.
e.zh: 不同的贝类产生强度各异的足丝。

e.en: Scientists collected {byssuses} for analysis.
e.zh: 科学家们采集足丝以供分析。

e.en: The cafe sits on a quiet {bystreet}.
e.zh: 那家咖啡馆位于一条幽静的小街上。

e.en: He ducked into a narrow {bystreet}.
e.zh: 他闪进了一条狭窄的小街。

e.en: She wandered down a shaded {bywalk}.
e.zh: 她沿着一条树荫笼罩的小径漫步。

e.en: An old {bywalk} led to the orchard.
e.zh: 一条古老的小径通向果园。

e.en: Translating became her steady {bywork}.
e.zh: 翻译成了她稳定的副业。

e.en: He earns extra money through evening {bywork}.
e.zh: 他通过晚上的副业赚外快。

e.en: Rancid butter has a strong {butyric} smell.
e.zh: 变质的黄油有强烈的丁酸气味。

e.en: The lab tested for {butyric} acid in the sample.
e.zh: 实验室检测了样品中的丁酸含量。

buxomest.t: 最丰满的；最健康丰腴的

e.en: She was the {buxomest} of the three sisters.
e.zh: 她是三姐妹中最丰满的一个。

e.en: The painter chose the {buxomest} model for his canvas.
e.zh: 画家选了最丰腴的模特来画他的作品。

e.en: We need staff {buy-in} before launching the policy.
e.zh: 在推行这项政策前我们需要员工的支持。

e.en: The CEO secured board {buy-in} for the merger.
e.zh: 首席执行官争取到了董事会对合并的认同。

e.en: The management {buy-out} was completed last week.
e.zh: 管理层收购上周完成。

e.en: He accepted the {buy-out} offer and retired early.
e.zh: 他接受了买断条件提前退休。

e.en: Not everything in life is {buyable}.
e.zh: 生活中并非一切都可以用钱买到。

e.en: He claimed the judge was {buyable}.
e.zh: 他声称那位法官是可以收买的。

buydown.t: 利率买断；预付以降低利率

e.en: The seller offered a mortgage {buydown} to attract buyers.
e.zh: 卖方提供利率买断以吸引买家。

e.en: A two-year {buydown} lowered our monthly payments.
e.zh: 两年期的利率买断降低了我们的月供。

e.en: London was hit by {buzz-bombs} during the war.
e.zh: 伦敦在战争期间遭到飞行炸弹袭击。

e.en: The {buzz-bomb} exploded near the harbor.
e.zh: 那枚飞行炸弹在港口附近爆炸。

e.en: "Synergy" became a corporate {buzz-word}.
e.zh: "协同效应"成了企业界的流行术语。

e.en: Avoid {buzz-words} in your résumé.
e.zh: 简历中要避免使用时髦词。

e.en: The whole pub was {buzzin} after the goal.
e.zh: 进球之后整个酒吧都沸腾了。

e.en: I'm {buzzin} about the trip tomorrow.
e.zh: 我对明天的旅行兴奋不已。

e.en: Don't be such a {buzzkill} at the party.
e.zh: 在派对上别这么扫兴。

e.en: The rain was a real {buzzkill} on our picnic.
e.zh: 那场雨真把我们的野餐搅黄了。

e.en: We'll meet again {by-and-by}.
e.zh: 我们不久之后会再见面。

e.en: {By-and-by} the storm passed and the sun came out.
e.zh: 过了一会儿暴风雨过去，太阳出来了。

by-bidder.t: 拍卖中的托儿；假出价人

e.en: The auction house was accused of using {by-bidders}.
e.zh: 那家拍卖行被指控雇用托儿抬价。

e.en: A {by-bidder} drove the price artificially high.
e.zh: 一名假出价人把价格抬得虚高。

e.en: {By-bidding} is illegal in most jurisdictions.
e.zh: 虚假出价在大多数司法辖区都属违法。

e.en: They suspected {by-bidding} at the art auction.
e.zh: 他们怀疑那场艺术品拍卖存在托儿抬价。

e.en: The novel's hero turns out to be a nobleman's {by-blow}.
e.zh: 小说主角原来是某贵族的私生子。

e.en: His remark was a sly {by-blow} aimed at me.
e.zh: 他那句话是冲着我来的旁敲侧击。

e.en: Farming was his main job, with carpentry as a {by-business}.
e.zh: 务农是他的主业，木工是副业。

e.en: She runs a small {by-business} from home.
e.zh: 她在家经营一项小副业。

e.en: Boats slipped through a quiet {by-channel}.
e.zh: 船只从一条安静的支流里穿过。

e.en: The {by-channel} eventually rejoined the main river.
e.zh: 这条旁支水道最终汇入了干流。

e.en: Higher prices were a {by-effect} of the new tariff.
e.zh: 价格上涨是新关税的一个副作用。

e.en: The reform had several unintended {by-effects}.
e.zh: 这项改革带来了几个意想不到的附带影响。

e.en: A {by-election} was called after the MP resigned.
e.zh: 那位议员辞职后举行了补选。

e.en: The party lost badly in the {by-election}.
e.zh: 该党在补选中惨败。

e.en: Two {by-elections} will be held next month.
e.zh: 下个月将举行两场补选。

e.en: The government suffered defeats in recent {by-elections}.
e.zh: 政府在近期的几场补选中接连失利。

e.en: He helped us with no {by-end} in mind.
e.zh: 他帮我们时并无私心。

e.en: His charity hid a selfish {by-end}.
e.zh: 他做慈善其实暗藏私心。

e.en: We escaped through a narrow {by-lane}.
e.zh: 我们从一条狭窄的小巷溜走。

e.en: The shop is hidden in a quiet {by-lane}.
e.zh: 那家店藏在一条幽静的小巷里。

e.en: The town passed a new noise {by-law}.
e.zh: 该镇通过了一项新的噪音法规。

e.en: Smoking here violates a city {by-law}.
e.zh: 在这里吸烟违反了市政法规。

e.en: The club's {by-laws} require annual elections.
e.zh: 俱乐部章程规定每年举行选举。

e.en: Local {by-laws} prohibit parking on this street.
e.zh: 地方法规禁止在此街道停车。

e.en: The article carried her {by-line}.
e.zh: 这篇文章署有她的名字。

e.en: He earned his first {by-line} at twenty.
e.zh: 他二十岁时第一次拿到署名。

e.en: Several {by-lines} appeared on the front page.
e.zh: 头版上出现了好几个署名。

e.en: Junior reporters rarely get {by-lines}.
e.zh: 初级记者很少能拿到署名。

e.en: We took a {by-road} to avoid the traffic.
e.zh: 我们走小路避开了拥堵。

e.en: The cottage sat at the end of a muddy {by-road}.
e.zh: 那间小屋坐落在一条泥泞支路的尽头。

e.en: An innocent {by-stander} was injured in the crash.
e.zh: 一名无辜的旁观者在车祸中受伤。

e.en: Several {by-standers} called the police.
e.zh: 几名旁观者报了警。

e.en: They wandered down a forgotten {by-way}.
e.zh: 他们沿着一条被遗忘的小道闲逛。

e.en: The map showed every {by-way} in the county.
e.zh: 地图标出了该郡的每一条小路。

e.en: He hammered the {barrelhead} into place.
e.zh: 他把桶盖敲到位。

e.en: The seller wanted cash on the {barrelhead}.
e.zh: 卖家要求当场付现金。

e.en: She folded the {bed-cover} every morning.
e.zh: 她每天早上把床罩叠好。

e.en: A faded {bed-cover} lay across the guest bed.
e.zh: 一条褪色的床罩铺在客床上。

e.en: The waves were {bedashing} the rocks below.
e.zh: 海浪正拍打着下面的岩石。

e.en: Rain was {bedashing} the window all night.
e.zh: 雨整夜都在敲打窗户。

e.en: The {before-mentioned} rule applies to all members.
e.zh: 上述规则适用于所有成员。

e.en: Please review the {before-mentioned} documents first.
e.zh: 请先查看前面提到的文件。

e.en: The compound contains a {benzyl} group.
e.zh: 该化合物含有一个苄基。

e.en: They used {benzyl} alcohol as a solvent.
e.zh: 他们使用苯甲醇作溶剂。

e.en: I must {bethink} myself before answering.
e.zh: 回答之前我必须仔细想想。

e.en: She tried to {bethink} where she had seen him.
e.zh: 她试着想起在哪里见过他。

e.en: They sold fuel through a {blackmarket} network.
e.zh: 他们通过黑市网络出售燃料。

e.en: The painting entered a {blackmarket} after the theft.
e.zh: 那幅画被盗后流入了黑市。

e.en: She finished the edge with {blanket-stitch}.
e.zh: 她用锁边针法收完边。

e.en: The child's name was sewn in {blanket-stitch}.
e.zh: 孩子的名字是用毯边针绣上的。

e.en: The nurse checked my {blood-group} before surgery.
e.zh: 护士在手术前查了我的血型。

e.en: A rare {blood-group} can complicate transfusions.
e.zh: 罕见血型可能使输血变复杂。

e.en: The fisherman used a {blood-worm} as bait.
e.zh: 渔夫用红虫作鱼饵。

e.en: A {blood-worm} wriggled in the muddy water.
e.zh: 一条血虫在泥水里扭动。

e.en: The boiler's {blowoff} valve opened suddenly.
e.zh: 锅炉的放气阀突然打开了。

e.en: Her reply sounded like a polite {blowoff}.
e.zh: 她的回答听起来像礼貌的推脱。

e.en: She wore a {blue-and-white} dress to dinner.
e.zh: 她穿着蓝白相间的裙子去吃晚饭。

e.en: The shelf held several {blue-and-white} porcelain bowls.
e.zh: 架子上放着几个蓝白瓷碗。

e.en: A {boa-constrictor} coiled around the branch.
e.zh: 一条蟒蛇盘在树枝上。

e.en: The zoo keeps a large {boa-constrictor}.
e.zh: 动物园养着一条很大的蟒蛇。

e.en: Traditional {boat-building} requires patient handwork.
e.zh: 传统造船需要耐心的手工活。

e.en: He studied {boat-building} on the coast.
e.zh: 他在海边学习小船建造。

e.en: The defender delivered two hard {bodychecks}.
e.zh: 防守队员做了两次有力的身体冲撞。

e.en: Youth leagues often limit {bodychecks} for safety.
e.zh: 青少年联赛常为安全限制身体冲撞。

e.en: We bought our tickets at the {booking office}.
e.zh: 我们在售票处买了票。

e.en: The station {booking office} closes at six.
e.zh: 车站售票处六点关门。

e.en: The company focuses on the {bottom end} of the market.
e.zh: 这家公司专注于市场的低端部分。

e.en: The cable was damaged at the {bottom end}.
e.zh: 电缆在最下端受损了。

bottom-feeder.t: 底栖取食动物；底层逐利者

e.en: Catfish are often described as {bottom-feeders}.
e.zh: 鲶鱼常被称为底栖取食动物。

e.en: He called the dishonest trader a {bottom-feeder}.
e.zh: 他把那个不诚实的交易员称作底层逐利者。

e.en: Some investors began {bottom-fishing} after the market crash.
e.zh: 市场崩盘后，一些投资者开始抄底买入。

e.en: She went {bottom-fishing} for bargains at the antique fair.
e.zh: 她在古董集市上低价搜罗便宜货。

e.en: The {bottom line} is that we need more time.
e.zh: 关键是我们需要更多时间。

e.en: Higher costs hurt the company's {bottom line}.
e.zh: 成本上升损害了公司的最终利润。

e.en: House prices are finally {bottoming out}.
e.zh: 房价终于开始触底了。

e.en: The car kept {bottoming out} on the rough road.
e.zh: 汽车在崎岖路面上不断托底。

e.en: The key was in the {bottommost} drawer.
e.zh: 钥匙在最底下的抽屉里。

e.en: Only the {bottommost} layer was still wet.
e.zh: 只有最底层还是湿的。

e.en: The old contract mentioned {bottomry} on the merchant ship.
e.zh: 那份旧合同提到了商船抵押借款。

e.en: Few modern lawyers ever deal with {bottomry}.
e.zh: 现代律师很少处理船舶抵押借款。

e.en: He wore a bright {boubou} to the ceremony.
e.zh: 他穿着一件鲜艳的布布长袍参加仪式。

e.en: The tailor embroidered the {boubou} by hand.
e.zh: 裁缝手工刺绣了那件布布长袍。

e.en: Several men arrived in white {boubous}.
e.zh: 几名男子穿着白色布布长袍到场。

e.en: The market sold colorful {boubous} for festivals.
e.zh: 市场出售节日用的彩色布布长袍。

e.en: The chef served a warm {bouchee} before dinner.
e.zh: 厨师在晚餐前端上一份温热的一口点心。

e.en: Each {bouchee} was filled with mushrooms.
e.zh: 每个一口小点心里都填了蘑菇。

e.en: The tray was covered with tiny {bouchees}.
e.zh: 托盘上摆满了一口大小的小点心。

e.en: Guests enjoyed the cheese {bouchees} with wine.
e.zh: 客人们配着葡萄酒享用奶酪小点心。

e.en: The timber was {boucherized} to resist decay.
e.zh: 木材经过鲍彻法处理以防腐。

e.en: Engineers tried to {boucherize} the railway sleepers.
e.zh: 工程师尝试用鲍彻法处理铁路枕木。

e.en: The festival included an evening of opera {bouffe}.
e.zh: 艺术节安排了一晚滑稽歌剧。

e.en: His speech turned into political {bouffe}.
e.zh: 他的演讲变成了政治闹剧。

e.en: The old wall began to {bouge} outward.
e.zh: 那堵旧墙开始向外鼓起。

e.en: A small {bouge} appeared in the leather cover.
e.zh: 皮革封面上出现了一个小凸起。

e.en: The {boughless} trunk stood alone after the storm.
e.zh: 暴风雨后，那根无枝的树干孤零零地立着。

e.en: In winter, the {boughless} trees looked almost silver.
e.zh: 冬天里，那些秃枝的树看起来近乎银白。

e.en: She placed roses in a small {boughpot}.
e.zh: 她把玫瑰插进一个小花枝瓶里。

e.en: The antique {boughpot} stood on the mantelpiece.
e.zh: 那个古董插枝花瓶摆在壁炉台上。

e.en: Grandma disliked {boughten} bread from the store.
e.zh: 奶奶不喜欢商店里买来的面包。

e.en: He wore a {boughten} suit to the wedding.
e.zh: 他穿了一套现成买来的西装去婚礼。

e.en: Their new cafe feels a little {bougie}.
e.zh: 他们的新咖啡馆有点装阔的感觉。

e.en: The doctor inserted a {bougie} to dilate the passage.
e.zh: 医生插入探条来扩张通道。

e.en: The child began to {bouk} after the ride.
e.zh: 坐完车后，孩子开始干呕。

e.en: He felt ready to {bouk} at the smell.
e.zh: 闻到那股味道，他觉得快要吐了。

e.en: She {bouked} into the sink after dinner.
e.zh: 晚饭后她对着水槽吐了。

e.en: He nearly {bouked} when the smell hit him.
e.zh: 那股气味扑来时，他差点干呕。

e.en: We bought croissants at the corner {boulangerie}.
e.zh: 我们在街角的法式面包店买了羊角面包。

e.en: The {boulangerie} opens before sunrise every day.
e.zh: 那家法式面包店每天日出前就开门。

e.en: The ancient {bouleuterion} could hold hundreds of citizens.
e.zh: 那座古希腊议事厅可容纳数百名公民。

e.en: Archaeologists mapped the ruined {bouleuterion} near the agora.
e.zh: 考古学家测绘了集市附近的议事厅遗址。

boulevardier.t: 逛林荫大道的闲人；鸡尾酒

e.en: He dressed like a Parisian {boulevardier}.
e.zh: 他打扮得像个巴黎街头的闲逛绅士。

e.en: She ordered a {boulevardier} before dinner.
e.zh: 晚餐前她点了一杯 Boulevardier 鸡尾酒。

e.en: The old text called the condition {boulimia}.
e.zh: 那本旧书把这种病症称为贪食症。

e.en: Doctors now usually write bulimia rather than {boulimia}.
e.zh: 医生现在通常写作 bulimia，而不是 boulimia。

e.en: The cabinet was decorated with {boulle} marquetry.
e.zh: 那个柜子饰有布尔镶嵌工艺。

e.en: Collectors prize genuine {boulle} furniture.
e.zh: 收藏家珍视真正的布尔镶嵌家具。

e.en: Her confidence showed a quick {bounce-back}.
e.zh: 她的信心很快恢复了。

e.en: The market saw a strong {bounce-back} after Monday's fall.
e.zh: 周一下跌后，市场出现强劲反弹。

e.en: The red ball was the {bounciest} of all.
e.zh: 那个红球是所有球里最有弹性的。

e.en: She chose the {bounciest} tune for the party.
e.zh: 她为派对选了最欢快的一首曲子。

e.en: The ball rolled {bouncily} down the steps.
e.zh: 球一弹一弹地滚下台阶。

e.en: She walked {bouncily} into the meeting room.
e.zh: 她步伐轻快地走进会议室。

e.en: The sofa lost its {bounciness} over time.
e.zh: 这张沙发用久后失去了弹性。

e.en: The song needs more {bounciness} in the chorus.
e.zh: 这首歌的副歌需要更有活泼感。

e.en: Remote work created a more {boundaryless} office culture.
e.zh: 远程办公催生了更无边界的办公室文化。

e.en: The artist imagined a {boundaryless} world of color.
e.zh: 艺术家想象了一个没有边界的色彩世界。

e.en: His {bounderish} jokes made everyone uncomfortable.
e.zh: 他那些粗俗无礼的玩笑让大家都不舒服。

e.en: She disliked his {bounderish} manners at dinner.
e.zh: 她不喜欢他在晚餐时那种无赖般的举止。

e.en: The poem imagines a strange {boundlessment} beyond time.
e.zh: 这首诗想象了一种超越时间的奇异无限状态。

e.en: He spoke of {boundlessment} as pure freedom.
e.zh: 他把无边无际说成纯粹的自由。

e.en: New leaves {bourgeon} after the spring rain.
e.zh: 春雨过后，新叶开始萌发。

e.en: Small clubs began to {bourgeon} across the city.
e.zh: 小型俱乐部开始在全城迅速发展。

e.en: The doctor noted the patient's {brachydactylic} hand shape.
e.zh: 医生注意到病人手部有短指特征。

e.en: A {brachydactylic} trait can run in families.
e.zh: 短指特征可能在家族中遗传。

e.en: Relax, {brah}, everything is fine.
e.zh: 放松点，哥们儿，一切都没事。

e.en: He greeted every surfer with a casual {brah}.
e.zh: 他随口用“兄弟”招呼每个冲浪者。

e.en: My sister is {brainier} than I am.
e.zh: 我姐姐比我更聪明。

e.en: The team needed a {brainier} solution.
e.zh: 团队需要一个更有头脑的解决办法。

e.en: Each {branchia} helps the animal breathe underwater.
e.zh: 每个鳃都帮助这种动物在水下呼吸。

e.en: The diagram labels the {branchia} clearly.
e.zh: 图表清楚标出了鳃的位置。

e.en: Fish use their {branchiae} to take oxygen from water.
e.zh: 鱼用鳃从水中获取氧气。

e.en: The specimen's {branchiae} were visible under the microscope.
e.zh: 显微镜下可以看到标本的鳃。

e.en: The fish has seven {branchiostegal} rays on each side.
e.zh: 这种鱼每侧有七根鳃盖条。

e.en: Researchers measured the {branchiostegal} membrane carefully.
e.zh: 研究人员仔细测量了支鳃膜。

e.en: The marsh is a {breeding-ground} for mosquitoes.
e.zh: 这片沼泽是蚊子的滋生地。

e.en: Poor oversight became a {breeding-ground} for corruption.
e.zh: 监管不力成了腐败的温床。

e.en: The coat's {bulkiness} made packing difficult.
e.zh: 这件外套太笨重，打包很困难。

e.en: They reduced the machine's {bulkiness} without losing power.
e.zh: 他们在不降低功率的情况下减少了机器的庞大体积。

e.en: Her arrow hit the {bull's-eye}.
e.zh: 她的箭射中了靶心。

e.en: His prediction was a {bull's-eye}.
e.zh: 他的预测完全命中。

e.en: The defenders stopped the sudden {bull-rush}.
e.zh: 防守队员挡住了这次突然猛冲。

e.en: Police feared a {bull-rush} through the gates.
e.zh: 警方担心人群会猛冲过大门。

e.en: A {bullet-hole} marked the old wooden door.
e.zh: 旧木门上有一个弹孔。

e.en: Investigators photographed every {bullet-hole} in the wall.
e.zh: 调查人员拍下了墙上的每一个弹孔。

e.en: The landlord sent a {bullyboy} to scare tenants.
e.zh: 房东派了个打手去恐吓租户。

e.en: He behaved like a political {bullyboy}.
e.zh: 他的举止像个政治恶霸。

e.en: The coach would {bullyrag} players after every mistake.
e.zh: 队员每犯一次错，教练就会粗暴责骂。

e.en: Do not {bullyrag} people into agreement.
e.zh: 不要用威吓逼别人同意。

e.en: He {bullyrags} his staff in every meeting.
e.zh: 他每次开会都粗暴责骂员工。

e.en: The sergeant {bullyrags} recruits to test their nerve.
e.zh: 那名军士威吓新兵，以考验他们的胆量。

business-related.t: 与商业有关的；业务相关的

e.en: Please keep {business-related} receipts for tax records.
e.zh: 请保留业务相关的收据以备报税。

e.en: She missed dinner because of a {business-related} call.
e.zh: 她因为一通工作电话错过了晚餐。

e.en: He was {betaking} himself to the library at dawn.
e.zh: 黎明时他正动身去图书馆。

e.en: She spoke of {betaking} her talents to the stage.
e.zh: 她谈到要把自己的才华投向舞台。

e.en: Red blood cells have a {biconcave} shape.
e.zh: 红细胞呈双凹形。

e.en: The lens was ground into a {biconcave} form.
e.zh: 这片透镜被磨成双凹形状。

e.en: The report gave a {boiled-down} version of the findings.
e.zh: 报告给出了研究结果的浓缩版本。

e.en: Her argument was {boiled-down} to one clear demand.
e.zh: 她的论点被归纳为一个明确要求。

e.en: Water reaches its {boiling-point} at about 100 degrees Celsius.
e.zh: 水大约在摄氏100度达到沸点。

e.en: Public anger was near {boiling-point} after the scandal.
e.zh: 丑闻之后，公众愤怒几乎到了爆发点。

e.en: The {brigadier-general} inspected the troops before sunrise.
e.zh: 准将在日出前检阅了部队。

e.en: She was promoted to {brigadier-general} after decades of service.
e.zh: 服役数十年后，她被晋升为准将。
